# Sidecar infrastructure: technical design

Status: draft for peer review, revised 2026-11-04 after the first peer review (see [DESIGN-REVIEW-RESPONSE.md](DESIGN-REVIEW-RESPONSE.md)), on 2026-11-05 with the v1 additions of owner decisions [150](#od-150)-[184](#od-184) (versionless objects, the search index, CLI and MCP search, the indexer, the team directory and history drops), and on 2026-11-06 after the final meta review ([DESIGN-REVIEW-META.md](DESIGN-REVIEW-META.md)), with owner decisions [185](#od-185)-[191](#od-191), and at the implementation handoff, with owner decisions [192](#od-192)-[196](#od-196), on 2026-11-09 with [owner decision 197](#od-197), on the apps' network extensions, and from 2026-11-10 with the build's owner answers, [owner decisions 198](#od-198) onward, as the design-records tracks fold them. The owner signed G0 on 2026-11-06 ([owner decision 193](#od-193)), and M0-M10 build on the `sidecar` branches ([owner decision 194](#od-194)); nothing has shipped.

This document designs the sidecar infrastructure: the shared substrate under recURd, the private record of agent work, and under burner email, the consumer product in the URnetwork apps. It covers the new `github.com/urnetwork/sidecar` repo (the `sidecar.Sidecar` core, the sidecar subprotocol, the stdio MCP server, the `ur` CLI and the service engines); the horizontally scaled services that the server repo hosts for it (evs, gkm, sockets, dns with its dns edges, certs, tlsedge, smtpedge and mxedge), with the team-management and access-control additions; `sdk/sidecar.go`; the changes these need on connect's `sidecar` branch; and their build and deployment through sn, warp, config, vault, build, xops, mmm and the `urnetwork/minio` fork. It starts from the owner's PLAN.md (sidecar/design/PLAN.md). Out of scope: the apps, console and extension UI (only their seams are designed), harnesses and model hosting, the feedback service, recURd's record semantics beyond the X20 primitives (RECORD.md, an M0 deliverable designed separately), and prices beyond §20's tier and quota mechanics.

## Owner directive

The owner's words, 2026-11-03 (CONVENTIONS.md §0; the directive overrides PLAN.md where they conflict):

> **"End to end encryption is a must. The storage, tls edge, mail must only see encrypted bytes and some small header values like sni and spam headers."**

It is a requirement, not an open question, and it binds every section. In short:

- **TLS edge (X1).** TLS terminates in the listening sidecar. `tlsedge` routes by SNI (passthrough), never holds a user's TLS key and has no termination mode; PLAN.md:84's edge termination is superseded.
- **Storage (X2).** evs and gkm see only encrypted bytes plus small header values. Paths, file names, commit messages, author fields beyond the authenticated client id, and contents are encrypted; PLAN.md:59's plaintext paths are superseded. The published metadata list (§2.8, Appendix G) enumerates every header value.
- **Outbound mail (X7).** TLS runs end to end from the sidecar's mail server to the destination MX through `smtpedge`, which sees only ciphertext plus a small declared preamble. Edge-terminated submission and an SES relay are ruled out.
- **Inbound mail (X6).** TLS terminates on a device or a customer-run sidecar, never at a URnetwork edge. The edge may see SNI, the connecting IP, the EHLO name and spam-relevant values; encrypt-on-receipt at the edge is ruled out. The one exception is `rpt.bringyour.com`'s report and role-mail listener, which terminates TLS to accept abuse reports and role mail, parses headers and aggregate report data only (D-SMTP-23), HPKE-seals the raw bytes to the network mail key (§14.8) and persists no plaintext (§15.4's mx-4; §2.8's statement and I-2 carry the same clause).
- **Everything else.** Connect traffic between sidecars requires e2e encryption (Required, never Opportunistic or Off). gkm sees only encrypted MLS handshake data plus small headers. DNS data is public but reveals as little as possible (opaque labels, wildcards). A server component that would see plaintext content is a design error and is never offered as an option.

The sections cite the directive as "the directive", "owner directive 2026-11-03", "CONVENTIONS §0" or "§0".

## Owner rules

Hard constraints (CONVENTIONS.md §1); the sections do not re-litigate them.

1. **Code placement.** New pieces, the MLS implementation included, live in the sidecar repo. The server repo adds the horizontally scaled services that support them, integrates them, and takes the network and team client management and access-control enhancements. The sdk exposes the sidecar components.
2. **Dependency direction.** `sidecar` depends on `connect`, never on `server` or `sdk`; `server` and `sdk` import `sidecar`.
3. **Deleted code.** The message repo and connect/MESSAGEREVIEW.md are being deleted; nothing uses, cites or reuses them.
4. **Branches.** All sidecar work happens on a branch named `sidecar` in every repo it touches.
5. **Layout.** PLAN.md's tree: `go.mod`, `sidecar.go`, `protocol/`, `mcp/`, `cli/main.go`; server-only engines go in child packages ([owner decision 104](#od-104), §4.4).
6. **Scope.** The apps are out of scope; they use the sidecar directly, and the extension runs it as a web worker. This design covers their seams, not their UI.
7. **Product facts.** recURd is not tokenized and uses the URnetwork network for worldwide reach.
8. **PLAN.md is the default.** PLAN.md statements are requirements; a technical problem with one keeps the PLAN position visible and goes to the owner as a Q- item.

## Branch policy

All sidecar work happens on a branch named `sidecar` in every repo it touches (owner rule 4). Owner decisions [117](#od-117) and [118](#od-118) (2026-11-04) set the rest; §4.8, §23.9 and D-REPO-5 give the detail.

- **Public now, unscrubbed.** The sidecar repo is public from 2026-11-04 as it is, its documents and history included: no scrub, no archive, no filtered clone and no business-material allowlist ([owner decision 117](#od-117); D-REPO-8 is withdrawn). Its documents, DESIGN.md and `design/design-research/` among them, are on `main`; code starts on the `sidecar` branch (§4.11).
- **No private mirrors.** Every repo's `sidecar` branch uses that repo's normal remote, public where the repo is ([owner decision 118](#od-118); D-REPO-9 is withdrawn). The extension and app repos get one only if the owner opts in.
- **Branch starts** (§23.4): every touched repo in M0 ([owner decision 196](#od-196)): sidecar, connect, server, sdk, build, sn, xops, warp, config, mmm and vault, and the `urnetwork/minio` fork ([owner decision 195](#od-195)).
- **Merge, never rebase.** `main` merges into every `sidecar` branch weekly and before each gate, in the order connect, sidecar, sdk, sn, server, warp/config/vault/xops/mmm, build, re-pinning the source-graph lock each time.
- **To `main` at every exit review.** At each milestone's exit review (Gn-out, §23.8), every touched repo, server and sdk included, merges `sidecar` into `main` in that order, connect's default-off changes first, once the pinned set passes its checks and its migrations are additive and release-compatible. Deploys, pilots and releases build from `main`, with features dark behind `config/<env>/sidecar.yml` (D-OPS-10). Each §19.7 migration group stays pending under the `sidecar_pending` build tag until its own milestone's Gn-out registers it, and never changes after (D-OPS-6), so one track's merge never applies the other's group (FS-54) and M3's pilot runs on production ([owner decision 118](#od-118)). Nothing waits for publication or for RS1 (D-PHASE-5 is withdrawn).

## How to review

- **Where the decisions and questions are.** Every section follows one template: purpose and scope, requirements, what exists today, design, alternatives considered, decisions proposed, open questions, departures from PLAN.md, interfaces, risks and phasing. The [owner decisions](#owner-decisions) section below gives X1-X20, the [open owner questions](#open-owner-questions) (one, raised with [owner decision 197](#od-197)), the items [closed by peer review](#closed-by-peer-review) and the [owner decisions by number](#owner-decisions-by-number). [Appendix A](#appendix-a-decision-register) lists all 460 D- items (16 withdrawn). [Appendix B](#appendix-b-open-questions-register) lists all 202 Q- items: 174 decided by the owner, 11 closed by peer review on 2026-11-04, 12 closed by the 2026-11-03 design-review round, which reviewers may reopen (§3.11), 4 withdrawn, and 1 open for the owner.
- **Id families.**
  - `X1`-`X20`: cross-cutting decisions. Each has one owning section, which resolves it in a Q- item whose text starts with the X id.
  - `R-CODE-n`: a requirement in section CODE's requirements table, with its source (a PLAN.md line, a product source, an owner decision, or "derived").
  - `D-CODE-n`: a proposed decision with its rationale (*Why:*), a decided one that names its owner decision, or a withdrawn one that names what superseded it.
  - `Q-CODE-n`: a question with options, a recommendation, what it blocks and its decider (owner or peer review). It is open, decided by the owner, closed by the design-review round, closed by peer review, or withdrawn; a decided item records the decision and any residual.
  - `I-1`..`I-20`: the security invariants of §2.9, binding on every section.
  - CODEs: CTX §1, TRUST §2, ARCH §3, REPO §4, CORE §5, PROTO §6, TEAM §7, ACL §8, SOCK §9, KEYS §10, EVS §11, DNS §12, TLS §13, SMTP §14, MAIL §15, MCP §16, BRIDGE §17, SDK §18, OPS §19, QUOTA §20, ABUSE §21, TEST §22, PHASE §23.
  - Other families: C1-C19 (connect changes, §4.6, Appendix E), F1-F13 (flows, §3.7), KF1-KF7 (MLS flows, §10.7), S1-S13 (test scenarios, §22.7), FI-1 to FI-30 (fault-schedule invariants, §22.8), FS-1 to FS-125 (fault schedules, §22.8), I-EVS-1 to I-EVS-17 (evs storage invariants, §11.8), P0-P2 (§11.13's write-budget classes; P0 is also the staged auth fix, §7.4), AD1-AD4, AU1-AU4 and TS1 (approval-decision, approval-use and taint invariants, §16.6), RV1-RV4 (restore invariants, §16.7), DP1 (the device posture invariant, §18.6), WK1-WK5 (wake invariants, §18.7), E-a to E-e (escrow draw invariants, §20.9), M0-M10 (milestones, §23.4), G0, Gn-in and Gn-out (review gates, §23.8), RS1-RS3 (recURd stages) and BS1 (the burner launch), W1-W11 (warp changes, §19.5), Y1-Y2 (load years, §19.6), MG0-MG9 (migration groups, §19.7), T1-T6 (test tiers, §22.4), TL1-TL4 (MX authentication levels, §14.4), E1-E3 and Z1-Z9 (preamble proof checks, §14.5) and π1-π3 (its proof parts), EX1-EX8 (operator capabilities, §2.8), TB1-TB3 (trust boundaries, §2.4), H1 and H3 (connect carriers), and the metadata rows of §2.8 (connect-1, api-7, evs-11, ...). An id after a `[R:key]` link, such as "§5 R8" or "S11", names an item inside that research sheet. No external review gates any milestone ([owner decision 99](#od-99)).
- **Notation** (owner/APPLY.md §3; D-ARCH-1).
  - `<root>` is the user-content root, ur.network ([owner decision 13](#od-13)). `<net>` is the network's opaque, immutable label ([owner decision 14](#od-14)), or the opt-in alias where the user chose one. `<blabel>` is a burner's generated word-number label, so a burner address is `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` ([owner decision 32](#od-32)).
  - Burners use a wildcard MX `*.<net>.<root> MX 10 mx.<net>.<root>`, a DANE TLSA record at `_25._tcp.mx.<net>.<root>` and SNI `mx.<net>.<root>`. A wildcard owner name carries no CNAME (RFC 1034 §3.6.2, RFC 2181 §10.1); wildcard A and AAAA records (the shared lb addresses) sit beside the wildcard MX, and a replying burner's label carries an explicit copy of them (D-DNS-11).
  - Platform and service names live on bringyour.com ([owner decision 16](#od-16)). ur.io is the web; recURd runs at ur.io/recurd, and recurd.dev redirects there ([owner decision 15](#od-15)).
  - The bridge overlay is a random IPv4 /16 per network, drawn from 100.64.0.0/10 by default, and a chosen block lies in 100.64.0.0/10 or RFC 1918 (owner decisions [28](#od-28), [132](#od-132)).
  - `<host>` is a zone-relative host. `<scope>` is a v1 Team scope sublabel for a member or tag ([owner decision 40](#od-40)), whose hosts are `<label>.<scope>`. `<me>` appears only inside PLAN.md quotations.
- **Owner decisions.** "Owner decision N" cites entry N of the owner's record, owner/DECISIONS.md: entries 1-111 come from the interview of 2026-11-03; entries 112-125 from the follow-up of 2026-11-04, which answered the owner questions the fix rounds raised; entries 126-135 from that follow-up's second round, which answered those the conformance pass raised; entries 136-140 from the owner's evaluation of the storage tier; and entries 141-145 from the answers to the owner questions the 2026-11-04 peer review raised, all of 2026-11-04; entry 140's record was corrected the same day, withdrawing its first ~10-15 KiB of drive writes a push, a design-team estimate, for the binding budget (Q-EVS-9). Every such citation links to row N of [owner decisions by number](#owner-decisions-by-number), which gives the entry's date, states the decision in one line, notes supersession (owner/APPLY.md §2 and the later entries) and lists the sections that cite it. "Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decision N)" or "Decided by owner 2026-11-04 (owner decision N)" marks a Q- item the owner settled; "implied by owner decision N" marks one that follows from it; "Closed by peer review 2026-11-04" marks one the peer review answered.
- **PLAN.md is the default.** PLAN.md statements are requirements unless a D- or Q- item says otherwise. Each section's "Departures from PLAN.md" lists its exceptions, and [Appendix F](#appendix-f-planmd-traceability) traces every PLAN.md line.
- **Source keys.** P5 = sidecar/design/pitch5.html, PM = sidecar/design/product.md, MK2 = sidecar/design/market2.md, FB = sidecar/FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md, MM = sidecar/design/mocks/urnetwork-mobile.html, RA = sidecar/design/mocks/recurd-app.html, TM = sidecar/design/mocks/team-management.html, REC = sidecar/design/reports/Agent work record gaps and features.md, UI = cli/UI.md, EXT = connect/EXTENDERUPDATE.md, PLAN = sidecar/design/PLAN.md.
- **Citations.** Code is cited as `repo/path/file.go:LINE`, relative to the urnetwork checkout. `[R:key]` links a research fact sheet in [design/design-research/](design/design-research/) ([Appendix H](#appendix-h-research-sources)). "CONVENTIONS §0" is the owner directive above, "CONVENTIONS §1" the owner rules, and "CONVENTIONS §7" the X registry that the X1-X20 table replaces.

## Owner decisions

The owner answered 111 questions on 2026-11-03, after the end-to-end-encryption directive, then on 2026-11-04 14 more (entries 112-125) and 10 more (126-135), which settled every owner question that the fix rounds and the conformance pass raised; 5 entries on the storage tier (136-140); and 5 more (141-145), which answered the five owner questions that the 2026-11-04 peer review raised. That review closed the eleven Q- items left to it. The owner then corrected entry 140's record: its ~10-15 KiB of drive writes a push was a design-team estimate, unreachable when [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s head overwrite alone writes ~14 KiB, and the requirement is the PM9A3 profile itself, which the design meets at ~27-43 KiB a push, gated at 43 KiB (D-TEST-11). That decided [Q-EVS-9](#1118-open-questions), the one owner question raised while the sections were edited to the review, so no owner question was then open. The sections are edited to these answers. Where two answers disagree, owner/APPLY.md §2's supersession table and the later entries govern, and the table of [owner decisions by number](#owner-decisions-by-number) notes each case. The assembly's checks (decision citations, item status, residuals, and a grep for superseded options and for decided questions that still read as open) found no section text that contradicts a decision, except where a decision's own clauses conflict: [owner decision 114](#od-114)'s read-at-once and reap revocation do for Delegation-admitted agents, which §10.5 states as a residual. Entry 145's record was corrected on 2026-11-05 to the sections' sizing: ~490-650 pushes/s on the first set alone, ~400-450 a set once load spans clusters (batches per cluster), and five to six sets in year two. On 2026-11-05 the owner decided the four findings the second-round checks left partial (146-149: SL-N1, WR-N1, ST-N1 and AU-N2). Also on 2026-11-05 the owner named the indexer (150), set the v1 search index, versionless objects and CLI and MCP search (151-166), created the team directory (171), set no indexer by default (177, 178), and answered every owner question the v1 designs raised (167-170, 172-176, 179-184), so no owner question was then open. On 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06, with the owner's SDK fixes and the final meta review, the owner extended the presence countersignature (185, 187, 189), kept P0 writes unlimited outside the wear bound with their excess forgiven (186, 190), and kept [owner decision 176](#od-176)'s five-page promise through accounting windows (188, 191). On 2026-11-06, at the implementation handoff, the owner ratified the countersignature on a `DelegationRevoke` that parks other devices (192), signed G0 (193), set M0-M10 to build straight through on the `sidecar` branches (194), gave D-OPS-20's MinIO build a fork of its own (195) and opened every touched repo's `sidecar` branch at M0 (196). On 2026-11-09, as the build planned the apps' integration, the owner put only IP and port forwarding in every app's VPN component, always on and self-contained, and ran Android's sidecar only while the app is open (197), amending owner decisions [87](#od-87) and [12](#od-12); designing it raised two owner questions, [Q-SDK-7](#1813-open-questions), which owner decisions [215](#od-215) and [216](#od-216) decide, and [Q-BRIDGE-8](#1714-open-questions), open below. From 2026-11-10 the design-records tracks number the owner's answers to the build's questions as they fold them: the nightly count's shard sums (198), Team subscriptions (199), the fold's leaf places (200), gkm's owner marker (201), forwarding reader keys at gkm (202), the orphan horizon (203), the drop job's horizon (204), amending [owner decision 183](#od-183), settings in rows (205), the sweep's triggers (206), a reported URL's path (207), the sealed abuse mailboxes (208), head readers' read records (209), the primary's physical copies (210), the key origin served direct (211), the compromise rebind's procedure (212), no apt or yum repository in v1 (213), the witness call outside the planes (214), forwarding's iOS executable budget and compile cap (215, 216), the key origin's per-network databases (217), multi-use bridge approvals (218), the key origin's sign-in hand-off (219), requested grants' sealed detail (220), promoted key-origin builds (221), wintun.dll left unbundled (222), the ur.io/recurd page (223) and C16's latch (224). This section lists the cross-cutting decisions, the open owner questions, what peer review closed, and every decision with the sections that implement it.

X1-X20 are the cross-cutting decisions the research surfaced (CONVENTIONS §7). Each row is built from its owning section's `[Xn]` Q- item: its question, the decision with the owner decisions that settle it, and its residual as the item states it. Every X item is decided, and no residual waits for the owner; X6's row notes the one launch call the owner keeps outside the Q- items.

### Open owner questions

One, raised on 2026-11-09 in designing [owner decision 197](#od-197)'s forwarding: [Q-BRIDGE-8](#1714-open-questions) (an app device's overlay address), to whose recommendation the sections are written, marked "(proposed; [Q-BRIDGE-8](#1714-open-questions))". The other raised with it, [Q-SDK-7](#1813-open-questions) (forwarding's budget in the iOS network extension), was decided on 2026-11-10 (owner decisions [215](#od-215), [216](#od-216)). Every other Q- item whose decider was the owner is decided. Owner decisions [112](#od-112)-[135](#od-135) answered those the fix rounds and the conformance pass raised, and owner decisions [141](#od-141)-[145](#od-145) the five that the 2026-11-04 peer review raised ([Q-EVS-8](#1118-open-questions), [Q-MCP-6](#1614-open-questions), [Q-OPS-9](#1914-open-questions), [Q-KEYS-15](#1012-open-questions), [Q-OPS-10](#1914-open-questions)). [Q-EVS-9](#1118-open-questions), raised while the sections were edited to that review, is decided by [owner decision 140](#od-140)'s record as corrected on 2026-11-04: the binding budget, gated at 43 KiB a push per drive (D-TEST-11); the record's first ~10-15 KiB a push, a design-team estimate, is withdrawn. Outside the Q- items, the owner keeps one launch call on measured data: accepting the SNI loss that M7's census measures, before BS1 (D-MAIL-9; [owner decision 34](#od-34); §23.6).

### Closed by peer review

No Q- item is open for peer review. The items whose decider was peer review were closed on 2026-11-04; each now reads “Closed by peer review 2026-11-04” in its section, with its answer, and §23.6 lists what each still gates. Decided items leave two engineering residuals: [Q-SDK-1](#1813-open-questions)'s size spike, which decides C17 ([Q-REPO-2](#414-open-questions)), and [Q-OPS-3](#1914-open-questions)'s, which leaves the Postgres-held sidecar rows to peer review: D-OPS-18's daily off-site dump, whose design closure M0's entry review needs (§23.6), and 19.10's reconcile. The items the 2026-11-03 design-review round closed ([Appendix B](#appendix-b-open-questions-register)) were not closed by human peer review, and reviewers may reopen them (§3.11).

| <a id="od-192"></a>192 | 2026-11-06 | Presence countersignature | A `DelegationRevoke` that parks other devices (`since_n` > 0) also carries the countersignature: the final meta review's extension, following [owner decision 187](#od-187)'s intent, ratified as written. | §5, §7, §22, §23 |
| <a id="od-193"></a>193 | 2026-11-06 | G0 | The owner signs G0 on 2026-11-06; the re-checks of the 21 items DESIGN-REVIEW-RESPONSE.md places at G0, the density review and RECORD.md's draft run beside M0's bootstrap, and their findings return as Q- items. | §23 |
| <a id="od-194"></a>194 | 2026-11-06 | Build order | M0-M10 build straight through in dependency order on the `sidecar` branches: each gate's local checks run and are reported, and anything needing hardware, production or people stays listed open. §23.8's freezes do not move. | §22, §23 |
| <a id="od-195"></a>195 | 2026-11-06 | D-OPS-20 | D-OPS-20's MinIO build lives in a new `urnetwork/minio` fork, a sibling checkout with its own `sidecar` branch, keeping MinIO's AGPL source in one public place; the owner creates the GitHub repo before any push. | §3, §4, §19, §23 |
| <a id="od-196"></a>196 | 2026-11-06 | Branch starts | A `sidecar` branch on all repos the work touches: warp's, config's, mmm's and vault's all open at M0, so §19.11 lands W5 at M0 and W2 and W8 by M4 on warp's branch. | §4, §19, §23 |
| <a id="od-197"></a>197 | 2026-11-09 | [Q-SDK-2](#1813-open-questions), [Q-MAIL-2](#1513-open-questions) | Every app's VPN component runs the device's IP and port forwarding and nothing else of sidecar, always on and self-contained with its own forwarding key, amending [owner decision 87](#od-87); Android's sidecar runs only while the app is open, as iOS's does, amending [owner decision 12](#od-12). | §1, §2, §3, §4, §5, §6, §7, §8, §10, §11, §12, §15, §17, §18, §19, §20, §22, §23 |
| <a id="od-198"></a>198 | 2026-11-10 | Stored count | The nightly pass's shard jobs keep per-network sums for the night in Redis `{evsn_<night>}` (48 h); a closing job writes each network's count once every shard of every metadata cluster has reported, and a night left unfinished keeps the old count. | §2, §19, §20 |
| <a id="od-199"></a>199 | 2026-11-10 | Team billing | A `team_subscription` row (MG6) records each Team's Stripe subscription, customer, anchor and start, written at the first `invoice.paid` and ended at `customer.subscription.deleted`; only a live row is granted a period. | §2, §19, §20 |
| <a id="od-200"></a>200 | 2026-11-10 | Path epochs | The fold records each folded version's place in its statement's change list (`leaf_part`, `leaf_index`), so evs serves the proof of a version an older path epoch wrote and the reader checks the leaf names its token. | §2 |
| <a id="od-201"></a>201 | 2026-11-10 | Group owner | A group's first object is `gkm/<group_id>/owner` (repo and network), created If-None-Match from the token; every group route resolves through it, so no other repo's form can claim the group. | §2, §10 |
| <a id="od-202"></a>202 | 2026-11-10 | Forwarding keys | A forwarding Delegation's row carries its reader key's SHA-256, and the 1,216 B key is the gkm object `gkm/dkey/<delegation_id>`, keeping 5,000-device rows near 2.2 MB under §8.8's 4 MiB. | §2, §10 |
| <a id="od-203"></a>203 | 2026-11-10 | Segment GC | An unadopted segment goes once no batch is left from before its upload + 24 h + 2 min, 49 to 75 h, so GC raises no fence; evacuation fences a ref with no head by a placeholder head. | §2, §11, §19, §22 |
| <a id="od-204"></a>204 | 2026-11-10 | Drop history | A drop job marks only once evacuation's horizon has passed each covered drop's commit by 2 min, so a `now` drop's deletions start about 25 to 26 h after it, amending [owner decision 183](#od-183)'s 25-minute fence. | §2, §11, §22 |
| <a id="od-205"></a>205 | 2026-11-10 | Settings in rows | `self_admit` and `scim_signer` compile into `ProjectionRows.settings`, which full readers check against the head and api and the gates take, so every verifier judges a self-admission alike. | §2 |
| <a id="od-206"></a>206 | 2026-11-10 | Versionless sweep | `AbuseHoldPass` queues a hold's end pass before it deletes `hold/`, and `sidecarctl evs purge-turn-on` queues the turn-on pass in the step that sets `format2.purge: on`. | §2, §11 |
| <a id="od-207"></a>207 | 2026-11-06 | Abuse cases | A case keeps a reported URL's path and query until its first review ends, at most its review clock; never a reporter's address or free text but an appeal's own reason. | §2, §13, §21 |
| <a id="od-208"></a>208 | 2026-11-06 | Abuse mailboxes | The abuse and legal-request mailboxes sit at one provider outside URnetwork's Postgres and clusters; each record is sealed to a vault-held HPKE key before it leaves api, so the provider and SES see sender, time and size. | §2, §19, §21 |
| <a id="od-209"></a>209 | 2026-11-06 | Head reads | Head readers keep a sealed record per path read (ref, path, entry version, pin), at most 16,384 a network, and read a recorded path from its record's pin, so the published limit is a path never read or no longer remembered. | §2, §5, §11, §22 |
| <a id="od-210"></a>210 | 2026-11-06 | D-TRUST-7 | The primary's physical copies count as backups: each is refreshed or destroyed within 7 d, and the 24 h edge records' partitions are UNLOGGED, so no physical copy holds them. | §2, §19 |
| <a id="od-211"></a>211 | 2026-11-06 | Key origin | `sidecar.ur.io` is served direct, unproxied, never through Cloudflare, which terminates https://ur.io; §2.8's EX7 discloses that Cloudflare sees page requests and can alter page script. | §2, §18, §19 |
| <a id="od-212"></a>212 | 2026-11-06 | Recovery rebind | After a compromise rebind at r, `--compromise` lists the member's devices, clamps the rebind signer's since_n to r + 1 so the rebind stands, and revokes that signer last, by the replacement it enrolls. | §2, §5, §7, §10, §18, §22 |
| <a id="od-213"></a>213 | 2026-11-06 | Linux packages | v1 ships no apt or yum repository: `.deb` and `.rpm` stay direct downloads through `install.sh`'s verified path, with no GPG key or repository host. | §2, §4 |
| <a id="od-214"></a>214 | 2026-11-06 | D-ARCH-2 | A checkpointer's own HTTPS call to a witness its log admin named is no URnetwork carrier: it carries a signed note and a consistency proof, never an entry, and no URnetwork server takes part. | §3 |
| <a id="od-215"></a>215 | 2026-11-10 | [Q-SDK-7](#1813-open-questions) | Forwarding adds at most 6 MiB of stripped executable to the iOS network extension, whose signed ceiling rises from 50 MiB to 54 MiB; one implementation of the rule table stays. | §1, §3, §4, §18, §22, §23 |
| <a id="od-216"></a>216 | 2026-11-10 | [Q-SDK-7](#1813-open-questions) | A forwarding compile in the Apple extensions needs 5 × rows + 2 × head + 1 MiB within a 10 MiB cap and the room under a 30 MiB ceiling, about 4,300 devices; a larger network keeps its last verified state there and alarms, and no wait for a compile makes it pending. | §1, §3, §17, §18, §22, §23 |
| <a id="od-217"></a>217 | 2026-11-10 | Key origin storage | The key origin keeps one IndexedDB database per network, `urnetwork-sidecar-v1-<network_id>`, each its own instance and root key, so the per-network Web Lock covers everything a Worker writes. | §18 |
| <a id="od-218"></a>218 | 2026-11-10 | Bridge approvals | `BridgeApproval.template_action` carries a multi-use decision's template beside each use's action, so readers check the use against it and one decision files up to its uses bridge rules. | §17 |
| <a id="od-219"></a>219 | 2026-11-06 | Key origin sign-in | The key origin signs a page Worker in by the ur.io session's hand-off: a one-time `/auth/code-create` code by postMessage, redeemed at `/auth/code-login` to mint its client, the network token then dropped. | §7, §18, §23 |
| <a id="od-220"></a>220 | 2026-11-06 | Requested grants | A requested `dial` or `route` grant's prefixes and ports move into its CanonicalAction's sealed `sealed_detail`, so api checks the grant by ids alone. | §8, §16, §17 |
| <a id="od-221"></a>221 | 2026-11-06 | Key origin builds | `sidecar.ur.io` serves only a promoted build, its loader and `sidecar.wasm` listed in the release's signed `SHA256SUMS` and the wasm's hash pinned in the loader; no browser checks them on load. | §2, §4, §18 |
| <a id="od-222"></a>222 | 2026-11-06 | `ur tun` on Windows | `ur tun` neither bundles nor fetches wintun.dll; it loads one beside `ur.exe` or at the app's path only once its hash and signer match the Windows app's pins. | §17 |
| <a id="od-223"></a>223 | 2026-11-06 | ur.io/recurd | A minimal real ur.io/recurd page (label, key-origin frame, sign-in, records, downloads) is built on mmm's `sidecar` branch; its visual design stays out. | §18, §23 |
| <a id="od-224"></a>224 | 2026-11-06 | C16 | C16's receive gate latches at this side's seal for M4; before M8 turns it on for app-device hosts the plaintext in flight at a seal is measured, and a visible loss moves the latch to the peer's first sealed frame within `TlsTimeout`. | §4, §17, §18 |

## 1. Context, goals, and requirements

### 1.1 Purpose and scope

This section defines the sidecar infrastructure, its consumers, goals, and non-goals, and holds the R-CTX catalog and PLAN.md's tier table. It designs no mechanism and owns no X item; trust is §2, pricing §20, milestones §23.

### 1.2 Requirements

From [R:product](design/design-research/product.md) §2.2 and PLAN.md, as the directive and the cited owner decisions amend them; source keys and placeholders follow the front matter.

| Id | Requirement | Source | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-CTX-1 | `github.com/urnetwork/sidecar`, public from 2026-11-04, imports only connect; server and sdk import it; new pieces live there | PLAN.md:5-7; [owner decision 118](#od-118) | §4 |
| R-CTX-2 | `sidecar.Sidecar` holds an authenticated JWT, connect client, api, and encryption key | PLAN.md:14 | §5 |
| R-CTX-3 | `ur` speaks stdio MCP by default (help on a terminal), as a userspace subprocess of any harness | PLAN.md:17-20; PM:17; [owner decision 57](#od-57) | §16 |
| R-CTX-4 | One daemon serves many harnesses; runs in cloud containers without TUN or root; dials only allow-listable endpoints | UI:10-19; MK2:537; EXT:172-174; [owner decision 49](#od-49) | §5; §18.9 |
| R-CTX-5 | `sdk/sidecar.go` exposes key controls and joins the device (ip addr, port forward); the extension runs it as a web worker | PLAN.md:28-31; [owner decision 26](#od-26) | §18 |
| R-CTX-6 | A sidecar subprotocol carries peer and service messages; services push in real time | PLAN.md:15-16,55,119 | §6 |
| R-CTX-7 | A sidecar is a network client, enrolled interactively or headless; the free tier runs "any number of agents" | RA:929-930; P5:844; [owner decision 4](#od-4) | §5 |
| R-CTX-8 | A client token cannot administer the network or mint a network login | derived (`server/api/route_authz.go:123`) | §7 |
| R-CTX-9 | Agent tokens last at most 1 h, bind to the sidecar's key, and never enter the agent's environment | FB:139 | §5 |
| R-CTX-10 | Many users per network: roles, invitations, device approval, auth keys, tags; SSO on Team | PLAN.md:5,363; TM:384-1124 | §7 |
| R-CTX-11 | Once written, deny-by-default policy over clients, groups, networks, and sockets, signed into the encrypted config repo that every admitted sidecar evaluates; servers enforce its signed id-only projection; grants carry approver and expiry; one switch revokes an agent's reach | PLAN.md:74,119; P5:680,729; owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6), [72](#od-72), [105](#od-105) | §7, §8 |
| R-CTX-12 | MLS-managed keys: one group per directory, member devices its leaves, agents on per-generation X-Wing wraps; a network's member devices past the first 1,000 read its config and team directory groups by wraps; key generations wrapped in GKM; one accepted Commit per epoch; no server holds group secrets or plaintext keys; lazy rewrap by checkpoint | PLAN.md:44-53,155-161,221; owner decisions [59](#od-59), [60](#od-60), [64](#od-64), [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182) | §10 |
| R-CTX-13 | One directory is one git repo served by the sidecar; git identity is the client id; paths, names, messages, and contents are encrypted; the server sees only §11.5's header values | PLAN.md:53-59; directive; owner decisions [2](#od-2), [24](#od-24), [81](#od-81) | §11 |
| R-CTX-14 | Diffs plus a checkpoint every N commits for versioned files, versionless ones keeping only their head (R-CTX-34); head read without a clone; subpath subscriptions; per-agent branches, tip compare-and-swap on git-mode refs, plain-git export | PLAN.md:55,63; MK2:513-531; owner decisions [141](#od-141), [158](#od-158) | §11 |
| R-CTX-15 | Blobs, and all durable evs and gkm state, in a new MinIO file cluster: an HDD segment cluster, and NVMe metadata clusters added whole under a drive write budget, each repo and its gkm group placed on one at creation; only rebuildable soft state in Redis | PLAN.md:61; owner decisions [2](#od-2), [94](#od-94), [116](#od-116), [136](#od-136)-[140](#od-140), [145](#od-145) | §19 |
| R-CTX-16 | Vault and change set: every session and changed file, any harness or tool path, under the developer's keys, secrets redacted; restores are previewed, confined to the run's changes, and recorded | PLAN.md:107-109; P5:617-622 | §16 |
| R-CTX-17 | Two key domains: session contents for their author unless shared, actions and approvals for admins, while in a team network a run's who, what and where reach teammates by default (R-CTX-38); without the author's signed consent, admins add to the author's repos only the visible audit member, whose reads the author sees | P5:579,640; owner decisions [63](#od-63), [126](#od-126), [170](#od-170) | §8.5, §10 |
| R-CTX-18 | Record primitives: signed append-only entries, approval and reach receipts, run coverage, retention, erasure | P5:892-904,941; [owner decision 25](#od-25) | §16 |
| R-CTX-19 | Listen on an abstract `<net>:<name>`; a dial reaches one listener, chosen by load | PLAN.md:69; [owner decision 65](#od-65) | §9 |
| R-CTX-20 | `<root>` (PLAN.md's ur.network) is its own zone, for user content only; each network owns `<net>.<root>`; Team adds custom domains | PLAN.md:25,80,364; owner decisions [13](#od-13), [14](#od-14) | §12 |
| R-CTX-21 | The lbs pass `*.<root>` names to tlsedge, which routes them unterminated, by SNI, to a listening sidecar, where TLS ends; certificates are automatic | PLAN.md:80-84; directive; owner decisions [34](#od-34), [39](#od-39) | §13 |
| R-CTX-22 | Public names are explicit, authenticated by default, short-lived; the certificate key stays in the sidecar | P5:698-699; owner decisions [41](#od-41), [42](#od-42) | §13 |
| R-CTX-23 | SMTP edge: daily caps; end-to-end TLS to the MX behind a ZK-verified preamble (routing path, Message-ID); abuse reports join back to the sending network for tiered, domain-scoped halts (§14.8) | PLAN.md:87-97; owner decisions [30](#od-30), [35](#od-35), [37](#od-37), [99](#od-99) | §14 |
| R-CTX-24 | A local SMTP server on a receiver, reliably on a mail indexer (R-CTX-33), terminates `mx.<net>.<root>` (PLAN.md:104's `mail.<me>.ur.network`), stores mail encrypted, and sends through the edge; with no receiver online, mail waits on sender retries; the edge holds nothing | PLAN.md:104; directive; owner decisions [12](#od-12), [32](#od-32), [34](#od-34), [150](#od-150) | §15 |
| R-CTX-25 | Ids and burners: unlimited aliases and groups; burner addresses `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` under the network's wildcard MX, linkable through `<net>`; password, one-time auth, URL, notes | UI:68-73; MM:918; owner decisions [29](#od-29), [32](#od-32) | §15 |
| R-CTX-26 | Outside mail is untrusted; first mail to a new recipient awaits an I-8 approval, never an email reply; group fan-out | P5:707,736; RA:1584; owner decisions [75](#od-75), [80](#od-80), [142](#od-142) | §15, §16 |
| R-CTX-27 | Route a client's subnets to that client; rewrite destination ip:port when IP-providing for the same network; a stable private address per sidecar in the network's random /16, which admins may cycle, or choose in 100.64.0.0/10 or RFC 1918 | PLAN.md:115-117; P5:686; owner decisions [4](#od-4), [28](#od-28), [132](#od-132) | §17 |
| R-CTX-28 | With a policy, agents reach only granted ranges and model servers, and leave only through customer-run exits; without one, sidecar sources keep today's same-network reach, LAN, loopback, link-local and overlay included, disclosed in product copy | P5:689,774-781; owner decisions [50](#od-50), [105](#od-105), [120](#od-120) | §8, §17 |
| R-CTX-29 | Servers hold only ciphertext plus a published metadata list | P5:745,932; directive | §2 |
| R-CTX-30 | Tier limits (§1.8) only through `config/all/pro.yml` and `model.Pro()`; traffic bytes count toward the transfer balance, capacities are quotas | PLAN.md:346-364; owner decisions [10](#od-10), [27](#od-27) | §20 |
| R-CTX-31 | `ur share add` makes a link that `ur share get` redeems at most `--count` times; file transfer counts toward the transfer balance | UI:35-38,97 | §9 (D-SOCK-16) |
| R-CTX-32 | Each service is added vertically, through sidecar to server | PLAN.md:36 | §23 |
| R-CTX-33 | A network designates indexers, its always-on point devices for background services: receiving mail, mirroring record-class repos, search-index roll-ups and verification, keeping the all search partition synced, answering phones' searches (R-CTX-37), embedding later, and other services that need an always-on device; none by default, several may serve, a Team's receivers are indexers chosen for mail, and a designation grants no access | owner decisions [12](#od-12), [58](#od-58), [150](#od-150), [177](#od-177) | §3.6, §7.9 |
| R-CTX-34 | Versioning per object: a file version is versioned (every version kept, as diffs) or versionless (only the head kept, whole). A replaced versionless version's content is purged once its replacement is certain, after about a minute for readers in flight, and versions written while versioning was on stay unless a repo admin drops the path's history (R-CTX-39). Each network has a default rule, versioning off above 64 MiB on the platform default, which admins edit, applied when a path is created ([owner decision 167](#od-167)). No versionless file in config or mailcfg repos or on git-mode refs; a repo admin may lock a repo versioned. Large files in git go through git-lfs on a versionless store, collected once no ref tip and no commit of the last 30 days (per repo) references them | owner decisions [158](#od-158), [160](#od-160)-[165](#od-165), [167](#od-167) | §11 |
| R-CTX-35 | An encrypted search index, always versionless, in every repo but config, mailcfg and secret ones (D-EVS-43), locked repos included ([owner decision 168](#od-168)), on unless a repo admin turns it off, and always on in the team directory ([owner decision 171](#od-171)). Each committer adds its document-level trigram delta to the current bucket, in its push or, for git-mode refs and record streams, a companion push at most once a minute per writer on 1 KiB XFS blocks, else once every 5 minutes ([owner decision 172](#od-172)), binaries skipped. Devices download it whole and search locally (I-19): two buckets of a per-repo window (30 days by default, 7-365) at once, an all partition in the background or on "search more", the newest version winning; an indexer (R-CTX-33), else a writer, rolls each expired bucket into all. Desktops and indexers keep all synced and verify against local text; phones and pages fetch it on "search more" or on Wi-Fi while charging, each device able to override, and show possible matches; once an indexer is designated, a phone's "search more" asks it instead (R-CTX-37). An erasure removes a document's postings | owner decisions [151](#od-151)-[157](#od-157), [159](#od-159), [160](#od-160), [168](#od-168), [171](#od-171), [172](#od-172) | §11, §15, §16, §18 |
| R-CTX-36 | `ur search`, `ur agents` and MCP search tools: scope (repo, network, all), filters (agent, time, kind, path prefix, field) and "search more"; agents found by task, hits grouped by agent; hits labeled confirmed, possible or near; the daemon's per-network index cache (§5.9); only repos the caller may read, owner-bound ones under the owner's consent; untrusted hits' text only on request, the run tainted first (I-9) | owner decisions [126](#od-126), [166](#od-166) | §16 |
| R-CTX-37 | Once its network designates an indexer that may answer (none by default), a phone's "search more" asks it end to end while it is online and gets verified hits: an owner-bound repo only on its owner's consented device, replies padded to 16 KiB steps and the pair's reported bytes a fixed floor a window, so up to five pages report as none, another member's device only after the app names that member; otherwise the phone downloads all and searches its own index, with possible matches | owner decisions [175](#od-175)-[178](#od-178), [188](#od-188) | §4.6, §6.10, §11.14, §18.4 |
| R-CTX-38 | One team directory per team network announces runs, workers and repos, each with who, what and where: runs by default, members opting out per member and project; every general and record repo at creation, unless its owner marks it private, and an owner may revoke an announcement. Members and their agents request access to repos and workers through it, access to a worker being reach to the services it announces, approved by the worker's owner or a tagged worker's sponsor. Session contents stay in the vault; the directory is its own MLS group under the config group's leaves rule | owner decisions [170](#od-170), [171](#od-171), [179](#od-179)-[182](#od-182) | §16.11 |
| R-CTX-39 | In v1 a repo admin, or in an owner-bound repo only its owner, can drop a path's history on a file-mode ref outside config and mailcfg repos: a signed action pending 7 days, in which any of them can cancel, unless `now` skips the wait; it deletes only content that the dropped versions alone name, keeps every statement and the head, and under a preservation hold defers its deletions silently | owner decisions [126](#od-126), [173](#od-173), [183](#od-183), [184](#od-184) | §11.7, §11.13 |

### 1.3 What exists today

Nothing in this design is built. The sidecar repo holds documents and no code, in two commits on `main` (2b5b0ab, 2026-11-03; 708bb45, 2026-11-05, which moved the business documents under `design/` and added DESIGN.md, its reviews, README.md, the research sheets and the search-index report and notes), published as it is, history included, from 2026-11-04 (owner decisions [117](#od-117), [118](#od-118); §4.3, §4.11); `sdk/sidecar.go` does not exist. The server has one `admin_user_id` per network, no members, roles, or policy, and only the `free` and `pro` tiers (`server/db_migrations.go:351-358`; `server/model/pro.go:429`; §20.3). §6.3, §13.3, §14.3, and §19.3 describe connect and the edges today.

### 1.7 Goals, non-goals, and promises that bind the infrastructure

Goals: one substrate for both products and the apps; every PLAN.md service designed to implementable depth, PLAN.md positions visible unless superseded (§1.14); servers see only ciphertext and the metadata list (R-CTX-29); runs where consumers run; scales horizontally on warp.

Non-goals: a harness, agent, model host, or eval product (PM:21,47; MK2:618-620); a token (P5:934; owner decisions [15](#od-15), [108](#od-108)); app, console, or extension UI (PLAN.md:28), including OS password-manager registration (MM:465); a general exit for agent traffic; the feedback service (D-CTX-4); record semantics and exports (RECORD.md; [owner decision 25](#od-25)); the instruction-file writer (P5:629) and run cost.

Promises (D-CTX-3):

| Promise | Binds | Conflict |
|---|---|---|
| "Private from us"; sessions "stay with their author unless shared"; storage "hold[s] no key" (P5:579,745) | R-CTX-13, R-CTX-17, R-CTX-29, R-CTX-38 | none for session contents (directive; [owner decision 126](#od-126)); in a team network a run's who, what and where reach teammates unless its member opts out ([owner decision 170](#od-170)) |
| "The relay carries only ciphertext"; the "certificate key stays in the sidecar"; mail "encrypted on arrival" (P5:681,699,708) | sidecar traffic, R-CTX-21, R-CTX-22, R-CTX-24 | none (directive; D-PROTO-6) |
| [Owner decision 72](#od-72)'s policy wording, replacing TM:814 | R-CTX-11 | none (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6)) |
| "end-to-end encrypted" (P5:928) | R-CTX-29 | claimed now, without P5:930-931's audit and reproducible builds; the security page discloses the unaudited cryptography (owner decisions [77](#od-77), [99](#od-99), [119](#od-119)) |
| Agents "reach only granted ranges, and leave only through exits you run" (P5:689) | R-CTX-28 | holds once a network writes a policy; the allow-all before it is disclosed ([owner decision 120](#od-120)) |

### 1.10 Glossary seed

Terms are defined once, in Appendix C. The one most sections share is the **indexer**: a device its network designates as an always-on point device for background services, such as receiving mail and mirroring record-class repos; a network has none until an Owner, an Admin or a member designates one (R-CTX-33; §3.6; owner decisions [150](#od-150), [177](#od-177)).

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| One substrate (PLAN.md:5-31) | One identity, storage, edge, abuse pipeline | Burners linkable per network ([owner decision 32](#od-32)); one mail reputation, shared with api and connect ingress (owner decisions [29](#od-29), [124](#od-124)) | Adopt |
| A stack per product | Isolates reputation | Duplicates everything; contradicts PLAN.md | Reject (owner decisions [15](#od-15), [108](#od-108)) |

### 1.12 Decisions proposed

**D-CTX-1 (proposed).** The sidecar infrastructure is the `sidecar` module and `ur` CLI, the new server services (§3.8) with team management and access control, and `sdk/sidecar.go`; consoles, app UI, harnesses, and model hosting are outside it. *Why:* PLAN.md:5-31; owner rule 6.

**D-CTX-2 (proposed).** R-CTX's Owner column, with Appendix F's trace of each PLAN.md line, is the traceability root; section tables gain no R-CTX column. *Why:* Appendix F's join makes a per-section column redundant.

**D-CTX-3 (proposed).** The §1.7 promises are requirements as the directive and the owner's decisions amend them, and product copy follows each amendment (owner decisions [119](#od-119), [120](#od-120), [170](#od-170)); owning sections record departures from PLAN.md. *Why:* owner rule 8.

**D-CTX-4 (proposed).** The feedback service (FB) is out of scope; R-CTX-9 is the one FB requirement this design takes. *Why:* FB has its own spec.

**D-CTX-5 (proposed).** Model access is a bridge forward plus a per-sidecar, per-model grant (§17, §8); model-name routing and per-request signing (P5:779) stay out of scope. *Why:* both need an HTTP proxy that PLAN.md lacks.

### 1.13 Open questions

**Q-CTX-1.** Must the server services be self-hostable (P5:576,903)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 48](#od-48)):** at the later assured stage; engines reach URnetwork-only infrastructure only through `ServiceHost` interfaces (D-REPO-3), and v0 ships no bundle. *Residual:* none.

**Q-CTX-2.** Which runtime serves browser surfaces besides the extension? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 76](#od-76)):** the extension's `sidecar.wasm` ([owner decision 26](#od-26)), in a page Worker admitted read-only and labeled as served code (§2.8 EX7; §18.8), ephemeral for the quick burner (Q-SDK-4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-CTX-3.** What is a recURd team in URnetwork terms? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 59](#od-59)):** a new team network ([owner decision 55](#od-55)) plus each member's personal network, one daemon hosting a `Sidecar` per network ([owner decision 23](#od-23); §7.5). *Residual:* none.

**Q-CTX-4.** Cross-cutting (§9, §11). Who designs `ur share` (R-CTX-31)? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a), §9 (D-SOCK-16): a blinded `share/<token>` socket served while the sharing sidecar runs, a 256-bit secret in the link's fragment, a durable use count under §16's reserve-before-effect discipline (D-MCP-11), an expiry (24 h by default, at most 30 days; `ur share rm` ends one early), bytes on the transfer balance; (b) would change format 1, which freezes at M2. *Residual:* none.

## 2. Trust model and threat model

### 2.1 Purpose and scope

This section sets the adversary model, trust boundaries, server visibility, key custody, the "private from us" statement and metadata list, and invariants I-1..I-20 for every section; §5-§18 own mechanisms, §21 abuse, §22 tests.

### 2.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-TRUST-1 | Storage and the sequencer hold no group secret or key | PLAN.md:221 |
| R-TRUST-2 | Servers see only ciphertext and published small header values, except D-SMTP-19's report and role-mail intake (mx-4; D-TRUST-4); "end-to-end encrypted" comes with a malicious-server threat model and the unaudited-cryptography disclosure | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:745, :927-933; owner directive; [owner decision 119](#od-119) |
| R-TRUST-3 | Signed membership stops a breached server from adding a reader | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:745; [owner decision 3](#od-3) |
| R-TRUST-4 | TLS keys stay in the listening sidecar; tlsedge never terminates | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:699; X1 |
| R-TRUST-5 | With a policy, agents reach only granted ranges and exit only through customer exits; sidecar-bound agent tokens last ≤1 h and stay out of agents' environments | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:689; sidecar/FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md:139; [owner decision 120](#od-120) |
| R-TRUST-6 | Untrusted content cuts egress. New recipients need approval. One switch revokes reach | sidecar/design/improve.md:126-127; sidecar/design/pitch5.html:729 |
| R-TRUST-7 | Admins see actions, not transcripts; session contents open only when shared, while in a team network a run's who, what and where reach teammates by default; authors see admin reads | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:640; owner decisions [126](#od-126), [170](#od-170) |
| R-TRUST-8 | Client tokens never administer networks. Revocation is forward-only | [R:server-identity](design/design-research/server-identity.md) §3 item 3; PLAN.md:327 |

### 2.3 What exists today

- **Encryption.** connect defaults to Off (connect/transfer_encrypt.go:788), the sdk to Opportunistic (sdk/device_local_provider.go:258), and ControlId traffic is never encrypted (connect/transfer_encrypt.go:3671-3686).
- **AUTHZ1** (§7.3): on non-Embed networks any client token mints a network login through `/auth/code-create`, and same-user processes read the network credential in `.auth_state` (sdk/local_state_auth.go:28-36) and in the extension's `chrome.storage.local` (extension/src/background/index.ts:134).
- **Missing:** members, signed membership, customer keys, a metadata list, and ur.network's DS, CAA and SPF records (dig, 2026-11-03).

### 2.4 Assets and boundaries

Assets: content (files, sessions, mail, burner logins), keys and credentials, authority (config repo, approvals, record), names, metadata, shared reputation, availability.

```text
TB1 device:  sidecar daemon (keys, plaintext), harness and agents as one OS user (owner decision 47);
             an app's VPN component, a network process, with only forwarding's keys and the config's
             contents (owner decision 197; §18.6);
             for a cloud agent (owner decision 49), the sandbox operator (the VM host, its snapshot store
             and its egress proxy), whose VM snapshot holds the keys and whose TLS-terminating proxy would
             see service tokens, is inside the device boundary, like the OS;
             web: script running in a decrypting page's origin, Cloudflare's altered page script included,
             is inside the plaintext boundary (EX7); keys and tokens stay in §18.8's key origin, which is
             served direct (owner decision 211);
             the daemon stops tool misuse, not same-user reads; other users and the LAN are outside
TB2 members: trusted for granted content; admins admit alone and change authority under k of n
             (owner decision 110), but add no reader to a member's owner-bound repos without that
             member's consent (owner decision 126); admin vs author key domain (X20); a member whose
             device is designated as a network-scope search indexer sees the queries members' phones
             send it over the team repos it answers, as an owner's indexer sees those over a repo the
             owner shared (owner decisions 175, 178); no device is designated by default (owner
             decision 177)
TB3 servers: behind connect e2e (I-3); untrusted for content and authority
outside:     CAs, CT logs and search, DoH resolvers, IP-listing feeds, mailbox providers, Stripe,
             APNs/FCM, model providers, other tenants (§2.8 ext-*)
```

### 2.5 Server visibility matrix

| Service (§2.8 rows) | Where encryption ends; what stays sealed |
|---|---|
| connect, tlsedge, certs (connect-*, tls-*, cert-*) | At each sidecar (I-3, X1) |
| smtpedge, mxedge (smtp-*, mx-*) | At the destination MX or the receiver (X6, X7); mx-4 excepted (§2.8's statement) |
| evs, gkm (evs-*, gkm-*) | On readers' devices; names, contents, keys; gkm sees members and wrap recipients as sidecar ids (owner decisions [72](#od-72), [114](#od-114), [115](#od-115), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)) |
| api, sockets, dns (api-*, sock-*, dns-*) | No content passes; policy text and internal names stay sealed (owner decisions [67](#od-67), [72](#od-72)); DNS records are public |

### 2.6 Key custody

| Key | Holder | Who can misuse it |
|---|---|---|
| ClientKey, identity and local root keys; tokens, auth codes | Device keychain (§5); device files; a browser's key origin (§18.8) | Holder, same-user agents and a cloud agent's sandbox operator; tokens administer until the P0's stages (§7.4) |
| AdminSet (Owner, Admin, Network and IT admin), approval, presence and recovery keys | Holders' devices (§7, §16); recovery codes offline ([owner decision 62](#od-62)) | Holder; authority statements need k signers, target excluded, k = 1 when n ≤ 2 ([owner decision 110](#od-110)); a recovery code counts as one of k after a vetoable 72 h ([owner decision 127](#od-127)) and admits its member's devices, with an admin cosign when `self_admit` is off, and under a binding the compromise cascade restored only after that vetoable 72 h ([owner decision 149](#od-149); §7.9) |
| MLS secrets, repo and path keys, the socket-name key | Readers' devices; agents', and in the config and team directory groups member devices past a network's first 1,000, by X-Wing wraps (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182); §10); each member's recovery key by RecoveryWraps ([owner decision 62](#od-62)); wraps as ciphertext | Readers; every admitted sidecar, agents included, reads the config's policy, AdminSet, the emails policy names, `K_sock` and share signers' seeds (owner decisions [6](#od-6), [67](#od-67); below), and in a team the directory ([owner decision 171](#od-171)); removed readers for generations held and path tokens until rotation (evs-11); holders of a Delegation's reader key (its agents, reaped ones and ephemeral ones past their own `not_after` included, and copies of its auth key) until the key drops at DelegationRevoke, `not_after`, a revocation for any reason but reaped or a `Suspend` of one of its agents, or a compromise revocation whose cascade voids it, and a copy of the whole auth key, which holds the signing seed, admitting fresh agents, each with its own wraps once the key has dropped, until the Delegation ends (§7.9's delegation row, §10.5); a recovery code's holder with its member's login or the operator's help, for every generation wrapped to it, at once and whatever the window or a veto, until `RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}` or a cascade void of its binding (§7.9) |
| An app's forwarding key, forwarding reader key and forwarding clients' keys (§5.5, §18.6; [owner decision 197](#od-197)) | Its VPN component's own store (§5.9), generated there and never exported | That process, or a compromise of it: forwarding as its sidecar through that sidecar's grants, and the config generations wrapped to its reader key, until its forwarding Delegation ends at a `DelegationRevoke`, a newer one or its sidecar's revocation (§7.9); never mail, another evs repo, an MLS leaf secret, or the sidecar's identity, client, reader or recovery keys |
| A bridge share's ShareKey and ShareSigner seeds (§17.9) | The ShareKey in the accepting network's approving admin's owner-bound `secret`; each config generation's seed in its `BridgeShareSigner` config file | The secret's readers (§8.5), a removed one until the share is revoked; every config reader, agents included, one its network's policy denies too on an operator-minted contract (§8.11), a removed one until a later ShareCert reaches the host, at most 7 days (§2.10) |
| TLS, DKIM and mail-host keys | Each listening, sending or receiving device (D-TLS-6, [owner decision 36](#od-36), D-MAIL-4) | Holder; receivers see their hosts' mail in transit |
| Platform keys: JWT, OAuth, key history, ACME, DNSSEC, registrar, platform mail, evs receipt MACs | api's issuer, certs, the dns edge, mxedge, evs, vault | Insiders or hijackers: tokens, EX1, EX2, EX6 and URnetwork's mail |
| Release signing keys | Offline two-person key over `SHA256SUMS`; code signing (§4.10); no GPG key, since no apt or yum repository ships ([owner decision 213](#od-213)) | Holders; the build pipeline |

### 2.7 Client-id-to-key binding and ghost members

The server creates client ids and serves their keys (`/key/<id>`, server/api/route_authz.go:248), so a malicious one could add a ghost peer, substitute a key at first contact, or pass off its own KeyPackage or external commit as a member's new device (RFC 9750 §8.4.3).

Mitigations (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [113](#od-113)): config-repo admissions chain to the genesis key that invites and auth keys carry (§7.9), so clients refuse underived peers, readers, rules and membership commits, leaving a breached server only denial or delay, within §2.8's exposure bound; `Hello` bindings and safety numbers stop first-contact substitution (EX5, EX6).

### 2.8 "Private from us"

Statement (D-TRUST-4): *URnetwork's servers never receive plaintext content or keys, in any mode, except `rpt.bringyour.com`'s report and role-mail listener, which terminates TLS, parses headers and aggregate report data only (D-SMTP-23), seals the raw bytes to the network mail key and persists no plaintext (mx-4, §14.8). They see the values listed below. URnetwork builds no prospective collection ([owner decision 93](#od-93)) but could be compelled to record these values from now on (§21.9).*

An active or compelled operator keeps:

- **EX1.** Certificates in URnetwork zones ([owner decision 39](#od-39)); CT watch (D-TRUST-6); CAA `accounturi` excludes Team custom domains in strong mode only (customer A and AAAA, or an ALIAS flattening only those), and a weak-mode custom host (a CNAME into an operator zone) stays exposed (§12.8); the canary probe that catches an ALIAS also flattening CAA is URnetwork's own (certs), the ordering desktops repeating only the walk, so against a compelled operator such an ALIAS is as exposed as weak mode, the CT watch (D-TLS-8) its remaining control.
- **EX2.** Forged TLSA, CAA, MX, DKIM or MTA-STS records in URnetwork-signed zones ([owner decision 69](#od-69)); zone watch (D-TRUST-9).
- **EX3.** Interception of inbound mail from senders validating neither DANE nor MTA-STS, undetected; labeled "opportunistic" unless REQUIRETLS or a listed enforcing operator makes it "validated" (owner decisions [98](#od-98), [135](#od-135); §15.5), a match mxedge can fake (§2.18); an operator listed only for MTA-STS makes burner mail "validated" though burner domains publish no policy; the operator list is an operator-reputation inference, and REQUIRETLS records only the final hop's requirement, never that URnetwork did not read the message (§15.5).
- **EX4.** A send the user allowed to an unauthenticated MX ([owner decision 38](#od-38)), labeled "readable by an active URnetwork edge".
- **EX5.** Trust on first use of a genesis key no invite or auth key carried ([owner decision 5](#od-5)); safety numbers; a code-only recovered device, which has no admitter, commits, wraps, seals or signs nothing until the config head its RecoveryWrap, or under a binding a cascade void restored the ReaderWrap it is given (§7.9's restored order), opens chains to a genesis its RecoveryBind's `genesis_sig` signs under the key its code derives (§7.9's anchor), so the recovery public keys every config reader and rotator holds let no server fake that genesis; a server can forge the wrap or the ReaderKey gkm serves, but not a head that chains to that genesis.
- **EX6.** connect key substitution at first contact until M2's admission check (§6.4); first-use pins.
- **EX7.** Code URnetwork ships: signed releases ([owner decision 77](#od-77)) and labeled decrypting web pages ([owner decision 76](#od-76)); undetected; any script in a decrypting page's origin reads views while it runs (§18.8). Cloudflare terminates https://ur.io, so it sees page requests and can alter page script, and through it request views while that script runs, never the key origin's code, key or token, since `sidecar.ur.io` is served direct (§19.5's W10; [owner decision 211](#od-211)). The key origin serves only a promoted build, whose loader and `sidecar.wasm` the release's signed `SHA256SUMS` lists, so anyone can compare the served bytes, though no browser checks them on load (§18.8; [owner decision 221](#od-221)).
- **EX8.** URnetwork login as the `members` audience authority ([owner decision 42](#od-42)); undetected (§13.7).

**Exposure bound** ([owner decision 129](#od-129)): a writer learns of a withheld Remove at its first HeadCheck with a device that holds it, or with a peer that relays it as `proven` or `unverified` within 8 hops of a holder (D-TRUST-10, §6.4); with the withholding proof it stops at once, and without it the pin stays UNVERIFIED, so, as with no consistent witness, the writer stops sealing shared-group content at `ServiceSettings.witness_bound_hours` (default 72 h, 24-168 h). Exposure is unbounded across a split, where the server leaves no HeadCheck path of up to 8 hops between a holder and the writer, including when every device that holds the Remove is offline, and in own groups, where writers only alarm: personal networks, and with them the v0 pilot ([owner decision 102](#od-102)), have no bound.

**Also disclosed:**
- Burner linkability (§15.9).
- No fork detection without a shared pin.
- I-10's no-policy allow-all, in product copy too ([owner decision 120](#od-120)).
- §2.18's unaudited cryptography.
- A head reader's trust in evs for which writer-signed version, or a refused push's writer-signed entry that was never a version, is current at its first pin, for a path it never read or no longer remembers (its sealed read record evicted, or its pin past the budget; [owner decision 209](#od-209)) and, after a re-pin past §11.9's 4 MiB catch-up budget (shown as `verified since <time>`), for every path, HeadCheck confirming the pin, not those versions (§11.9).
- A shredded repo's statements and ciphertext in shared batches up to 26 h past key destruction (§11.12).
- P0 safety work runs at once whatever its volume ([owner decision 186](#od-186)), so a wave of it on one metadata cluster, legal within every network's rates, holds that cluster's evacuation from when it empties the write budget's bucket until the wave ends (§11.13; [owner decision 190](#od-190)): each bound in this list that rests on hourly evacuation, the 26 h ones, stretches meanwhile (§11.21).
- Erasure paced, at the storage limit or while spent, by each eraser's daily closure allowance, which §21 never cuts below its floor: an entry's own keys go at once, while its derived fields (`i/` entries and search-index copies) stay openable to their key holders, masked from search, for up to the wait §11.13 and §15.7 state from the erasure's closure bytes, not a fixed time per message, and longer while a ref's full erasure set holds back the erasure's CUT (§11.12's cut row); an erasure whose eraser's device is lost waits for another device that may finish it (§11.12's reconcile row; [owner decision 146](#od-146)).
- Versionless content (§11.7): a writer may turn versioning off for a path, except in config and mailcfg repos, on git-mode and creates-only refs and, through a repo admin's lock, in a locked repo, after which each replaced version's content is purged about a minute after its replacement (staged content with its batch, at most 26 h; evs-12), beyond recall, while its signed statement keeps its hash, padded size, time and signer; the setting shows the server which paths are versionless and which hold the search index ([owner decision 168](#od-168)); under a hold, versionless content that existed at placement stays until the hold ends.
- Dropped history (§11.7, §11.13): a repo admin may drop a path's history on a file-mode ref outside config and mailcfg repos, after a 7-day window in which any repo admin can cancel, or at once with `now`; in an owner-bound repo only its owner drops or cancels (owner decisions [126](#od-126), [183](#od-183)); each dropped version's statement keeps its hash, time and signer, and its content goes beyond recall; inline content stays as unserved ciphertext in packs until compaction, and in slot-keyed repos is unreadable at once; under a hold the content stays until the hold ends, while the drop reads, lists and bills as finished ([owner decision 184](#od-184)); deleted blocks persist on the drives until overwritten (evs-28).
- Search (§11.14, §16.10): no query or result reaches a server; an ephemeral sidecar's first sync of a repo's index and any device's fetch of a repo's all partition at "search more" show evs that and when the device searched, never what (desktops and indexers, syncing in the background, show neither); each opened hit, and each candidate `ur search --verify fetch` opens, is an ordinary document read, so their set shows evs a query-dependent access pattern (evs-26); an app host's "search more" that a designated indexer answers goes end to end to that device, which sees the query (another member's device only for team repos or a repo that member shared, the app naming that member first), while relays see when each search and page runs, in fixed sizes, connect's stored reports show each window's fixed floor rather than its pages, its contract rows a search's time only when the search fails over or re-establishes a session lost in the foreground, and evs sees nothing (connect-5; owner decisions [175](#od-175), [176](#od-176), [178](#od-178), [188](#od-188), [191](#od-191)).
- The team directory (§16.11): in a team network every admitted sidecar, agents and the audit reader included, reads each member's run titles, projects and branches unless the member opts out ([owner decision 170](#od-170)), and the name and description of every general and record repo unless its owner marks it private or revokes its announcement ([owner decision 181](#od-181)), a revocation hiding the name from honest readers at once and destroying its copies' keys once a directory admin's device runs its erasure request, so a modified reader can open them until then; evs learns per sidecar when its runs start, end and move, and per access request which requester asked which approvers' devices (evs-27).

Feedback (sidecar/FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md:11) and hosted models are out of scope.
