**F8. A harness recording work through MCP** (X20 and approvals: owner decisions [25](#od-25), [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75), [80](#od-80), [126](#od-126), [142](#od-142)).

```text
   harness      daemon       evs          approver
1  |--ur mcp--->|            |            |
2  |--hooks---->|            |            |
3  |            |--records-->|            |
4  |--O tool--->|--request-->|            |
5  |            |            |--hint----->|
6  |            |<--decision--------------|
7  |<--result---|            |            |
8  |            |--coverage->|            |

1  the harness spawns `ur mcp --agent a` (bare `ur` does the same when stdin is not a terminal), which
   relays to the daemon over a Unix socket that checks the peer uid; tools take a `network` argument
   defaulting from the project's `.ur` file, else the daemon's only network, and refuse otherwise
   (§5.8; owner decisions 23, 57, 84; §5 D-CORE-9; §16 D-MCP-2)
2  hooks call `ur hook` (at most 300 ms, fail open) and the daemon tails the transcript; it redacts
   secrets, then seals (§16 D-MCP-5)
3  vault entries form a signed per-writer chain with a key slot per entry, written as in F2; each
   RecordEntry is sealed whole, and owned refs in record repos refuse FORCE and DELETE (owner decisions
   25, 61; §16 D-MCP-6; Q-ARCH-9 (a)). A device the author has not consented to only deposits into
   the author's vault (owner decision 126; §8.5). Team-record entries go by drop key (§10 D-KEYS-8)
4  an outward (O) tool, such as tls_publish or mail_send to a new recipient, writes an ApprovalRequest
   and returns pending (§16 D-MCP-4)
5  an evs hint and a content-free phone wake notify the approver (owner decision 88; §16.8)
6  the approver's identity key on another device, or a presence key, signs the ApprovalDecision; a
   single-device user approves in the harness's own prompt, which in a tainted run counts only where
   the matching `requests` rule names harness evidence, or with a presence prompt. The record labels
   the evidence type, a network policy may demand stronger evidence, and high risk adds an SSHSIG; no
   approval comes by email (owner decisions 75, 80, 142; §16.6)
7  the daemon executes only if the decision's hash matches its own canonical payload and the decision
   names this sidecar, reserving the use before the effect (§16 D-MCP-4, D-MCP-11, D-MCP-12); once
   the run is tainted, no standing grant or approved recipient passes, and it refuses as stale a
   decision whose request was untainted, Authorize filing a tainted request, though a use reserved
   before the taint completes (§16.6's TS1; §5.4); a requested grant activates once, as a
   `GrantActivate` carrying the decision under its fixed `grant_id` (§16.6, §8.8; §8 D-ACL-7; owner
   decisions 3, 74)
8  at run end, a coverage entry lists every gap (§16.8)
```

**F9. Remove a member** (X3 and X12 as in F1 and F3; owner decisions [59](#od-59), [64](#od-64), [83](#od-83), [113](#od-113), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128), [129](#od-129), [144](#od-144)). Actors: an admin; api; the removed member's devices; gkm; a remaining writer leaf; evs.

```text
   admin        api          removed      gkm          writer       evs
1  |--remove--->|            |            |            |            |
2  |--revocation, into the config repo----------------------------->|
3  |            |--cut off-->|            |            |            |
4  |            |            |            |--pending-->|            |
5  |            |            |            |<--commit---|            |
6  |            |            |            |            |--write---->|

1  member-remove, remove-client or SCIM deprovisioning: one api transaction removes the member,
   deactivates the member's own clients, revokes their tokens and logs an admin event; tagged agents
   the member enrolled stay, with their tags' grants, and admins may reassign their sponsorship (owner
   decision 83; §7.10, D-TEAM-10)
2  the admin's device signs the revocation into the config repo, where members read it; one admin
   signature suffices, except that removing an AdminSet member, or their devices, is an authority
   statement needing k of n, the target never counting (owner decisions 3, 5, 110; §7.9). Its
   projection v' closes the write gate of every repo the member read (§11.8)
3  api, sockets and the edges refuse the tokens at once; evs and gkm, which verify tokens offline,
   honor the signed revocation object in the cluster and drop the subject's scope with their newest
   verified projection, and tokens lapse within 15 min (§7.8, §8.9); connect closes the clients within
   90 s; their listeners, publishes, forwards, DKIM selectors and certificates end (owner decisions 2,
   36; §13.8; I-15)
4  gkm hints pending on the per-client gkm topic of each group's writers, the revoking device first
   (owner decision 113; §6.8; §10.6, KF4)
5  a writer leaf commits the Remove with a path, as a PrivateMessage whose clear authenticated_data
   carries only GkmCommitHeader (generation, auth pin), with no roster delta; members derive the
   change from the config repo at v' and reject a Remove without the signed revocation (owner
   decisions 59, 113; §10.9); then any writer rotates, claiming gen/<g+1> after staging its wraps
   (§10.5). In the config group the revocation's signer, when it is a leaf, may commit the Remove even
   if not a config writer (owner decision 128). No wrapped device commits a Remove: agents never do,
   and in the config group neither do member devices past its first 1,000, so a wrapped signer
   rotates and the next leaf commit removes the target (owner decisions 114, 144; §7.9); an agent's
   revocation is a new generation not wrapped to it, which any writer writes (owner decision 114). gkm
   stores the commit and the gen/ claim with If-None-Match: * (owner decision 2; §10 KF4)
6  the gate reopens at g+1: writes use generation g+1 and a rotated path key with an old-to-new token
   map, and the first write to each file is a full checkpoint (owner decisions 2, 64); new names in
   general, config and mailcfg repos wait until that map lands (§11.6). The removed party keeps what
   it already decrypted (§10.8). Until a writer, agents included, claims g+1, pushes get 412 (§11.8);
   until a writer leaf commits the Remove, no leaf wrap uses an epoch that holds the removed leaf
   (§10.5). A server withholding the Remove delays it within §2.8's exposure bound, which a split it
   makes by dropping traffic defeats: shared-group writers without a consistent witness alarm at 24 h
   and stop at witness_bound_hours (default 72 h), while rotations, Removes and revocations never stop
   (owner decision 129; D-TRUST-10)
```

**F10. Burner lifecycle** (X6 residual Q-MAIL-3: [owner decision 32](#od-32); launch at M8, receive-only until F5 ships: owner decisions [34](#od-34), [35](#od-35)).

```text
   app          evs          receiver     mxedge       smtpedge
1  |[label]     |            |            |            |
2  |--mailcfg-->|--hint----->|            |            |
3  |            |            |<--mail-----|            |
4  |--reply, as F5, once outbound ships--------------->|
5  |--burn----->|--hint----->|            |            |
6  |            |            |--550 RCPT->|            |

1  the app's sidecar role generates <blabel>, a word-number label such as otter-4821, that avoids the
   network's published hosts and burned labels; the address is <name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>, and an
   alias in place of <net> shows the network's name (owner decision 32; §15.9)
2  the label goes into the signed mailcfg, written as in F2, and receivers learn it from the hint; the
   wildcard MX *.<net>.<root> -> mx.<net>.<root> covers it, so it has no DNS record, no quota use and
   no server state (§15 D-MAIL-7)
3  inbound mail arrives as in F6 with SNI mx.<net>.<root>, so mxedge routes by network, and the
   receiver checks RCPT against mailcfg (§15.5)
4  a reply goes as in F5 from <name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>, flagged BURNER, with Received and client
   headers removed (§15.10); smtpedge checks that the From domain lies in the network's zone; until
   <root> is on the PSL, a burner that replies gets its own DKIM selector and MX records, which
   publish its label: guessable and visible in DKIM headers, not walkable under §12.6's compact denial
   (owner decision 79 accepted walkable; owner decision 35; §15.9-15.10)
5  burn is local: the label is marked burned in mailcfg and never reissued (owner decision 32)
6  receivers answer 550 5.1.1 for it from then on; for a receive-only burner nothing changes in DNS or
   on the server. Correspondents can link a network's burners through <net> (owner decision 32;
   §15.9)
```

**F11. Search, and find agents working on a task** (owner decisions [10](#od-10), [23](#od-23), [63](#od-63), [126](#od-126), [142](#od-142), [150](#od-150) and [151](#od-151)-[157](#od-157), [166](#od-166), [170](#od-170)-[172](#od-172); v1). Actors: the writer, another agent (in a team network, another member's); evs; the network's indexer, if one is designated; the searching daemon with its index cache; an agent in a harness.

```text
   writer       evs          indexer      daemon       agent
1  |--claim---->|            |            |            |
2  |            |--hint------------------>|            |
3  |            |<--sync latest-----------|            |
4  |            |            |            |<--search---|
5  |            |            |            |--page 1--->|
6  |            |<--roll-up--|            |            |
7  |            |<--all, by position------|            |
8  |            |            |            |--groups--->|
9  |            |<--read, receipt first---|<--open-----|

1  the writer's run claims its task (record_append, kind claim: its text and targets): in a team
   network the claim joins the run's announcement in the team directory, indexed in the push that
   writes its card (§16.11; owner decisions 170, 171); in a personal network it is a vault entry whose
   index entry follows on the vault's ur/index in the writer's next companion push, at most a minute
   later on 1 KiB XFS blocks, else five minutes (owner decision 172); a head keeps one entry per
   document (§11.14; §16.8, §16.10; owner decisions 151, 153)
2  in a personal network as F2 steps 5-6, a daemon that follows a record stream only for search
   holding a whole-ref lease on its ur/index (§11.10); in a team network the daemon instead syncs the
   directory at each search or view, coalesced to 30 s, every 15 min while it serves a harness
   session, else hourly (§5.4; §16.11, §18.4)
3  the daemon replays the ref's statements after its pin and fetches the changed index files into its
   sealed cache, checking each against its entry version's content_sha256, by sync position, never by
   query; from the directory's changed cards it derives their writers' index heads, fetching a head,
   and alarming, only where the derived one differs from its entry version's content_sha256 (§5
   D-CORE-16; §11.14; §16 D-MCP-20)
4  search_agents("rate limiter", since 7d): the scope is the session's network (`.ur`), every repo this
   sidecar reads by §8's local evaluation, the team directory included (§16.11), less secret, config,
   mailcfg and deposit-only repos, unconsented owner-bound repos and repos whose index is off (owner
   decisions 23, 126; §16 D-MCP-21)
5  phase 1: both latest buckets at once, the newest version winning by document key; doc-table fields
   confirm header matches, and the daemon's plaintext confirms the rest where it holds it, else they
   stay possible; hits group by (sidecar, agent label), active groups first, then the newest;
   untrusted hits and the directory's announcements, requests and decisions return as stubs, so the
   run stays untainted (I-9; owner decision 142; §16 D-MCP-22 to D-MCP-24, D-MCP-29)
6  once per bucket length the indexer, else the first writer after the bucket expires, rolls the
   expired bucket into all under a per-ref lock and drops it; the expired bucket answers until the
   roll-up lands (owner decisions 150, 153, 157)
7  desktops and indexers fetch the changed all shards in the background; an ephemeral or cloud daemon
   fetches every all shard it lacks, whole and youngest first, only for `more`; downloads debit the
   transfer balance (owner decisions 10, 154)
8  phase 2's hits follow phase 1's under the same cursor, so a returned page is never revised (§16
   D-MCP-25)
9  opening a hit is a read as in F2 step 7, which checks a possible hit; an EvsShare or audit reader of
   an owner-bound repo deposits a read receipt first (§16 D-MCP-18; owner decisions 63, 126)
```

**F12. A phone's "search more" answered by an indexer** (owner decisions [10](#od-10), [126](#od-126), [150](#od-150), [151](#od-151)-[155](#od-155), [175](#od-175)-[178](#od-178); v1). Actors: an app host's sidecar, the phone; connect relays; a designated search indexer, the member's own or, for team repos, a network-scope one; evs.

```text
   phone        relays       indexer      evs
1  |--Hello, HeadCheck------>|            |
2  |[search own]|            |            |
3  |--SearchRequest--------->|            |
4  |            |            |[verify]    |
5  |<--SearchReply-----------|            |
6  |[merge]     |            |            |
7  |--next page------------->|            |
8  |--read, on open---------------------->|

1  at foreground, where the network designates a search indexer (none by default, owner decision 177)
   and the phone's mode is on, its default, the phone sends Hello to its first-choice own search
   indexer, or to another member's once that member's notice is answered, on the pair's Network
   contract: data where reach allows, else the `control` class, which carries SEARCH only to a sidecar
   advertising Hello feature bit 0; it checks the indexer's designation, admission and identity
   binding in its own state, and runs HeadCheck if due (§6.4, D-PROTO-21; §18.7, D-SDK-27)
2  keystrokes search the phone's own buckets and any cached all (§11.14); nothing leaves the phone
3  "search more": the scope by §16.10's rules, its repos split by §11.14's eligibility, own indexers
   first; an owner-bound repo goes only to its owner's consented devices (owner decision 126), and a
   team repo that no own indexer serves to one network-scope search indexer, another member's device
   only after the app has named that member once (§18.4's notice); each request is one 4,016 B body
   naming at most 64 repos (owner decision 175)
4  the indexer checks the requester and each repo in its own state (§8.5, §8.12), pins its cached
   snapshot and verifies candidates newest first against the text it holds, inside its remote budget
   and outside every MCP session and run, fetching nothing from evs, api or gkm (§5.8, D-CORE-17;
   I-19)
5  one 16 KiB step, failures after parsing included: verified hits, each repo's coverage and pinned
   (v, C_v), and checked_through_ms
6  the phone compares equal-version chains as HeadCheck does, merges by doc key, keeps its own
   confirmed hits, collapses possible matches the checked span disproves, and labels the hits that
   indexer verified "verified by <device>" (§11.14; §18.5)
7  each further page, on scroll, in the same sizes; relays see only each request's and reply's time and
   fixed size, connect reports the pair's bytes per window, in both directions, at a fixed floor that
   up to five pages leave unchanged (§6.10), and every byte debits the transfer balance (owner
   decisions 10, 176, 188; §4.6 C19; §2.8 connect-5)
8  opening a hit is a read as in F2 step 7, whose text the phone checks, a mismatch alarming and naming
   the indexer; with no designated indexer answering, the default, step 3 falls back to a download of
   all as in F11 step 7, by sync position under §18.4's metered rule, and owner decision 155's
   possible matches
```

**F13. Announce, find and request** (owner decisions [8](#od-8), [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75), [126](#od-126), [142](#od-142), [161](#od-161), [169](#od-169)-[171](#od-171), [179](#od-179)-[182](#od-182); v1). Actors: member A's daemon and run; evs; member B's daemon and agent; the repo admin's device.

```text
   A's daemon   evs          B's daemon   B's agent    repo admin
1  |--announce->|            |            |            |
2  |            |<--sync-----|            |            |
3  |            |            |<--find-----|            |
4  |            |            |<--request--|            |
5  |            |<--file-----|            |            |
6  |            |--hint, wake------------------------->|
7  |            |<--grant, decision--------------------|
8  |            |--decided-->|            |            |
9  |--ended---->|            |            |            |

1  at SessionStart A's daemon announces A's run within 10 s, `claims` being auto in a team network
   unless A opted out, per member or project, and renews it hourly while the run moves: an `announce`
   entry in A's directory stream at M6, A's card on the `cards` ref from the directory's format 2
   (§16.11); it carries the run's who (member, sidecar, agent label, harness), what (its redacted
   title, claims and state) and where (the repo id and, if the repo is announced, its name and branch,
   else `private`), and nothing else of the session leaves A's vault (owner decisions 126, 170, 171;
   I-20)
2  B's daemon syncs the directory by sync position (I-19) at each search or view, coalesced to 30 s,
   every 15 min while it serves a harness session, else hourly (§5.4, §18.4); it reads it through the
   directory's own MLS group, in which the first 1,000 live member devices are leaves and later ones
   and agents read by wraps (owner decision 182; §10.4), and ignores, with an alarm, any item not
   signed and pushed under §16.11's path rules by an admitted writer, consented where it is a member
   device (I-EVS-14)
3  B's agent looks for active runs on its task: `directory_list` at M6, a local filter over the folded
   state, and `search_agents` from M10 (owner decision 169); both return directory stubs, attested and
   identifier fields without prose, so B's run stays untainted (I-9; owner decision 142)
4  B's agent calls `directory_request` for read on A's repo, which the directory announced at its
   creation (owner decision 181) or shows only by its id and `private`; as an O-tier tool it passes
   §5.4's Authorize, which builds an `access_request` action and waits for member B's endorsement:
   harness evidence in an untainted run, device or presence in a tainted one (owner decisions 74, 75,
   142)
5  B's daemon files the request entry in B's directory stream, then a notice under the repo's prefix
   q/<repo_id>/, which names no approver (§16.11)
6  evs hints the repo admin's devices, which lease that prefix (§11.10); §18.7 wakes their phones from
   M8, and a desktop raises SidecarEvent access_request (§5.4)
7  a person, on /dev/tty or in an app and never through MCP, signs the RepoGrant into the repo's access
   log, the decision entry and the notice's rewrite to decided (owner decision 8; §8.8); an owner-bound
   repo's requests reach only its owner, whose consented device decides by EvsShare (owner decision
   126). A request to a worker asks to dial the services it announces (owner decision 179), and its
   owner, or a tagged sidecar's sponsor, approves as autogroup:dst-owner (owner decision 180; §8.4)
8  B's daemon reads the decision, verifies the grant at its log position and records the outcome in
   B's vault; KF3 then seats the subject's devices in the repo's group, member devices as leaves and
   agents by wraps (§10.7), and an approved worker request activates once, as a GrantActivate (§16.6)
9  at SessionEnd A's daemon marks the run ended, or handed off: a newer announce entry at M6, a card
   rewrite from format 2, whose replaced version is purged a minute later (owner decision 161);
   readers show the run ended for 24 h
```

### 3.9 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted sidecar (X14 b) | no install | keys and plaintext on servers | ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03; [owner decision 26](#od-26)) |
| Edge termination of customers' TLS or mail | filtering, coverage | plaintext at URnetwork | ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03) |
| Server-compiled ACL slices | per-client rules only | a breached server could forge rules | superseded (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6)) |
| Bulk evs over the exchange | one transport | contract per pair; 16 KiB frames | rejected (§6, §11) |

Owners weigh the rest: a sidecar on the device client (§5.11), a sealed client index (§11.16), agents as MLS leaves (§8.13), per-network addresses (§15.11), and Redis or MinIO pools for the metadata tier (§19.12; owner decisions [136](#od-136), [145](#od-145)).

### 3.10 Decisions proposed

**D-ARCH-1 (proposed).** This document writes `<root>` for X4's user-name root (ur.network; [owner decision 13](#od-13)), `<net>` for X5's immutable network label ([owner decision 14](#od-14); PLAN.md:25's `<me>`), which an opt-in alias may replace in user-facing names, `<host>` for a zone-relative host and `<blabel>` for a burner's generated label, so a burner domain is `<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, served by the mail host `mx.<net>.<root>` ([owner decision 32](#od-32)); `<me>` appears only inside PLAN quotations. The front matter carries it. *Why:* one value, one spelling; no mechanism changes.

**D-ARCH-2 (proposed).** The architecture has the six planes of 3.5 and no others; a new carrier needs an owner's decision, as the dns edge and phone wakes had (owner decisions [71](#od-71), [88](#od-88)), and a checkpointer's own HTTPS call to a witness its log admin named is ruled none ([owner decision 214](#od-214)). *Why:* §6 D-PROTO-3, D-PROTO-5, D-PROTO-6 and §11 D-EVS-1 already split traffic this way, and §19 and §22 need one map.

**D-ARCH-3 (proposed).** F1-F13 implement the directive and the owner decisions each names, and are redrawn when a decision changes. They are §22.7's scenarios: S1-S3 are F1-F3, S4 is F9, S5-S9 are F4-F8, S10 is F10, S11 is F11, S12 is F12 and S13 is F13, with S3 and S4 in device form (§10 KF2, KF4) from M2 and member form at M6. *Why:* OUTLINE §22 asks for tests "mirroring §3", and tests of superseded flows test the wrong system.

**D-ARCH-4 (proposed).** Each flow names the owner decisions it implements. G0's assembly check (§23.8) maps every owner decision to the section text that implements it, and fails on a decision without such text, a citation of a withdrawn D- item, a decided question shown as open, or a Q- option the owner has not chosen presented as the design, unless it is an open question's recommendation marked "(proposed; Q-...)". *Why:* the owner's decisions arrived in rounds while sections were drafted and reviewed; only a mechanical check keeps the body, the decision list and §22's scenarios in step.

### 3.11 Open questions

None open. The 2026-11-03 design-review round, not human peer review, closed these, so peer reviewers may reopen them.

**Q-ARCH-1 (closed 2026-11-03).** Q-PROTO-3 (b), adopted by [owner decision 11](#od-11): Service mode (C9) for edges, FriendsAndFamily (C13) for shares; applied in §6.10.1.

**Q-ARCH-2 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a), confirmed by [owner decision 39](#od-39): certs proxies CSRs and alone writes DNS-01 in URnetwork zones; an `accounturi` pin appears only in Team customers' own CAA records; applied in §12.8, §13.8.

**Q-ARCH-3 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a): smtpedge splices mail for an MX on mxedge's router interfaces to mxedge over the host LAN, TLS still sidecar to sidecar; applied in §14.4.

**Q-ARCH-4 (withdrawn).** The directive is a requirement (CONVENTIONS §0); ruled-out modes appear only as Alternatives or Departures rows. Q-MAIL-7 goes with it.

**Q-ARCH-5 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a), with wakes in v0 ([owner decision 88](#od-88)); applied in §18 (tokens, payloads), §19 (sender) and §2.8.

**Q-ARCH-6 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a), confirmed by [owner decision 4](#od-4): no sidecar shares the device client, which runs Opportunistic; applied in §5.5 and Q-PROTO-2.

**Q-ARCH-7 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a), at M4 ([owner decision 85](#od-85)): C14's `UpgradeMux.SetLocalZone` and a `ur tun` resolver answer private names; applied in §12.9, §17.

**Q-ARCH-8 (closed 2026-11-03).** (c): an ephemeral reap is §7.10's removal; it starts a new generation only where the agent held a key that no live Delegation still delivers (§10.5; [owner decision 114](#od-114)); headless sidecars read the config and otherwise only deposit, by §8.5's kind defaults, unless a grant or EvsShare names them, which §8.6's ceiling enforces for ephemeral ones ([owner decision 6](#od-6)); applied in §7.7, §8.

**Q-ARCH-9 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a): RecordEntries are sealed whole, record repos' owned refs refuse FORCE and DELETE, and readers find gaps by chain pins; applied in §11.8, §16.8.

Disagreements raised elsewhere are settled there: Q-EVS-3, Q-TLS-6, Q-MCP-5 and Q-MAIL-8 closed in the same round, and owner decisions [2](#od-2), [34](#od-34), [70](#od-70), [75](#od-75) and [86](#od-86) decided Q-EVS-1, Q-MAIL-1, Q-DNS-6, Q-MCP-3 and Q-BRIDGE-6.

### 3.13 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the maps, planes, topologies with the indexer's definition and fallbacks (3.6), F1-F13 (§22.7's scenarios, D-ARCH-3), the service summary, the closure register (3.11) and the decision trace (D-ARCH-4).
- **Consumes:** §1-§23 and the owner's decision record (front matter).
- **Subprotocol messages, API routes, Tables, Services and config:** none new.
- **Assumptions about other sections:**
  - Owners carry what the flows cite: §5.8 the `.ur` file, the submission port and pairing (F5, F8, 3.6); §7.9 admissions, authority and the recovery anchor, with the records `sidecar/device` verifies in `protocol/bridge/`, and forwarding Delegations (F1, F7, F9, 3.8); §8.5 owner consent and §8.8 access logs (F1, F3, F7, F8); §7.10, §8.12 and §10.9 the committers of owner decisions [113](#od-113), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128) and [144](#od-144) (F1, F3, F9); §11.11 new-commit identity (F2); §14.5's proof parts and §14.16 TL1 at M9 (F5); §17.9's `WindowDelegation` and share signers (F7); §12, §13 and §15 the host `mx.<net>.<root>` (F6, F10).
  - §10.6's gkm checks and §10.9's table accept, from a non-writer signer in the config group, an agent's first wrap, a Remove and the rotation it requires, under the gkm `rw` scope §7.8 gives member devices in the config group, and a recovery-admitted device's external commit, and follow §7.9's `leaves` and `move` rows, where a wrapped signer only wraps or rotates and a lost entitlement is a Remove input (owner decisions [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144); F1, F9).
  - evs and gkm keep each repo's metadata on the cluster its `place/<repo_id>` names, and §11.10's leases, the push sequence and the head cache in Redis (owner decisions [136](#od-136), [145](#od-145); F2, F3).
  - §5.9 keeps the index cache, and §16.10 states the scope, taint, paging and grouping rules F11 cites; §11.14's index provides buckets and all, roll-ups by the indexer or the first writer after expiry, and entry versions naming each index file's plaintext hash; §7.9's `IndexerSet` designates 3.6's indexers, none by default (owner decisions [150](#od-150), [151](#od-151)-[157](#od-157), [166](#od-166), [177](#od-177)).
  - §11.14 states remote search's eligibility, fixed sizes and merge rules, §18.4 its notice and setting and §18.7 the foreground Hello; §6.4's control contracts carry SEARCH, and §4.6's C19 reports a requester-indexer pair that §6.11's bit 1 marks per §6.10's windows, both directions, at a fixed floor (owner decisions [175](#od-175)-[178](#od-178), [188](#od-188); F12). §16.11 states the directory's announcements and requests in their M6 and M10 forms, §8.4 `autogroup:dst-owner`, and §10.4 the directory's group under §7.9's leaves rule (owner decisions [170](#od-170), [171](#od-171), [179](#od-179)-[182](#od-182); F13).
  - §22.7 draws S1-S13 from F1-F13 and ties its `GkmCommitHeader` assertion to S3 and S4; §23 schedules §11's v0b (the local git server) with v0a at M2 (F2) and orders the flows ([owner decision 9](#od-9)).

### 3.14 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sections lag the directive or the owner's decisions, so §22's scenarios test superseded flows | High | High | decision citations in flows; D-ARCH-4's check at G0 (§23.8); I-18 |
| A removed leaf stays in a repo's MLS tree until a writer leaf commits its Remove ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) | Medium | Low | agents' rotations reopen the gate meanwhile, and no leaf wrap uses an epoch that holds it (§10.5); hints wake writer leaves |
| Outbound mail waits on sound BDAT and DATA preamble proofs | High | High | burner email launches receive-only (F6, F10); both proofs sit on the mail team's critical path (owner decisions [9](#od-9), [35](#od-35), [125](#od-125)) |
| A site or Hurricane Electric outage stops every flow and both nameservers; losing the site loses server-held data | Medium; Low | Critical | accepted (owner decisions [94](#od-94), [123](#od-123)); an out-of-hours rota pages from M3 ([owner decision 143](#od-143)); mail senders retry (§15.3); devices re-seed from local copies and Postgres rows from D-OPS-18's daily off-site dump (§19.10); record repos and their slots mirror to an indexer where one is designated (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [150](#od-150), [177](#od-177)) |
| P0 safety work (revocations and their rotations, Removes, shreds, erasures) runs at once whatever its volume ([owner decision 186](#od-186)), so a wave of it on one metadata cluster, legal within every network's rates (100 large Teams each shrinking every 5 minutes ask ~2.9 TiB a day a drive, about twice the refill), wears its drives past 0.8 DWPD and their 1 DWPD rating, stops its pushes and evacuation while it lasts, past the 26 h NVMe bound, keeps its forgiven excess as wear ([owner decision 190](#od-190)), and outruns the M2 sizing, which bounds wear only at the admitted mix | Low | High | §11.13's per-class rates, and the cluster's pushes and evacuation restarting as the wave ends, ramping up as the write budget's bucket refills; §19.8's P0 page within an hour and §19.10's runbook: capacity, placement, the networks; §11.21 |
| Repos stay on the cluster placed at creation until a later move tool, so the first metadata cluster's writes can outgrow its set ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) | Medium | High | §11.13's write budget refuses the heaviest network first ([owner decision 140](#od-140)); new repos go to the next cluster from §19.9's triggers; §19.9's cohorts row tracks each cluster's own growth, builds the move tool before the earliest projected exhaustion and, until it exists, holds a full cluster to maintenance (507 CLUSTER_FULL) |

### 3.15 Phasing

§23 orders milestones (X15): after the shared M0-M2, recURd and mail run as two tracks ([owner decision 9](#od-9)). F1 needs §5 and §7's P0 with 7-day sidecar tokens (M1; owner decisions [45](#od-45), [103](#od-103), [131](#od-131)), then the config repo (M2; owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [112](#od-112)-[114](#od-114), [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144)); F2 needs §10, §11's v0a and v0b and the PM9A3 metadata set, whose benchmark gates format 1 on drive writes per push (M2; [owner decision 140](#od-140)), then the production cluster (M3); F8 adds §16 (M3). Member-level F3 and F9 arrive with Team at M6 ([owner decision 102](#od-102)); their device forms (§10 KF2, KF4) run from M2. F7 needs C5, C6a, C13 and C14 (M4), Linux first, and C18 for cross-network invites (M6). F4 needs C9, the dns edge, the 443 SNI split and ports 8443, 8883 and 5671 (M5; [owner decision 121](#od-121)). F6 needs mxedge on port 25, DNSSEC and TLSA (M7), with phone wakes from M8's app hosts ([owner decision 88](#od-88)). F10 launches burner email receive-only at M8, once the owner accepts M7's census loss ([owner decision 34](#od-34); D-MAIL-9). F5 and burner replies wait for M9's sound BDAT and DATA proofs (owner decisions [35](#od-35), [125](#od-125)). F11 and F2's versionless steps need §11's format 2, with the index, at M10 (owner decisions [163](#od-163), [169](#od-169)), behind its computed drive-write gate ([owner decision 174](#od-174)); F11 reaches other members' claims in the team directory and the team record's run cards once M6's exist. F12's serving side ships at M10, its app-host steps at the later of M10's and M8's exits and its team-indexer steps at the later of M10's and M6's; F13 runs at M6 on format 1's record streams, its phone wakes from M8 and its cards and search steps at M10 (D-PHASE-11). Edges and mail start dark in main ([owner decision 91](#od-91)). recURd needs F1, F2 and F8, then F7; burner email needs F6 and F10, then F5.

## 4. Repositories, code placement, branches, and build

### 4.1 Purpose and scope

This section decides where code lives and how it is built, branched, versioned, published and shipped, including X9's connect changes and the checkout's documents. Components are §5-§18, deployment §19, tests §22, milestones §23.

### 4.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-REPO-1 | CLI and components in sidecar; services, team management and access control in server; sdk exposes the components | PLAN.md:5 |
| R-REPO-2 | sidecar imports connect only; server and sdk import sidecar | PLAN.md:7 |
| R-REPO-3 | go.mod, sidecar.go, protocol/, mcp/, cli/main.go; service code in the root | PLAN.md:9-21 |
| R-REPO-4 | New pieces, MLS included, in sidecar; all work on `sidecar` branches | owner rules 1, 4 |
| R-REPO-5 | No parent package imports a child; commits carry no AI attribution | connect/CODESTYLE.md:24-47, 80-83 |
| R-REPO-6 | Go 1.27.3, pinned siblings, rollout classes, no cgo in sidecar packages | server/README.md:5-14; sdk/js/Makefile:69 |
| R-REPO-7 | Open source, signed releases, one calendar version; reproducible builds a goal, not a gate | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:930; build/README.md:3-7; [owner decision 77](#od-77) |
| R-REPO-8 | sidecar public from 2026-11-04 as it is; every touched repo merges `sidecar` into `main` at each exit review | owner decisions [117](#od-117), [118](#od-118) |

### 4.3 What exists today

- **Repos** (`gh repo view`, `git log`, 2026-11-05). sidecar holds two `main` commits and no code: `2b5b0ab` (2026-11-03, 119 documents) and `708bb45` (2026-11-05, the design checkpoint: the business documents moved under `design/` as renames, so their history follows, and DESIGN.md, its reviews, README.md with its images, the research sheets and the search-index report and notes added). INTERNAL and unlicensed before [owner decision 118](#od-118)'s flip, it is now PUBLIC, its README stating MPL-2.0, whose full text is the first `sidecar` commit (4.9); connect, sdk, server, sn (`urfoundation/sn`), build, warp and extension are PUBLIC too, config, vault and xops PRIVATE, mmm INTERNAL. None has a `sidecar` branch.
- **Replaces and pins.** Replaces are not inherited, so server, sn and four sdk modules repeat them (server/go.mod:213-236; sn/go.mod:205-223; sdk/go.mod:107-115). server's lock pins complete commits of nine clean siblings on one `go` line (server/local/source-graph/source_graph_test.go:90, 113-143, 200-235); build pins its submodules as gitlinks (build/.gitmodules).
- **Release, hooks, CI:** `yyyy.m.d-code` versions (build/all/run.sh:1186-1195). connect and sdk declare unversioned modules (connect/go.mod:1; sdk/go.mod:1), which consumers require at v0.0.0 beside sibling replaces (server/go.mod:48, 213), and the release rewrites each to `/v2026` on a version branch (4.9). An unclassified service exits 64 (build/all/deploy-rollout.zsh:37-39). All touched repos but sidecar, config and vault share one commit-msg hook. With no hosted CI, policy lives in Go tests, a leg per shipped build (sdk/dependency_boundary_test.go:81-92).

- Of this module's packages, the root imports only `protocol` and `protocol/bridge`, std-and-protobuf packages, as connect's root imports `connect/protocol` (Q-REPO-3). `protocol` imports `protocol/bridge`, never the reverse, so a type both use is declared only in `protocol/bridge` (4.9). The root never imports `device/`: `cli/` (`ur tun`, `ur bridge`) and sdk's `DeviceLocal` wire `device.Bridge` to the root's `BridgeState`, so Apple's network extensions, the `ios_extension` leg, link of the root only §18.10's forwarding files and of `protocol` only its config, acl, evs and gkm descriptors (D-SDK-20; [owner decision 197](#od-197)).
- **Build tags.** Desktop-only code (the OS tun, §17.10; installers; the macOS keychain, §5.10) lives in `cli/` or carries `!ios && !android && !sdk_mobile_bind`. Package connect links gVisor into every importer through its untagged tun.go (connect/tun.go:38-47), so root files that use package connect (client generations and `SidecarEnv`, `Subprotocol` and streams, remote search, sockets dial and listen, the bridge, tls and smtp listeners) carry `!sidecar_http`, as do the engine host interfaces (`host_*.go`), since no hosted server engine runs in the page Worker, whose search engine needs none. The rest, §5.4's events, actions, binding and `Sign` included, uses the root's own `Id` ([16]byte), `Logger`, `MonitorValue` and `CallbackList`, and reaches api through the net/http `SidecarApi` (bearer plus DPoP signer), in both legs; connect-facing files convert at that boundary, and §4.7 fails the `sidecar_http` leg on any connect or gVisor package (§18.10).

| bridge (§17) | `bridge_` (the compiler builds `BridgeState`, in the daemon or an app's VPN component); `device/` (the forwarding role's packet side); `protocol/bridge` | sdk DeviceLocal imports `device/` (sdk/device_local.go:5707, 5800); connect C5, C18 |

```go
// host_service.go: supplied by the hosting process; engines never import server, so go-redis,
// minio-go and prometheus stay out of sidecar.
type ServiceHost struct {
	Authenticator Authenticator       // jwt -> Principal (server/session)
	Quota         Quota               // reserve, commit, release (§20)
	Metrics       Metrics             // prometheus in server
	Tasks         Tasks               // once-keyed jobs (taskworker)
	Redis         Redis               // cas, incr, scripts, TTLs, hash-tagged keys; evs and gkm keep only soft state
	                                  // they rebuild there (owner decision 136); keyspace events only via the shared
	                                  // subscriber, never per client, the pattern that melted the cluster on
	                                  // 2026-07-15 (server/model/peer_model.go:32-37)
	Blobs         BlobStore           // the segment bucket and each metadata cluster's bucket, by cluster id, the
	                                  // first holding place/ (owner decision 145): If-Match and If-None-Match
	                                  // puts, streamed put, ranged get, prefix list, delete (X13)
	Push          Push                // server to client (X8)
	ServiceClient ServiceClientSource // jwt and urls for the engine's connect client
}

// Each engine that a server/cli/<svc> hosts; server wraps it with readiness, /status, stats and
// PROXY-unwrapped listeners. pushservice's types run inside existing services instead.
type Engine interface {
	Handler() http.Handler // or Serve(net.Listener) for stream engines
	Ready() bool
	Drain()
	Close()
}
```

evs and gkm keep durable state only in `Blobs` (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [19](#od-19), [21](#od-21)): a repo's metadata objects and its gkm group's live on the metadata cluster that the repo's create-only `place/<repo_id>` on the first cluster names, which the engines resolve and cache ([owner decision 145](#od-145); §11.8). Other engines take a store (`SmtpEdgeStore`, …) that server/model implements beside the migrations.

- **Imports:** besides this repository's modules, connect and its replaced forks are the only first-party modules a sidecar module requires, never proxy or the userwireguard it requires (proxy/go.mod:9-10), so `ur proxy add` (cli/UI.md:39-41) runs in `cli/` on §17's userspace `connect.Tun`.
- **Third-party:** `dependencies.yml` lists each module with SPDX id, reason and leg (client, engine, cli, test). Allowed: MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC, MPL-2.0; refused: GPL family, SSPL, BUSL, custom, unlicensed. Initial: protobuf v1.36.11, x/crypto, docopt-go, pires/go-proxyproto, go-sdk v1.7.0 for mcp/ and go-winio v0.6.2 for §5.8's pipe (server/go.mod:30, 67), purego v0.11.2 for the macOS Keychain (Apache-2.0), wireguard's tun (MIT) for `cli/`'s OS tun (§17.10); in the test leg, `mlsinterop/`'s peers [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md).
- **Versions:** shared modules match connect, sdk and server, because an uncoordinated bump fails server's `-mod=readonly` build (server/README.md:12); protobuf follows §18.10; golang.org/x/text follows §11.14's normalizer 1: one module version on every leg, at least server's and sn's v0.43.0 (server/go.mod:59; sn/go.mod:191), so connect and sdk bump together from v0.40.0 (connect/go.mod:33, sdk/go.mod:97) and gomobile's v0.41.0 (sdk/build/go.mod:96), whose NFC wrongly composes 19,960 two-rune strings (every two-rune string checked under go1.27.3, 2026-11-05), U+05D2 U+0307 into U+105C9 and U+10044 U+0307 into U+1E0A among them, which v0.43.0 normalizes correctly under the same reported Unicode version, 17.0.0 (v0.40.0 and v0.41.0 key recomposition on runes clipped to 16 bits, .gomodcache/golang.org/x/text@v0.40.0/unicode/norm/forminfo.go:217).

### 4.8 Branches and cross-repo pinning

- **Branches.** Every repo the work touches gets a `sidecar` branch at M0 (§23.4; [owner decision 196](#od-196)), on its normal remote, public where the repo is ([owner decision 118](#od-118)); the extension and apps only if the owner opts in. `urnetwork/minio`, the new fork that holds D-OPS-20's build, is a sibling checkout with its own `sidecar` branch, and the owner creates its GitHub repo before any push ([owner decision 195](#od-195)). `main` stays production-ready (build/README.md:5).
- **Pins.** server@sidecar's lock and build@sidecar's submodules pin the same `sidecar` commits, which server's source-graph tests confirm.
- **Merge, never rebase.** A rebase orphans pinned commits and skips the commit-msg hook (connect/.githooks/commit-msg:17-18). Merge `main` in weekly and before each gate, in the order connect, sidecar, sdk, sn, server, warp/config/vault/xops/mmm, build, re-pinning each time.
- **To `main`** at each milestone's Gn-out (§23.8): every touched repo, server and sdk included, in that order, once the pinned set passes its checks, migrations are additive and release-compatible (connect/CODESTYLE.md:85-89), connect's default-off changes lead and the code is dark (D-OPS-10). Branch migrations stay pending until their own Gn-out registers them (D-OPS-6), so one track's merge never applies the other track's group, and M3's pilot runs on production ([owner decision 118](#od-118); §23.9).

### 4.9 Generation, targets, versions, license, style

- **Protobuf:** `protocol/Makefile` runs `protoc -I=. --go_out=. --go_opt=paths=source_relative protocol/*.proto protocol/bridge/*.proto` from the repo root, so files register as `protocol/<name>.proto` and `protocol/bridge/<name>.proto` in package `urnetwork.sidecar`; sdk and server link connect's and sidecar's packages, and a duplicate path or name panics at init (protobuf@v1.36.11/reflect/protoregistry/registry.go:42, 128, 152), so `config.proto`, `acl.proto` and `directory.proto` import the types 4.4 lists for `protocol/bridge`, never redeclare them. `tool` pins protoc-gen-go v1.36.11, and output is committed.
- **Mobile, wasm, C ABI:** gomobile binds only sdk (§18.3). `make size` gates from v0: the `ios_extension` leg (`device/`, `protocol/bridge` and the root's forwarding files; D-SDK-20) fails if sidecar adds over §18.10's budget, 6 MiB stripped (owner decisions [197](#od-197), [215](#od-215)), and the `sidecar_http` js leg is measured unstripped from M2 against §18.10's 41,943,040 B goal and miss rule (D-SDK-19). No C ABI: desktop apps use the `ur` daemon (§5) or sdk's generated ABI (sdk/cgo/gen/gen.go).
- **Versions.** Development paths stay unversioned, as connect's and sdk's do; the release runs their steps (build/all/run.sh), which §22.4's release fixture checks:

```text
branch     v<version> in each repo (:1302)
root       go mod edit -module .../sidecar/v2026 (:1540-1543); quoted import paths in Go files and Makefiles
           rewritten (:1560-1566); the tree moved into v2026/, nested modules left in place (go_mod_fork,
           :1639-1683); tag v2026.M.D-<code> (:1781-1786)
smtpproof  the same as its own module: .../sidecar/smtpproof/v2026, tag smtpproof/v2026.M.D-<code>; in every
           repo its paths are rewritten before the root's subpackage pass, which skips lines already carrying
           /vN (:1564-1566)
cli        requires both tags, builds ur, never tagged as a module
version    the release sed fills Version, as for sdk (sdk/sdk.go:737; :1964)
generated  .pb.go files are committed, never regenerated on the release branch; descriptors keep
           protocol/<name>.proto and protocol/bridge/<name>.proto, so one module identity registers each
           descriptor once
fixture    the tags served through GOPROXY=file:// with GOWORK=off, an empty module cache and no replaces:
           root, protocol and an engine package import at the tag, ur builds from cli/, go list -m all shows
           one sidecar path, each descriptor registers once, and sdk's go mod graph holds no smtpproof or
           prover dependency
```

- **License and style.** The full MPL-2.0 text, copyright 2026 BringYour, Inc., is the first `sidecar` commit and reaches `main` at M0's Gn-out; GitHub reads connect's abbreviated notice (connect/LICENSE:1-3) as "Other". CODESTYLE.md adopts connect's plus the leaf, host and dependency rules; `.githooks/commit-msg` is copied byte for byte into sidecar, config, vault and minio before their first `sidecar` commit.

### 4.10 CLI distribution

| OS | Artifacts and signing | Path |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | `.pkg` and `.tar.gz` of a Developer ID `ur` bundle with a provisioning profile and hardened runtime (D-CORE-12), notarized and stapled (run.sh:2644-2673) | `/usr/local/bin/ur`, linked into the bundle |
| Linux | `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.pkg.tar.zst` (nfpm) and `.tar.gz`, direct downloads through `install.sh`'s verified path, with no apt or yum repository, GPG key or repository host ([owner decision 213](#od-213)) | `/usr/bin/ur`; the script uses `/usr/local/bin/ur` |
| Windows | `.zip`, winget later; signtool SHA-256 with a timestamp (windows/app/SIGNING.md:17) | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\URnetwork\ur.exe` |

- **`git-remote-ur`** ships beside `ur` in every package as a link to the same binary, which dispatches on argv[0] (a copy in the Windows zip); git runs it for `ur://` URLs from PATH (gitremote-helpers(7); §11.11), so Windows users add the zip's directory to PATH.
- **Build.** `CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath` from `cli/`'s module, archive times from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (server/cli/api/Makefile:1, 4); macOS's keychain goes through purego (D-CORE-12).
- **Release integrity.** Signing is the gate ([owner decision 77](#od-77)): a VirusTotal scan (run.sh:2257-2298), then a `SHA256SUMS` SSH-signed by an offline two-person Ed25519 key (§2.6), whose public key the repo and ur.io publish. `install.sh` on ur.io (mmm's branch from M0, §23.4; owner decisions [15](#od-15), [16](#od-16), [196](#od-196)) pins the key, verifies signature and checksum (`ssh-keygen -Y verify`, OpenSSH 8.1+) and refuses on any failure. From M4 the sums also list the key origin's loader and `sidecar.wasm`, which `sidecar.ur.io` serves only from a promoted build (§18.8; [owner decision 221](#od-221)).
- **Harness configs (§16)** use `ur`'s absolute path, since GUI-launched hosts lack the shell PATH ([MCP debugging](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2025-03-26/tools/debugging.md)). v0 has no self-updater.

### 4.11 The documents in the sidecar checkout

The checkout holds documents only, on `main` (§4.3): at the root, README.md (its images in `design/readme/` and `design/mocks/previews/`), DESIGN.md with its reviews (DESIGN-REVIEW1.md to DESIGN-REVIEW3b.md and DESIGN-REVIEW-RESPONSE.md), FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md and `research_notes/`; under `design/`, the business and input documents: PLAN.md, product.md, the pitches (pitch1.html to pitch5.html, with PDFs of the last three), the market notes (market.md, market2.md, gap.md, improve.md, improvements4.md, sentiment2.md), two overview PDFs, a saved IETF draft (d.html), mocks/, reports/ (among them the Tailscale, agent-work-record and 2026-11-05 search-index reports), design-research/ (the sheets behind DESIGN.md's research links) and cold5/'s outreach drafts. All of it is public as it is, history included, the move into `design/` kept as renames (owner decisions [117](#od-117), [118](#od-118)), so DESIGN.md's citations (`sidecar/design/pitch5.html`, `sidecar/design/market2.md`, `sidecar/design/reports/Encrypted repo search index formats.md`) resolve publicly, and its research links point into `design/design-research/`. Code starts on the `sidecar` branch (§4.8).

### 4.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scrub, then publish a filtered clone (D-REPO-8 as drafted) | Business material stays private | A second repository, a rewrite and a path allowlist | Rejected ([owner decision 117](#od-117)) |
| `/v2026` in development paths | One identity in every build | Breaks connect's and sdk's convention and consumers' v0.0.0 requires; the rewrite already publishes `/v2026` | Rejected (D-REPO-1) |
| `cli/` in the root module | One module | The root requires `smtpproof`, whose requirements then enter every consumer's graph, sdk's legs included | Rejected (D-REPO-2; [owner decision 104](#od-104)) |

§23.10 rejects D-REPO-9's private mirrors ([owner decision 118](#od-118)).

### 4.13 Decisions proposed

**D-REPO-1 (proposed).** Use §4.7's go.mod, §4.9's proto naming, an unversioned development path, and the release rewrite to `/v2026` that connect and sdk use (§4.9). *Why:* §4.3's replace and lock rules, protobuf's init-time panic, and the release convention; Go accepts a v2026 tag only on a `/v2026` path, which only the release tree has.

**D-REPO-2 (proposed).** Use §4.4's tree: MLS in root `mls_*` files ([owner decision 43](#od-43)), server-only engines in `<svc>service` packages ([owner decision 104](#od-104)), the forwarding role's packet side in the leaf `device/` over `protocol/bridge`, which alone declares the types it parses, linked in apps' VPN components with only the root's forwarding files (D-SDK-20; [owner decision 197](#od-197)), connect-facing and engine-host root files under `!sidecar_http` (D-SDK-19), test peers only in `mlsinterop/`; `cli/` and `smtpproof/` are nested modules the root never requires. *Why:* CODESTYLE groups files by prefix (connect/CODESTYLE.md:49-62); owner rule 1; a message declared twice panics at init, and importing connect links gVisor; test peers must not raise consumers' versions, and a root requirement reaches every consumer's module graph.

**D-REPO-3 (proposed).** Engines live in sidecar behind §4.5's `ServiceHost` and stores, and server hosts each one (Q-REPO-1). *Why:* logic stays in sidecar, persistence beside the migrations, and URnetwork-only infrastructure behind interfaces ([owner decision 48](#od-48)).

**D-REPO-4 (proposed).** Enforce §4.7 with `make check` and §4.9's v0 `make size` gate; ship no binding or C ABI. *Why:* no hosted CI exists, sidecar must be checked as the bindings build it, and a cgo file would enter gomobile's macOS slice.

**D-REPO-5 (proposed).** X9 changes are generic, additive, off by default and wire-compatible, tested in connect and merged to connect `main` first. *Why:* connect serves every client.

**D-REPO-6 (proposed).** Consumers wire sidecar as §4.7 lists, and branches follow §4.8. *Why:* the gates fail closed, pins must stay reachable (owner rule 4), and migration versions are positions.

**D-REPO-7 (proposed).** License, style, hook and distribution per §4.9 and §4.10, with offline-signed sums. *Why:* the open-source promise, the owner's commit rule, and no single origin may ship a client.

**D-REPO-8 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 117](#od-117): no scrub, archive, filtered clone or path allowlist; the repo keeps its documents and history.

**D-REPO-9 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 118](#od-118): no private mirrors; every `sidecar` branch uses its repo's normal remote and merges to `main` at each Gn-out.

### 4.14 Open questions

**Q-REPO-1.** How do PLAN.md:5-7's repos split a service? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 19](#od-19)):** (a), a sidecar engine that server hosts and backs with its stores (D-REPO-3). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-2.** [X9] Which connect changes may land on connect's `sidecar` branch? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 22](#od-22)):** (b), §4.6's dispositions, as owner decisions [85](#od-85), [86](#od-86) and [176](#od-176) amend them. *Residual:* C17, for the extension's streaming Worker only, after §18's spike.

**Q-REPO-3.** May `protocol/` be an exception to connect/CODESTYLE.md:26? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 52](#od-52)):** (a), with a `make check` test that `protocol/` and `protocol/bridge` import nothing else from sidecar (§4.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-4.** When does sidecar go public, and with which documents? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 (owner decisions [117](#od-117), [118](#od-118)):** now, as it is (§4.11), superseding the scrub and later publication of owner decisions [51](#od-51) and [107](#od-107); nothing waits for publication (§4.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-5.** Should server-only engines live in the root (PLAN.md:13)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 104](#od-104)):** (b), child packages, and (d), a nested module for the X7 prover (§4.4); `cli/` is a nested module too, so the root never requires the prover (§4.7). *Residual:* none.

### 4.15 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:13** ("all service code goes in the root"): engines live in `<svc>service` child packages and the X7 prover in a nested module, so no mobile or wasm build links them ([owner decision 104](#od-104); Q-REPO-5), and the forwarding role's packet side in the leaf `device/`, so the iOS extension links of the root only its forwarding files (Q-SDK-5, closed by peer review; D-SDK-20; [owner decision 197](#od-197)).
- **PLAN.md:9-21** (the tree) stands; `cli/` carries its own go.mod so the prover's requirements stay out of consumers' module graphs ([owner decision 104](#od-104)).

### 4.16 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the tree and modules, `ServiceHost`, the X9 rows, the checks, §4.8's and §4.11's rules, §4.9's release rewrite, and §4.10's install paths (§11, §16).
- **Consumes:** §6 (X8; §6.4's requester feature bit, §6.11's marked pair and §6.10's windows, which C19 keys on), §10 (X12), §11 (X19; placement; §11.14's normalizer 1, which x/text follows), §13 (X1), §17 (X18; C5's dial fence and per-flow idle, `WindowDelegation`, C18's alias map), §18 (X14; `sidecar_http`, `device/`), §19's gates and pending migrations (D-OPS-6), §22.4's `sidecar_testhooks` and release fixture, §23's milestones.
- **Subprotocol messages, API routes, tables:** none (routes: C11).
- **Services and config:** §4.5's server column; lock.yml; build/.gitmodules; run.sh; deploy-rollout.zsh; dependencies.yml.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §6 adds no protobuf `service` blocks; §6, §9-§15 and §19 follow §4.5's placement; §6.9, §7.9, §8.8 and §17 declare what `device/` parses only in `protocol/bridge`'s `signed.proto`, `auth.proto` (§8.8's `GrantRevoke`, `Suspend` and `Unsuspend` included) and `bridge.proto`, which `config.proto`, `acl.proto` and `directory.proto` import (4.4); §5.4 and §18.10 keep connect types out of the `sidecar_http` leg's files, and §18.10 excludes `host_*.go` (4.4); §10, §11 and §19 keep each repo's metadata on the cluster its `place/` object names ([owner decision 145](#od-145)); §5.8 and §11.11 define `git-remote-ur`'s daemon mode; §17, §2.10 and §22 cover C18, and §2.8's connect-5 and §20.6 state what C19 leaves visible and costs; §23.9 merges every touched repo at each Gn-out.

### 4.17 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engine or root code bloats the iOS extension, which since [owner decision 197](#od-197) links the root's forwarding files | Medium | High | `<svc>service` packages; the leaf `device/` and the `ios_extension` leg's file and descriptor lists; `make size` at [owner decision 215](#od-215)'s budget |
| Branches drift from mains that release almost daily | High | Medium | Weekly and per-milestone merges; pending migration groups (D-OPS-6) |
| A secret or AI-attributed message on a public branch stays served by hash (https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/removing-sensitive-data-from-a-repository, read 2026-11-03) | Low | Medium | The hook in every clone (connect/.githooks/commit-msg:23-27); `--scan` before each push and at each Gn-out (§23.8); secrets only in vault |
| A Go release breaks purego, leaving macOS pass-only | Low | High | Pinned version; a Keychain round trip in `make check`; cgo fallback |
| A tagged consumer resolves two sidecar module paths or registers a descriptor twice | Low | High | 4.9's rewrite; §22.4's release fixture |
| C19 misreports a remote-search window, or a window's background passes its allowance, so its pages show to a 128 KiB step | Low | Low | One floor constant and §6.10's table; FS-125's sweep in connect's own tests before the merge to `main` (D-REPO-5); only traffic past the scheduled background at its maximum overflows |

### 4.18 Phasing

- **v0, before code (M0):** LICENSE, the hook, the root's and `cli/`'s go.mod, dependencies.yml and `make check` on sidecar's `sidecar` branch, merged at M0's Gn-out (DESIGN.md and the documents are on `main` already, 708bb45); M0's branches; the lock entry, the release step and its fixture.
- **v0, first usable:** §4.6's M1, M4 and M5 rows; the first hosted engine; signed `ur` packages; the `make size` gate; `sidecar_http`'s import rule (M1) and size measure (M2); `device/` and its `ios_extension` rule, with the root's forwarding files (M4; [owner decision 197](#od-197)).
- **v1:** C18 (M6); C19's window accounting (M10; owner decisions [176](#od-176), [188](#od-188)) and 4.7's x/text bump, ahead of M10's index code; Homebrew and winget; no apt or yum repository, `.deb` and `.rpm` staying direct downloads ([owner decision 213](#od-213)). **Later:** C4 with §18's worker, and C17 for that streaming Worker if its spike needs it.
- **Blocking:** M0's `make check` blocks the first consumer pin; C13 blocks C18; C19 blocks M10's Gn-out, since §2.8's connect-5 assumes it.

## 5. The Sidecar core: identity, keys, lifecycle, local state

### 5.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns `sidecar.Sidecar` (lifecycle, components, events, the outward-action gate); the client identity (X10); the client side of login, enrollment, pairing, admission, owner consent, refresh, revocation and AUTHZ1; and the daemon, local IPC, local state, keys, recovery and platform variants. §6 owns the subprotocol; §7 enrollment routes, auth keys, OAuth, the AUTHZ1 server fix and config records; §8 policy; §10 MLS; §11 evs; §16 MCP and approvals; §18 hosting; §20 counting.

### 5.2 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-CORE-1 | Import connect only | PLAN.md:7 |
| R-CORE-2 | Hold "an authenticated jwt, connect client, api, and encryption key" | PLAN.md:14 |
| R-CORE-3 | The CLI speaks stdio MCP by default | PLAN.md:19-20 |
| R-CORE-4 | Run in the sdk, the apps, and the extension's web worker | PLAN.md:28 |
| R-CORE-5 | The git identity is the sidecar client id | PLAN.md:59 |
| R-CORE-6 | `--instance`; `ur login/logout/status/daemon/install-daemon/uninstall-daemon` | cli/UI.md:10-19 |
| R-CORE-7 | A keychain encoded with a pass; changing the pass re-encodes it | cli/UI.md:82-85 |
| R-CORE-8 | Any number of in-daemon agents, free, with their bytes debited (pitch5's "never metered" changes) | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:844, :849; owner decisions [4](#od-4), [10](#od-10) |
| R-CORE-9 | `ur connect --token`; "Log in with URnetwork" | sidecar/design/mocks/recurd-app.html:712, :930 |
| R-CORE-10 | Agent tokens ≤1 h, key-bound, never in the agent's environment | sidecar/FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md:139; §2 I-7 |
| R-CORE-11 | No sidecar credential can administer the network | §2 I-6 |
| R-CORE-12 | Identities survive the client reaper | server/model/network_client_model.go:4179, :4199 |
| R-CORE-13 | Settings-owned tunables; a `Logger` with connect's methods; pure Go for wasm; mobile budgets | connect/CODESTYLE.md:140-151, :179-182; [R:sdk-clients](design/design-research/sdk-clients.md) §3 |
| R-CORE-14 | Outward actions need an I-8 approval from every entry point | §2 I-8; [owner decision 75](#od-75) |
| R-CORE-15 | One person in several networks, no key linking them | §7 R-TEAM-3; [owner decision 23](#od-23) |
| R-CORE-16 | Admission and revocation only by signed config-repo records, from v0 | owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [127](#od-127) |
| R-CORE-17 | Owner-bound repos take only consented devices; members' devices alarm on admissions under them that they did not sign | [owner decision 126](#od-126) |
| R-CORE-18 | Each network's search index cache stays sealed on the device, is fetched by sync position, holds no query, and is deleted with the content or access it derives from | [owner decision 166](#od-166); §11 D-EVS-26 |
| R-CORE-19 | An indexer's remote serving leaves local searches their targets and persists no query | [owner decision 175](#od-175); I-13 |

### 5.3 What exists today

**connect**
- `BringYourApi` has `AuthNetworkClient(Sync)`, `RemoveNetworkClient` and `GetClientKey`, but no refresh (connect/api.go:20-62, :256-330, :548-570). `NewClient` (connect/transfer.go:2267) takes a `ClientKeySeed` (:1657-1663) and `ClientAuth` (connect/transport.go:348-364).
- `ClientKeyManager.Sign` signs without a label (connect/transfer_key.go:221-229), and the key history does not stop an operator malicious from first contact (connect/transfer_key_history.go:22-26). The ClientKey is plain Ed25519 from a 32-byte seed (connect/transfer_key.go:127-129).
- Package connect's untagged tun.go imports gVisor (connect/tun.go:38-50), so a file using any connect type, even `Id` (connect/id.go:15), `Logger` (connect/log.go:41), `MonitorValue` or `CallbackList` (connect/util.go:74, :220), links the IP stack.

**server**
- A client token creates only its own children (`source_client_id`, server/model/network_client_model.go:191, :374-394). A child is exempt from the client caps (:535, :757-779), never becomes a peer (connect/transfer.go:17611-17617) and ends with its parent (server/session/by_jwt.go:679-700).
- The reaper deactivates a top-level client after 30 idle days and deletes it 30 days later, and deletes a child after 30 days unseen (server/model/network_client_model.go:4179, :4199, :4467). One resident serves each client id and instance (server/model/network_client_resident_model.go:62-68).
- `/auth/code-create` escalates a client token (server/api/route_authz.go:123), and expiry is not enforced (server/session/AUTH.md:229; §7.3); a removed client's tokens stop at once (server/session/AUTH.md:197). `GET /auth/refresh` takes a bare Client token (route_authz.go:115), and `POST /network/auth-client` (OwnClient) mints and reissues client tokens (:132), neither with a proof of possession.

**Missing:** everything below.

### 5.4 Sidecar: fields, settings, lifecycle, components

```go
// Every leg: sidecar.go, settings.go and the root's id, log and monitor files use no connect type, so
// §18.10's sidecar_http leg links them (§4.4). Sidecar is safe for concurrent use.
type Id [16]byte // connect.Id's layout (connect/id.go:15); connect-facing files convert: connect.Id(id)

type Logger interface { // connect.Logger's methods (connect/log.go:41); connect-facing files adapt it
	Info(args ...any)
	Infof(format string, args ...any)
	Warningf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
	V(level int32) Verbose // Verbose: Enabled(), Info, Infof
}

// MonitorValue[T comparable] and CallbackList[T any]: the root's copies of connect/util.go:74, :220.

type SidecarApi struct { // net/http: bind, refresh, the exchange and the sidecar routes (§7-§20)
	stateLock  sync.Mutex
	byJwt      string                                        // the authenticated jwt
	dpopSigner func(method, url, ath string) (string, error) // the ClientKey's proof (§7.4), by crypto/ed25519
	transport  http.RoundTripper // connect leg: dials by its ClientStrategy's ConnectSettings().DialContext
	                             // (connect/net_http.go:777, connect/net.go:232), egress-bound as
	                             // connect/net_http.go:3663-3668 requires; sidecar_http: net/http's fetch
}

type Sidecar struct {
	host           SidecarHost // Store(); KeyStore() (nil: pass only); TokenSource() (nil: D-CORE-8's refresher)
	settings       *SidecarSettings
	sidecarApi     *SidecarApi
	state          *MonitorValue[SidecarState] // Locked → Unenrolled ⇄ Offline ⇄ Online (5.6); a locked
	                                           // store → Locked (5.9); only a verified SidecarRevoke → Revoked
	eventCallbacks *CallbackList[SidecarEventFunction]

	stateLock sync.Mutex
	keychain  *keychain        // nil while locked; holds this network's root key R_n (5.9)
	identity  *SidecarIdentity // ids and identity public key
	leg       *sidecarLeg      // declared per leg: !sidecar_http, a BringYourApi on the same jwt, the components
	                           // and one connect.Client per client generation; sidecar_http, the long-poll (§6.8)
}

type SidecarAction struct { // every outward action (I-8)
	Kind      SidecarActionKind // tls/ or smtp/ publish or listen; forward; expose; egress change; invite or share;
	                            // alias create or delete; agent-config write or delete in a shared repo (§16.5);
	                            // DNS user record set or delete; mail to a non-member not yet approved, or to
	                            // any non-member in a tainted run; an access request through the team
	                            // directory (§16.11; CanonicalAction version 3); payment
	Canonical []byte            // built by the daemon; payload_sha256 = SHA-256(Canonical)
	Risk      SidecarRisk       // max(policy, daemon classifier); an agent may only raise it
	RunId     *Id               // a decision binds (approval_id, run_id, agent_id) and authorizes at most
	AgentId   *Id               // `uses` distinct actions, each once (§16 D-MCP-11)
}

type SidecarEvent struct { // AddEventCallback, `ur status`, the sdk listener (§18.5), ur://acl/grants
	Kind        SidecarEventKind // state, approval_pending, member_added, member_removed, key_changed, refused,
	                             // admission_alarm, recovery_rebind, recovery_window, recovery_unseen (5.6),
	                             // admissions_near_cap: on admin devices, from 90% of config_admissions' cap, with
	                             // §7.10's cleanup list,
	                             // head_alarm (§6.4); index_mismatch, index_malformed (§11.14); search_alarm: an
	                             // indexer's hit that its text disproves, or a local hit it omitted (§11.14);
	                             // history_drop: a drop's state changed (§11.7); access_request: an approver's
	                             // pending directory request, and access_decided: the requester's, with its
	                             // outcome; directory_erasure: a repo owner's revocation still waiting for the
	                             // directory's erasure runner past 24 h, then done (§16.11); erasure: an erasure
	                             // this device runs or may finish changed state (§11.12); mail_send: an internet
	                             // send's outcome for a recipient domain changed (§14.5)
	State       SidecarState
	Reason      SidecarStateReason // Unenrolled: expired, refused, parent_lost, session_ended, keystore_lost;
	                               // Revoked: signed (§18.5's GetStateReason)
	GroupId     *Id // membership kinds: the §10 group
	SidecarId   *Id // membership kinds: the leaf or wrapped reader; admission_alarm: the admitted sidecar;
	                // recovery_rebind: its signer; recovery_unseen: the recovered device; head_alarm: the peer;
	                // index alarms and history_drop: the signer; search_alarm: the indexer
	RepoId      *Id    // index alarms, search_alarm, history_drop, directory_erasure, erasure
	RefId       *Id    // index alarms, history_drop
	Path        string // index alarms: the alarmed path; history_drop: its first listed path (§18.5's Drops
	                   // lists all); a path local to this device, never logged (I-13)
	DropId      *Id              // history_drop
	DropState   SidecarDropState // history_drop: pending, cancelled, executing, done (a held drop reads done,
	                             // owner decision 184), refused, or invalid: it failed this device's checks (§11.7)
	NotBefore   time.Time        // history_drop: its window's end (owner decision 183)
	SearchAlarm SidecarSearchAlarm // search_alarm: mismatch (an opened hit's text disproves it) or omission (a
	                               // local confirmed hit that no page of the checked span returned)
	RequestId   *Id // access_request, access_decided: the directory request; directory_erasure: its erasure request
	Outcome     string // access_decided: approved, denied, cancelled or expired; directory_erasure: pending or done
	SendId      *Id // mail_send: the send, whose outcomes §18.5's GetSendResult reads
	ApprovalId  *Id
	HeadAlarm   SidecarHeadAlarm // head_alarm: fork, withheld (PROOF OF WITHHOLDING), unverified, or unwitnessed
	                             // (24 h without a consistent witness; 1 h for a revocation it signed)
	Evidence    [2][]byte        // head_alarm: my pin and the peer's or api's, as §6.5 encodes them (AuthPin,
	                             // GroupHead, GenHead or RefHead); recovery_rebind at a void: the AuthPins
	                             // at which keychain.wrap was sealed to the voided binding and re-sealed (5.9)
	Erasure     *SidecarErasure  // erasure: its id, state and what is left (§11.12, §11.13's wait)
}

type SidecarErasure struct { // §11.12's erasure as its eraser's device, or a device that may finish it, sees it
	ErasureId   Id
	State       string    // fenced: its CUTs committed, its documents masked and unpublishable, its own keys
	                      // gone with the first ERASE; rewriting; waiting: a 429 for its allowance or turn, or
	                      // room for its CUT in a ref's full erasure set (§11.12's cut row);
	                      // done: every key destroyed; stalled: no device that may finish it is running
	ObjectsLeft int64     // rekey objects not yet re-keyed (§11.13's wait row)
	BytesLeft   int64     // their closure bytes
	NextTry     time.Time // the last 429's retry_after_ms; zero when none waits
	Finish      time.Time // §11.13's bound from BytesLeft, the allowance and the turns; zero below the limit
}

type SidecarStatus struct { // Status(): `ur status`, §18.5's GetState and GetStateReason
	State       SidecarState
	Reason      SidecarStateReason
	Generation  int64     // the bound client generation (5.5)
	WitnessedAt time.Time // the newest consistent HeadCheck witness (§6.4); zero: none yet
	Unverified  [][]byte  // the open UNVERIFIED auth pins (§6.4), as AuthPin bytes; empty: none
}

type SidecarIdentityBinding struct { // 5.5; signed by the ClientKey and the identity key

}

	                                        // false on app hosts

// search, where connect links; §16.10's tools and `ur search` call it, and §18.5's SidecarSearch wraps it.

	Since, Until time.Time           // zero: unbounded

	AllowMetered bool                // scope all may fetch past §18.4's 25 MiB on a metered link

}
type SearchHit struct {
	Repo, Ref  Id

	Fields     []SearchField  // display fields: title or subject, from, and kind-specific ones
	Snippet    string         // verified hits: around the match; mail: i/'s snippet; else empty
	State      SearchHitState // SearchVerified, SearchConfirmed, SearchPossible, SearchNear, SearchUnmatched (a
	                          // local possible or near hit an indexer's checked span disproved, §11.14's merge)
	Partition  SearchPartition
	Correction string         // SearchNear: the corrected term
	By         string         // "": this device; else the answering indexer's config name (§11.14)
}
type SearchProgress struct {
	Searched, Total          int       // partitions
	FetchBytes, FetchedBytes int64     // scope all: bytes still to fetch, and fetched so far
	Uncovered                int       // changes not yet searchable

	CoveredFrom              time.Time
	Remote, FallbackReason   string    // §18.5's remote states and fallback reasons
	RemoteBy                 *Id       // the indexer asked, or the one a notice names
}

func (self *Sidecar) GetSearchStatus(repoId *Id) (*SearchStatus, error) // search_status (§16.10), GetStatus (§18.5)
func (self *Sidecar) SetSearchConditions(unmetered, charging, lowPower bool) // the host's reports (§18.7)

                                                          // (§18.7); unreported counts as background

func (self *Sidecar) AcknowledgeSearchIndexer(memberId *Id, allow bool) error // the notice; false sets own

// the engine host interfaces (host_*.go), since no hosted server engine runs in the page Worker, whose search
// engine needs none (§4.4); the sidecar_http leg declares SidecarConnectSettings empty and NewSidecar without
// components.
type SidecarConnectSettings struct {
	ClientStrategySettings    *connect.ClientStrategySettings
	ClientSettings            *connect.ClientSettings // Required, no P2P; provides Network, plus Service while on tls/ or smtp/ (§13.6) and FriendsAndFamily while sharing (§8.11); never Public (§6)
	PlatformTransportSettings *connect.PlatformTransportSettings
}

type SidecarComponent interface {
	Name() string                 // "evs", "sockets", "mail", "bridge", "tls"
	Attach(env *SidecarEnv) error // per client generation; returns promptly
	Close()
}

type SidecarEnv struct { // immutable; Ctx ends with the generation
	Ctx         context.Context
	Client      *connect.Client
	Api         *connect.BringYourApi
	SidecarApi  *SidecarApi
	Identity    *SidecarIdentity
	Secrets     SidecarSecrets // keychain namespace
	Store       SidecarStore   // component directory, streaming I/O
	Subprotocol *Subprotocol   // §6: inline, zero-wait handlers; streams
```
