- **No committer online:** the gate refuses writes until any writer, wrapped ones included, claims a covering generation (§10.5); removed devices keep only what they could decrypt (lazy revocation, PLAN.md:47-50). No server transaction changes readers (owner decisions [5](#od-5), [59](#od-59)).
- **Sponsors** ([owner decision 83](#od-83)): a removed member's tagged agents keep their tags' grants and their directory cards; until an admin's `SponsorSet`, `autogroup:sponsor`, and so `autogroup:dst-owner` for them ([owner decision 180](#od-180)), resolves to `autogroup:admin`, which their cards show as who, and their approval requests go to the team record (§8.4, §16.8, §16.11).

### 7.11 Audit log and SIEM

- **Server log.** `network_admin_event` records every admin action the server executes (per-network `seq`, actor, action, target, result, request id, hash chain; no client IP) for 400 days; Auditors and above read `GET /network/admin-events`, and HMAC-SHA256-signed SIEM webhooks retry for 24 h.
- **Server-visible fields** and TTLs: §2.8's api-1, api-3 to api-8, api-11; member, IdP, IdP-identity and webhook rows stay until removed.

### 7.12 Network names for teams

All three rename routes (server/controller/account_controller.go:13,160-256) call one `model.RenameNetwork`: §12's label rules and reserved list, the distance-1 check, 2 per day, the Admin permission, an admin event, a `network_name_reclaim` tombstone held 24 h (Q-TEAM-9), and refusal of any name in `dns_label`, label or alias, live or tombstoned (§12.5). Create and claim read tombstones; deletion writes one. Policy names networks by id, so a reclaimed name captures no grant.

### 7.13 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every admitted sidecar a config leaf | one key path | a commit per CI join and reap; 1,000 leaves | rejected ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) |
| Cap member devices at 1,000, or grow the config tree | no member wraps | the cap refuses Teams past ~330 members; 5,000 leaves make a 7.9-14 MB tree | rejected ([owner decision 144](#od-144)) |
| A recovery key alone signs authority statements | a lone Owner recovers | bypasses k of n | rejected ([owner decision 127](#od-127)) |
| Recovery keys sign only AuthorityProposals | one recovery signature per statement | admins who all lost their devices cannot reach k | rejected: a recovery cosign restarts the window (7.9) |
| ApiTick activates a restored binding's scoped admission by statement id | no proposal | a second activation list; vetoes keyed on statements too | not chosen: an AuthorityProposal reuses both ([owner decision 149](#od-149)) |
| End a Delegation's admissions at every drop of its key | a copied bundle stops at any agent's revocation or Suspend | one CI agent's removal or Suspend stops the pipeline's enrollments until an admin re-issues its secret | rejected: its `DelegationRevoke` or a compromise revocation of one of its agents ends it (7.9's delegation row) |

### 7.14 Decisions proposed

**D-TEAM-1 (proposed).** P0 stage 1 refuses child and admin-refused tokens on all 37 routes before any sidecar, after 14 days log-only, confines `strict_exp` bearers to 7.4's route allowlist and closes AUTH.md:202. *Why:* [owner decision 45](#od-45).

**D-TEAM-2 (proposed).** `admin_user_id` stays immutable under a synthetic owner-of-record. *Why:* the refusal cache stays sound.

**D-TEAM-3 (proposed).** Seven roles, signed in the config repo; unmapped routes are owner-only. *Why:* fails closed.

**D-TEAM-4 (proposed).** OIDC only, keyed `(idp_id, sub)` (7.6). *Why:* blocks IdP-asserted and pre-registration takeover.

**D-TEAM-5 (proposed).** Auth keys replace `urn_` keys for `ur connect --token`; a pre-approved key's Delegation secrets ride a client-only bundle (D-TEAM-22). *Why:* scoped, expiring, revocable.

**D-TEAM-6 (proposed).** OAuth clients mint ≤1 h auth keys; CI's Delegation admits their sidecars. *Why:* the server cannot admit.

**D-TEAM-7 (proposed).** `ur-cli` tokens last 1 h, need code-matched consent and bind by DPoP to one command, whose method, path and body their `cmd` claim covers; api spends the jti in the command's transaction. *Why:* agents can drive the browser.

**D-TEAM-8 (proposed).** The exchange trades a client JWT and ClientKey proof for a 15-min, one-audience token scoped from the projection and voided by `rev/`. *Why:* [owner decision 2](#od-2).

**D-TEAM-9 (proposed).** Tags, groups, device names and sponsors live in the config repo. *Why:* owner decisions [46](#od-46), [83](#od-83).

**D-TEAM-10 (proposed).** Removal denies at the server at once, and evs refuses writes until a generation covering it is claimed (7.10). *Why:* nothing removed reads new data.

**D-TEAM-11 (proposed).** Server audit `network_admin_event`: hash-chained, no IPs, 400 days, webhook. *Why:* the server executes admin actions.

**D-TEAM-12 (proposed).** 7.9's records freeze in v0 as §6 `Signed` statements; authority statements (the four config-signing roles and their devices) need `authority`: k of n, a recovery key counting as one under the recovery window and its veto (7.9). *Why:* owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [127](#od-127).

**D-TEAM-13 (proposed).** One rename function; create reads tombstones; deletion writes one. *Why:* closes three takeover paths.

**D-TEAM-14 (proposed).** Sidecar-held child and admin-refused tokens expire after 7 days under `strict_exp`, which one verifier enforces everywhere, and renew only with the ClientKey proof. *Why:* owner decisions [103](#od-103), [131](#od-131), with no app release.

**D-TEAM-15 (proposed).** Edge login issues members a 60 s, nonce-bound, one-origin ID token; its session counts only on same-origin requests or navigations (§13.7). *Why:* no open redirect, replay or cross-network forgery.

**D-TEAM-16 (proposed).** A member's consented devices admit its untagged devices unless `self_admit` is off, and revoke them whatever `self_admit` says; its recovery key admits them too, with one admin's cosign while `self_admit` is off; admins alone add no other reader to owner-bound repos (§8.5); tag owners and Delegations admit within scope. *Why:* owner decisions [5](#od-5), [63](#od-63), [112](#od-112), [126](#od-126).

**D-TEAM-17 (proposed).** One authorization log per network; positions rise, entries chain by hash and never fall, and HeadCheck compares (n, A_n), unwitnessed writers in shared groups stopping at `witness_bound_hours` and those in own groups only alarming. *Why:* the server can only withhold, visibly once a HeadCheck crosses the split ([owner decision 129](#od-129); §2.8).

**D-TEAM-18 (proposed).** The first 1,000 live member devices by `live_since` are the leaves of the config group and of the team directory's, promoted in rank order and never demoted while live; later ones and agents hold wraps; an admission's or revocation's signer commits it there, a wrapped one by wrap or rotation (7.9). *Why:* owner decisions [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182).

**D-TEAM-19 (proposed).** One linear, hash-chained authorization log per network orders bases and statements; its position n is the projection version and (n, A_n) the pin every consumer names; api's If-None-Match PUT of `proj/<network_id>/<n>/_` linearizes it, within per-network append limits; no base lowers its config head or fold point, and a config writer folds it every 1,024 entries or 24 h; after a site loss, member devices' verbatim entries resume it unchanged, each adopted once devices of two members hold it (7.9). *Why:* bases plus delta sequence numbers commit neither content nor order, so readers could agree on different states; a re-sequenced log would fork every reader, and one device's upload could pre-empt a position.

**D-TEAM-20 (proposed).** Every log statement carries a StatementHeader (network, the signer's AuthPin, nonce, not_after ≤ 7 d), refused when off-chain, more than 4,096 positions old or before the retention point, expired or repeated; type rules close the rest (7.9). *Why:* typed signed statements still need replay rules, which every reader, a new device included, must judge alike.

**D-TEAM-21 (proposed).** k-of-n and recovery-signed statements are an AuthorityProposal plus AuthorityCosigns, counted per distinct member; an authority statement with a recovery-key signature, in its proposal or a cosign, or a scoped admission by a binding a cascade restored, stays pending, delivering no key to the proposed device, until an api tick 72 h after its newest such signature's entry with no valid RecoveryVeto, and a veto kept off the log forks only devices that held it before the activation (7.9). *Why:* owner decisions [110](#od-110), [127](#od-127) and [149](#od-149) need a wire form, a clock and an activation path, a late recovery cosign must not skip the window, and a veto's `at` is its signer's claim.

**D-TEAM-22 (proposed).** A pre-approved auth key carries its Delegation's seeds only in a client-only `#<bundle>` split off before any request; enrollment has no field for it and api refuses an `auth_key` containing `#` (7.8). *Why:* the server must never receive admission authority or read keys.

**D-TEAM-23 (proposed).** JIT links an IdP identity to an existing user only after that user logs in with its existing credential in the same flow (7.6). *Why:* a verified-domain email alone would hand a pre-registered account to the IdP.

**D-TEAM-24 (proposed).** `SidecarAdmit.capabilities.read_only` limits a device to reading, its own sign-out, its own key upkeep (ReaderKeys, KeyPackages, its leaf's path-only commits, resyncs and acks, under the r scopes §10.6 maps), receipts and HeadCheck; it is never one of k, and never delivers a key. *Why:* a read-only browser must not carry its member's signing authority ([owner decision 76](#od-76)'s served code).

**D-TEAM-25 (proposed).** SCIM removals deny at once and are cryptographic only once an admin device, or the admin's indexer that `ServiceSettings.scim_signer` names ([owner decision 150](#od-150)), signs the MemberRevoke (7.6). *Why:* a server queue is not a removal.

**D-TEAM-26 (proposed).** `SidecarRevoke{reason: compromise, since_n}`, `since_n` a required position, parks the closure P of what the device signed in entries from `since_n` on, and is refused if P holds one of its signers: each sidecar whose admission it or a sidecar in P signed, whose park such a sidecar's AdmissionConfirm lifted, or whose consent rests only on such a sidecar's OwnerConfirm, a confirmation of a device already unparked and consented adding none, each sidecar a recovery key admitted under a binding one of them signed, and each admitted under a Delegation one of them signed, which is void, while the Delegation that admitted the revoked sidecar, if one did, ends at the revocation, each sidecar it admitted from `since_n` joining P (D-TEAM-30); their RecoveryBinds and Rebinds, KeyRegisters and EvsShares there are void, and a binding a void restores is no current binding: it takes no wrap or keychain seal, its member's devices re-sealing, and admits only through the vetoable 72 h window, a scoped admission as an AuthorityProposal with no counted cosign ([owner decision 149](#od-149)); each device that sealed keychain.wrap to a voided binding is listed, and revoked for compromise and enrolled anew if its backups may hold that sealing; only a signer outside P lifts a park or re-signs a voided record, and a consent resting on P's signatures returns only through the member's consented device outside P; grants, approvals and config heads signed in P stand until revoked, listed for admins (7.9); after a compromise rebind at r, a revocation's proposed since_n is clamped to r + 1 for the rebind's signer, which goes last, revoked by the replacement it enrolls, and for any device whose closure would reach it ([owner decision 212](#od-212)); signed by a sidecar that registered a live presence key, it carries that key's countersignature (D-TEAM-32; [owner decision 185](#od-185)). *Why:* a stolen device's admissions, and what those admit, bind or register, must not survive it; an entry position, unlike a signer's `at`, cannot be backdated; a revocation must neither freeze its own signer nor hand back a retired code, nor may a stolen device's redundant confirmations pull the devices that would revoke it into P; and a voided code must open no keychain.

**D-TEAM-27 (proposed).** A network designates its indexers (§3.6) by `IndexerSet` statements in the config repo (7.9): an Owner or Admin at network scope, a member's consented device at member scope for that member's own devices, and the subject itself to retire either; a designation names services, grants no key, grant or read, and decides only who runs a service first, so each service keeps a fallback when none is designated. A network starts with none ([owner decision 177](#od-177)). For search, a designation also bounds which devices a phone asks, so a query reaches only designated devices (owner decisions [175](#od-175), [178](#od-178)). *Why:* owner decisions [150](#od-150) and [177](#od-177); [owner decision 126](#od-126) leaves members' own repos to their own devices, and a duty must never widen reach.

**D-TEAM-28 (proposed).** `team-create`'s first Owner device files the directory's `RepoCreate` after the config's first base. `ServiceSettings.directory`, signed by an Owner or Admin, holds the team's defaults: for runs (auto unless set) and for workers (on). *Why:* owner decisions [170](#od-170) and [171](#od-171); one record holds a network's defaults (7.9).

**D-TEAM-29 (proposed).** Whichever device admits a member's page Worker, an admin's where `self_admit` is off included, signs in that act, under its one presence check where 7.9's presence row asks ([owner decision 187](#od-187)), `SidecarRevoke{reason: removed}` for each of the member's page Workers that §10.9 removed as stale from every group it is a leaf of that seated it, at least one, and that holds a leaf in none of them, checking again before each post or retry, and for an AdminSet member at k > 1 as proposals of their own beside the admission's, which its cosigners also cosign; in its admission act an admin's device revokes or lists no other device of the member, while the member's consented device revokes the stale Workers its own groups show and offers to revoke the rest, in its own admission act or, after an admin's, at its `OwnerConfirm` or admission-alarm answer (7.10's `stale` row); from 90% of `config_admissions` every admin device lists each member's page Workers but its newest for an admin to revoke (7.10's `cleanup` row). *Why:* with `self_admit` off no member device admits, so a weekly re-enroller's evicted Workers would pile up toward Team's 5,000 `config_admissions` (§20.4); a stale-removed Worker has had no leaf change for 90 days and holds no leaf in that group, an admin's device sees the member's owner-bound groups only through the member's own share, and revoking a live device in an admission act stays the member's choice ([owner decision 126](#od-126)); and a member with no device that answers, such as one with only page Workers, would reach the cap unseen, while an admin may revoke a member's device ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), so admins see the pile and free it first.

**D-TEAM-30 (proposed).** A Delegation other than a forwarding one (D-TEAM-33) admits only sidecars carrying exactly its tag_ids and, unless ephemeral, a `not_after` no earlier than its own, up to `max_admits`, which rows count for its life; it ends at its `DelegationRevoke`, its void or a compromise revocation of a sidecar it admitted, after which api and every reader refuse an admission its key signs; a `DelegationRevoke` with `since_n`, and that compromise revocation, park the sidecars it admitted from `since_n` on as the cascade parks, the rest reading on as uncovered agents; a `Suspend`, or a lost or removed revocation, of one of its agents drops only its key (7.9's delegation row, §10.5). *Why:* a covered agent must read exactly what its Delegation's key opens; every copy of a reusable auth key holds the signing seed, which an honest daemon's erasure cannot reach and a colluding operator's fresh client cannot stop, so a leak needs a customer-signed end with a positional park; ending admissions at every key drop would stop a CI pipeline's enrollments at one agent's removal.

**D-TEAM-31 (proposed).** A tagged sidecar's revocation or `Suspend` shows a plan that names the agent, its Delegation's shared reader key and that Delegation's admission authority apart, with the agents and repos each reaches; `--compromise` ends the Delegation, any other act offers `ur admin delegations revoke`, and revoking an auth key at api alone says that a copy of its bundle still admits (7.10's agents row). *Why:* the three are separate capabilities, a person stopping a leaked key must see which one each act ends, and only the customer-signed end stops a copied bundle.

**D-TEAM-32 (proposed).** A `SidecarRevoke{reason: compromise}`, a presence key's `KeyRegister` or `KeyRevoke`, any other `SidecarRevoke` or `Suspend` of another sidecar, a `DelegationRevoke` with `since_n` > 0 and a `RecoveryVeto`, a `SidecarAdmit`, `AdmissionConfirm` or `OwnerConfirm` of an untagged sidecar, an AdminSet change, a `MemberRevoke`, a `RecoveryBind` or `RecoveryRebind`, and an `AuthorityProposal` carrying one or an `AuthorityCosign` of it, signed by a sidecar that registered a live presence key, carry that key's countersignature in §6.9's `Signed.webauthn`, which api, evs, gkm and every member device verify, each statement alone by its inclusion path to the act's Merkle root, UV required; a sidecar with none signs on its person's confirmation (D-CORE-13) (7.9's presence row). *Why:* owner decisions [185](#od-185) and [187](#od-187): a presence check that only the signing device ran was skipped by modified software on a stolen unlocked device, which could then lock the member out; one prompt must still cover an act of several statements that land separately; without the `KeyRegister` rule a thief would register a key of its own to countersign with; without the `DelegationRevoke` rule a compromised device would park other devices with no presence check ([owner decision 192](#od-192)); and without the admission, confirmation and binding rules a thief would admit a device with no key, or rebind the member's recovery code, and act from there ([owner decision 189](#od-189)).

**D-TEAM-33 (proposed).** A sidecar authorizes its app's forwarding by a forwarding Delegation that it alone signs, naming the keys its VPN component generated: it admits nothing, its key signs only that sidecar's `WindowDelegation`s, its reader key reads the config alone, a newer one supersedes it, and it has no `not_after`, ending only at its `DelegationRevoke`, its sidecar's revocation or its void (7.9's forwarding row; §18.6). *Why:* [owner decision 197](#od-197)'s self-contained forwarding, on the Delegation's existing signer path, rows, reader wraps, revocation and cascade, without a second sidecar per device or an expiry that would wait on the app.

### 7.15 Open questions

**Q-TEAM-1.** How far does the P0 go? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 45](#od-45)):** three stages, the last a hard gate (7.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-2.** Convert personal networks? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 55](#od-55)):** (a) no; new team networks only. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-3.** Is SCIM in Team v1? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 56](#od-56)):** (a) yes. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-4.** OIDC or SAML? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 46](#od-46)):** (a) OIDC; SAML-only customers broker through an OIDC IdP. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-5.** Is the key authority opt-in? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [45](#od-45)):** no; enforced from v0, member-signed admission subsumed. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-6.** How many signatures admit? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 110](#od-110)):** (a) one; AdminSet and authority-key changes need k of n. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-7.** Cross-cutting (§2). Does the server hold the member directory? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 46](#od-46)):** only users, emails and roles (§2.8 api-3). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-8.** Do a departing member's tagged agents leave? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 83](#od-83)):** (b) no; they keep their tags' grants under `SponsorSet` (7.10). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-9.** How long is a released name held? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 83](#od-83)):** (a) 24 h. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-10.** Cross-cutting (§5.6, §10.4). May a member's own device alone admit that member's new device? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 112](#od-112)):** (a) yes, as a scoped statement unless `self_admit` is off; an AdminSet member's new device still needs k of n, its existing device counting as one. It subsumes §10's DeviceAdmit; the signer commits the config group's Add or, if wrapped, a first wrap (owner decisions [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEAM-11.** Cross-cutting (§5.9, §10.8). May a recovery key sign an authority statement? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 127](#od-127)):** (b) as one signature toward k, after a 72 h window any admin device may veto. Teams with k > 1 still need other signers ([owner decision 110](#od-110)); a personal network (k = 1) recovers alone after the window. *Residual:* §2.10's row for an operator colluding with a recovery-code thief: the window bounds admission, not reads, so the code opens its recovery wraps at once, and after a rebind or a cascade void stops new wraps keeps opening what was wrapped to it and reads the current generation until the next rotation, which `--compromise` makes a remove rotation with a path epoch at once; keychain backups sealed to a code before its rebind or void stay open to it (7.9).

### 7.16 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:119**, met in part (§8.16): stored rules are signed and encrypted, and every device reads the whole config (owner decisions [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6), [72](#od-72)).
- **PLAN.md:147** ("participants are leaves"): member devices are leaves; agents, and member devices past the first 1,000 of the config group and the team directory's, hold wraps there (Q-ACL-9, Q-KEYS-15, Q-KEYS-16; owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)).

### 7.18 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A missed `admin_user_id` read lets a member act as owner | Medium | High | classify the 133 reads; fail closed |
| A reusable auth key leaks: its reader seed reads later generations, past reaps, until its Delegation's key drops, and its signing seed admits fresh agents, which read by their own wraps, until the Delegation ends | Medium | High | expiry, uses, `max_admits`, which rows count for the Delegation's life; `not_after` ≤ 90 d, 30 d for CI; a `Suspend` or any non-reap revocation of one of its agents drops the key (§10.5); `DelegationRevoke`, whose `since_n` parks a leak's admissions, or a compromise revocation of one of its agents ends the Delegation; the revoke plan names the agent, the key and the admission authority apart (7.10) |
| A `Suspend`, or a lost or removed revocation, of one CI agent drops its Delegation's shared key, so the Delegation's later agents read only once a holder wraps to them | Medium | Low | the plan lists the agents and repos the drop reaches; the console replaces the Delegation as at a CI secret rotation (§10.5) |
| An agent drives `ur-cli` through the user's browser | Medium | High | consent code, `auth_time`, DPoP |
| Strict expiry strands an offline sidecar | Medium | Medium | early refresh; re-enrollment keeps the `sidecar_id` |
| A team loses its admin keys | Medium | High | k of n; recovery keys ([owner decision 127](#od-127)) |
| n ≤ 2 forces k = 1: either admin alone can remove the other or change the AdminSet | Medium | High | the console recommends n ≥ 3; AdminSet notices (7.8) |
| An admin's leaked recovery code signs authority statements, alone at k = 1 | Low | Critical | the 72 h window from the newest recovery signature, a late cosign included, on every member device; any admin device vetoes; a `RecoveryRebind` of the code's member voids every pending proposal the code signed or cosigned; a server hiding that signature from every admin device defeats the veto, detected on first sight |
| A stolen recovery code admits a device under a non-admin member at once | Low | High | the member's devices alarm ([owner decision 126](#od-126)); `RecoveryRebind` |
| A compromised AdminSet device gossips a veto backdated before a recovery activation | Low | Medium | devices that applied the activation only alarm; those still before it fork until the log reverses it, by a compromise revocation of the recovered device, whose member then recovers again; admins revoke the vetoing device (7.9) |
| An admin admits a device as a new member's first, consented under §8.5 or JIT | Low | High | the member's real device, parked, alarms; admins re-invite the member |
| SCIM deprovisioning waits for an admin's signature | Medium | Medium | server denial at once; the console's unsigned-removal list; `scim_signer` on an admin's indexer |
| No admin device online to sign a member's revocation, or no admitting device online after a reap | Medium | Medium | server denial; own-device revocations commit at once ([owner decision 128](#od-128)); the gate refuses writes (412) |
| A designated indexer stays offline, so its services wait on their fallbacks, and a Team's mail on sender retries | Medium | Medium | per-service fallbacks (§3.6); two mail indexers (§15.6); `ur status` lists each indexer's services and newest sign of life |
| An admin designates its own device as a network-scope search indexer to collect members' queries | Low | High | no designation by default ([owner decision 177](#od-177)); own indexers first, and other members' owner-bound repos never reach it ([owner decision 126](#od-126)); the app names the answering member before the first query and again when it changes; a per-device `own` or `off` mode (§18.4); designations are signed and listed in every config and `ur indexer ls`; one other member's device at a time (§11.14) |
| After a site loss, one compromised member device pre-empts log positions with a forged TICK (any time_ms), a reordered statement or one it signs, forking every longer tail, or a device's longer tail goes unuploaded | Low | High | uploads only from member devices in reseed mode, matched to the restored `network_acl_head`; api adopts an entry only once devices of two members hold its digest, and checks the newest adopted base against the re-seeded config repo; a forged activation raises `recovery_unseen`; a device whose tail passes the stop sees a FORK and keeps the evidence (7.9) |
| A compromised device spends its network's daily append limit, delaying admissions and approvals | Low | Medium | revocations, Suspend and vetoes are exempt, so admins revoke it at once; 429s carry `retry_after_ms`, and the day's budget refills within 24 h (7.9) |
| A thief holding a member's unlocked device that registered no presence key, or who knows its passcode or its security key's PIN, signs what 7.9's presence row covers on a confirmation alone | Low | High | `ur login` and the apps offer a platform presence key ([owner decision 142](#od-142)), after which every such statement needs its countersignature (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187), [189](#od-189)); every member device sees each revocation and offers to revoke its signer; disclosed (§2.10) |
| A device's only presence key, a security key, is lost, so the device signs nothing 7.9's presence row covers, a new key's `KeyRegister` included, until another device of its member revokes that key or its `not_after` passes | Low | Medium | `ur keys rm` from another of the member's devices, countersigned by that device's own presence key, which a device with none first registers (§16.6's register and remove rows); a second key registered while the first works; a member with no other device admits one by its recovery code (§5.9), since the lost key also blocks this device's admissions ([owner decision 189](#od-189)) |
| A member whose devices are all page Workers, which §8.5 never consents, or one that never answers its alarms after an admin's device admits its Worker (always so with `self_admit` off), keeps each Worker that no group of the admitting device seated, one admission per eviction toward `config_admissions` (7.10's `stale` row; §20.4) | Low | Medium | admins' devices revoke every Worker they saw stale-removed (D-TEAM-29); the member's next `OwnerConfirm` or alarm answer frees the rest; from 90% of the cap every admin device lists each member's page Workers but its newest for an admin to revoke (7.10's `cleanup` row), so none waits for the cap's refusal; FS-97 |

### 7.19 Phasing

- **P0, before any sidecar:** stage 1 (D-TEAM-1, with 7.4's allowlist and auth-code fix), D-TEAM-14 and its proof.
- **v0, personal networks (§23 M1-M2):** auth keys and their bundles, enrollment, token exchange, `rev/` objects, key sets, `ur-cli`'s auth-key scope, ephemeral reaping with its lease and close capability (MG1), API-key scopes, rename unification; the enforced config repo (M2; owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5)): the authorization log with its read cache, append limits, fold cadence and site-loss resumption, k-of-n verifier and proposals, the presence countersignature rule (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187)), recovery window, consent rule, read-only admissions, compromise cascade, Delegation ends and their parks (7.9's delegation row) with the CLI's agent and Delegation revoke plans (7.10's agents row), committers and recovery path, and `IndexerSet` ([owner decision 150](#od-150)), tested though personal networks have n = 1; config.proto reserves `ServiceSettings.directory` (D-TEAM-28).
- **With §13's v0:** edge login.
- **v0, app hosts (§23 M8; [owner decision 197](#od-197)):** the forwarding Delegation and the `forward_only` mark with its exchange rule, the Delegation's `forward` fields reserved in config.proto at M2 with 7.9's records.
- **v1, Team (M6):** members, roles, invitations, switching, OIDC, domains, JIT, SCIM and `scim_signer`, OAuth clients, full `ur-cli` admin, audit log, multi-admin teams, and config wraps for member devices past the first 1,000 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)); the team directory, created with the team, its group under 7.9's leaves rule, and `ServiceSettings.directory` (owner decisions [170](#od-170), [171](#od-171), [182](#od-182)).
- **v1, every network (§23's M10, with storage format 2; [owner decision 169](#od-169)):** `VersioningRules` (§11.7), its type reserved at M2 with 7.9's records, and `IndexerSet`'s `search` service, which includes answering remote searches (§11.14; owner decisions [157](#od-157), [163](#od-163), [164](#od-164), [175](#od-175), [178](#od-178)).
- **On app migration:** stage 3 (7.4).
- **Blocking:** the `admin_user_id` audit blocks members; stage 1 and D-TEAM-14 block the first sidecar, stage 2 the first desktop sidecar; token exchange and `rev/` block evs (§11); the config repo needs §10 and §11 and blocks §8's gates, and its records and log freeze at M2 (§23.8).

## 8. Access control: policy, compilation, distribution, enforcement

### 8.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns the access-control model and its evaluation; X3, the customer key authority (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5)-[8](#od-8), [110](#od-110), [126](#od-126)); policy rows in the signed projection, grant chains and repo access logs; gate caches; enforcement points; and evs readers, with data repos' leaf seats (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)). §7 owns the config repo's records, the authorization log and its read cache, the config and directory groups' `leaves` rule, members, roles, tokens and removal; §10 MLS; §11 repo kinds and drops; §16.11 the team directory; §17 bridge rules.

### 8.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-ACL-1 | Specify which clients, groups and networks reach a client, group, network or abstract socket | PLAN.md:74 |
| R-ACL-2 | Rules stored on the server; each client gets its rules in real time and decides locally | PLAN.md:119 |
| R-ACL-3 | One deny-by-default HuJSON policy with tags, groups, autogroups and tests; default `tag:recurd` → `autogroup:self` tcp:443 | team-management.html:813-929 |
| R-ACL-4 | Every reach grant names an approver and an expiry; one switch revokes an agent's forwards, addresses, names and mail | pitch5.html:680,729 |
| R-ACL-5 | With a policy, agents reach only granted ranges; public names authenticated by default, short-lived | pitch5.html:689,698; [owner decision 120](#od-120) |
| R-ACL-6 | Invite an external network to forward in; accept an invite | cli/UI.md:50-51 |
| R-ACL-7 | A breached server cannot add a reader | pitch5.html:745; team-management.html:940 |
| R-ACL-8 | No added query for networks without the feature; no PostgreSQL per packet | server/model/subscription_model.go:1727-1730; connect/CODESTYLE.md:106-107 |
| R-ACL-9 | The ACL decides evs readers, which clients verify; app devices, and untagged sidecars until a policy exists, keep today's reach | derived; owner decisions [105](#od-105), [120](#od-120) |
| R-ACL-10 | Tests, change audit, rollback, propagation target | team-management.html:907-929,1021-1029 |
| R-ACL-11 | Session contents stay with their author unless shared, while in a team network a run's who, what and where reach teammates by default; admins read actions, not transcripts | pitch5.html:579,640; owner decisions [126](#od-126), [170](#od-170) |
| R-ACL-12 | Admin keys sign policy from v0; a breached server can only deny or delay (§2.8's bound), and sees policy only as ids | owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [72](#od-72) |

### 8.3 What exists today

- No group, tag or policy table exists [R:server-identity](design/design-research/server-identity.md).
- `GetProvideRelationshipDetails` returns Network iff both clients share a `network_id`, else Public, in one query (`server/model/network_client_model.go:2528-2606`). `CreateContract` resolves it at `server/controller/connect_controller.go:859`, picks the mode at `:933`, and settles same-network companion (reply-direction) requests as Network without an origin check (`:917-927`).
- FriendsAndFamily (`connect/protocol/transfer.proto:357`) escrows nothing (`connect_controller.go:1296`) and is never computed.
- Providers allow Network sources every destination, LAN and loopback included (`connect/ip_security.go:567`); other modes get public-only rules (`:385-390`).
- Contracts expire within 60 min (`server/model/subscription_contract_expiration.go:14`), and the contract-hole projection, a Redis pair lease, gates forwarding (`connect/CODESTYLE.md:107-110`).

### 8.4 Model

**Subjects** are sidecars (`sidecar_id`, mapped to the current client through §5's binding) and other clients (`client_id`: app devices, legacy clients); untagged children such as sdk window clients act as their nearest subject ancestor (D-ACL-3), so a sidecar's forwarding client and its window clients act as that sidecar, their tokens confined by `forward_only` (§7.4, §18.6; [owner decision 197](#od-197)). Before expansion each is classed as a member device (untagged, not ephemeral), an ephemeral sidecar, a tagged sidecar or another client (D-ACL-19). An untagged subject's atoms are its owner's user, groups and role, and its autogroups; an ephemeral subject's evs access is capped as 8.6 says; a tagged subject has no user atoms, and its §7 *sponsor* stands in: the admitting member or the one an admin's `SponsorSet` names, else `autogroup:admin` once that sponsor is removed ([owner decision 83](#od-83)). In-daemon agents share their sidecar's grants, which the daemon may narrow ([owner decision 4](#od-4), §5.5).

```text
selector (src or dst unless noted)   meaning
user:<email>, group:<name>           untagged subjects
tag:<name>                           via tagOwners
sidecar:<id>                         across client generations
client:<id>                          resolved through §5's binding
role:, principal:                    Embed networks
autogroup:member|owner|admin|auditor|sidecar|tagged|network
autogroup:untagged                   untagged non-sidecars; untagged sidecars are in autogroup:member
autogroup:ephemeral                  src: untagged ephemeral sidecars
network:<net>                        as that network permits (§8.11)
autogroup:public                     src: anonymous tlsedge clients
autogroup:internet                   dst: public destinations via an exit
autogroup:self                       dst: subjects sharing the source's owner or sponsor; approver: the requester's
autogroup:sponsor                    approver
autogroup:dst-owner                  approver: the destination subject's owner, or a tagged sidecar's sponsor; for a
                                     socket, its listeners' owner or sponsor where all are one; otherwise
                                     autogroup:admin (owner decision 180); acl.proto fixes its atom at M2, when the
                                     implicit document names it (8.5); Team documents name it from M6

resource                             actions; notes (* matches within a label or segment, a bare * all of a kind)
a subject, optional ip ports         dial; its addresses too (§17)
sock:<name>                          dial, listen; this network's sockets only (others reach a listener by IP, §8.11);
                                     rows carry application names as §9.4's token paths under K_sock
                                     (owner decision 67), tls/ and smtp/ names in clear; services authorize ur/ names
ip:<cidr>, ports, via subjects       route; 0.0.0.0/0 excludes loopback and link-local
evs:<repo>                           read, write (implies read), admin (lifecycle, drops), deposit; an id or config
                                     label, never a path (X2)
dns:<host>, sock, audience,          publish, admin (zone records); <host> is @, one label or, in a v1 Team
  app_mode, link_spki_sha256         scope, <host>.<scope> (dns:*.<scope> covers one scope; Q-TLS-3); audience:
                                     members (default), members-device, link or public (owner decision 42);
                                     app_mode: http (default), or raw only under public or link, a raw link's
                                     grant pinning its client certificate's SPKI SHA-256 (§13.7)
mail:<alias>                         send, listen; checked only by clients
* (as a dst)                         any subject, application socket, ip range (exits included) or general or
                                     record repo here; outward resources (tls/ and smtp/ sockets, dns:, mail:,
                                     other networks) and §8.5's kinds must be named
```

### 8.5 Policy document and worked examples

The policy is HuJSON in the config repo, parsed by `github.com/tailscale/hujson` (BSD-3-Clause, untagged) or in-repo (§4 decides). Beyond the example it has `hosts`; grant fields `id`, `via`, `sock`, `audience`, `app_mode`, `link_spki_sha256` (8.4) and `note`; an `approvers` count on `requests`, which subjects, a harness `reach:` block (recurd-app.html:1743-1749) or a team directory request (§16.11) file; and document-level `expiresDefault` (1 h) and `evidenceDefault` (all §16.6 channels; harness only in untainted runs unless a rule names it, [owner decision 142](#od-142), §16.6).

```hujson
{
  "groups":    { "group:eng": ["dana@acme.com", "amir@acme.com"] },
  "tagOwners": { "tag:recurd": ["group:eng"], "tag:db": ["autogroup:admin"],
                 "tag:api": ["autogroup:admin"], "tag:audit": ["autogroup:admin"] },
  "grants": [
    { "src": ["autogroup:untagged"], "dst": ["autogroup:self"], "allow": ["dial", "route"] }, // 1 laptop→phone
    { "src": ["tag:recurd"], "dst": ["evs:repo-x"], "allow": ["write"] },                     // 2
    { "src": ["group:eng"], "dst": ["sock:db"], "allow": ["dial"] },                          // 3
    { "src": ["tag:db"],    "dst": ["sock:db"], "allow": ["listen"] },
    { "src": ["network:partner-y"], "dst": ["tag:api"], "allow": ["dial"], "ip": ["tcp:443"], // 4 share over §17's
      "expires": "2026-12-31T00:00:00Z" },                                                  // IP path (owner decision 86)
    { "src": ["tag:recurd"], "dst": ["autogroup:self"], "allow": ["dial"], "ip": ["tcp:443"] },
  ],
  "requests": [ // 5: ur bridge public-tls app-preview:3000 publishes app-preview.<net>.<root> for up to
                //    24 h, approved from a device or presence key, never a harness prompt
    { "src": ["tag:recurd"], "dst": ["dns:*-preview", "sock:tls/443/*-preview"], "allow": ["publish", "listen"],
      "approver": ["autogroup:sponsor"], "maxExpiry": "24h", "evidence": ["device", "presence"] },
  ],
  "audit": { "reader": "tag:audit", "repos": ["kind:team_record", "kind:vault", "kind:mailbox"] }, // 6 Team
  "tests": [ { "src": "dana@acme.com", "accept": ["sock:db#dial"], "deny": ["evs:secrets#read"] } ],
}
```

**Kind defaults** compile ahead of every document; `*` never matches these kinds, which §11.12 fixes at creation, and documents may add readers only to the last two:

| kind | read (and write where noted) | deposit |
|---|---|---|
| `config` (§7.9) | every admitted sidecar; heads from config writers (§8.8) | — |
| `directory` (one per team network, §16.11; [owner decision 171](#od-171)) | every admitted sidecar of the team; every one that is not read_only writes only its own paths and stream, and a device KF2 parks for consent writes nothing that counts (I-EVS-14); documents neither add nor remove readers (D-ACL-24) | — |
| `vault`, `mailbox`, `secret` (owner-bound to member M; group inboxes stay general; each `secret` holds one secret, such as §13.8's ACME account key or §17.9's ShareKey, and §16.6 refuses `secret` repos to MCP's evs tools) | M's consented devices (below), which also write; their `EvsShare`s' subjects (§8.8); the `audit` reader where its block names the kind or repo | receipts from readers that do not write (§16.8); in `vault` and `mailbox` also M's other untagged subjects, the tagged subjects M sponsors, `tag:mail` mail indexers ([owner decision 150](#od-150)) |
| Team record | `autogroup:admin`, `:auditor` | `autogroup:member`, tagged subjects |
| `mailcfg` | `tag:mail` mail indexers; members write the records they sign (§15.8) | — |

**Owner consent ([owner decision 126](#od-126)).** One admin's signature admits a device under member M ([owner decision 110](#od-110)), but in M's owner-bound repos admins only revoke or add the audit reader. One predicate, which §5.6 and §7.9 cite, names M's consented devices (D-ACL-22):

```text
consented(d, M) = d's admission names member M, d is neither ephemeral nor parked by §7.9's compromise
  cascade, and one of these holds on a signature by neither a sidecar then in that cascade's set P nor a
  recovery key whose binding one signed:
  scoped     M's consented device or M's recovery key signed d's SidecarAdmit, alone or as one of k
             (§7.9, owner decision 112)
  invited    d is the first device admitted under M that is neither ephemeral nor read_only, enrolled from
             an invite addressed to M: §7.5's member invite, or the invite an admin device issues when it
             admits a JIT-pending member (§7.6), neither of which an ephemeral enrollment redeems
  genesis    d signed the network's Genesis (the owner's first device)
  confirmed  M's consented device signed OwnerConfirm{d} (§8.8), as after an admin's admission, or the
             AdmissionConfirm{d} that lifted d's park (§7.9)
```

Members and grantor leaves refuse other Adds and wraps there, and KF2 parks d (§10.7, §10.9). A device whose consent rested on what P signed regains M's owner-bound repos only by an `OwnerConfirm` or `AdmissionConfirm` from M's consented device outside P; an admin's `AdmissionConfirm` restores only its other access (§7.9). M's devices alarm on any admission under M that M's keys did not sign and offer to confirm it (`approval_pending`; §5.4, §18.5). Only consented devices that are not read-only (§7.9) sign M's `EvsShare`s, `OwnerConfirm`s, `RecoveryBind`s, owner-bound `RepoAdmin` adds, and DROP pushes and their cancels in M's owner-bound repos (§11.7), so admins neither drop nor cancel drops there (owner decisions [173](#od-173), [183](#od-183)).

**Audit reader ([owner decision 63](#od-63); Team, v1).** Example 6's `audit` block counts only while a k-of-n `AuditOptIn` (§8.8) exists, and members see that reader in each affected reader list before it gets a key (§10.8).

The **implicit document**, versioned in the sidecar repo, serves Community and Pro networks without one; writers compile it into the projection's rules whenever `has_document` is false, so gates and clients evaluate the same rows (D-ACL-20). Team starts from grant 1, the `tag:recurd` default and the implicit document's last rule, the team directory's reach requests (D-ACL-23), which its document may narrow, give two approvers or remove ([owner decision 74](#od-74)); the implicit document carries that rule from its M2 version, so readers of every version compile the same rows.

```hujson
{ "grants": [  // owner decision 105: untagged sidecars (autogroup:member) and app devices
               // (autogroup:untagged) keep today's reach, and providers keep allow-all LAN and
               // loopback, disclosed (owner decisions 50, 120)
    { "src": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:untagged"], "dst": ["*"], "allow": ["*"] },
    { "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["evs:*"], "allow": ["write", "admin"] },
    { "src": ["autogroup:tagged"], "dst": ["evs:*"], "allow": ["deposit"] },
    { "src": ["autogroup:tagged"], "dst": ["autogroup:self"], "allow": ["dial"], "ip": ["tcp:443"] } ],
  "requests": [
    { "src": ["autogroup:network"], "dst": ["dns:*", "sock:tls/*", "sock:smtp/*"], "allow": ["publish", "listen"],
      "approver": ["autogroup:admin"], "maxExpiry": "7d" },                             // §13.9
    { "src": ["autogroup:tagged"], "dst": ["*", "sock:*", "evs:*", "mail:*"],
      "allow": ["dial", "route", "listen", "read", "write", "send"],
      "approver": ["autogroup:self"], "maxExpiry": "30d" },                             // owner decision 74
    { "src": ["network:*"], "dst": ["*"], "allow": ["dial", "route"],
      "approver": ["autogroup:admin"], "maxExpiry": "30d" },                            // shares (§8.11)
    { "src": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:tagged"],                                  // the team directory's
      "dst": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:tagged", "sock:*"], "allow": ["dial"],     // reach requests
      "approver": ["autogroup:dst-owner"], "evidence": ["device", "presence"],          // (§16.11; owner
      "maxExpiry": "30d" } ] }                                                          // decisions 179, 180)
```

An ephemeral sidecar's evs access takes 8.6's ceiling: the config's and its team directory's read, the directory's own-path writes, kind-default deposits, and grants and EvsShares that name it. Standing publishes need a Pro or Team document; §13.9 caps the rest, and §21.7's probation is a hard deny.

### 8.6 Evaluation semantics

```text
allowed(s, a, r, t) = not hardDeny(s, a, r, t)
                      and exists g in rows(t): s in src(g), r in dst(g), a in allow(g), ports match,
                      ceiling(s, r, g)
rows(t)          = the state's AclRows: the network's document, or the implicit document when it has none
                   (has_document = false), compiled into the same rows; kind defaults, the audit block,
                   standing grants, activated requests, access-log RepoGrants and EvsShares, unexpired at t,
                   not revoked by a GrantRevoke or RepoRevoke, and no EvsShare that §7.9's cascade voids
ceiling(s, r, g) = true unless s is ephemeral and r is an evs: resource; then g names s (sidecar:<id>,
                   client:<id>, autogroup:ephemeral, or a tag s carries), is a kind default's deposit row,
                   the config kind default's read row or the directory kind default's read and own-path
                   writes, or is an EvsShare to s; so every ephemeral sidecar that hardDeny spares, never a
                   parked one, reads the config (owner decision 6) and its team's directory, and none
                   writes a config head
ports match      = for a rule with ip CIDRs or ports, each reader's check against the policy it compiles from
                   the sealed source (AclLocalPolicy); rows carry only whether a rule limits ports
                   (ports_limited, 8.8), so api and the gates check ids, and readers check a requested grant's
                   prefix against its rule
hardDeny         = unadmitted, revoked or parked sidecar (§7.9; parked by its compromise cascade or by a
                   leaked bundle's DelegationRevoke, unlike KF2's consent park) | unapproved client (§7) |
                   suspended subject | abuse halt (§21) | quota (§20)
```

- **Base.** Grants form a union over a deny base, without precedence, as in Tailscale (https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/syntax/grants); hard denies win, and no deny grants exist.
- **Direction.** The src initiates; replies are implied. Deposit implies no read, subscription, key or place in `RepoReaders`. Publish requires listen on the bound socket. Gates use server time and clients allow ±60 s of skew, so a daemon reserves a server-gated use only until 60 s before its `not_after` (§16.6).
- **Requests (owner decisions [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75), [142](#od-142), [180](#od-180)).** A requested grant matches a `requests` rule and lasts its `expires`, else `expiresDefault` (1 h), up to `maxExpiry` (30 days by default; publishes follow §13.9). The rule's approvers approve, by default the requester's owner or sponsor; an admin does for grants touching other members, shares or `autogroup:public`, whatever the rule says, except that a touched member who approves as `autogroup:dst-owner` meets it for reach to a device that member owns or sponsors ([owner decision 180](#od-180), amending [owner decision 74](#od-74) for this case); two do where a Team rule's `approvers` asks. Approvals are §16.8 `ApprovalDecision`s on channels the rule's `evidence` lists, harness evidence in a tainted run only where the rule itself names it, checked by clients, `harness_ok` and api; they activate the grant as a §7.9 delta (§8.8), whose `grant_id` the approval fixes, so a replay is refused.
- **One switch.** A `Suspend` (§8.8's signers) removes a subject's atoms and activations across client generations; contracts, sockets, names, aliases, bridge rules and evs (§8.12) then refuse it, as for §21's halts, and for an agent a live Delegation admitted it also drops that Delegation's shared reader key at its position, so the next generation reaches the Delegation's other agents only by their own wraps and never the suspended one, which an `Unsuspend` returns uncovered (§10.5). Suspensions, revocations and cascade parks close open contracts, whose forwarding stops within 5 s; contracts a narrowed rule no longer allows lapse within 60 min (§8.3).

### 8.7 Policy authority (X3)

Owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5) and [6](#od-6) settle X3 (§7.9, Q-ACL-1): config writers sign the policy, every admitted sidecar evaluates it, and gates enforce its id-only projection (§8.8-§8.10). A breached server can only withhold or delay, visibly once a HeadCheck crosses the split (I-16), within §2.8's exposure bound ([owner decision 129](#od-129)). It sees the reach graph and keyed ids, never member-chosen names, rule text or tests ([owner decision 72](#od-72); §2.8 api-7).

### 8.8 The policy in the config repo: rows, grant chains, saving

**Placement.** The policy source, repo labels and `K_sock` are config repo files that only config writers' heads change ([owner decision 5](#od-5)). Server gates know policy only as `AclRows`, §8's part of §7.9's ProjectionRows, which the writer compiles at each base and readers recompile, alarming on a mismatch:

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/acl.proto: §8's rows inside §7.9's ProjectionRows. Ids only.
message AclRows {
  bool has_document = 1;                  // owner decisions 50, 105
  repeated AclAtom atoms = 2;             // §7.9's keyed tag and group ids -> member_ids, sidecar_ids
  repeated AclRule rules = 3;             // rule_id, src atoms, targets, actions, expires; a
                                          // publish's audience, app_mode and link_spki_sha256 (8.4), the
                                          // pin in full, as a requested grant's GrantActivate shows it to
                                          // api anyway (§16.6 AD4); ports (5) reserved: bool
                                          // ports_limited = 11 says the rule has an ip port list, never
                                          // which, for 8.10's legacy rule; a route rule's targets are its
                                          // via subjects, or with no via the advertisers that
                                          // BridgeRoute.route_rule_ids names (§17.8); CIDRs and ports stay
                                          // in each reader's AclLocalPolicy (8.6)
  repeated AclRequestRule requests = 4;
  repeated AclRepo repos = 5;             // repo_id, kind, owner_member_id and the owner's consented
                                          // sidecar_ids (§8.5), whose consenting admission, AdmissionConfirm
                                          // and OwnerConfirm signers and positions §7.9's SidecarRow keeps;
                                          // its access log folded: repo admins, RepoGrants and EvsShares
                                          // with their expires, each with its signer sidecar_id and its
                                          // carrying entry's log position (§7.9's cascade), config writers'
                                          // standing RepoRevokes, the newest RepoDelete with any RepoRestore
                                          // of its deletion_id; the newest RepoVersioning's lock (folded from
                                          // M2, enforced from format 2); holders_shrunk_at: the newest log
                                          // position that dropped a key holder (§7.9)
  bytes bridge = 6;                       // §17's id-only section
  AclAudit audit = 7;                     // owner decision 63; Team only
}
message AclRequestRule {
  bytes rule_id = 1; repeated bytes src_atoms = 2; repeated AclTarget targets = 3;
  repeated uint32 actions = 4; repeated bytes approver_atoms = 5; uint32 approvers = 6;
  int64 default_expiry_seconds = 7;       // expiresDefault: 1 h unless the document overrides it
  int64 max_expiry_seconds = 8;           // maxExpiry: 30 days unless the rule overrides it
  repeated uint32 evidence = 9;           // accepted ApprovalDecision.channel values (§16.8); default all three
}
message AclAudit {                        // a reader every member sees (owner decision 63)
  repeated bytes reader_atoms = 1; repeated uint32 repo_kinds = 2; repeated bytes repo_ids = 3;
  bytes audit_opt_in = 4;                 // the k-of-n AuditOptIn record, which api and readers verify
}
message AclTarget {                       // exactly one kind set
  bytes atom = 1; bytes sidecar_id = 2; bytes network_id = 3; bytes repo_id = 4;
  repeated bytes socket_tokens = 5;       // §9.4's token path
  bool socket_prefix = 6;                 // whole-segment prefix; finer globs project to their literal prefix
  string public_name = 7;                 // tls/ and smtp/ sockets, dns hosts
  reserved 8;                             // an ip target's CIDR, kept in AclLocalPolicy, never in rows
  bool mail_send = 9;
}
```

**Grant chains.** These statements act at once as §7.9 deltas, checked by api and readers against the state at their log position until a writer folds them in, so none waits for an admin (owner decisions [8](#od-8), [74](#od-74)). Each opens with §7.9's `StatementHeader`, whose `at` pins the signer's state:

```text
statement (§6 Signed, purpose acl unless noted; ids only; in       signer
  acl.proto, which imports sidecar/protocol/bridge/auth.proto
  (§4.4), where GrantRevoke, Suspend and Unsuspend are declared,
  since sidecar/device's posture applies them between states (§17.8))
GrantActivate{header, grant_id, canonical_action, decisions}       any admitted sidecar; authority only from the
  canonical_action: the approved §16.8 CanonicalAction, whose      embedded ApprovalDecisions, each signed by an
  grant fields are rule_id, subject, grant_dst, grant_allow and    approver the requests rule names (8.6) on a
  expires_millis, and a publish's also app_mode and                channel its evidence lists, binding the
  link_spki_sha256; a dial or route grant's prefixes and ports     canonical action's hash and its subject (§16.6)
  only in its sealed_detail (owner decision 220; §17.8)
GrantRevoke{grant_id}                                              an approver, the subject, or an admin
Suspend{subject, suspend_id}                                       an admin, or the subject's owner or sponsor;
                                                                   for an AdminSet member's device, its owner
                                                                   or k of n (§7.9); never changes AdminSet or
                                                                   its n; of another sidecar, countersigned as
                                                                   §7.9's presence row asks (owner decision
                                                                   187)
Unsuspend{subject, suspend_id}                                     the class that suspended it or a higher one
                                                                   (owner or sponsor < admin < k of n, with no
                                                                   admin class for an AdminSet member's
                                                                   device), never the subject itself; lifts
                                                                   only that suspend_id
EvsShare{repo_id, subject, expires}                                a consented device of the repo's owner (8.5),
  expires optional, defined at M2 and honored by every reader as   for owner-bound kinds
  RepoGrant's is, so a time-bound share ends with no device
  online (a reader ignoring it would widen access)
OwnerConfirm{sidecar_id}                                           a consented device of the sidecar's member
                                                                   (8.5; owner decision 126)
access log of one repo_id (owner decision 8):
```
