### 10.3 What exists today

- **GKM** appears only at PLAN.md:53; no repo has code for it [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md).
- **Go 1.27.3** (connect/go.mod:3). `crypto/hpke` implements X-Wing as `MLKEM768X25519()`, KEM 0x647a, from draft-ietf-hpke-pq (GOROOT/src/crypto/hpke/pq.go:21, :39-41); `crypto/mldsa` arrived in Go 1.27 (GOROOT/api/go1.27.txt:4).
- **Constraints.** The browser build is `CGO_ENABLED=0` (sdk/js/Makefile:69). server's `BlobStore` has `PutIfAbsent` but no Delete, If-Match or ranged read (server/blob.go:160-192); `ServiceHost.Blobs` adds them, per metadata cluster (§4.5, §19).
- **Test material** (2026-11-03). The mlswg's 16 vector files carry only RFC 9420's classical suites (https://github.com/mlswg/mls-implementations/tree/main/test-vectors). MIT differential peers: thomas-vilte/mls-go v1.6.0 (0x0001-0x0003; [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.4); tmc/mls, whose provisional 0x004F has exactly 0x0010's algorithms (wire.go:33-50); OpenMLS, whose unregistered 0x004D pairs X-Wing with ChaCha20-Poly1305 (https://cryspen.com/post/pq-openmls/).

### 10.4 Implementation, ciphersuite, credentials

**Subset (D-KEYS-12).** Only what evs uses; anything else is refused when parsed.

| RFC 9420 feature | v0 |
|---|---|
| Tree math; codec, mls10 only (§6, App. C) | yes |
| Labeled crypto, key schedule, exporter (§5, §8) | yes |
| Secret tree, PrivateMessage, transcript hashes (§6.3, §8.2, §9) | handshakes only |
| TreeKEM, parent and tree hashes, validation (§7) | yes |
| Add, Remove, GroupContextExtensions, inline (§12.1); path-only commits for self-update (§12.4) | yes |
| Welcome, `ratchet_tree`, ExternalInit (§12.4.3) | external commits only to resync or recover |
| KeyPackages, last resort; credential 0xF552 (§10, §16.8, §17.5) | yes |
| PSK, ReInit, branching, application messages, external senders, standalone and Update proposals | refused |

**Conformance.** No vectors exist for 0x0010, so every mlswg vector file covering a v0 feature runs under 0x0001; 0x0010 adds X-Wing known-answer tests (KATs) and [owner decision 43](#od-43)'s differential runs: mls-go under 0x0001, tmc/mls under 0x004F mapped to 0x0010, and OpenMLS's 0x004D once an M0 KAT matches its X-Wing to Go's. **The 0x0010 gate (D-KEYS-10)** adds what those cannot show:

```text
specified  the MLS wire (credential 0xF552, GkmCommitHeader, GenRotate, ur_group), the delivery wire
           (ReaderKey, KeyDelivery under its ReaderWrap and DelegationWrap types, 10.6's wrap and recovery
           paths) and suite 0x0010, at M2's entry review; no field is removed after it
frozen     at M2's exit review (D-PHASE-7), on §22.10's 0x0010 interop artifact:
  kem      X-Wing KATs: tmc/mls's encapsulation and decapsulation equal Go's crypto/hpke MLKEM768X25519() on
           fixed seeds
  stacks   one scripted lifecycle in both directions between mls_* and tmc/mls (0x004F mapped to 0x0010): at
           least 10 epochs with a Welcome, path commits, a Remove, an external commit with ExternalInit and a
           PrivateMessage decrypted per epoch, both sides computing equal epoch_authenticator and "UR evs 1.0
           kek" exporter outputs
  ladder   GenWrap's, LeafWrap's and GenLink's AAD and KeyDelivery's wrap_aad (10.5), reproduced by
           mlsinterop/'s own code
  gaps     no stacks step may be a gap: one tmc/mls lacks holds the freeze unless a second peer runs it in
           both directions (OpenMLS's 0x004D, once its M0 KAT matches); mlswg vectors under 0x0001 count toward
           no part of it
```

**Ciphersuite ([owner decision 44](#od-44); D-KEYS-12).** 0x0010, MLS_128_MLKEM768X25519_AES128GCM_SHA256_Ed25519, in groups and credentials from v0 (draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites-07, Publication Requested 2026-11-01; [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.1). Each MLS AEAD key is used once, so wasm's table-based AES (GOROOT/src/crypto/internal/fips140/aes/aes_generic.go:58-74) is no practical timing target.

**Framing (D-KEYS-3).** Member commits are PrivateMessage (RFC 9420 §6.3), whose clear header shows group_id, epoch and content type; only external commits (resync, recovery self-join) are PublicMessage, as RFC 9420 §6 requires for non-members. `authenticated_data`, clear but bound into the AEAD and signature, adds only what the gate needs and no roster delta ([owner decision 59](#od-59)):

```proto
message GkmCommitHeader {   // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto, in authenticated_data of every commit
  uint64  generation = 1;   // the generation of this epoch's GenWrap: the newest gen/ the committer holds;
                            //   0 only for a recovery self-join that carries no GenWrap (10.6's epoch PUT, 10.8)
  AuthPin auth = 2;         // the state (§7.9) the new roster was checked against
}
```

**Leaves and readers (D-KEYS-2, D-KEYS-23).** Member devices that read a repo are its group's leaves, at most 1,000 (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [7](#od-7), [60](#od-60)); in a data repo, those past the 1,000 seats wait keyless (§8.12). Agents read by 10.5's wraps, outside that cap ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). Readers are §8's `RepoReaders`, which every device evaluates ([owner decision 6](#od-6)) and the projection carries as ids. In the config group, which every admitted sidecar reads, §7.9's `leaves` rule alone ranks member devices, whose admissions carry no not_after, and moves them between leaf and wrap, as a function of the log ([owner decision 144](#od-144)); the team directory's group, its own MLS group ([owner decision 60](#od-60)), which every admitted sidecar of a team network reads (§16.11), follows the same rule: the first 1,000 live member devices are its leaves, and a rotation costs ~1.3 KB a wrap per overflow device ([owner decision 182](#od-182)). In both, the rest, and an entitled device not yet added, read by ReaderWraps (wrapped) and stay leaves of their data repos. §10 adds:

```text
adds      in both groups members accept an Add or external join only of a leaf-entitled device (§7.9); one
          without a KeyPackage reads by ReaderWrap until it uploads one, and no other device takes its place
wrapped   a wrapped member device commits no Add or Remove in them, only first wraps and rotations (10.9)
```

**Credential.** Private-use type `ur_sidecar = 0xF552` (RFC 9420 §17.5), required through `required_capabilities`; KeyPackages are public, so it names no member, tag or client:

```proto
message UrMlsCredential {                         // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto
  bytes sidecar_id = 1;                           // durable leaf identity (§5)
  bytes identity_public_key = 2; string identity_alg = 3;  // §5; ed25519 in v0
  bytes mls_signature_public_key = 4;             // rotated by self-update
  uint32 cipher_suite = 5; int64 not_after = 6;   // 0x0010 (owner decision 44)
  bytes admission_sha256 = 7;                     // its §7.9 SidecarAdmit; Genesis for the first device
  bytes identity_signature = 8;                   // §6 signing, purpose mls-credential, fields 1-7
}
```

- **Admission (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [127](#od-127)).** Members accept a credential only if an unrevoked, unparked `SidecarAdmit`, verified through the authorization log back to the genesis and signed as §7.9 allows (one admin, the member's own device unless `self_admit` is off, or k of n for AdminSet members), names its sidecar_id and identity key. Only a network's first device is trusted on first use, against its safety number (§2.8 EX5). Clients pin that key, refuse a second and share pins through §6's `Hello` (D-PROTO-13). After a `SidecarRevoke`, GKM deletes the sidecar's KeyPackages.
- **Self-updates and forks.** A leaf that commits no path for 7 days (30 in groups above 50 leaves) commits a path-only commit (D-KEYS-14). Clients pin each push's sealed (group_id, epoch, epoch_authenticator) (§11.6) and each generation's C_g, refuse a lower or conflicting pin with an alarm and compare pins by §6's `HeadCheck`, whose generation heads serve holders that are not leaves (I-16, D-PROTO-14, D-TRUST-10; [owner decision 129](#od-129)).

### 10.5 The key hierarchy: what "one session key stored in GKM" means

The MLS exporter changes every epoch, is not forward-secure (draft-ietf-mls-extensions-11 §4.4), and gives a new member nothing earlier, so the evs keys sit above MLS:

```text
MLS epoch e --MLS-Exporter("UR evs 1.0 kek", repo_id, 32)--> KEK_e (key-encryption key)
RK_g: repo key generation g, 32 random bytes = PLAN's "session key"; cause_g ∈ {remove, request, schedule}
GKM stores only:
  GenRotate_g = the Signed record in gen/<g> (below): C_g, parent C_{g-1}, cause, auth pin, time, holders
                hash, the wrap count, GenLink_g, an optional LeafWrap, the drop key and its expiry
  GenLink_g   = XChaCha20-Poly1305(K_link_g, RK_{g-1}; aad repo_id||g||cause_g)         the ladder
  GenWrap_e   = XChaCha20-Poly1305(KEK_e, RK_g; aad group_id||e||g)    in epoch object e, g its newest
  LeafWrap    = XChaCha20-Poly1305(KEK_e, RK_g; aad group_id||e||g)    in GenRotate_g, for every leaf of e
  GroupInfo_e = XChaCha20-Poly1305(K_groupinfo, GroupInfo incl. ratchet_tree; aad group_id||e)
                inside each epoch object at <= 16 leaves; on demand above (10.6)
  RecoveryWrap_{m,g}   = HPKE-XWing(recovery_pub_m, RK_g)                                    (10.8)
  ReaderWrap_{g,s,k}   = §6 Signed, purpose reader-wrap, a KeyDelivery (below): {group_id, g, C_g, s, k,
                         staged or late, a late one's auth pin and time, HPKE-XWing(ReaderKey_{s,k}, RK_g)}
  DelegationWrap_{g,d} = the same to the reader key of d, which d fixes, d = delegation_id = SHA-256(Signed
                         Delegation); k = SHA-256 of the X-Wing public key sealed to, its incarnation
RK_g --HKDF-SHA256(salt repo_id, info "UR evs 1.0 "||purpose||u64be(g) [||group_id||u64be(e)])-->
     link|fek|manifest|path|ref|drop|groupinfo|index
ReaderKey_{s,k} = §6 Signed, purpose reader-key, {sidecar_id, xwing_public_key, not_after}, not_after at most
              7 days after signing; every reader holds one, a fresh X-Wing pair once it is 6 days old, k its
              incarnation (readerkey, below)
ur_group    = GroupContext extension {network_id, repo_id, kind, owner_member_id}, fixed at creation; kind is
              one of §11.12's kinds, directory among them from M2's reservation (owner decision 171)
```

- **PLAN.md:53, precisely.** One current key, RK_g, encrypts every new object, and GKM stores it only wrapped (I-1). It rotates when a key holder drops or its authorization expires (`remove`), on `ur keys rotate` (`request`) and after 30 days (`schedule`); Adds and self-updates keep it, so in-flight writes stay valid.
- **Ladder.** RK_g opens every earlier generation, so a joiner gets the whole history; to withhold history, use a new repo (§11). A removed reader gets no later KEK, RK or wrap, but keeps every generation it held and opens files untouched since its removal until they are rewritten or `ur evs rekey` re-checkpoints them. MLS updates heal the tree and its KEKs, but a copied keychain derives every KEK until the device's own next path commit (10.4) and opens every delivery to a ReaderKey it holds, to which a rotator or deliverer seals only before that key's not_after, at most 7 days after its signing, whatever advertisement gkm serves (readerkey, below); so content heals only at the first generation sealed after both. A passive copy (the keychain's bytes, used only to open what the operator serves, a stale advertisement included) therefore reads, while the device runs, what is sealed up to about 37 days after the copy, 60 above 50 leaves (the path commit within 7 days, 30 above 50 leaves, the newest copied ReaderKey's not_after within 7, then up to 30 days to the next generation), and every earlier generation through the ladder; while the device does not run, its copied leaf derives each later epoch's KEK until it commits again or a stale Remove (10.9) removes it, and a copy of a wrapped reader's keychain heals at that not_after whether or not the device runs. An active clone, one that uses the copy's identity key or ClientKey, signs fresh ReaderKeys and KeyPackages and commits as the device, so no path commit or key replacement ends it: only a `SidecarRevoke{reason: compromise}` from a since_n at or before the copy, whose cascade parks what the clone admitted (§7.9), and the device's enrollment anew, since `--replace` keeps its identity key (§5.5), as for a compromised backup (10.8). A Delegation's reader key in it reads as the Residual below says. X-Wing protects ciphertext against harvest-now-decrypt-later by a passive adversary ([owner decision 44](#od-44)); signatures are Ed25519, so an adversary that can forge them (a future quantum computer, say) and that the operator serves could forge admissions and, through the ladder, read all retained history. External resync needs RK_g, under which the GroupInfo is sealed, never a published identity key alone.
- **Authentication.** The key schedule and every GroupInfo signature bind `ur_group`; clients accept RK_g only if it matches `gen/<g>`'s signed C_g; the newer, verified generation authenticates each GenLink, whose AAD covers the cause §11's rewrap rule reads; a missing key is refused, never defaulted (ePrint 2024/546).

**Generations (D-KEYS-15).** C_g = SHA-256("UR evs 1.0 commit" ‖ repo_id ‖ u64be(g) ‖ RK_g), and every evs head carries the generation pin {group_id, g, C_g} (§11.8). `gkm/<group_id>/gen/<g>`, created If-None-Match, is the only place a generation exists: MLS commits change the tree and give joiners the newest generation's key in GenWrap_e, and the rotation a Remove requires is a separate gen/ claim, by any writer.

```proto
message GenRotate {              // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto; §6 Signed, purpose gen-rotate, by the rotator's identity key
  bytes   group_id = 1; bytes repo_id = 2;
  uint64  generation = 3;        // g; generation 1 is written with epoch 0 (KF1) and has no parent
  bytes   parent_commitment = 4; // C_{g-1}
  bytes   commitment = 5;        // C_g
  uint32  cause = 6;             // 1 REMOVE, 2 REQUEST, 3 SCHEDULE; REMOVE iff it covers a shrink, an
                                 //   authorization expiry or a compromise retirement since the parent (10.9)
  AuthPin auth = 7;              // the state KeyHolders was computed at (§7.9); never below the previous
                                 //   base or the parent's auth
  int64   time_ms = 8;           // the evaluation time for expiries; within 10 min of gkm's clock
  bytes   holders_sha256 = 9;    // SHA-256 over the sorted KeyHolders(R, auth, time) identities (below)
  uint32  wrap_count = 10;       // staged wraps and recovery wraps, for completeness checks
  bytes   genlink = 11;          // GenLink_g
  LeafWrap leaf_wrap = 12;       // optional: one wrap for every leaf of that epoch, 72 B
  bytes   drop_public_key = 13;  // only for kinds that take deposits (D-KEYS-17)
  int64   drop_not_after_ms = 14;
}
message LeafWrap { uint64 epoch = 1; bytes ciphertext = 2; }  // RK_g under KEK_epoch, aad group_id||epoch||g
message KeyDelivery {              // the body of a ReaderWrap or DelegationWrap, gkm's wrap/ object (10.6)
  bytes   group_id = 1;
  uint64  generation = 2;          // g
  bytes   commitment = 3;          // C_g, all 32 bytes
  bytes   recipient = 4;           // sidecar_id; a DelegationWrap's, the delegation_id
  bytes   recipient_key_sha256 = 5;  // SHA-256 of the X-Wing public key sealed to: a ReaderKey's, which a
                                     //   replacement changes, or the Delegation's reader_xwing_public_key
  uint32  delivery_kind = 6;       // 1 STAGED: by gen/<g>'s rotator before its claim; 2 LATE: after it (10.9)
  AuthPin auth = 7;                // LATE only: the signer's newest verified state when it signs
  int64   time_ms = 8;             // LATE only: the signer's clock or, if later, gen/<g>'s time_ms; within 10 min of gkm's
  bytes   ciphertext = 9;          // HPKE-XWing(that key, RK_g), info "UR evs 1.0 wrap", aad wrap_aad
}
message ReaderWrap { KeyDelivery wrap = 1; }      // §6 Signed, purpose reader-wrap, by the signer's identity key
message DelegationWrap { KeyDelivery wrap = 1; }  // the same, to a Delegation's reader key
// wrap_aad = u8(1 ReaderWrap | 2 DelegationWrap) || group_id || u64be(g) || C_g || SHA-256(recipient)
//            || recipient_key_sha256 || u8(delivery_kind), then, LATE only, u64be(auth.version) || auth.chain
//            || i64be(time_ms)
```

```text
Rotate: one algorithm for every cause and every rotator
1  S = my newest verified state (n, A_n); t = now; H = KeyHolders(R, S, t); require me in H or covered by a
   Delegation in H, and me ∈ writers(R, S) or, in the config group, me = the signer of an admission or
   revocation this rotation answers (owner decision 128) or, after api's reap of an uncovered ephemeral
   agent, of its admission (§7.10)
2  g = the newest generation (GET gen/<g+1> answers 404); RK' = 32 random bytes; persist RK' and the
   GenRotate draft in my keychain
3  stage deliveries for g+1, each a STAGED KeyDelivery at wrap/<g+1>/<c8>/<recipient>/<k8> (10.6), c8 =
   hex(C_{g+1}[0:8]), up to 16 PUTs at once:
     leaves        if I am a leaf at the current epoch e and e's tree holds no leaf outside H, one leaf_wrap
                   under KEK_e inside GenRotate; else a ReaderWrap to each leaf's ReaderKey
     wrapped       in the config and directory groups, member devices in H that e's tree lacks, wrapped or not
                   yet added, a device a restored binding admitted among them once activated (10.8): a
                   ReaderWrap each (owner decisions 144, 182); in other groups they join by Add (KF2)
     agents        not covered by a live Delegation: a ReaderWrap each
     Delegations   live ones in H: a DelegationWrap each
     recovery      members reading R with a current RecoveryBind: a RecoveryWrap each
4  PUT gen/<g+1> If-None-Match                                          <- the linearization point
     201      done; hint (D-KEYS-19); the generation is complete, since every delivery already exists
     412      GET it and check it (10.9); if it covers every shrink and expiry I rotate for, adopt it and fetch
              my wrap; else go to 1, rotating at g+2
     unknown  GET gen/<g+1>: my commitment = done; another = 412; 404 = repeat 4 with the same bytes
5  seal content to g+1; delete my keychain draft
retry      the GenRotate bytes, named by their commitment; every delivery precedes the claim, so a crash before
           4 leaves only staged objects, which GC removes after 24 h, and one after it a complete generation;
           a recipient whose ReaderKey appears or changes later gets a LATE delivery to that key from any
           holder but a read_only one (10.6's late wraps, 10.9)
remove X   a writer leaf commits Remove(X) at epoch e+1 (the revoking device first, 10.9); then any writer
           rotates (in the directory group, in 10.9's order), a leaf by leaf_wrap under KEK_{e+1}, which X
           cannot derive; until a leaf commits the Remove, a wrapped writer (an agent, or in the config or
           directory group a wrapped member device, 10.4) may rotate by ReaderWraps to every remaining leaf,
           no leaf_wrap uses an epoch whose tree holds X, and the next leaf commit must remove X; wrapped
           writers never commit Removes (owner decisions 114, 144, 182), yet no repo stays gated while every
           leaf is offline
```

**Key holders (D-KEYS-16).** For repo R at state S and time t:

```text
KeyHolders(R, S, t) = leaf(s)        member devices reading R (§8.12), MLS leaves of R's group; in the config
                                     and directory groups wrapped ones (10.4) hold wraps and keep this identity
                    ∪ agent(s)       other admitted sidecars reading R, unless covered
                    ∪ delegation(d)  live Delegations whose reach holds R
                    ∪ recovery(m)    members reading R with a current RecoveryBind
covered(s, R)  = s was admitted under a Delegation d with delegation(d) ∈ KeyHolders(R, S, t)
reach(d)       = the config, in a team network the directory, and each repo that a read or write grant
                 naming one of d's tags reads (the grants §8.6's ceiling counts for a tag a sidecar carries);
                 every agent d admits carries exactly d's tag_ids (§7.9's scoped), so a covered agent reads
                 each repo d's key opens; a forwarding Delegation's is the config alone (owner decision 197)
live(d)        = d has not ended (§7.9's delegation row) at S, t < d.not_after, and no Suspend, and no
```

**Residual ([owner decision 114](#od-114)).** Every holder of a Delegation's reader key reads every later generation of the Delegation's reach (the config, a team network's directory and its tag repos) until the key drops: each agent it admitted, reaped ones and ephemeral ones past their own `not_after` included, since such an agent can close itself, and api can reap it, before any cutoff keyed to that `not_after` (§7.7), and each copy of its auth key. The key drops, at its position, at `DelegationRevoke`, at a revocation for any reason but reaped or a `Suspend` of one of its agents, and at a compromise revocation whose closure voids the Delegation (§7.9's cascade), and at `not_after`; reaping an agent does not drop it. A copy of the whole auth-key bundle also holds the Delegation's signing seed, which no honest daemon's erasure reaches: it admits fresh agents, uncovered once the key has dropped and so reading by their own ReaderWraps, until the Delegation ends at its `DelegationRevoke`, its void or a compromise revocation of one of its agents, or passes `not_after` or `max_admits`, after which api and every reader refuse its admissions, whatever bearer or client the operator supplies (§7.9's delegation row). A lost or removed revocation, or a `Suspend`, thus retires the key but not the admission authority; the revoking device's plan says so and offers `DelegationRevoke`, whose `since_n`, like a compromise revocation's, parks the agents the Delegation admitted from that position on (§7.10's agents row). Bounds: `not_after` is required, at most 90 days (§7.8); `max_admits` counts every admission for the Delegation's life; the console gives CI and cloud Delegations 30 days and replaces them (a new Delegation, then `DelegationRevoke` of the old) at each CI secret rotation and after a key drop.

| Content key | Use (symmetric sealing with XChaCha20-Poly1305; ids, tokens and pads with HMAC-SHA256) |
|---|---|
| `fek` | Wraps each object's random 256-bit key (PLAN.md:148) in a sealed segment header (general repos) or a deletable slot (record-class repos, group inboxes; 10.8); a versionless path in those repos, the search index's files included, keeps one key in a slot only that path's versions name, until a REMOVE generation, a CLOSURE or `ur evs rekey` replaces it (§11.7, §11.14) |
| `manifest` | Names, entry fields, push metadata and ref names (§11) |
| `path` | Token keys per path epoch (§11.6, [owner decision 2](#od-2)) |
| `ref` | Ref ids and the search index's document keys, from RK_1 for the repo's life, since ref ids name every `head/`, `log/` and `idx/` key (§11.6) and a document's key must not change at a rotation (§11.14) |
| `drop` | An X-Wing key pair for deposits that depositors cannot read back, published in its generation's GenRotate under the depositor rule below |
| `groupinfo` | Seals GroupInfo and its tree per (group_id, epoch) |
| `index` | Draws the keyed pad that hides which trigrams a search-index shard's documents share (§11.14); per generation, which the shard's header names, so a removed reader cannot predict a later shard's size |

```text
depositor (D-KEYS-17)  before sealing to generation g's drop key, a depositor, which reads the config,
           requires: GenRotate_g verifies; g is the newest generation gkm serves (10.14's drop-key route); g
           covers R's holders_shrunk_at and every holder expiry up to now in its own state (§7.9); now <
           drop_not_after_ms; g is not below its pin for R, which it then raises; else it waits for a newer
           rotation, which the gate makes writers write
```

Clients cache every RK_g in the §5 keychain, keep MLS state, trees included, on disk under §5's AEAD, load one group's tree at a time (§18.4's budgets) and delete other epoch secrets (RFC 9420 §9.2). Every derivation and unwrap calls §22's `testHookSecret`.

### 10.6 GKM: the Delivery Service and wrapped-key store

GKM is a strongly consistent Delivery Service (DS; RFC 9750 §5.2.1) with no state of its own: its records are metadata-cluster objects ordered by conditional writes (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [21](#od-21), [145](#od-145)). It verifies 15-minute capability tokens offline (aud `gkm`; scopes `repo:<id>:r|rw|admin`, `deposit` on the drop-key route only, and an unadmitted client's `recovery:<member_id>` for that member's own recovery wraps), honors an `r`, `rw` or `admin` scope only while its subject reads or writes the repo, as the scope says, in gkm's newest verified state (§8.12), and honors §7.8's `rev/` objects. Each route takes the scope the scopes block below gives.

Target: p99 close-to-reopen ≤5 min with a writer online, in the directory group a hinted or pushing one (10.9); alarm at 1 h.

```yaml
gkm-1:
  sees: GroupForm chain (repo_id, group_id, previous group, generation, signer); epoch 0 (network_id, cipher suite 0x0010 (owner decision 44), creator); each group's owner marker (repo_id, network_id), written first at a creation or re-form, through which alone gkm resolves the group (owner decision 201); and each forwarding Delegation's reader public key, by delegation_id, which gkm and every rotator check against its row's digest (owner decision 202)
  why: one accepted commit per epoch; re-forming; one repo to a group; sealing to forwarding Delegations (§10.5)
  ttl: life of the repo, epoch 0 while epoch/0 exists; an owner marker until the repo's shred, a re-seed's form writing it again; a forwarding Delegation's reader key until 24 h after the Delegation ends or is superseded
gkm-2:
  sees: epoch objects; group_id, epoch, content type, generation, auth pin, size, time, uploader sidecar_id; the commit as PrivateMessage ciphertext; GenWrap; at most 16 leaves, the sealed GroupInfo and the generation that seals it
  why: ordering; the write gate
  ttl: 30 d, then until every leaf acking in the last 30 d has applied it; never the newest epoch
gkm-3:
  withdrawn: no roster delta in the clear (owner decision 59); membership shows only as sidecar ids in gkm-4, gkm-5, gkm-7 and gkm-10, as in api-7
gkm-4:
  sees: "KeyPackages (init and leaf HPKE keys, signature key, credential: sidecar_id, identity key and its algorithm, suite, not_after, admission hash, signature); claims (group, claimer, target); ReaderKeys (owner decision 114)"
  why: asynchronous adds; wrapped readers
  ttl: KeyPackages until claimed, or 90 d; claims 90 d; ReaderKeys until replaced or past their not_after, at most 7 d
gkm-5:
  sees: Welcome objects and pointers; recipient sidecar_ids and KeyPackageRefs in the clear; secrets and GroupInfo encrypted
  why: deliver joins
  ttl: until every recipient has acked, at most 90 d
gkm-6:
  sees: external commits, for resync and recovery only (PublicMessage); the joiner's leaf and credential, its removed old leaf, their ExternalInit and Remove proposals and their UpdatePath's public keys and encrypted path secrets
  why: offline catch-up and recovery
  ttl: as gkm-2
gkm-7:
  sees: key ladder; GenRotates (group, generation, parent and own commitments, cause, auth pin, time, holders hash, the count of its staged and recovery wraps, signer; GenLink and leaf-wrap ciphertexts; the drop public key and its expiry where the kind takes deposits); GroupInfo pointers and, above 16 leaves, sealed GroupInfo and the generation it names; staged and late wraps (group, generation, commitment, recipient sidecar_id or delegation_id and the SHA-256 of the key sealed to, staged or late, a late one's auth pin and time, ciphertext, signer; owner decisions 114, 144, 182)
  why: ladder, resync, deposits; wrapped readers
  ttl: life of the repo, a gen pack's GenRotates as gen/'s; GroupInfo until superseded; wraps until the next generation's exist, staged wraps of a lost claim 24 h, a recipient's wrap to an older key 30 d after one to a newer key exists
gkm-8:
  sees: recovery wraps (member_id, group_id, generation, the 8-byte prefix c8 of the generation's commitment, which gkm-7 shows whole, an 8-byte prefix of the binding's Ed25519 key hash, which the authorization log already shows, HPKE ciphertext); the bindings are §7.9's RecoveryBind config records, not gkm objects
  why: recovery after losing every device
  ttl: until a RecoveryRebind replaces them or the repo is deleted; staged ones of a lost claim 24 h
gkm-9:
  sees: request log; client, route, group, time, bytes (GroupInfo requests included)
  why: rate limits, abuse
  ttl: 7 d
gkm-10:
  sees: acks in Redis {gka_<group_id>}; group_id, sidecar_id, newest applied epoch, time; written at most daily
  why: retention
  ttl: overwritten by the leaf's next ack; 31 d after its last write; deleted with its group's gkm objects at a shred (§11.12); soft state outside the rdb bundles, lost with Redis, after which gkm deletes no epoch for 30 d; a hold's copy excepted (api-14)
```

### 10.7 Flows

**KF1. Create a repo.** A member's device C files §8.8's `RepoCreate`, creates the repo in evs as `keying` (§11.12), placing it ([owner decision 145](#od-145)), and becomes its admin ([owner decision 8](#od-8)); a config repo follows §7.9's bootstrap. `POST /gkm/groups` writes `epoch/0` (a random 16-byte group_id, GenWrap_0 and the sealed GroupInfo), `gen/1` (the GenRotate of a new RK_1, without a parent) and C's GroupForm. C writes generation 1's deliveries (10.5's step 3: ReaderWraps, DelegationWraps, RecoveryWraps) while the repo is still keying, resuming from its keychain after a crash, and only then has evs activate it, so no content predates its recovery wraps. C then adds the other leaves in one Add-only commit with its Welcome and GroupInfo.

**KF2. Add a device D.** D enrolls, its `SidecarAdmit` enters the authorization log (§5.6, §7.9), and it uploads a ReaderKey and, as a member device, KeyPackages (a device a restored binding admitted, only once anchored, 10.8). Once the state lists D where its subject reads, and again at D's first KeyPackage upload (10.6), GKM hints `pending` to the writers, and a committer per 10.9 claims a KeyPackage and commits the Add with other pending changes, the Welcome, the sealed GroupInfo and GenWrap; an agent, or in the config or directory group a member device that is wrapped or has no KeyPackage (10.4; owner decisions [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)), gets a late ReaderWrap of the current generation instead, signed at a state that lists D (10.9's late row), and a covered agent reads at once through its Delegation's wrap. D checks RK_g against `gen/<g>`'s C_g and walks the ladder (10.5). Owner-bound repos park a D without its owner's consent (§8.5; [owner decision 126](#od-126)), whose devices raise `approval_pending` until an `OwnerConfirm`.

**KF3. Add a member N.** A repo or network admin signs N's grant into the repo's access log (§8.8; owner decisions [7](#od-7), [8](#od-8)), or in an owner-bound repo the owner's device an `EvsShare` ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), and KF2 runs for N's devices: the granting device at once, other writer leaves after 15 s plus jitter; while none is online, N waits and nothing leaks.

**KF4. Remove a member or device X** (§7.10). The revocation's log entry n' drops X from the key holders of every repo it read, so evs refuses writes whose generation does not cover n' (10.6, §11.8), and evs and gkm refuse X's tokens (§7.8). A committer per 10.9, the revoking device first, commits the Remove with a path; any writer then rotates (10.5), staging its wraps before it claims `gen/<g+1>`, at the latest through `EnsureWritable` before its next write, so reaps batch. A wrapped X needs only the rotation, and a wrapped revoker in the config or directory group rotates first, leaving a leaf X's Remove to the next leaf commit (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)). D-TRUST-10's witness stop never holds a Remove, rotation or revocation ([owner decision 129](#od-129)).

```text
   api (§7.10)       evs               gkm               writers
1  |--entry n'------>|                 |                 |   holders_shrunk_at = n': 412 below; receivers 451
2  |                 |                 |--hint pending-->|   per-client gkm topic, the revoking device first
3  |                 |                 |<--epoch/<e+1>---|   a writer leaf: Remove + path; header (g, (n', A'))
4  |                 |                 |<--gen/<g+1>-----|   any writer: staged wraps, then the claim at (n', A')
5  |                 |<--write at g+1, auth >= n'---------|   the gate passes it
```

**KF5. Offline catch-up.** Up to 100 epochs behind, the device replays each later commit in order (each epoch derives from the previous `init_secret`). Further behind, or if commits were pruned, processing fails or its leaf was removed as stale, it opens the current sealed GroupInfo (10.6) with the key of the generation it names, from its wrap (a device none of whose keys opens a delivery of it, its ReaderKey lapsed or past retention, publishes a new one and asks for a late delivery to it, 10.6's late wraps), and resyncs by external commit (ExternalInit, a Remove of its old leaf, GenWrap_{e+1}); else it awaits a re-add or uses its recovery code (10.8). Nothing is lost.

**KF6. Concurrent commits.** The 409 loser, having stored no Welcome, processes the winner and retries what remains. Rotations race only on `gen/<g+1>` (10.5).

**KF7. gkm unavailable.** Cached keys serve reads and deposits; evs checks the gate itself from the authorization log, so writes continue while every shrink is covered, and a removal still stops them until gkm returns and a writer rotates. Joins, catch-up and membership changes wait.

### 10.8 Revocation, erasure, recovery, re-seeding, key domains

**Removed or expired holder X ([owner decision 64](#od-64)).** X keeps what it held up to generation g and loses everything after: the generation that covers its drop is cause REMOVE (10.9), so content rewraps lazily, each file's next write a full checkpoint under a fresh object key (§11.7; Q-KEYS-10), the search index's versionless files included (its heads at their writer's next push, its shards at their next merge or roll-up; §11.14), and path tokens re-key through §11.6's path epoch, at once for a member's device or a compromise, within 24 h for other drops and for expiries ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), or, while two source epochs stand, once one drops; §11.6 reconciles the two.

**Erasure ([owner decision 61](#od-61)).** An entry's key lives only in a deletable slot (§11.12), so an ERASE push deleting it, cached copies and mirrors' slot copies (§11.12) shred the entry even if ciphertext survives; §11.12's CUT first fences the index's publication of it, then its CLOSURE rewrites the search index's files holding its postings without it, under fresh keys in new slots, and the ERASE destroys their old slots' keys, one of which every older stored version of those files uses, staged bytes in a batch included (§11.14); no operator copy holds slots or wraps ([owner decision 90](#od-90)), and owner devices' mirrors hold slot copies and apply each erasure (§11.13). gkm, like evs, refuses a `deleted` repo but for a re-seed's GroupForm (below; [owner decision 82](#od-82)); its shred (§11.12) deletes the repo's gkm objects and `{gka_}` acks, and again after 10 min for writes in flight (10.6's checks), even under a preservation hold, subject to counsel ([owner decision 133](#od-133)), and members drop its keys.

**Recovery when M loses every device (owner decisions [62](#od-62), [127](#od-127), [128](#od-128), [149](#od-149)).** §5.9's recovery code derives X-Wing and Ed25519 keys that §7.9's `RecoveryBind` binds to M; every rotator, agents included, wraps RK_g to every reading member's current X-Wing recovery key, a public key every config reader holds, and the ladder opens older generations.
- With the code, a new device is admitted by the recovery key under §7.9's window and veto, meanwhile reading only the authorization log and M's own recovery wraps (10.14). The window and veto bound admission, not those wraps, which the code opens at once: a code holder with M's login holds every generation wrapped to M's recovery key and, through the ladder, each earlier one, and with the operator's ciphertext reads them, whatever a veto does: a rebind or a cascade void stops new wraps, and the code keeps opening what was wrapped to it and reads the current generation until the next rotation, which `RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}` makes a remove rotation with a path epoch at once; revoking the device it admitted does not retire the code (§2.10). It fetches its recovery wraps (the newest per group whose b8 names its code's binding, 10.6) and, once admitted, first passes §7.9's `anchor` on its config-group RecoveryWrap, raising §5.4's `head_alarm` (fork) and acting no further otherwise; only then does it open each group's sealed GroupInfo, self-join by external commit the config group and every group M writes ([owner decision 128](#od-128)), join the others through KF2, revoke M's lost devices through §5.6's calls (D-CORE-20; k of n for an AdminSet member's devices, its own signature counting as one), remove their leaves and rotate (10.5), in any order: a self-join may leave revoked leaves if it carries no GenWrap (generation 0) and its next commit removes them, so no generation reaches a thief's leaves. Above 16 leaves, a self-join waits for one leaf online to write the current GroupInfo; past the first 1,000, the device reads the config and the team directory by their RecoveryWraps, then by wraps (§7.9; owner decisions [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)).
- A binding a void restored takes no RecoveryWrap until a signer outside P signs it again (§7.9's cascade), so the device it admits, once its proposal activates, keeps §7.9's `restored` order, anchoring on a ReaderWrap, never an Add: it uploads its ReaderKey but no KeyPackage, fetches the late ReaderWrap of the config group's current generation that a config writer gives it (KF2), or one a later rotation stages while e's tree lacks it (10.5), and passes the anchor on that wrap's RK_g, with the same alarm and stop on a failure. Only then does it self-join the config group if leaf-entitled, by the one sealed GroupInfo that RK_g opens (else reading the config by those wraps), upload KeyPackages, so that KF2 adds it to its other groups, revoke, remove and rotate as above, and offer `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9), whose binding takes RecoveryWraps again; a group whose leaves are all in P opens to it only through that binding's surviving RecoveryWraps.
- `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9) signs a `RecoveryRebind` (§7.9), re-wraps each group's current generation to the new binding at that binding's own b8 path (10.6), deletes M's old binding's wraps only once every new one exists, so a crash between leaves both and its retry finishes, and requests a `request` rotation in M's groups, or, for a code retired as compromised (`RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}`), a `remove` one, which starts an immediate path epoch and full checkpoints (§11.6, §11.7). No rebind or void reaches a keychain backup sealed before it, whose `keychain.wrap` the retired or voided code still opens (§5.9), yielding that device's identity key, ClientKey seed, ReaderKeys and key cache, so after a compromise rebind or a void each device whose backups may hold such a sealing is revoked as compromised (§7.9) and enrolled anew, since `--replace` keeps its identity key (§5.5); after a rebind by §5.9's procedure, which keeps the rebind standing and revokes its signer last ([owner decision 212](#od-212)).
- Without the code, admins revoke the lost devices and admit a new one (§7.9), moving every team repo M read to a new generation; M's owner-bound repos, which need M's consent ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), and single-member repos are lost.

**Site loss (D-KEYS-13; order in §19.10).** gkm objects have no off-site copy (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94)), but devices keep each group's MLS state and every RK_g: a device 10.6's GroupForm rules allow, a repo admin's and for owner-bound kinds the owner's consented device, re-forms each group under a GroupForm linked to the cached RK_g, re-uploads the ladder and re-adds readers and RecoveryWraps, and members check the signer and their cached C_g. A repo re-seeded as deleted (§11.13) takes only that GroupForm, with its epoch 0 and ladder, while deleted ([owner decision 82](#od-82)): devices open its files from their cached RK_g once it is restored, its readers rejoin by KF2 and late wraps, and a shred deletes the group. Slots return from owner devices' mirrors (§11.13). Repos no device holds are lost (§2.18).

**Key domains ([R:product](design/design-research/product.md) S4)**, each its own repo and group, take §8.5's kind defaults as readers, which policy narrows (owner-bound kinds: [owner decision 126](#od-126)).

| Domain | Readers (agents by wrap) | Deposits by drop key |
|---|---|---|
| Author vault ([R:product](design/design-research/product.md) S1, S2) | the author's consented devices; `EvsShare` recipients | the author's other devices, tagged and headless sidecars |
| Team record ([R:product](design/design-research/product.md) S3; X20) | admins' and auditors' devices | members' and tagged sidecars; authors keep copies |
| Shared team repos | every reading sidecar (§8) | — |
| Config (§7.9); a team network's directory (§16.11) | every admitted sidecar; member devices past the first 1,000 by wrap (owner decisions [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)) | — |
| Burner vault and mailbox (§15) | the user's consented devices | `tag:mail` mail indexers ([owner decision 150](#od-150)), which cannot read the archive |

**Escrow ([owner decision 63](#od-63)).** None by default, and never silent: Team's v1 opt-in `tag:audit` reader on a customer device (sidecar/design/improve.md:106-108; §8.5's `audit` block under a k-of-n `AuditOptIn`) gets ReaderWraps only once every member's config holds the block and each affected reader list shows it.

### 10.9 Authorization of MLS operations

GKM sees no proposal ([owner decision 59](#od-59)), so members verify each decrypted commit and each wrap against its header, the authorization state at its auth pin (§7.9) and the repo's access log (§8.8). On a mismatch a member alarms and never adopts or encrypts to the epoch or generation; a bad commit can stall a group until an admin revokes its committer and the group re-forms through the ladder. GKM originates nothing; no group has external senders (I-4).

**Committers (owner decisions [113](#od-113), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)).** The signed input, not the committer, carries the authority, so no membership change waits for an admin, and members reject a commit without it. Wrapped writers (agents, and the config and directory groups' wrapped member devices, 10.4) rotate by re-wrapping but never commit an Add or Remove.

```text
Add            committer  a writer leaf, the granting device first; for a first wrap (an agent's, a
                          Delegation's or a wrapped member device's), any holder but a read_only one by the
                          delivery checks' late row, gkm hinting writers first (10.6); in the config and
                          directory groups also the admission's signer, by an Add from its leaf, or by the first
                          wrap if it or the device is wrapped, and from its leaf the signer of a revocation that
                          made the device leaf-entitled (§7.9's move)
               check      a signed grant in the access log, admission or EvsShare, or owner decision 63's audit
                          assignment; in an owner-bound repo only the owner's consented devices (§8.5) and their
                          EvsShares (owner decision 126); in the config and directory groups a leaf only for a
                          leaf-entitled device (§7.9); admitted, unrevoked, unparked, outside URnetwork platform
                          networks, key pinned, KeyPackage claimed for this group

                          revocation's signer from its leaf, a wrapped signer rotating instead; never the target
                          (RFC 9420 §12.2)
               check      its signed input: a SidecarRevoke or MemberRevoke (which a server deactivation

                          directory groups the target's loss of leaf entitlement at the auth pin under §7.9's
                          rank (it reads on by wraps), or staleness, whose input is §7.9's stale_leaf_days (90)

                          and the epochs' times; a stale-removed device returns by resync (KF5)
Rotation       committer  any writer that holds the key, as a holder or covered by a Delegation, at a pin
  alone                   covering what it rotates for, wrapped ones included (owner decision 114); in the config
                          group also the signer of the admission or revocation (owner decision 128) or, after

Self-update    committer  the leaf itself, by a path-only commit

External       committer  the sidecar itself
  commit       check      resync (same sidecar_id and key, removing at most its old leaf), or a recovery-admitted

          group, the signer of the statement it answers (owner decision 128) or, after the reap of an
```
