```text
          read_only (§7.9)
judged    at the delivery's auth, a STAGED one's being gen/<g>'s, only from my previous base to my tip, and
          invalid if a row above fails, an auth off my chain included; one above my tip waits until I reach
          it, one I cannot reach being withheld (§7.9's retain row); one before my previous base I do not
          judge, and it counts against no one
history   a delivery valid at its own state stays valid after its recipient's or signer's revocation, a key
          replacement or a replay, and poisons nothing later
use       the recipient opens only a delivery to itself and to a key it holds whose body verifies and whose
          RK_g matches C_g, then judges it as any member does
```

### 10.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| PublicMessage handshakes or a clear roster delta | GKM checks proposals or rosters | GKM reads credentials, proposals, the tree (RFC 9420 §16.4) or the roster | Ruled out (owner directive; [owner decision 59](#od-59)) |
| Every admitted sidecar a leaf | One key path; read is membership | A commit per CI join and reap; agents share the 1,000 leaves | Rejected ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) |
| Generations raised both by MLS commits and by wrapped writers | No separate claim object | Two paths mint g+1 and fork the ladder | Rejected (D-KEYS-15) |
| A rotation at every reap of a Delegation-covered agent | Each reap looks like a removal | Excludes nothing the Delegation's key still reads | Rejected (D-KEYS-16) |
| Suspend as a server-only control | No rotation or individual wraps when one agent pauses | A suspended agent opens what the server still delivers to its Delegation's key; the one-switch claim and §8.12's invariant would need another exception | Rejected (D-KEYS-16) |
| A time identity at each covered agent's own `not_after` | Keeps non-ephemeral admissions shorter than their Delegation | An admission landing after a rotation's pin would shorten a holder's life that the generation never saw; an ephemeral agent closes itself, or api reaps it, before any such cutoff | Rejected: §7.9 floors a non-ephemeral one at its Delegation's `not_after`, and an ephemeral one ends as a reap (D-KEYS-16) |
| 1,000 member devices per network, or a larger config tree | No member wraps | The cap refuses Teams past ~330 members; 5,000 leaves make a 7.9-14 MB tree and path commits to ~6 MB, past §18.4's budgets | Rejected ([owner decision 144](#od-144)) |
| Proxy re-encryption (PLAN.md:223, :284-327) | The server re-wraps headers blind | Semi-honest (PLAN.md:323), against D-TRUST-1; no supported Go pairings (golang.org/x/crypto/bn256 is deprecated: bn256.go:22-23) | Rejected |

### 10.11 Decisions proposed

**D-KEYS-1 (proposed).** MLS, built in house, distributes key-encryption keys under 10.5's hierarchy from v0 (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [43](#od-43)). *Why:* tree post-compromise security for KEKs; against a passive keychain copy, content keys heal only at the first generation after a device's next path commit and its copied ReaderKeys' 7-day not_after, and against an active clone only after a compromise revocation and a new enrollment (10.5); the ladder keeps §11's format distributor-independent.

**D-KEYS-2 (proposed).** One MLS group per evs repo, with a leaf per reading member device, at most 1,000; other readers hold ReaderWraps, and in the config and team directory groups so do member devices past §7.9's first 1,000, which commit there only wraps and rotations. *Why:* owner decisions [1](#od-1), [7](#od-7), [60](#od-60), [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144) and [182](#od-182).

**D-KEYS-3 (proposed).** Member commits are PrivateMessage whose clear header adds only the generation and the auth pin; only external commits are PublicMessage. *Why:* [owner decision 59](#od-59); the gate needs both.

**D-KEYS-4 (proposed).** Credential 0xF552 binds the MLS key to `sidecar_id` and the identity key under a config-repo `SidecarAdmit`; only the genesis rests on trust on first use, and owner-bound repos add only consented readers (10.9). *Why:* owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [126](#od-126); R-KEYS-8, R-KEYS-9.

**D-KEYS-5 (proposed).** GKM keeps no state of its own and orders, claims, delivers and retains through conditional object writes on its repo's metadata cluster, with acks as Redis soft state (10.6). *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2), [136](#od-136), [145](#od-145); RFC 9420 §14.

**D-KEYS-6 (proposed).** Commit before write: an authorization-log entry that shrinks a repo's key holders, or a holder's expiry, closes evs's gate (D-EVS-18) until a generation covering it is claimed (§7.9, 10.5), which is cause REMOVE (10.9); generations also rotate on request and every 30 days. *Why:* no server transaction changes readers ([owner decision 5](#od-5)), and an expired holder must lose new content as a removed one does (R-KEYS-4).

**D-KEYS-7 (withdrawn).** Superseded by owner decisions [113](#od-113) and [128](#od-128): the signed statement, not an admin committer, authorizes each membership change (10.9).

**D-KEYS-8 (proposed).** Drop keys in each generation's signed GenRotate give write-only deposits, which depositors accept only if the generation covers every shrink they know (10.5); each key domain is its own repo. *Why:* agents deposit sessions they cannot read (R-KEYS-9).

**D-KEYS-9 (proposed).** Rotating devices wrap each generation to every reading member's current `RecoveryBind` key; Team's only escrow is a visible audit reader. *Why:* owner decisions [62](#od-62), [63](#od-63), with no server-guessable secret.

**D-KEYS-10 (proposed).** M2's entry fixes the MLS wire's fields and the delivery wire's (ReaderKey, KeyDelivery, 10.6's wrap and recovery paths); its exit freezes them and suite 0x0010 on §22.10's 0x0010 interop artifact (10.4), with 10.4's conformance plan, fuzz targets run as Go tests and 10.6's sizes measured (§22.8); the security page says this MLS on draft suite 0x0010 is not independently audited. *Why:* owner decisions [99](#od-99), [101](#od-101), [119](#od-119) (§2.18).

**D-KEYS-11 (proposed).** Tagged, ephemeral, CI and cloud sidecars read and write through ReaderWraps, and live Delegations get DelegationWraps that cover their agents (10.5). *Why:* [owner decision 114](#od-114): no commits, and reads with no member online.

**D-KEYS-12 (proposed).** MLS is 10.4's subset on ciphersuite 0x0010 from v0, migrating through GroupForm and the ladder if IANA assigns this suite another value. *Why:* [owner decision 44](#od-44).

**D-KEYS-13 (proposed).** After a site loss, repo admins' devices, and for owner-bound kinds the owner's consented devices, re-seed each group from their keychains under a GroupForm linked through the ladder (10.8). *Why:* gkm has no off-site copy (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94)).

**D-KEYS-14 (proposed).** Groups scale by 10.6's sizes: 10.4's self-update interval, KF5's resync, GroupInfo on demand above 16 leaves, daily acks, trees on disk. *Why:* a full 1,000-leaf tree is 2.8 MB, which a per-epoch GroupInfo would rewrite about 143 times a day.

**D-KEYS-15 (proposed).** `gkm/<group_id>/gen/<g>`, created If-None-Match by the rotating writer, is the only place a generation exists; MLS commits never raise the generation, and a removal is a Remove commit followed by an independent rotation (10.5). *Why:* two paths minting g+1 fork the ladder; one claim object serializes every rotator (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128)).

**D-KEYS-16 (proposed).** KeyHolders are leaves (in the config and directory groups, member devices past their first 1,000 by wrap), uncovered agents, live Delegations over their reach (the config, a team's directory and the repos a grant names one of their tags for; a forwarding Delegation's, the config alone, its holder its sidecar's forwarding, which a newer one keeps; [owner decision 197](#od-197)) and recovery keys; live Delegations get DelegationWraps keyed by delegation_id; a covered agent's reap, or an ephemeral one's own `not_after`, is no shrink, and a Delegation's key drops at its end (`DelegationRevoke`, a void, or a compromise revocation of one of its agents; §7.9), at `not_after`, and at any other revocation but a reap, or any `Suspend`, of one of its agents, which no `Unsuspend` undoes (10.5). *Why:* [owner decision 114](#od-114)'s read-at-once, bounded, with no dropped party signing the rotation that excludes it; a suspended agent must lose what the server can still deliver to its Delegation's key, and an ephemeral agent can close itself, or api reap it, before any cutoff keyed to its own expiry.

**D-KEYS-17 (proposed).** Drop keys ride each generation's signed GenRotate, only for kinds that take deposits; a depositor seals only to a generation that covers every shrink and expiry it knows and is not below its pin; the deposit scope reaches only the drop-key route (10.6, 10.14). *Why:* a stale but unexpired drop key would reach a removed reader.

**D-KEYS-18 (proposed).** At most 16 leaves, the epoch object carries the sealed GroupInfo and `group-info` is a pointer rewritten at each Add and by gkm with any epoch 16 or more past it, resync probing to a 404; KF1 writes its first wraps, recovery wraps included, before evs activates the repo; above 16, recovery and resync need one leaf online (10.6-10.8). *Why:* a crash between two PUTs must not break code-only recovery.

**D-KEYS-19 (proposed).** `gkm:<group_id>` is versioned epoch × 2^24 + generation, and work hints go on the per-client `gkm` topic of the sidecars that must act (10.14). *Why:* same-epoch work hints and commit-less rotations must not be dropped as stale.

**D-KEYS-20 (proposed).** Retention never deletes a group's newest epoch, moves the `group-info` pointer before deleting the epoch it names, and keeps every GenRotate for the repo's life, as a gen/ object or in a gen pack (10.6, 10.16). *Why:* the next commit needs its predecessor, and code-only recovery needs no epoch history.

**D-KEYS-21 (proposed).** gkm acks are Redis soft state, and the epoch reconciler deletes only while the ack family is 30 days old; a GroupInfo above 16 leaves is written at most once per epoch, on request. *Why:* acks are rebuildable ([owner decision 136](#od-136)), and a 1,000-leaf GroupInfo costs ~0.7 MB on each drive.

**D-KEYS-22 (proposed).** The search index's document keys derive from `ref` (RK_1), and its keyed pad from a per-generation `index` key that each shard's header names. In slot-keyed repos each versionless index file keeps one key, in a slot only that path's versions name, until a REMOVE generation, a CLOSURE or a rekey replaces it (§11.7). *Why:* document keys must survive rotations, or every rotation reindexes the repo; a removed reader must not predict new shards' sizes; and an ERASE must reach postings ([owner decision 61](#od-61)) without a slot object per index write ([owner decision 140](#od-140)).

**D-KEYS-23 (proposed).** The team directory's group follows §7.9's leaves rule as the config group does: the first 1,000 live member devices are leaves, and later member devices and agents read by per-generation wraps ([owner decision 182](#od-182)). An admission's signer seats its subject at once; gkm hints only the statement's signer and the config writers, and other writers rotate only for a push the gate refuses, after up to 15 s of jitter (10.9). *Why:* every admitted sidecar reads the directory, and §8.12's data-repo seats would leave members of a large Team keyless; every sidecar but read_only ones also writes it, so hinting every writer would race rotations that each stage a wrap per wrapped reader.

**D-KEYS-24 (proposed).** Every ReaderWrap and DelegationWrap is a typed `KeyDelivery` whose immutable identity, in its path `wrap/<g>/<c8>/<recipient>/<k8>`, its body and its wrap_aad, includes the recipient key it seals to, so a delivery to one ReaderKey never blocks, replaces or opens as one to another, and a rebind's RecoveryWraps take their binding's own path (10.6, 10.8). A STAGED delivery is its claim's and is judged against the claim's holder set; a LATE one, first or replacement, carries its signer's AuthPin and time, is judged at that state, may be signed by any holder that is not read_only, and stays valid after later revocations (10.9). *Why:* a fresh ReaderKey needs a delivery its old one's object cannot occupy, and a delivery made after its generation's claim needs its own authorization state, which neither the claim's pin nor a verifier's newer one gives.

**D-KEYS-25 (proposed).** A ReaderKey is valid at most 7 days after signing and replaced at 6 days, its private key kept 30 days past its not_after, and rotators and deliverers seal only to an unexpired one valid no longer than that; so a passive keychain copy heals at the first generation after the device's next path commit and that not_after, about 37 days after the copy (60 above 50 leaves) whatever advertisement gkm serves, and an active clone, which signs fresh keys, ends only at a compromise revocation and a new enrollment (10.5). *Why:* gkm serves one overwriteable advertisement with no authenticated retirement, so only the key's own validity bounds a stale one, and whoever holds an identity key can sign another.

**D-KEYS-26 (proposed).** gkm's routes take 10.6's scopes: a sidecar's own ReaderKey and KeyPackages under any gkm token of its own; reads, acks and a member device's commits under r; GroupInfo and deliveries under r from a sidecar that is not read_only; claims, Welcomes and KeyPackage claims under rw; members, not gkm, check what a commit carries (10.9). *Why:* reader-only and read_only leaves must keep their keys and leaves current (D-TEAM-24), and gkm cannot see a PrivateMessage's proposals.

### 10.12 Open questions

**Q-KEYS-1.** [X12] Build MLS or fork it? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 43](#od-43)):** build 10.4's subset in house (~5-8k lines); its audit is deferred ([owner decision 99](#od-99)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-2.** [X12] Which ciphersuite? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 44](#od-44)):** 0x0010 (X-Wing, Ed25519) from v0; groups migrate through the ladder if IANA assigns another value. *Residual:* post-quantum confidentiality against a passive adversary only; a future Ed25519 forgery is retroactive through the ladder (10.5, §2.18) until 10.16's hybrid signatures.

**Q-KEYS-3.** [X12] At what granularity are groups formed? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 60](#od-60)):** per repo, grants mapping onto membership; agents hold wraps ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-4.** [X12] What do "GKM" and "one session key stored in GKM" mean? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 59](#od-59)):** a DS plus wrapped, laddered generations (10.5) in the file cluster. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-5.** What admission evidence must a credential carry? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110)):** a config-repo `SidecarAdmit` chained to the genesis, subsuming DeviceAdmit; a member's own device may sign it ([owner decision 112](#od-112)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-6.** Is per-entry crypto-shredding required? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 61](#od-61)):** for record-class repos and mail, through format 1's key slots. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-7.** How does a member recover after losing every device? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 62](#od-62)):** a recovery code receiving wraps under a signed, rotatable binding, plus admin re-add of team repos (10.8); its key counts as one of k after a 72 h veto window ([owner decision 127](#od-127)); a binding the cascade restored admits only through that window, its device anchoring on a config ReaderWrap ([owner decision 149](#od-149)). *Residual:* §2.10's row for an operator colluding with a recovery-code thief: the code opens its wraps at once, whatever the window or a veto, and after a rebind or a cascade void stops new wraps keeps opening what was wrapped to it and reads the current generation until the next rotation, which `RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}` makes a remove rotation with a path epoch at once (revoking the device it admitted does not retire it), and keychain backups sealed before a rebind stay open to the old code (10.8).

**Q-KEYS-8.** Should teams get escrow? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 63](#od-63)):** a visible audit reader on a customer-operated device, a Team opt-in in v1, never silent (10.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-9.** [X12] Does v0 ship MLS, or per-device wraps with MLS in v1? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 1](#od-1)):** MLS in v0 (PLAN.md:44); agents' wraps carry its generations ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-10.** Is 10.8 the right reading of PLAN.md:50 and :338? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 64](#od-64)):** lazy rewrap, a full checkpoint at the first write after a `remove` generation, plus `ur evs rekey`. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-11.** How long does GKM keep epoch objects? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a), 30 days, then until every leaf that acked in the last 30 days has applied them, on four conditions (10.6): the newest epoch is never deleted, and the `group-info` pointer moves before the epoch it names goes; nothing the ladder, resync or recovery needs lives in an epoch (generations are `gen/` objects, GroupInfo rides in the newest epoch at 16 leaves or fewer or in `group-info` above, and recovery wraps are their own objects), so a device past retention resyncs from GroupInfo; a preservation hold pauses the sweep ([owner decision 133](#od-133)); and §19.9 sizes the family at M2's benchmark: a 10-leaf group keeps about 42 commits of 11-17 KB plus inline GroupInfo (1.2-1.9 MB), a 1,000-leaf group about 26 MB. *Residual:* §19.9's measured size.

**Q-KEYS-12.** [X12; directive residual] Which header values does gkm see? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 115](#od-115)):** 10.6's rows: ciphertext, group id, epoch, sizes and sidecar ids (membership, as api-7 shows it; [owner decision 72](#od-72)), never, in a member commit, a proposal, credential change, tree or key; external commits show gkm-6's values. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-13.** Does [owner decision 7](#od-7)'s "only from keys allowed to grant" bind the committer or the change? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 113](#od-113)):** (b) the change (10.9), withdrawing D-KEYS-7. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-14.** Who commits the config group's membership changes, when only admins write config records (§8.8)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 128](#od-128)):** (a) also the leaf that signed the admission or revocation; recovery-admitted devices self-join by external commit (10.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-15.** How many member devices may one network hold, given the config group's 1,000-leaf cap? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)):** (b), with no member-device cap: from the start, member devices past the first 1,000 read the config group by per-generation wraps, as agents do, and stay leaves of their data repos, each still at most 1,000 leaves, amending [owner decision 114](#od-114) for the config group only; §20.4 keeps 5,000 Team admissions. §7.9's `leaves` rule ranks and promotes (10.4); wrapped devices commit no config-group Add or Remove, so a wrapped signer writes an admission's first wrap or a revocation's rotation, and the next leaf commit removes a leaf (10.9). Cost: ~1.3 KB of wrap per wrapped device per config rotation. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-16.** Cross-cutting (§7.9, §8.12). How does the team directory's group seat every admitted sidecar? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 182](#od-182)):** (a), its own MLS group under §7.9's leaves rule, extending [owner decision 144](#od-144) to one more group, at ~1.3 KB a wrap per overflow device per rotation (options (b), keys derived from the config group, and (c), data-repo seats, not taken). 10.4 and 10.9 apply it with the config group's committers, gkm hinting only a statement's signer and the config writers, since every sidecar but read_only ones writes the directory. *Residual:* none.

### 10.13 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:147** ("participants are leaves"). Member devices are leaves ([owner decision 60](#od-60)); agents hold wraps ([owner decision 114](#od-114) on Q-ACL-9; D-KEYS-11), as do member devices past the first 1,000 in the config and team directory groups (owner decisions [144](#od-144) and [182](#od-182) on Q-KEYS-15 and Q-KEYS-16).
- **PLAN.md:148.** Per-object keys are wrapped under RK_g, which the epoch KEK or a holder's wrap delivers (Q-KEYS-4).
- **PLAN.md:221.** Narrowed by the owner directive: gkm holds ciphertext plus 10.6's header values (Q-KEYS-12).
- **PLAN.md:223, :284-327.** Proxy re-encryption is rejected (10.10).

### 10.14 Interfaces

- **Provides:** `GkmClient` (`CurrentRepoKey`, `RepoKey(repoId, generation)`, `EnsureWritable`, which first commits the pending changes its device may, `DropKey`); `EvsRepoKey.DeriveKey(purpose, context)`; credential validation and pins (also for §6's `Hello`); GenRotates and drop keys, ReaderWraps and DelegationWraps (`KeyDelivery`, 10.5) with 10.9's delivery checks, and recovery wraps; 10.5's KeyHolders and 10.6's gate predicate (§7.9, §11.8, §11.12).
- **Consumes:** keys, bindings, keychain, recovery code, `SidecarEvent` (§5); topics, `Signed`, `HeadCheck` (§6); tokens, `rev/` (§7.8); the authorization log, `AuthPin`, causal identities, recovery, the `leaves` rule and removals (§7.9, §7.10); `RepoReaders`, seats, kind defaults, consent, `OwnerConfirm`, access logs, `audit`, `EvsShare` (§8); kinds, `repo/` state, `place/`, slots, manifests, path epochs, the head-CAS gate and the write budget (§11); `ServiceHost.Blobs` per cluster and Redis (§4.5, §19).
- **Subprotocol messages:** `GkmHint{group_id, epoch, kind, recipient}` in `PushHint` (§6.11, 0x1301): commit on `gkm:<group_id>` (version = epoch × 2^24 + generation); pending, welcome, key-packages-low and wrap-pending (a GenWrap, wrap or sealed GroupInfo is missing; for 10.6's late wraps, `recipient` names the ask's `s:` or `d:` recipient, and a hint lost or coalesced comes again at the next ask) on the per-client `gkm` topic (§6.8).
- **API routes:** Client class, under 10.6's tokens and scopes, specified in connect/api/bringyour.yml.

  ```text
  POST /gkm/key-packages, /gkm/key-packages/claim, /gkm/reader-key;  GET /gkm/reader-key/<sidecar_id>
  POST /gkm/groups;  GET /gkm/groups/<id>;  POST /gkm/repos/<id>/forms    (GroupForm: create, re-form)
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/epochs?after=          epoch objects, in order, with their sizes
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/epochs/<n>             200, 409 (with the winner), 403, 429
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/gen/<g>                the claim: 201, 412 (with the winner), 403, 429
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/wraps/<g>/<c8>         staged or late ReaderWraps and DelegationWraps: 201, 412 (with
                                               the winner), 403, 409 (stale kind, generation or key), 429
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/welcome/<n>, /group-info, /ack (Redis)
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/gen?since=;  GET /gkm/welcomes
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/wraps/<g>?recipient=&want=<k8>&since=   the caller's deliveries of g, the object at
                                               want first, the recipient's prefix on a miss, which hints
                                               wrap-pending (10.6's late wraps)
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/drop-key?since=<g>     deposit, r, rw, admin: the newest GenRotate, up to 64 after since
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/group-info?want=<epoch>  sealed; an older one also hints wrap-pending (KF5)
  GET|POST|DELETE /gkm/recovery/<member_id>/wraps  GET also under an unadmitted client's recovery:<member_id>,
                                                   for that member's own wraps only (§7.8, §7.9)
  ```
- **Tables:** none; gkm's durable state is 10.6's objects (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [21](#od-21), [145](#od-145)), and Redis `{gka_<group_id>}` holds acks as soft state ([owner decision 136](#od-136)).
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/gkm` hosts `gkmservice` from v0; root `mls_*` and `gkm_*` files and the nested `mlsinterop/` test module (D-REPO-2, D-REPO-3, D-OPS-2); the reconciler (retention, hints, staged-wrap GC) in taskworker; limits in config/all/pro.yml.
- **Assumptions about other sections:**
  - §7.9 defines the authorization log, `AuthPin`, the causal identities (a compromise retirement shrinks though a rebind keeps the holder's identity; ReaderKey lapses are no expiry, 10.5) and `holders_shrunk_at`, `RecoveryBind` and its reasons, `stale_leaf_days`, Delegations, the recovery window, `anchor` and `restored` order, the compromise cascade, the Delegations it voids and the bindings it restores, which take no wrap until re-signed, the Delegations it or a `DelegationRevoke` ends, parking their agents admitted from `since_n`, the scoped rule giving each Delegation-signed admission exactly the Delegation's tags and, unless ephemeral, a not_after no earlier than its own, with `max_admits` counted for the Delegation's life, and the `leaves` rule of the config and directory groups, refusing a not_after on a member device's admission; §7.8 gives member devices other than read_only ones gkm `rw` in the config group, every sidecar but read_only ones `rw` in the team directory, and issues the `deposit` and `recovery:<member_id>` scopes; §7.10 and §8.12 name 10.9's committers, §7.10 also the reaped agent's admission signer, §8.12 the data repos' seats, which the directory does not take, and §8.5 consent and the directory kind default (every admitted sidecar of a team network reads, every one not read_only writes; §16.11), and §8.6's ceiling passes the config kind default's read row, so ephemeral sidecars read the config as 10.5's depositor rule needs; §7.9's read_only row accepts a read_only device's own ReaderKeys, KeyPackages, path-only commits, resyncs and acks under its r scopes and refuses its wraps and GroupInfo (10.6's scopes), and §5.9 keeps ReaderKeys and their private keys as 10.5's readerkey row says; §5.4 alarms on admissions a member's devices did not sign and raises `head_alarm` (fork) on a failed recovery anchor, and §5.9 has each device re-seal `keychain.wrap` at every change to its member's current binding, a void included, with no HPKE copy while none is current.
  - §11.8 enforces 10.6's predicate at each ref's head CAS, reissuing a timed-out head PUT only within 5 s of its validation, owns `place/` and lists the first cluster's families, gkm's per-sidecar objects included; §11 owns path epochs (authorization expiries batched within 24 h), §11.7's checkpoint after a REMOVE generation, deletion (its shred deleting the group's gkm objects and `{gka_}`, again after 10 min; a re-seed's GroupForm the only gkm route it admits while deleted), mirrors, re-seeding and §11.13's write budget, whose inputs count expiry rotations and path epochs; §19.6 sets the 10 s store request deadline; §19.9 sizes gkm's objects, gen/ unpacked until 10.16's packs start, expiry rotations, the config and directory groups' rotation wraps and the first cluster's per-sidecar ones included.
  - §11.14 derives search-index document keys under `ref` and shard pads under `index` through `EvsRepoKey.DeriveKey`, keeps each index file's key in its path's own slot in slot-keyed repos (§11.7), and destroys an erased document's index files' old slot keys by its ERASE.
  - §22.7 covers 10.5-10.9's cases, the gate's 412 (a compromise rebind's at the old generation included), an expired RepoGrant's REMOVE rotation, checkpoint and path epoch (FS-18), gkm accepting a generation-0 recovery self-join, a reap's config rotation by the admission's signer, an admin-only admission never reading its member's vault or mailbox, a recovery self-join with no leaf online, FS-20 also killing KF1's creator before activation and gkm between an epoch 16 past the pointer and the pointer's rewrite, a 1,001st member device reading the config and the team directory by wrap, the directory group's hint audience and rotation wait (10.9) and FS-87's directory Removes and rotation reaching leaves and wraps, and a Team member whose only device was stolen recovering by the restored code, its device anchoring after the window on its config ReaderWrap (a forged one raising `head_alarm`), then self-joining, KF2 adding it elsewhere; FS-6 holds a gkm commit at a barrier across a --now shred and restores a repo re-seeded as deleted; FS-103 to FS-106 test delivery identity, delivery authority, copied keychains and key upkeep under r; §22.8's M2 benchmark measures 10.6's sizes and drive costs, a 1,000-leaf group on the iOS surrogate cell and 1 h requested grants on large repos included; its schedules lose the ack family and race a repo's placement, its group landing on the repo's cluster.

### 10.15 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| The unreviewed in-house MLS misreads RFC 9420 or skips a check ([owner decision 99](#od-99)) | Medium | Critical | 10.4's subset, conformance plan and 0x0010 gate; disclosure (§2.18, [owner decision 119](#od-119)) |
| IANA assigns this suite another value, or X-Wing changes | Medium | Medium | Migration through GroupForm and the ladder ([owner decision 44](#od-44)) |
| An operator substitutes a network's first device at trust on first use | Low | High | Safety numbers; genesis in invites and auth keys |
| Every app device's forwarding Delegation adds a DelegationWrap of about 1.2 KB to each config rotation, about 6 MB at a 5,000-device team's ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) | High | Low | config rotations follow removals and the 30-day schedule, not rule edits; a newer forwarding Delegation is no shrink (10.5) |
| A copied forwarding reader key opens the config generations wrapped to it until its Delegation ends | Low | Medium | it never leaves the VPN component (§5.9); the app rotates it at every new client generation and after 90 days; `DelegationRevoke` shrinks the config at once (10.5) |
| A member stalls a group with a commit the others refuse | Low | Medium | Alarms; revocation; re-forming (10.9) |
| A rogue or compromised admin admits a device under a member | Medium | Medium | Consent gates owner-bound repos ([owner decision 126](#od-126); 10.9); the member's devices alarm (§5.4); team repos stay readable until revocation |
| A removed leaf stays in a repo's MLS tree until a writer leaf commits its Remove (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)) | Medium | Low | Wrapped writers' rotations reopen the gate meanwhile, and no leaf wrap uses an epoch that holds it (10.5); hints wake writer leaves |
| A reaped Delegation-admitted agent, an ephemeral one past its own `not_after`, or a leaked reader seed reads later config, directory and tag-repo generations, and a leaked whole auth key admits fresh agents ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) | Medium | High | `not_after` ≤ 90 d (30 d for CI), replaced at each CI secret rotation and after a key drop; any `Suspend` or non-reap revocation of its agents, or a cascade voiding it, drops the key; a `DelegationRevoke` or a compromise revocation of one of its agents ends its admissions (10.5, §7.9) |
| Large groups strain phones (10.6's sizes); a large Team's leaves sit in two 1,000-leaf groups, the config's and the directory's | Medium | Medium | D-KEYS-14; §22.8's benchmark |
| Short grants (1 h requested grants) expire often, and each covering generation is REMOVE, so files re-checkpoint at their next write and a repo's batched path epoch recurs daily, ~17 h of copying for a 1M-file ref (§11.6) | Medium | Medium | One rotation covers every expiry up to its time_ms, and writers batch them at a pending hint or their next write (KF4); 16-diff chains checkpoint anyway; at most one batched path epoch per repo a day (§11.6); §11.13's inputs and §19.9's gen/ row count these rotations and epochs, and §22.8's fixture of 1 h requested grants on large repos reports rotations, full checkpoints and path-epoch copy operations a day |
| A config or directory rotation stages a wrap per wrapped reader and a RecoveryWrap per member, up to ~6,000 objects (~7.5 MB, ~50 MiB a drive) at §20.4's 5,000 Team admissions, and a wrap per leaf more if its rotator is wrapped; the directory, whose writers push often, rotates at nearly every shrink of a Team's sidecars, and racing rotators would multiply each | Medium | Low | A leaf rotator's one LeafWrap covers every leaf; covered agents' reaps rotate nothing (10.5); the directory group hints only a statement's signer and the config writers, and unhinted writers rotate after a jitter (10.9); §11.13 runs REMOVE rotations at once as P0, never refusing them, so many large Teams shrinking at once can wear a cluster's drives past the budget ([owner decision 186](#od-186); §11.21's P0 row), and §19.9's projection counts both groups' rotations |
| With no witness, shared writes stop at `witness_bound_hours` (default 72 h), a lone cloud agent's included (§2.8's bound, which a split defeats) | Medium | Medium | Agents witness ([owner decision 129](#od-129)); 24 h alarm; up to 168 h; Removes, rotations and revocations never stop |
| After a void leaves M no current binding, M, its network's only config writer, loses every device: no config writer remains to give the device M's restored code admits its ReaderWrap (KF2), so it anchors only once a config holder that is not read_only, among the up to 64 other holders gkm hints 15 min after its ask (10.6's late wraps), runs, and never if none does ([owner decision 149](#od-149)) | Low | High | M's devices raise `recovery_rebind` at the void (§5.4), and any of them can run `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9) to bind a code that takes wraps; meanwhile only surviving RecoveryWraps open (10.8) |
| A device offline past its ReaderKey's 7-day not_after gets no staged wrap and, back with a new key, waits for a late delivery, longer where no writer is online | Medium | Low | Lapsed private keys kept 30 days for what was staged (10.5); any holder but a read_only one delivers, gkm hinting writers, then after 15 min up to 64 other holders (10.6); a leaf also takes the next GenWrap |

| Site loss erases every gkm object ([owner decision 94](#od-94)) | Low | Critical | Device re-seed (D-KEYS-13); owner-device mirrors |

### 10.16 Phasing

- **v0 (M2):** all of 10.4-10.9 but v1's items, with `directory` among `ur_group`'s kinds (§11.12), D-KEYS-10's gates, D-KEYS-14's scaling and `ur evs rekey`, a client job that re-checkpoints every file of a repo under the current generation in multi-part pushes of at most 1,024 entry writes, at most 50 files/s per repo, resumable from its last committed push.
- **v1:** the Team audit reader ([owner decision 63](#od-63)), and with Team at M6 the config group's wraps for member devices past the first 1,000 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)) and the team directory's group under the same leaves rule ([owner decision 182](#od-182)); at M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)), the `index` purpose, with storage format 2's search index ([owner decision 163](#od-163); §11.14), and format 2's one slot key per versionless path (§11.7).
- **Later:** 0x0020 by migration, with hybrid Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 authority signatures; SafeExportSecret (draft-ietf-mls-extensions-11); key transparency; moving a group with its repo once a move tool exists ([owner decision 145](#od-145)); gen packs, once §19.9's projection from §22.8's M2 count needs them: taskworker writes `gkm/<group_id>/genpack/<k>`, holding gen/<256k+1>..<256k+256> verbatim, If-None-Match with repo/ rechecked as for every gkm write, once 64 newer generations exist, then deletes those objects, a retry that finds the pack verifying it and resuming the deletes; a read falls back from `gen/<g>`'s 404 to `genpack/<⌊(g-1)/256⌋>`, and a claim still needs `gen/<g-1>` as an object, so none lands at or below a pack; packs count as gen/ for every other rule (gkm-7's life of the repo, shreds and their 10-minute repeat, re-seeds) and hold no slot, so erasure is unchanged.
- **Dependencies:** §7.9's authorization log and config repo, §8.5's consent, §11's format 1 and §19's conditional writes block v0; §22.8's M2 benchmark sets §19.9's epoch-retention size (Q-KEYS-11's residual).

## 11. Encrypted versioned storage: format, git service, head API, subscriptions

### 11.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns evs repos and kinds, `config` and `directory` included; the format and what the server sees (X2, [owner decision 2](#od-2)); the file-cluster objects, their placement and the push, commit and read protocols; refs and their modes, record streams and deposits; git compatibility and the local tier (X19, [owner decision 24](#od-24)); subscriptions; per-object versioning, the versionless purge and the drop-history action (11.7, 11.13; [owner decision 173](#od-173)); GC and evacuation, the metadata write budget and fair share, quotas, durability, deletion and export; and the encrypted search index's placement, format, upkeep, erasure and read path, with remote search, an app host's "search more" answered end to end by a designated indexer (11.14; owner decisions [175](#od-175), [178](#od-178)), whose search tools are §16's and §18's.

Keys come from §10, identity from §5, push from §6, tokens, the projection and grants from §7 and §8, hardware from §19 (X13), quotas from §20 and layouts from §15 and §16. The metadata clusters also store, and 11.13 budgets, §7's `proj/`, `projrows/` and `rev/`, §10's `gkm/` and §21's `hold/` objects.
