```text
          this subsection's plan over the buckets, retained buckets and all it holds, plus its local overlay for
          pushes past indexed_through that its text covers, verifying against its mirror, mounted tree or bare
          repository (11.11, 11.13), with masks, newest wins and searchable_days; it reads nothing from evs, api or
          gkm for a remote search, reporting in coverage what it lacks, so evs sees nothing of one on either device;
          a daemon designated for search keeps all of every repo it reads within Search.CacheByteCount (16 GiB),
          answers no index-off repo (REFUSED_INDEX_OFF), holds at most 8 MiB of working set a search, its masks
          probing the version table (newest, above), and persists no query (§5.9, D-CORE-17)
phones    never serve: readers ignore search on a read_only or ephemeral subject, ur indexer add refuses it on an
          app host, and app-host builds set Search.RemoteServe false and never advertise bit 0; a laptop daemon may
          serve, within the CPU window
merge     per (repo, ref, doc_key) over the remote pages and the phone's own hits: the higher version wins, and at
          one version a remote verified state wins; in a SERVED_TEXT repo a local possible or near hit with time_ms
          above checked_through_ms and at most ref_time_ms - 10 min that no page returned moves to a collapsed "n
          not matched by <device>" row; the phone's own confirmed hits always stay, hits newer than the pinned
          version keep the phone's state, and SERVED_INDEX hits merge as possible, dropping nothing; a hit from a
          repo the request did not name or the phone does not read is dropped with an alarm; the phone's ERASE
          and erasure-set masks and read checks (§5.9) apply; an opened hit is extracted and checked against the
          query, its doc_key and version, and a mismatch, or a local confirmed hit inside the checked span that
          no page
          returned, raises SidecarEvent search_alarm {mismatch or omission, indexer, repo} (§5.4), three mismatches
          in a day skipping that indexer for 24 h
```

**Erasure, holds, limits, on and off.**

```text
keys      in slot-keyed repos (record-class repos, group inboxes) each versionless index file keeps one key (settings
          is versioned), in a slot that only
          that path's versions name, reused by each next version until checkpoint rule (4), a CLOSURE or a rekey
          draws a fresh one in a new slot (11.7's versionless keys), so an overwrite writes no slot; in general
          repos it sits in the segment header (11.6) and goes with the segment
cut       an erasure's first push on the index's ref (the entry's own, or ur/index) is its CUT (11.12): it adds its
          documents to the ref's erasure set (x, Files and format) and moves the ref's index_epoch, so every index
          push but a CLOSURE built before it is refused and rebuilt without them (commit path's epoch row); readers
          mask each listed document, at or below its version, from the CUT on; a set version from a signer who may
          not erase its documents is ignored and alarms (the directory, §16.11)
erase     at a head at or after its CUT the eraser lists every index file holding the document: each writer's slots
          and large entries in each bucket, the bucket shard holding it, and the one all shard holding it, found by
          a/m's days and that shard's doc table (I-EVS-11), a list no later push lengthens; CLOSURE pushes on the
          index's ref rewrite each in place without the document (at the storage limit or while spent, in pairs
          sized to the eraser's allowance, 11.13's wait), padded to the replaced version's exact length, so 11.12's
          rekey bound holds and the size shows nothing, each under a fresh key in a new slot; each pair's ERASE
          destroys the old slots' keys (the entry's own going with the erasure's first ERASE, owner decision 61), and
          every stored version of those files, staged bytes still in a batch included, shares one of them; the purge
          deletes the old ciphertext and slots a minute later; the ERASEs also name the key of every index path whose
          retained version still holds the document (a version a hold kept, a writer slot reused after a merge, a
          shard the document left, a bucket a roll-up removed, found from the ref's history), a live one rewritten
          under a fresh key by a CLOSURE first, so no stored version keeps an openable key (owner decisions 61,
          133; FI-19); a CLOSURE refused 409 for a path another push changed after the list rereads that path's
          history and rebuilds; no watch follows an ERASE, and no indexer takes part
bound     an erasure's cost is the index file versions erase lists, not its document count: one message or entry with
          one version is one document per 1 MiB chunk of its text, each chunk in a writer's slot or a large entry,
          then a bucket shard, then all, and a backfill, a late companion push, an absorbed slot or a hold adds
          copies; 11.13's wait row bounds it from those bytes, the eraser's allowance and its turns (owner decision
          146; §20.7), and the eraser's device shows what is left (§5.4's erasure event); staged slots count as the
          CLOSURE's inline records
writers   a writer whose head an erasure rewrote, or whose push a CUT outdated, gets 409 at its next push and
          re-applies its entries without the erasure set's documents (commit path)
holds     a hold keeps the index content that existed at its placement, staged copies written to seg/ at
          evacuation, and later churn is purged as usual, since a hold collects nothing new (11.13's hold rule;
          owner decisions 133, 161); it never pauses an ERASE, so slot-keyed index content stays unreadable
limit     at the storage limit or while spent, heads ride content pushes and stop with them; merges, roll-ups and
          builds add payload and wait, search answering from the partitions as they stand; an erasure's CUT is
          maintenance, and its CLOSURE is taken within 11.12's bounds and its eraser's allowance, each index file
          one ?closure=1 upload
drop      a DROP push also rewrites in place, without the listed versions, each index file holding a listed version
          of a dropped path, padded to the replaced length as erase's rewrite is, with no ERASE or CLOSURE flag; the
          kept head's entries enter the signer's own head full, since no older version stays as a base; the purge
          deletes the replaced ciphertext a minute later, and a writer whose head it rewrote re-applies (writers,
          above); a signer not holding the index leaves the rewrite to an indexer serving the repo for search, else
          the next capable writer, within 10 min as a backfill, searches masking the older version meanwhile (newest
          wins); the rewrite lands at commit, so a cancel loses nothing; hosts with the text reproduce it and raise
          index_mismatch on one that left a listed version's postings; a DROP refused 409 INDEX_EPOCH is rebuilt and
          signed again by its device under the person's same confirmation, or sent without its index rewrites, left
          to that backfill
off       an admin's settings version turns the index off (never the team directory's); that device, or an
          indexer, removes <root> but settings in one push listing each file, whose content the purge deletes,
          the ref's erasure set staying for a later build to apply, and never DELETEing ur/index, which would
          drop the settings file whose absence means on; at the storage
          limit or while spent the settings version, a new inline record, is refused, so the device removes the
          files first (a deletion, accepted), writes the off version once under the limit and not spent, then
          removes heads writers re-created meanwhile
on        a device holding the repo's text builds the index under the lock: documents changed in the latest windows
          into their buckets' shards, older ones into all, in pushes of parts, the erasure set's documents left out
          (commit path's epoch row); migration to storage format 2 builds it the same way (§23)
rebuild   a new normalizer or index format builds .ur-index/i2 beside .ur-index/i1, then removes i1; the ref's
          erasure set and index_epoch serve both roots
site loss the index re-seeds as versionless files do, its erasure set first, or a device holding the text rebuilds
          it, applying that set: an indexer serving the repo for search, else its next capable writer (§19.10; owner
          decision 177)
```

**What the server sees** (§2.8's evs-26):

```text
shape     one versionless directory per indexed ref, or the ur/index ref: a small staged overwrite in each indexed
          push (the writer's head, whose size step shows roughly how much text the push indexed, as its content
          sizes already do); a shard rewrite per ~128 KiB of entries; once per window a bulk removal and shard
          rewrites, rarely with one newer bucket's file rewritten in place (roll-up's step 4); CUTs and CLOSUREs at
          erasure (a CUT a staged rewrite of its ref's erasure set, whose size step shows roughly how many
          documents pending erasures hold, and a 409 INDEX_EPOCH for each index push it outdates), and a drop's
          rewrites, shaped as an erasure's; on ur/index, pushes that trail content pushes by up to a minute on
          1 KiB blocks, else five minutes (owner decision 172)
reads     which index files each device reads, and when (evs-4, evs-7): a first sync of a repo's index, a fetch to
          verify and each opened hit show that the device read those files, and a phone's or browser's on-demand
          "search more" that no indexer answered, that its person searched past the buckets; background sync and
          reproduction hide most of it
remote    an app host's remote search: relays see each request's and page's time and fixed size, and api's contract
          rows each contract's creation and, for a pair that §6.11's bit 1 marks, one report a contract at each
          §6.10 window's end, both directions, the window's floor whatever up to five exchanges ran in it (C19;
          owner decisions 176, 188); evs sees nothing (§2.8's connect-5)
never     a query, which documents match it, or which trigrams documents share: fetches follow sync position, sizes
          are Padmé-padded (shards by the keyed pad as well), and nothing is compressed across documents
```

### 11.15 Performance and concurrency (verified in §22)

| Path | Target |
|---|---|
| Commit → hint at an online subscriber | p50 ≤ 300 ms, p99 ≤ 2 s |
| Local push (≤ 64 KiB) → remote commit, desktop | p50 ≤ 1 s |
| Agent commit on device A → visible on device B | p50 ≤ 2 s, p99 ≤ 5 s |
| Head read, file ≤ 1 MiB | p50 ≤ 250 ms on desktop, ≤ 600 ms on mobile |
| Head read 100 versions behind its pin | statements ≤ 100 KiB, verify ≤ 20 ms on mobile |
| Head read of a path a later 100,000-change push left alone | adjacent-leaf proofs of ~1.4 KiB a path level, never its change list |
| Throughput per repo | ≥ 50 MB/s on desktop, ≥ 5 MB/s on mobile |
| evs working set | ≤ 4 MiB in the iOS app process (§18.4); never a whole file, segment or delta base over 1 MiB in RAM |
| Drive writes per push on the metadata set | ≤ 43 KiB per drive at 2× year one's mix; ≤ 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS at any load but P0 work past the refill, which [owner decision 186](#od-186) exempts (11.13) |
| Versionless content after its replacement | readable ≥ 60 s; deleted within ~2 min, ≤ ~26 h when its committing process failed (the sweep) |
| Staged versionless content | ≤ 4 KiB per drive a version; no HDD write when replaced before its batch's evacuation |
| Index entries per push | proportional to the changed text where 11.14's dependency row allows a diff (an edit in the current bucket onto a base outside every head, or composed onto its own head diff's base), else the document's whole key set, as when another writer's head holds its previous version; a 1 MiB document per changed chunk of a large file (11.14) |
| Drive writes per indexed push | in-ref ~7 KiB on 4 KiB blocks, ~4.3 on 1 KiB; a companion push a whole push, at most one a minute per writer on 1 KiB blocks, else one every 5 minutes (11.13; [owner decision 172](#od-172)) |
| Latest buckets, 100 messages a day | both ≤ ~5.4 MB; each file ≤ 1 MiB, decrypted by frame within the working set above |
| Search masks | one probe per candidate, lazily in rank order, into §5.9's version table through 256 KiB of cached pages a process; no set of the partitions' keys in memory; the table updated at a swap within 1 MiB (11.14) |
| Cold "search more" | first progress ≤ 500 ms; each shard's hits ≤ 100 ms after it lands, ≤ 300 ms on phones and page Workers; complete within the missing bytes over the throughput, plus 1 s (§16.10's cold contract) |
| A drop | nothing deleted before `not_before_ms` + 25 min, nor before evacuation's horizon passes the drop's commit by 2 min, about 25 to 26 h after a `now` drop ([owner decision 204](#od-204)); a job's two passes read ≤ 32 MB/s; 10,000 segments deleted in about 17 min; ≤ ~0.3 MB written a metadata drive for a drop whose job runs 10 min |

**Concurrency.** Pushes to one ref meet only at its head's If-Match: a file-mode loser with disjoint paths retries inside evs, so one ref sustains roughly 20-50 pushes/s; a git-mode loser gets a stock non-fast-forward and merges. Distinct refs never contend. In the twenty-agent test (§22), agents write their own refs in real time, and a merge into main every 60 s meets another in its ~60 ms window about 2% of the time, then merges again.

### 11.16 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plaintext paths (PLAN.md:59), or a sealed client index ordered in Postgres (the drafted Q-EVS-1 (c)) | Server-side paths; or only repos and refs visible | Names, shape and sizes in the clear; or 3-RTT cold reads, client-side GC, Postgres on the storage path | Ruled out (owner directive; [owner decision 2](#od-2)) |
| A per-ref lock with a fencing token | No retries | One more round trip; a stalled holder still writes, since no store condition spans two objects | Rejected; the git-mode seal lease lives in the head |
| Disjoint git landing, then a merge push by any writer | No client retry | No defined tip until the merge; two pushes per landing; automatic merges | Rejected ([owner decision 141](#od-141)) |
| A server-made deterministic merge commit | No client work | Merges shared branches automatically (sidecar/design/market2.md:519) | Used only for file-mode export |
| Folds every ~10 s or 32 versions | Fresher entries | Agents pushing every ~10 s fold each push alone: ~3 index writes, ~54 KiB a drive | Rejected |
| One head PUT for several pushes, or batches per repo | Fewer writes | Gains only past ~50 pushes/s a ref; most repos see under one a second | Rejected |
| A head per version, created If-None-Match | ~5 KiB less a push | [Owner decision 2](#od-2) fixes the head If-Match as the commit point | Rejected |
| MinIO pools for the metadata tier | One namespace | A multi-pool PUT checks its precondition only in the pool it picks (11.3) | Rejected ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) |
| go-git as the local server | No git binary | v6 is a beta (https://github.com/go-git/go-git) | Rejected |
| Versioning per ref, or a separate per-path attribute object | Simplest purge | The index must change in the content's push; or a mutable object outside the commit point | Rejected |
| Purge at evacuation, 25-26 h after replacement | No queue in evs; a day to restore | Replaced content lingers a day | Rejected ([owner decision 161](#od-161)); kept as the sweep |
| Small versionless content as its own NVMe object, HDD segment or inline record | Simple | ~12.5 KiB a drive a version; an HDD PUT and DELETE a version; or kept in packs | Rejected: staged in batches |
| A purge watermark in batch headers | No redundant HEADs at the sweep | A field, look-ahead reads and a rule for ~1% of year two's HDD operations | Only if §22.8's hdd row shows the redundant HEADs matter |
| A fresh key and slot per versionless version in slot-keyed repos | Uniform | A slot create (~9 KiB a drive) and delete per overwrite | Rejected: one key per path |
| A server-registered index prefix confining versioning 2 | evs enforces it | A prefix per ref, re-registered every path epoch | Rejected: readers check |
| A hold pausing every purge | Simple | Keeps content created after placement | Rejected ([owner decision 133](#od-133)) |
| Content-defined chunking for versionless dedup | Dedups insertions | Chunk sizes fingerprint content; keyed CDC's keys are recoverable (ePrint 2025/558) | Rejected |
| Versionless git blobs | No LFS | Breaks exact oids, export and old checkouts | Rejected |
| Trust git-lfs's pre-push uploads to cover a new tip | No daemon work | git-lfs uploads only objects of commits the remote's old tip does not reach, so a force push to an ancestor, a new ref at old history or `--no-verify` uploads nothing | Rejected: the tip check (11.11) |
| Touch every object a new tip requires on each push | No timing margin | A new branch over k objects writes k versions | Rejected: touch only versions 5 days old or more |
| A two-phase prune: condemn, wait, then remove | Pushes write only for condemned objects | A format field, and a fence every push must time | Rejected |
| Keep the newest n versions, or d days | Undo | n× storage, or due lists | Rejected ([owner decision 165](#od-165)) |
| A new index delta file per commit | No overwrite | An entry, a marker and its collection: ~15-37 KiB a push | Rejected |
| Sealing an index head into a new path per seal | Simple | ~27-40 KiB of path churn per seal | Rejected: a reused slot ring |
| Merging each full head into shards at once | No sealed slots | A <= 1 MiB HDD PUT and DELETE per seal (~125 a second in year two) | Rejected |
| One index head file per ref | One read gives the state | Every committer rewrites one path, so disjoint pushes collide | Rejected |
| zstd over shards, blocks or doc tables | ~25-40% smaller | A size oracle for injected mail and commits (DBREACH, https://crypto.unc.edu/papers/dbreach.pdf) | Rejected |
| Padmé alone on shards | Simpler | A probe at a padding boundary reads a trigram's presence per rebuild | Rejected: a keyed pad |
| 16 MiB all objects | ~10-25% smaller | Past 11.12's 1,088 KiB closure upload, so an erasure at the floor takes days | Rejected |
| All shards by doc-key hash range | A document's shard is computable | Every roll-up rewrites every shard | Rejected for roll-up order |
| Dead-document bitmaps in all | Cheaper roll-ups | Old postings linger; erasure still rewrites | Rejected: one version per document |
| Diffs on any earlier entry in the bucket | Smaller entries | The head's own replacement, or a merge absorbing a newer copy, drops the base a current diff needs | Rejected: bases outside every head, which merges keep (11.14's dependency row) |
| Every index entry full, no diffs | Self-contained entries | Each edit of a large file uploads its whole key set again as a large entry | Rejected: diffs onto bases outside every head |
| Deletions as empty doc-table rows or flag bits | No new table | An empty posting set is also a live document with no trigrams, and names no ref | Rejected: a tombstone table |
| Tombstones kept in all | Roll-ups never touch a newer bucket | All keeps every deletion for good | Rejected: a roll-up removes an older newer-bucket entry instead |
| A mask set of every bucket key, built per search | Simple | ~7.6 MiB of keys alone at 500,000 changed files, past a phone's 4 MiB working set | Rejected: §5.9's version table, probed per candidate |
| A watch after the ERASE, by the eraser's device or an indexer, re-closing racing copies (the 41ba6670 rule) | No format change | Not a barrier: a crash, or a push delayed past the watch, publishes a copy under a key the ERASE never named; no indexer exists by default ([owner decision 177](#od-177)) | Rejected: the CUT and index epoch (11.12) |
| A per-document erasure check at evs | Exact | evs cannot see documents (owner directive) | Rejected: an opaque epoch and a sealed erasure set |
| The epoch fencing CLOSUREs too | One rule | Another eraser's CUT would void a CLOSURE whose uploads its eraser paid for at the floor ([owner decision 146](#od-146)) | Rejected: CLOSUREs only replace versions, and path CAS orders them |
| A fixed per-message erasure wait, indexing at most one 1 MiB document a message | A next-day promise | Backfill copies, absorbed slots and holds still multiply copies, and long messages lose search | Rejected: the wait from closure bytes, with progress (11.13) |
| A companion ref per git ref | Per-branch isolation | A head and roll-ups per agent branch, no shared companion push | Rejected: one `ur/index` per repo |
| Drop by a path spec alone, with no signed list | A smaller payload | Epoch and token mistakes delete another path's history; no cross-check | Rejected: an explicit list that the client and resolve cross-check |
| Keep the old head unlisted, with no re-write | No extra version | Its diff chain keeps listed content reconstructable | Rejected: the head is written again |
| A reverse citation index (segment to citing versions) kept in `pidx/` at evacuation | Scans read `pidx/` only | A permanent NVMe cost on every push for a rare action | Later, if §22.8's `drop` row shows scans binding |
| Same-mode or no-stream reuse rules, so scans skip refs | Smaller scans | New format-1 rules, each a hole a skipped ref could fall through | Rejected: every ref is scanned ([owner decision 173](#od-173)) |
| One scan, no independent verify | Half the reads | One scanner bug deletes live content | Rejected |
| Rewrite shared slots and packs without the listed parts | Frees more at once | evs cannot see key indexes or record ownership, so a wrong list destroys live keys | Rejected; compaction owns containers |
| A hold refuses the DROP | A visible refusal | Reveals sealed holds | Rejected ([owner decision 184](#od-184)) |
| k-of-n signatures for a drop | Collusion needed | Blocks routine hygiene, where a window does the same | Rejected ([owner decision 183](#od-183)) |
| A boundary below the head | Keeps recent history | Keep-last-n by another name | Rejected ([owner decision 165](#od-165)) |
| The ref's owner may drop on owned refs | Self-service | Bypasses repo admins | Rejected: repo admins ([owner decision 173](#od-173)) |
| Store the drop in the access log | Ordered with grants | Not ordered with the path's versions, so the head re-write cannot be atomic with it | Rejected: a push on the ref |
| Ask an indexer for verified hits | No download; verified hits, better typo correction, exact CJK checks | Relays see timing; the indexer sees the query | Chosen where an indexer is designated, none by default (owner decisions [175](#od-175), [177](#od-177), [178](#od-178)) |
| Replies sized to the next 16 KiB step their content needs | Fewer bytes for short results | Sizes show a result-size class | Rejected: one fixed step (steps = 1), a round trip per ~20 hits |
| Requests sized to the query and scope, or padded to 16 KiB | Fewer bytes; or one step for both | Lengths show query and scope size; or 4× the bytes and five frames, hiding nothing more | Rejected: one 4,016 B body |
| An envelope Error for every failure, or a Cancel message | Simple; frees indexer work sooner | Sizes after parsing show failure kinds; a Cancel's small frame shows an abandoned search | Rejected: padded statuses after parsing; supersede and expiry |
| A contract class of its own | Policy could cut it | The gate marks which contracts carry search; a new class for C13 to seal | Rejected: the pair's Network contract, data or control (D-PROTO-21); admins retire `search` instead |
| Any member device answers, with no designation | More coverage | No anchor for disclosure; any member could collect queries | Rejected: [owner decision 175](#od-175) says indexers |
| Other members' indexers only by opt-in | Strongest privacy | Turns off what [owner decision 175](#od-175) turns on | Rejected |
| Blind the query: trigram ids, or PIR | The indexer learns less | Trigrams reveal the query; verification needs the words; PIR costs orders of magnitude more | Rejected |
| Phones as indexers | More indexers | Battery, 16-32 MiB budgets, no all, no text, iOS suspends | Rejected |
| The indexer brings partitions current before answering | Fresher results | evs sees a fetch at every search | Rejected: it answers from what it holds |
| The owner's indexer deposits a receipt for an `EvsShare` reader | Parity with D-MCP-18 | An evs write at search time | Rejected: the local served record (§5.9) |
| Remote search on every keystroke | Verified bucket hits while typing | Relays and team indexers see every keystroke's query | Rejected: "search more" only |
| Group by agent on the indexer | One call for agent views | Paging and merging groups across two sources | Rejected for v1: phones group the hits they hold |

### 11.17 Decisions proposed

**D-EVS-1 (proposed).** Plaintext git lives only on reading sidecars; evs holds segments, index entries and signed pushes and never parses git. *Why:* server plaintext is a design error (CONVENTIONS §0).

**D-EVS-2 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2): the token tree replaced the sealed client index (D-EVS-12).

**D-EVS-3 (proposed).** Blobs are git-delta chains under 11.7's checkpoint rules. *Why:* PLAN.md:50 and :63; a reconstruction reads at most 17 records and 1.5× the file size.

**D-EVS-4 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2): ref CAS lives in `head/` objects (D-EVS-13).

**D-EVS-5 (proposed).** Only the §5 identity key signs pushes, which name `sidecar_id` and `client_id` and are pinned as (ref, version, C_v); agent attribution is sealed. *Why:* I-4, I-16 and PLAN.md:59.

**D-EVS-6 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2): the server keeps a path index of objects (D-EVS-12).

**D-EVS-7 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 24](#od-24): the local git tier ships with `git-remote-ur` (D-EVS-15).

**D-EVS-8 (proposed).** Owned refs sync in real time; shared git-mode refs serialize by tip CAS, with explicit client merges, and file-mode refs land disjoint pushes by path-level CAS; no conflict is resolved automatically. *Why:* sidecar/design/market2.md:513-531; owner decisions [2](#od-2), [24](#od-24), [141](#od-141).

**D-EVS-9 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 2](#od-2): usage flows as events (D-EVS-16).

**D-EVS-10 (proposed).** Record-class owned refs are append-only streams, and deposits end in a reader's CONSUME. *Why:* §16's chains need streams a stolen writer cannot rewrite (Q-ARCH-9 (a)).

**D-EVS-11 (proposed).** Kinds are fixed at creation; `vault`, `mailbox` and `secret` (any number a member, such as §13.8's ACME account keys) bind `owner_member_id` and are read only by the owner's consented devices (§8.5), their `EvsShare`s' subjects and [owner decision 63](#od-63)'s audit reader. *Why:* [owner decision 126](#od-126); sessions and mail stay with their owner unless shared (R-ACL-11, R-KEYS-9, R-TRUST-7).

**D-EVS-12 (proposed).** Paths are 11.6-11.7's token tree, re-keyed by a signed map bound to its source head and keyed by its hash, plus a tail for paths created since: due at once on a member device's removal or a compromise, new names in name-bearing repos waiting for it, else (other shrinks, authorization expiries) due within 24 h, or, while two source epochs stand, once one drops; re-keyed when a mapper commits, which a creation block of at most 2 min, 10 min past due, assures; up to three source epochs overlap, the third kept for an immediate epoch, each cluster's copies sharing 250 operations a second that §19.9 plans by live entries per rotating ref, the copy translating directory rows a fold carried and removals during it leaving removed entries, so no read falls back to a stale source, and no name created after cut-over gets a source-epoch token. *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2) and [64](#od-64), with no index rewrite per CI reap, no epoch starved by steady creation and no batched epoch's copy backlog taking the source an immediate epoch needs.

**D-EVS-13 (proposed).** evs is stateless over 11.8's objects, each repo's on the cluster its `place/` names: only the head If-Match decides; all else a push writes is immutable or an index cache that committed records rebuild; readers use only versions the head history names. *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2), [20](#od-20), [145](#od-145); no lost response or cleanup removes committed data.

**D-EVS-14 (proposed).** Subscriptions are token-prefix leases per path epoch, Redis soft state that holders re-create after a loss, answered once the lease exists; hints carry only server-held fields, versioned by the push sequence, a Redis counter seeded from the master's clock, so it restarts above every earlier value. *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2), [17](#od-17), [136](#od-136).

**D-EVS-15 (proposed).** The local tier is the system git behind the daemon's authenticating fronts plus `git-remote-ur`, with plaintext only on loopback, TLS or ssh beyond it, and [owner decision 81](#od-81)'s committer hook. *Why:* owner decisions [24](#od-24), [81](#od-81), [84](#od-84) and [130](#od-130), without a go-git server.

**D-EVS-16 (proposed).** Stored bytes are each repo's `seg/`, `pack/` and `hp/` object sizes plus its batch-resident record lengths, less held-only objects and superseded containers, counted nightly and moved by usage batches; at the limit only payload-adding uploads and pushes stop, except re-seeding, an erasure's bounded CLOSURE push with its uploads, a DROP push that uploads no segment, and config and mailcfg pushes within §7.9's limits. *Why:* stateless evs has no counter to lock, and shared batches cannot be listed per repo.

**D-EVS-17 (proposed).** Owner devices, first the indexers designated for `mirror` ([owner decision 150](#od-150)), mirror record-class repos and the config in full, slots included, and re-seed evs after a site loss, erasures first and slots last; a repo admin's EvsReseed lets readers accept a shorter history as a loss. *Why:* owner decisions [90](#od-90) and [94](#od-94) keep no operator copy; a slotless mirror cannot open unread entries; an indexer's mirror stays current while other devices sleep.

**D-EVS-18 (proposed).** The write gate is the head CAS: a commit's authorization and generation pins pass §10.6's predicate against evs's newest authorization state, read within 5 s, and never fall below the head's. *Why:* [owner decision 5](#od-5) leaves no server transaction, and a separate gate object cannot fence the commit.

**D-EVS-19 (proposed).** Deletion is a `repo/` state machine that follows the access log: RepoDelete or RepoRestore is filed first and the route, or taskworker's reconciler, applies it; restore and shred contend for one CAS, the timer waiting out api's 7-day RepoRestore window; terminal `shredding` precedes any key destruction, and deletion ids fence jobs. *Why:* owner decisions [82](#od-82), [133](#od-133); no restore returns a keyless repo, and no re-seed trusts a log that shows a deleted repo live.

**D-EVS-20 (proposed).** A push over 1 MiB or 1,024 entry writes travels in up to 1,024 hashed parts that its signed statement binds and one head PUT commits; a git-mode one holds a seal lease of at most 2 min. *Why:* imports and large merges stay one atomic, verifiable git push.

**D-EVS-21 (proposed).** 11.13 budgets every metadata write in drive bytes, which bound its IOs too, with leases, the push sequence and gkm acks in Redis and a per-network fair share that sheds the heaviest network first. *Why:* every drive takes every write (owner decisions [21](#od-21), [116](#od-116), [140](#od-140)).

**D-EVS-22 (decided; [owner decision 141](#od-141)).** Refs have a mode fixed at creation: git-mode refs commit only on their tip and keep the original commits; file-mode refs use path-level CAS and export one deterministic commit per version; head mode writes file-mode refs only. *Why:* git commits bind tree and parents (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [24](#od-24), [81](#od-81)).

**D-EVS-23 (proposed).** A push id names one statement, whose retry returns its original version; an unknown outcome resolves from the head and at most two log pages, or stays unknown; a refusal the head does not settle for good is answered only once a head CAS records the push id, its code and its statement's time bound in the head, at most 8 records a ref and one a second, else 429, and every attempt of that push id that reads the record gets that refusal; no answer deletes anything, and evacuation deletes only a dead push's slots. *Why:* a store can apply a write and lose its response, and another attempt of the same push id, a client's retry or the lb's re-send, can reach evs at any time, even after another attempt's answer reached the client, so only state the commit point covers keeps a refusal true; a fence timed by attempts' arrival cannot.

**D-EVS-24 (proposed).** Log pages hold the signed statements (at most 1 KiB each), and the head window names each recent one's place and hash; head readers verify every statement after their pin and the one behind each entry they read. *Why:* [owner decision 7](#od-7) for every reader (Q-EVS-6), at one block per head write.

**D-EVS-25 (proposed).** Orphans are found without the log: hourly evacuation resolves every batch record, which names every slot its push wrote, fencing a pending record's ref, one with no head by a placeholder head; and an unadopted segment or path map, found by the nightly LIST, is deleted only once evacuation's horizon has passed every batch that could adopt it ([owner decision 203](#od-203)). *Why:* an upload that never reached the log is otherwise invisible; a grace period cannot fence a late commit, and a fence cannot reach a ref that does not exist yet, but every commit leaves its record first.

**D-EVS-26 (proposed).** Erasure is a committed ERASE push that destroys every key of every representation: each retained version, each derived-field chain, the search index's files included (re-keyed first, by a CLOSURE push that only replaces committed file versions, each new chain within Padmé of the one it replaces, taken at the storage limit with size-bounded uploads within its eraser's own rate and daily allowance, which has a floor §21 cannot lower) and the deposit, which is slot-keyed; with the index, a CUT on each index ref first fences its publication (D-EVS-66), and its first ERASE takes the entry's own keys, which re-key nothing. *Why:* owner decisions [61](#od-61), [133](#od-133), [146](#od-146); a shared index or live deposit would otherwise outlive the erasure, and no admin's closures spend another's.

**D-EVS-27 (proposed).** Segments are addressed only by content id, locators carry a kind with two reserved values, and `spidx/` is reserved, so packing needs no format change. *Why:* locators are signed and cannot be rewritten; Q-OPS-2.

**D-EVS-28 (proposed).** The local tier publishes through git's proc-receive hook with per-ref statuses, no atomic pushes and a durable journal resolved by push id. *Why:* a pre-receive hook cannot report per-ref outcomes or survive a crash between the remote and local updates.

**D-EVS-29 (proposed).** The head holds the commit point and a window of 64-byte entries (push id, statement hash prefix, place, path digest, flags), at most ~9 KiB: one block on each drive per commit. *Why:* every push rewrites the head on all 8 drives, plus a backup ([owner decision 140](#od-140)).

**D-EVS-30 (proposed).** evs group-commits push, part and seal records into immutable minute-bucketed batches of at most 256 KiB, written at once when load is light, within 20 ms under load, and evacuated whole after 25-26 h. *Why:* bursts, and a process's stream to a cluster past ~50 pushes/s, share one create and one delete per batch ([owner decision 140](#od-140)); at ~8 evs processes a set near capacity sees ~1-1.6 records a batch.

**D-EVS-31 (proposed).** `idx/` holds only committed versions, folded lazily (the oldest 64 at 96 unfolded, the rest after 10 min idle, always before a page-out and in a path epoch's own commit), a file's newest version per fold and every directory delta in order; a removal writes, If-Match and only over an older version, a marker that keeps the path's version, and markers go in head-announced collection windows once the horizon passes them by a base range, their DELETEs cancelled before the window ends, and folds over covered markers held past it, by margins that cover the clock bounds and the cancel's lag; a creation's version is max(its push's effective base version, on an overlay its base_version plus its chain's base versions, a standing removal's) + 1, so a path's versions never restart once its marker goes, nor fall below those it held on a base ref; reads and the CAS read an entry only after a head and merge the window versions after that head's folded_through. *Why:* a busy path is written once per fold, nothing pending evicts a committed version ([owner decision 140](#od-140)), and a DELETE, which MinIO applies unconditionally, could remove an entry a later fold wrote; versions must only rise, for 5g and the search index's newest-wins rule ([owner decision 148](#od-148)).

**D-EVS-32 (proposed).** Hourly evacuation moves each repo's records and log pages older than 24 h into one HDD pack once they reach 256 KiB; below that it moves the records into NVMe parcels while the log pages wait at log/, both packing within 7 d. *Why:* [owner decision 136](#od-136)'s residency, with whole-batch deletes and no tiny HDD objects.

**D-EVS-33 (proposed).** evs, gkm, api and taskworker share each metadata cluster's write budget (0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS on its busiest drive not under heal), a bucket that every measured drive byte drains, P0's included. P0 safety work (`rev/` and `proj/` writes, `repo/` lifecycle, shred steps, ERASE, CUT and CLOSURE pushes within their rate and every slot rewrite, Removes and REMOVE rotations) issues at once, never queued or refused, its bytes reported by kind and drawn from the bucket down to zero, past which they are P0's excess, forgiven; every other class issues only while the bucket holds it, restarting when a P0 storm ends and ramping up as the bucket refills, so their writes stay within the budget less the P0 writes the bucket held, and their IOs within it too (at least 512 B each, ≤ 39% of rated). P1 pays at admission for itself and the P2 work it causes, the deferred part moving into a prepaid wallet that funded P2 spends and the allowance never pays again, so a steady load is admitted at the full physical rate; unfunded P2 takes at most 40% of the allowance; P2 runs in deadline order; per-network fair queues refuse the heaviest network first, never P0 work; segment PUTs likewise queue per network on each segment cluster, refused heaviest first (503) past 50% of §19.6's measured drive-operation capacity. *Why:* [owner decision 140](#od-140), which [owner decision 186](#od-186) amends for P0 writes only: P0 work always runs at once and the wear bound exempts it, since per-tenant rates bound no cluster's aggregate safety work (100 large Teams each shrinking every 5 minutes ask ~2.9 TiB a day a drive, about twice the refill), so a P0 storm can wear the drives past 0.8 DWPD and their 1 DWPD rating, disclosed with §19.8's P0 alarms (11.21; Q-EVS-24); [owner decision 190](#od-190) forgives P0's excess, so a cluster's pushes and evacuation restart when a storm ends, at the cost of the storm's extra wear, ~0.23 drive-writes a 6-hour storm at that stress, which §19.8 counts against the rating; charging P2 at admission and again from the allowance would admit ~27% fewer pushes; a capped P2 would let evacuation outgrow 26 h.

**D-EVS-34 (proposed).** Segment uploads write nothing to the metadata cluster: evs returns a MAC'd receipt that the push presents, and GC deletes an unadopted segment only once every batch record that could adopt it has been evacuated, 49 h or more after its upload, by a DELETE that names the object ([owner decision 203](#od-203)). *Why:* markers cost three writes per segment.

**D-EVS-35 (proposed).** Versioning is a per-version setting of a file, signed in its entry version: 0 keeps every version, 1 only the newest's content, 2 the same for the search index's files; config and mailcfg repos, git-mode refs and creates-only refs refuse 1 and 2, and a repo lock refuses 1 ([owner decision 168](#od-168)). *Why:* owner decisions [158](#od-158)-[160](#od-160); authority histories and exact git need every version.

**D-EVS-36 (proposed).** Versionless content lives in one-record kind-5 segments whose headers name the introducing push, cited only by that path's next version or a rename target of the push removing it; content padding to at most 16 KiB is staged in its batch; slot-keyed repos keep one key per versionless path. *Why:* path-level CAS fences every citation; short-lived small content costs no HDD write or NVMe object, and an overwrite no slot.

**D-EVS-37 (proposed).** The committing evs process deletes replaced versionless content 60 s after the commit is certain; evacuation drops replaced staged content and HEADs every candidate, deleting any still present, so a lost queue leaves content at most ~26 h; a hold keeps only content that existed at its placement. *Why:* owner decisions [161](#od-161) and [133](#od-133), with no new object family or metadata write.

**D-EVS-38 (proposed).** Turning versioning off keeps every version written while it was on; turning it on starts history there, possibly adopting the replaced version's uploads; a replaced versionless version reads `collected`. *Why:* [owner decision 158](#od-158)'s per-revision rule.

**D-EVS-39 (proposed).** Format 1 reserves and refuses every format-2 construct as FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED; a repo migrates when its first push carrying one raises `repo/`'s format. *Why:* [owner decision 163](#od-163), with nothing rewritten.

**D-EVS-40 (proposed).** Directory removals and ref DELETEs list each versionless file below them, and the removal fold carries an omitted file's content ids into its marker, whose collection deletes them. *Why:* evs computes candidates at the commit; an omission costs at most a marker's life of storage.

**D-EVS-41 (proposed).** From v1, git-lfs pointers are backed by the repo's versionless `ur/lfs` store through a standalone transfer agent that touches each object it uploads; before a git-mode tip commits, the local tier's tip check touches each object the tip requires that the old tip did not and whose newest version is 5 days old or more, and refuses the update, naming the objects and `git lfs push --object-id`, when one is gone; an indexer or a device holding every ref prunes daily, from one read of every ref's head, what no tip of that read and no commit, upload or touch of the last N days references, N being 30 or a repo setting of at least 7 days (11.11). *Why:* owner decisions [141](#od-141) and [162](#od-162); reachability is a client computation; git-lfs uploads only what the remote's old tip does not reach, so a force push to an ancestor, a new ref at old history or a skipped hook uploads nothing; touches settle a prune's race at path-level CAS, and a version under 5 days old outlasts every prune start that could miss the tip.

**D-EVS-42 (proposed).** Writers set a new path's versioning from the rules in force at its creation: the repo's, else its network's, else versionless above 64 MiB, a present rule set replacing the next entirely; it persists until a writer changes it. *Why:* [owner decision 164](#od-164); no rule edit flips existing paths ([owner decision 167](#od-167)).

**D-EVS-43 (proposed).** A file-mode ref whose documents change in place holds its index under `.ur-index/i1`, changed in the push that changes a document; git-mode refs and streams share `ur/index`, written by companion pushes; every index file but its admin-signed settings is versionless; config, mailcfg and secret repos get none, and an index covers only documents every reader of its ref opens. *Why:* owner decisions [151](#od-151) and [159](#od-159); vault entries have narrower readers than their mailbox; it narrows [owner decision 156](#od-156) for secret repos: each holds one credential (11.12), which an index would only copy into postings, and MCP never reads them (§16.6).

**D-EVS-44 (proposed).** Index format 1 is document-level byte trigrams of normalized text on Unicode 17.0.0, one posting set over every field in VByte gaps or bitsets, a front-coded dictionary, doc tables and tombstone tables, with no compression across documents, a keyed pad on shards and byte-exact determinism. *Why:* substring and CJK search at about a word index's size; no compression oracle for injected mail; devices rebuild and verify instead of downloading; a merged deletion must still mask older partitions, and an empty posting set cannot say so.

**D-EVS-45 (proposed).** Buckets are UTC windows of the repo's W days (30, or 7-365) holding entries by signed push time, an entry going instead to the newest bucket already holding its document where that is newer; latest is the current and previous window, and expired buckets roll up oldest first. *Why:* owner decisions [152](#od-152) and [153](#od-153); every device computes the same boundaries.

**D-EVS-46 (proposed).** Each writer appends to a head of at most 16,208 B, staged in its push's batch, sealing into a ring of up to 8 reused slots that merges absorb by watermark into bucket shards. A diff rests only on its document's previous version outside every head in the current bucket, or carries over the base of the writer's own head diff it replaces, and merges keep a base a head names. *Why:* no index path per commit or seal: a new path costs ~27-40 KiB a drive, an overwrite one entry rewrite per fold; a head keeping one entry per doc_key would otherwise overwrite its own diff's base, and the purge leaves no older copy.

**D-EVS-47 (proposed).** Merges and roll-ups are functions of their base version's files, a merge's writers' heads included; a roll-up is one push moving its bucket into all under a versionless lock whose path-level CAS fences a stale runner, applying the bucket's tombstones, which its shards keep until then, and removing any older entry racing pushes left in a newer bucket, so all holds no tombstone; readers search every bucket present. *Why:* crash safety and idempotence with no server state ([owner decision 157](#od-157)); a deletion must outlive the slot that wrote it until all's row is gone.

**D-EVS-48 (proposed).** Index files are at most 1 MiB; an erasure's CLOSURE rewrites those holding the document, listed at or after its CUT, in place, padded to their replaced lengths, under fresh keys in new slots, the ERASE destroying the old slots' keys, which every stored version shares. *Why:* one closure upload per file within [owner decision 146](#od-146)'s floor; one destroyed key covers staged copies ([owner decision 61](#od-61)).

**D-EVS-49 (proposed).** Companion pushes carry a committer's journaled entries at most once a minute per writer on 1 KiB blocks, else every 5 minutes ([owner decision 172](#od-172)), with coverage; an indexer, else the next capable writer, backfills pushes unindexed after 10 min. *Why:* a companion per content push would cost a whole push each.

**D-EVS-50 (proposed).** Devices fetch whole index files only by sync position, and at "search more" every all shard they lack, youngest first; a search reads only the cache; a device holding a merge's, roll-up's or rewrite's inputs reproduces it against `content_sha256`, downloading only on a mismatch, which alarms. *Why:* the server learns when a device syncs, never what it searches (owner decisions [154](#od-154), [155](#od-155)); reproduction spares most bucket and roll-up traffic.

**D-EVS-51 (proposed).** A device with a stale cached all keeps the buckets rolled up since, masked, until its all shows them rolled up, an ERASE occurs in the repo or 2W days pass. *Why:* complete coverage with no refresh at search time.

**D-EVS-52 (proposed).** Newest wins: a hit counts only if its partition holds the document's highest version, tombstones and ref tombstones included, masked per candidate through the device's version table (§5.9) over the partitions it holds, the ERASE lists and the erasure sets. *Why:* [owner decision 152](#od-152); erased documents never show while caches catch up; a mask built from every bucket key at each search outgrows a phone's working set.

**D-EVS-53 (proposed).** Hosts with the text verify every candidate they show; others confirm from display fields, mail's `i/` and cached bodies, label the rest possible, fetch nothing to check them, and exclude only confirmed containment. *Why:* [owner decision 155](#od-155); no query-dependent fetch.

**D-EVS-54 (proposed).** Possible matches rank by trigram overlap, after matches and before near hits; under 3 exact hits, desktops expand a term against a local vocabulary and phones by one-edit variants checked in the index. *Why:* on 20 Newsgroups P@5 rose from 0.19 to 0.45 (0.54 with confirmations first), the true hit first from 21% to 68%; the intended word came first 76% (desktops) and 66% (phones) of the time, with no word index ([owner decision 155](#od-155)).

**D-EVS-55 (proposed).** Terms under 3 bytes match as whole words through boundary trigrams, and CJK runs are substring terms. *Why:* short words would match nothing, and a CJK character is one trigram ([owner decision 151](#od-151)).

**D-EVS-56 (proposed).** Hosts with the text re-extract each new document, check each tombstone against its path's history and reproduce merges and roll-ups, raising `index_mismatch` naming the signer and using their own result; indexers do so for every repo they read. *Why:* every writer of a ref writes its index (owner decisions [150](#od-150), [151](#od-151)).

**D-EVS-57 (proposed).** An app host's "search more" asks one of its network's designated search indexers (none by default) over §6.6's RPC on the pair's Network contract; the indexer authorizes the requester and each repo in its own state, pins its cached snapshot, verifies candidates newest first against its text and answers pages with each repo's coverage and pinned (v, C_v), fetching nothing from evs, api or gkm; with none answering, [owner decision 155](#od-155) applies. *Why:* owner decisions [175](#od-175) and [177](#od-177); evs stays blind on both devices, and a forged or stale requester view reaches nothing the indexer refuses.

**D-EVS-58 (proposed).** A repo is asked first of the requester's own search indexers that read it, an owner-bound repo only of its owner's consented ones, a team repo otherwise of one network-scope search indexer and an `EvsShare`'d repo of its owner's, each other member only after the app has named them once (§18.4); no app host, browser Worker, or ephemeral or read_only sidecar answers. *Why:* owner decisions [126](#od-126), [150](#od-150), [175](#od-175), [177](#od-177) and [178](#od-178); queries stay on the member's devices where they can, reach another's only knowingly and where entitled, and never fan out.

**D-EVS-59 (proposed).** Every request body is exactly 4,016 B and every reply the requester's steps × 16,384 B (1 in v1), failures after parsing included; only failures before parsing are small Errors, and nothing is compressed, cancelled or answered early. *Why:* [owner decision 175](#od-175)'s padding; with every size set by the requester, relays learn when searches and pages run and the indexer's answer time, never what was asked or found.

**D-EVS-60 (proposed).** The phone merges per doc key, the newest version winning and, at one version, a remote verified state; in a repo the indexer verifies by text, a local possible or near hit no page returned collapses into a "not matched" row when it is newer than `checked_through_ms` and at least 10 min older than the pinned version; the phone's confirmed hits, ERASE masks and read checks always apply, and an opened hit is checked. *Why:* pages stream newest first, so only the checked span proves a candidate false; this bounds what a faulty indexer can hide.

**D-EVS-61 (proposed).** The `directory` kind has one repo per team network, record-class: a shared file-mode `cards` ref, whose `d/`, `r/` and `q/` paths are versionless from its format 2 and checked by readers against their writers; per-writer streams; `ur/index`; and `erasure`, whose ERASE, CUT and CLOSURE take `admin`, as every repo's, held only by its consented, not-read-only admins, a repo owner's revocation erasing through §16.11's erasure runner. Its index is on by kind, with a 7-day window, and refuses `off`; its group seats readers under §7.9's leaves rule; its daemons read moved streams 64 to a request (11.9). *Why:* [owner decision 171](#od-171) gives this repo's index every announcement, specific beside [owner decision 156](#od-156); evs sees no path, so readers enforce writers, as Q-EVS-3's prefix rules do, but a reader's check after a key is destroyed restores nothing, so erasure needs an authority evs checks first; owner decisions [177](#od-177), [181](#od-181), [182](#od-182).

**D-EVS-62 (proposed).** A drop is a DROP push (flag 256) on the path's file-mode ref, signed by one repo admin (owner-bound: only a consented, not-read-only device of the owner; never MCP), listing per lineage every dropped version by entry hash and the version that stays; it waits 7 days, in which any repo admin may cancel, `now` skipping the window as RepoDelete's does, and a lock voids it; config and mailcfg repos, git-mode, creates-only and derived refs, directory paths and versionless heads refuse it. *Why:* owner decisions [126](#od-126), [173](#od-173) and [183](#od-183); a push orders the drop with the path's versions and the head fences it.

**D-EVS-63 (proposed).** A drop deletes only kind-1 segments and slots that only listed versions name; statements, hashes and entry versions without inline records stay, so history verifies, and listed inline content waits for compaction, unserved; the kept head is written as a fresh checkpoint or re-cited chunk set; readers show pending, then dropped, never missing or tampered. *Why:* no diff chain keeps dropped content, and no drop reads as tampering.

**D-EVS-64 (proposed).** From its commit no push may cite a listed version; the job starts 25 min after the window, marks every ref's live versions at one snapshot once evacuation's horizon has passed each covered drop's commit by 2 min ([owner decision 204](#od-204)), verifies with a separate implementation at a later one, deletes only objects over 25 h old, and resumes from `drops/`. *Why:* a mutator cannot move a reference past a scan of immutable history, and two implementations must agree before any DELETE.

**D-EVS-65 (proposed).** A hold defers a drop's deletions silently, the drop reading, listing and billing as finished; stored bytes fall as the job deletes; the DROP rewrites listed versions out of the index; mirrors apply it; compaction may later remove listed inline content, keeping every statement and every byte a live version needs. *Why:* owner decisions [93](#od-93), [133](#od-133), [159](#od-159), [165](#od-165) and [184](#od-184).

**D-EVS-66 (proposed).** An erasure's first push on each index ref of its documents is a CUT that rewrites the ref's erasure set, a versionless list of the documents pending erasure there, and moves the head's `index_epoch` to its own version; every other push creating or replacing an index file but a CLOSURE names that epoch at its head CAS, else 409 INDEX_EPOCH, and its builder has applied the set, so delayed, resealed and retried index work (fresh writer-head and large-entry paths, merges, roll-ups, builds, backfills, DROP rewrites and companion journals) cannot publish a listed document after the cut; the eraser lists index files only after it, so no watch follows the ERASE; an erasure resumes from the sets and its ERASE notes on its eraser's device, else after 25 h on another device of its member that may erase, else, once its eraser is revoked, on any such device. *Why:* the meta review's F09: path CAS fences only paths a CLOSURE rewrites, a hint is not a barrier and a network has no indexer by default ([owner decision 177](#od-177)), so FI-19 needs a durable cut at the index's one commit point; evs enforces an opaque counter and the set stays sealed (owner directive); CLOSUREs stay outside the epoch so that no eraser's CUT voids another's paid uploads ([owner decision 146](#od-146)).

**D-EVS-67 (proposed).** An erasure's wait is stated from its rekey objects, not per message: at the storage limit or while spent, with B closure bytes left when its allowance first refuses it and allowance A, its last pair commits after at most the ⌈B / (A - 1,088 KiB)⌉-th 00:00 UTC that follows plus one pacing turn per upload of that day; its CUT and its first ERASE, of the documents' own keys, land at once; the eraser's device reports each erasure's state, remaining objects and bytes, next try and finish (§5.4, §18.5). *Why:* the meta review's F19: one message is one document per 1 MiB chunk of its text, and backfills, absorbed slots and holds add copies, so the fixed next-day bound did not hold; [owner decision 146](#od-146) asks §11.13 and §15.7 to state the wait, and an estimate from the eraser's own allowance and turns is that statement.

### 11.18 Open questions

**Q-EVS-1.** [X2] Which header values may evs see, and how do head reads and subpath subscriptions work without plaintext paths? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 2](#od-2)):** keyed path tokens in an object index, token-prefix subscriptions, path-key rotation on member removal and all storage state as objects (11.5-11.8). *Residual:* Q-EVS-6, closed by peer review 2026-11-04.

**Q-EVS-2.** [X19] How does evs stay git-compatible? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 24](#od-24)):** a local git tier over authenticated http and ssh plus `git-remote-ur`; only the sidecar talks to evs; owner decisions [84](#od-84) and [130](#od-130) set the bind, with only TLS or ssh beyond loopback (11.11). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-3 (closed 2026-11-03).** Separate repos for path prefixes in v0; in v1, prefix rules in the encrypted repo config, enforced by sidecars with an alarm; applied in §8 (D-ACL-11) and 11.22. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-4.** How does PLAN.md:59's forced git identity apply to plaintext commits? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 81](#od-81)):** signed pushes authenticate commits, and the local git server refuses new commits whose committer is not the pushing sidecar, except signed imports (11.11). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-5.** Should repo deletion start as a soft delete? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 82](#od-82)):** yes: access ends at once, and keys are shredded after 7 days unless restored, or at once with `--now` (11.12). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-6.** Must a head reader that does not replay verify per-file freshness? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (c), made cheap: head readers replay signed statements, not payloads, from their pin, carried by the read response, and check the statement behind every entry they read (11.9), in D-EVS-24's format (statements of at most 1 KiB; for larger change lists, `changes_root` over sorted changes, so inclusion and adjacent-leaf proofs settle a path); phones keep durable pins and catch up by at most 4 MiB of statements and proofs, else re-pin and mark the gap. The sensitive classes (config, mailcfg, the mailbox's `vault/` and `i/`, approvals) are mirrored and replayed in full (11.13), and a head below a pin needs a verified EvsReseed. Disclosed limit (§2.8): for a path a head reader has never read or no longer remembers ([owner decision 209](#od-209)), which writer-signed version is current as of its first pin, and, after a re-pin past that budget, for every path, rests on evs; HeadCheck confirms the pin, not those versions. (b), a Merkle root over the token tree, is rejected: a PUT per path level, root contention, d+1 GETs per read. *Residual:* that limit.

**Q-EVS-7.** Cross-cutting (§11, §21). Does a preservation hold pause user-initiated shredding (`--now`, the 7-day timer, slot erasure)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 133](#od-133)):** (a) no: holds pause only the server's TTL sweeps and GC for in-scope records and, from M10, drops' deletions, silently ([owner decision 184](#od-184); §21.9), and user-initiated shredding always proceeds (11.12), if counsel confirms that deleting wrapped keys to ciphertext URnetwork cannot read is permitted (§21). A hold keeps only the ciphertext a shred leaves. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-8.** Cross-cutting (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [24](#od-24)). On a shared git ref, disjoint landing ([owner decision 2](#od-2)) leaves a tree no git commit has, so git compatibility and R-EVS-10's CAS cannot both hold. **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 141](#od-141)):** (a): git-mode refs commit only on their tip (D-EVS-22), and file-mode refs (vaults, mailboxes, records, the config) keep disjoint landing, so exact git oids and stock non-fast-forward errors hold; a loser pulls or merges, about 2% of merges in the twenty-agent test. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-9.** Cross-cutting (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [140](#od-140), [145](#od-145); §19, §22). Must the design meet the ~10-15 KiB of drive writes a push in [owner decision 140](#od-140)'s record, when [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s commit point, the head's If-Match overwrite, alone writes ~14 KiB a drive (~10.5 on 1 KiB blocks), since MinIO also rewrites the old xl.meta (11.3)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 140](#od-140), record corrected):** (a): the binding budget, gated at 43 KiB a push per drive (D-TEST-11). The ~10-15 KiB figure was the design team's first estimate, not the owner's requirement, which is the PM9A3 profile itself ("We have to make that iop profile work"): at most 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS at the design load. Not taken: (b) a head per version created If-None-Match, which departs from [owner decision 2](#od-2)'s If-Match commit point; (c) patching MinIO to skip the old xl.meta's copy on overwrite, which gives up its torn-write backup. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-10.** What happens to a path's history when versioning is turned off? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 158](#od-158)):** per version, as Perforce does: versions written with it on stay for the repo's life unless a repo admin drops them ([owner decision 173](#od-173); 11.7), and turning it back on restarts history (11.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-11.** Are the search index's files always versionless? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 159](#od-159)):** yes, so erasing postings is real (11.14). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-12.** Which repo kinds may hold versionless files? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 160](#od-160)):** all but config and mailcfg, with a repo admin's lock in v1 (§8.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-13.** How long does replaced versionless content stay? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 161](#od-161), revising about a day):** as briefly as is safe: a minute, a sweep catching failures, with no recovery window (11.13). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-14.** How do git-mode refs handle large files? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 162](#od-162)):** they stay versioned, with v1's git-lfs on a versionless store pruned outside a per-repo 30-day window (11.11). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-15.** When does versionless ship? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 163](#od-163)):** in v1 as storage format 2, its numbers reserved at M2, older repos migrating (11.6). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-16.** Is there a default versioning rule? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 164](#od-164)):** per network, versionless above 64 MiB by default, edited by admins in the config repo (§7.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-17.** Does replaced content count toward storage? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 165](#od-165)):** until it is purged (§20.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-18.** Should evs keep the newest n versions or d days? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 165](#od-165)):** never; no field is reserved. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-19.** Should v1 ship an admin "drop history" action for a path, which [owner decision 158](#od-158) allows? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 173](#od-173)):** (b), as 11.7 and 11.13 write: a repo admin's signed DROP push on a file-mode ref, refused in config and mailcfg repos, deletes after a 7-day window the kind-1 segments and slots that only the dropped versions name, found by scanning every ref's versions; inline records in packs wait for compaction; statements and hashes stay; under a preservation hold its deletions wait silently ([owner decision 184](#od-184)). Not taken: (a), deferring it to compaction. *Residual:* none (Q-EVS-23 decided).

**Q-EVS-20.** When does a network's versioning rule take effect? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 167](#od-167)):** (a), at a path's creation, from the rules then in force, as 11.7's `choose` row writes, so an edit reaches every repo without its own rules, for new paths, and no path changes without a writer's act; no field 15 is reserved. Not taken: (b) at a repo's creation, (c) at every unpinned write. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-21.** Cross-cutting (§19, §22). How often do git-mode refs and record streams update the index on `ur/index`? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 172](#od-172)):** at most once a minute per writer on 1 KiB XFS blocks (~34-37 KiB a push at 2× year one), else once every 5 minutes (~42-45 KiB on 4 KiB blocks), the block size being §22.8's M2 choice; either way each committer indexes its own commits and its own device searches its journal at once (11.13, 11.14). Not taken: an indexer pushing for every writer. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-22.** Cross-cutting (§8). Does a repo locked fully versioned ([owner decision 160](#od-160)) keep its always-versionless index ([owner decision 159](#od-159))? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 168](#od-168)):** (b), through the distinct value `versioning` 2, which the lock does not refuse, readers accept only under an index root and format 1 reserves at M2 (11.7, 11.14); the lock keeps content history, and the index is derived and rebuildable. Not taken: (a), the lock turning the index off. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-23.** Does a drop wait out a cancellable window before it deletes? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 183](#od-183)):** (a), a 7-day window in which any repo admin can cancel; `now` skips it, as RepoDelete's does; a repo lock voids a pending drop; deletion starts after the window and the 25-minute fence (11.7, 11.13). Not taken: (b) no window, (c) a network setting. *Residual:* none.

**Q-EVS-24.** Cross-cutting (§10.6, §19.6, §22.8; [owner decision 140](#od-140)). Must the PM9A3 write bound hold against aggregate safety work? Per-tenant rates bound each uploader, group and network, never a cluster: 100 large Teams on one metadata cluster, each shrinking every 5 minutes, ask ~57,600 config and directory rotations a day of ~50 MiB a drive, ~2.9 TiB a day against the 0.768 DWPD refill's ~1.5 TB, every rate respected (the meta review's F12). **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 186](#od-186)):** (b), P0 unlimited: P0 work runs at once, never queued or refused, its bytes measured, reported by kind and taken from the other classes' later allowances (11.13); FI-14 bounds the other classes' writes less P0's and leaves P0's unbounded, so a P0 storm wears the drives past 0.8 DWPD and their 1 DWPD rating while it lasts, disclosed with §19.8's P0 page; [owner decision 140](#od-140)'s hard budget is amended for P0 writes only. Not taken: (a) a bounded P0 with its fan-out paced ahead of pushes, which kept the bound unconditional at a write-availability cost in that stress; (c) a finite admitted liability, a count cap [owner decision 66](#od-66) rules out. **Amended by owner 2026-11-06 ([owner decision 190](#od-190)), refining [owner decision 186](#od-186) after the (b) orders had the other classes repay P0's excess:** P0's excess is forgiven, not repaid: the write budget's bucket floors at zero, P0's bytes past what it holds are counted and reported by kind (§19.8), and a cluster's pushes and evacuation restart when a storm ends and ramp up as the bucket refills (11.13); FI-14 subtracts from the other classes' bound only the P0 writes the bucket held; each storm's forgiven excess stays as wear, ~0.23 drive-writes a 6-hour storm at that stress, which §19.8 shows against the ~420 drive-writes that five years at the refill leave under the 1 DWPD rating, ~1,800 such storms. Not taken: repaying the excess from the other classes' later allowances, which kept long-run writes at the refill but stopped the cluster's pushes for about 2.2 times a storm's length. *Residual:* 11.21's P0 row: the storm's wear, its forgiven excess kept; its cluster's pushes and evacuation stopped while it lasts, batches passing 26 h; and an M2 sizing that bounds wear only at the admitted mix.

### 11.19 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:59**, second sentence (plaintext paths, the git-crypt model): superseded by owner directive 2026-11-03; paths are keyed tokens and names are sealed ([owner decision 2](#od-2)). Its first sentence stands (Q-EVS-4).
- **PLAN.md:57** is met at the sidecar's local git server; evs speaks an object API ([owner decision 24](#od-24)).
- **Not in PLAN.md:** cli/UI.md:94 requires an active remote to start the git server, but only the first sync needs one; cli/UI.md:11's 0.0.0.0 default stands ([owner decision 84](#od-84)), with TLS or ssh off loopback ([owner decision 130](#od-130); D-TRUST-8); cli/UI.md:87-89's quotas give way to PLAN's ([owner decision 27](#od-27)); git directories over 4,096 entries or 448 KiB of name table (3,584 entries whose names are under 64 B; 11.7) are refused in v0.
- **PLAN.md:50 and :63** (diff chains with periodic checkpoints) hold for versioned files; versionless files keep only a checkpoint or chunk set of their newest version (owner decisions [158](#od-158), [161](#od-161); 11.7).

### 11.20 Interfaces

- **Provides:** `EvsClient` and `EvsRepo` (`evs_*.go`: `CreateRepo`, `ReadHead`, `List`, `History`, `Write`, `Deposit`, `Consume`, `Subscribe`, `Shred`, `Erasures`, `Delete`, `Restore`, `Import`, `Export`, `Mount`, and v1's `IndexSettings`, `IndexStatus` and `IndexRebuild`; `Write` takes a versioning setting, and `List` and `History` report it and `collected`, 11.7), whose per-path version, signer and git oid answer §16.6's `Lookup(effect_key)` for an evs effect (D-MCP-11); the index writer the push builder calls, its format (`evs_index_*.go`, `sidecar/protocol/evsindex.proto`) and the partitions §16.10's engine reads (11.14); remote search, asking and serving, in the root engine (`search_remote_*.go`, `sidecar/protocol/search.proto`; 11.14); ref modes (11.7); the drop-history engine behind `ur history` and `SidecarEvs`'s four drop calls (`DropHistoryPreview`, `DropHistory`, `CancelDrop`, `Drops`; 11.7, 11.13, §18.5); the `directory` kind (11.12); the sync engine, local git server, `git-remote-ur` and v1's git-lfs transfer agent and tip check (11.11); the `sidecar/evsservice` engine ([owner decision 104](#od-104)); the push sequence that versions §6.8's `evs:<repo_id>`; `place/` and storage for `proj/`, `projrows/`, `rev/`, `hold/` and `gkm/`; 11.13's write budget, its classes, accounts and wallet, and fair share, shared with gkm, api and taskworker; §2.8's evs-1 to evs-26 and evs-28, and connect-5 (evs-10 is §19.6's, evs-27 §16.11's; evs-20 withdrawn).
- **Consumes:** §3.6's indexers; §5 `ServiceToken`, binding log, `git` hello, §5.9's index cache and served record; §6 hints, `Signed`, `HeadCheck` and `RefHead`, `PushReset`, §6.6's RPC and §6.4's control contracts; §7 token exchange and its re-seed mode, `rev/`, the authorization log and its `{acl_}e` cache, `AuthPin`, bootstrap, §7.9's `VersioningRules` and `IndexerSet`; §8 `RepoReaders`, writer sets, kind defaults, §8.5's consent (`consented`), `audit`, access logs (`RepoDelete`, `RepoRestore`, `RepoVersioning`), `EvsShare`, `OwnerConfirm`; §10 `GkmClient`, `DeriveKey`, `GenRotate`, the gate predicate, the `index` purpose; §12 `ResolveNetworkLabel`; §13 certificates; §16.11's path rules and fields; §18 wakes and §18.4's fetch policies and remote mode; §19 clusters, drive counters, `{nvb_<set>}` and §19.6's `{nvb_<cluster>}`, §19.11's `format2` gate and its `purge` and `drop` modes; §20 `ReportUsage`; §21.9 holds.
- **Subprotocol messages:** `EvsHeadChanged` (0x1401; server→client in §6 `PushHint`; a ref moved); `RefHead` inside §6's `HeadCheck` (compare ref pins); 0x1402-0x1403 stay reserved, never reused; `SearchRequest` in `SEARCH` (0x1404) and `SearchReply` in `SEARCH_RESULT` (0x1405) (app host to indexer and back over §6.6's RPC; remote search, 11.14; §6.11).
- **API routes:** Client class, authorized by a service token with aud `evs`, specified in connect/api/bringyour.yml.

  ```text
  PUT|GET|DELETE /evs/v1/repos/<id>[?now=1];  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/restore (409 SHREDDING past deleted), /reseed (admin);
       DELETE and restore answer 409 STATEMENT_MISSING without their projected RepoDelete or RepoRestore
  PUT  /evs/v1/repos/<id>/segments/<sid>?push=<push_id>[&closure=1] (rw, deposit; closure: admin, the team
       directory's included): 200 {EvsUploadReceipt}, or 409 SEGMENT_STALE, or 409 VERSIONING for a kind-5 header naming

       at the storage limit or while spent, §20.7's QuotaRefusal (402 with x402 terms when a
       purchase lifts the limit, else RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; a closure upload past its eraser's 60 a minute or daily
       closure allowance 429 with retry_after_ms, 11.12, §20.7)
  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/push {statement, payload, receipts}, /push/<push_id>/<k> {part, receipts}: 200 {place}

  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/push/<push_id>/lease, /path-epoch, /path-epoch/block (rw)
  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/read {..., fresh} (`base` {ref, version} for an overlay's path it holds no version of),

  POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/slots/delete (admin, the team directory's included);  POST|GET|DELETE /evs/v1/subscriptions

  GET  /evs/v1/repos/<id>/drops/preview/<preview_id> (admin) -> state, progress, list_match per path, versions,

  push refusals, each with the push id: 409 REF_MODE, PUSH_ID_REUSED, SEGMENT_GONE, SEGMENT_STALE, SLOT_STALE,

       uploads, and 507 CLUSTER_FULL with Retry-After for what the storage limit refuses while the repo's

       recorded: true, to every later attempt of its push id; 429 BUSY, FOLD_BEHIND, the budget's
       RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, a CLOSURE past its eraser's daily closure allowance (§20.7), a drop (never a cancel)
       past evs_drops_per_day, TIME_AHEAD, a refusal meeting 8 live refusal records or a refusal fence under

  ```
- **Tables:** none; evs keeps only 11.8's objects ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), plus Redis soft state: §6's hint keys, {evsl_} leases, the {evsq_} push sequence, the {evsh_} head cache and {evsd_} drop hints ([owner decision 136](#od-136)).
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/evs` (staged, stateless) with 11.13's `streamable_paths`; the segment bucket and one bucket per metadata cluster (owner decisions [94](#od-94), [145](#od-145)); limits in config/all/pro.yml (`<tier>.sidecar:` with `store_weight` and `evs_drops_per_day`, `sidecar_abuse:` with `evs_drop_previews_per_day`); the receipt keys; the `{nvb_<set>}` allowance, which taskworker publishes from §19.6's drive counters; GC, evacuation, path-epoch copies, drop jobs and dry runs, shredding and reconciliation in taskworker; §19.11's `format2` gate with its `purge` and `drop` modes; the system git where the local tier runs.
- **Assumptions about other sections:**
  - §2.8's evs rows follow 11.8's families (evs-8 and evs-24 in Redis; evs-21 to evs-23 `spidx/`, `pb/`, `hp/`; evs-25 `place/`; evs-28 `drops/`, `dropscan/` and `{evsd_}`; evs-20 withdrawn), evs-1 listing the `secret` kind, evs-3 a mapper's creation-block end (block_until_ms), an index ref's index_epoch, the time of the newest evacuation fence (fence_ms; GC raises none, [owner decision 203](#od-203)), the refusal records (each a refused push id's first 8 bytes, its statement prefix, code and until) with the newest's time (refused_ms), for a refused push that would have created its ref a placeholder head holding only them (and for a ref evacuation fences before its first commit, one holding only its fence), and a marker collection's done, through and window end, evs-4 whether an upload was a closure upload, evs-11 a carried row's epoch, each removal's marker (the removing push id and version, the path's version) until collected and, while sources stand, each entry's state (carried, fresh or removed), evs-12 the CLOSURE and CUT flags and an index push's index_epoch, an ERASE's or CLOSURE's erased-list hash (a CLOSURE's equals its ERASE's, linking the re-keyed paths to that erasure), a PATH_EPOCH's tail hash with its tail moves (old and new token paths, linking created paths across epochs as evs-15's maps do) and the source-paths hash with each change's source token paths, evs-24 each cached head's time and the push sequence value each ref's last commit raised (GET .../refs?moved_after=), and the head-reader disclosure every path after a re-pin past 11.9's budget; §3.7's F2 follows 11.8's commit and 11.9's statement reads; §22.7's guard lists the families, `place/` included, and lets evs, gkm, api and taskworker write their `{nvb_<set>}` reports.
