| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A flaw in the format, token tree or commit protocol, unaudited and so disclosed (owner decisions [99](#od-99), [119](#od-119)) | Medium | High | Peer review before format 1 freezes; vectors, fuzzing, a model check of 11.8 (§22) |
| The final MinIO build loses conditional-write or listing consistency | Low | High | One-object commit point; §22's suite gates every build |
| A 1M-file ref's path epoch copies for ~17 h, while readers read both epochs; a cluster's copies share 250 operations a second, so refs whose live entries times epochs a day pass ~7.2M keep sources standing, and an immediate epoch on a ref already holding three waits (EPOCH_SOURCES_FULL), creation blocked there | Medium | Medium | Epochs only on removal or compromise, else daily; up to three sources read in one round; the copy speeds to 150 operations a second with two sources, and a cluster's to 1,000 while pushes leave room; refs holding the most sources copy first; a batched epoch waits while two sources stand, keeping the third for an immediate one; §19.8's copy liability and drain time; §19.9 plans live entries per rotating ref; FS-118 |
| P0 work runs at once whatever its volume ([owner decision 186](#od-186)): safety work past the refill, legal within every rate, as from 100 large Teams on one cluster each shrinking every 5 minutes (~2.9 TiB a day a drive of rotations, about twice it), wears the cluster's drives past 0.8 DWPD and the PM9A3's 1 DWPD rating while it lasts, its excess forgiven and kept as wear ([owner decision 190](#od-190)), ~0.23 drive-writes a 6-hour storm at that stress; every push there is shed, and folds and evacuation wait once P0 empties the bucket, so batches stay on NVMe past 26 h until the storm ends; the M2 sizing bounds wear only at the admitted mix | Low | High | Each uploader's, group's and network's rates (11.13's classes); pushes and evacuation restarting within one interval of the storm's end and ramping up as the bucket refills (11.13); the drives' lifetime writes passing the refill's only by the bucket's depth and each storm's forgiven excess, ~1,800 such storms fitting in the ~420 drive-writes that five years at the refill leave under the rating; §19.8's P0 bytes by kind, forgiven excess and wear projection, and its page within an hour of P0 passing the refill, with §19.10's runbook (capacity, place_new, the networks); FS-117; Q-EVS-24 |
| No writer able to map is online when an epoch is due, so creation stays blocked in a name-bearing repo, and dropped holders keep testing names past due elsewhere | Low | Medium | Writers alarm 1 h past due_by_ms, batched epochs included; `ur status` names the ref; any capable writer maps, a tail and a 2-min creation block landing it under steady creation |
| A writer floods a ref with refusals, so others' refusals there answer 429 until a record lapses, at most about an hour for a seal's | Low | Low | 8 refusal records a ref, one added a second, each kept only until its statement's time bound plus 1 s; a refusal ends no other push's attempt, lease, part or seal; evs counts full lists; FS-1, FS-113 |
| Counsel does not confirm [owner decision 133](#od-133)'s condition (shredding under a hold) | Low | High | §21's counsel item, before holds ship (M5) |
| Site loss destroys repos no device mirrors | Low | High | Mirrors; coverage in `ur status`; re-seeding |
| Read and subscription patterns leak more than 11.5 states | Medium | Medium | Whole small reads; 64 KiB alignment; publish the leak |
| A client bug corrupts history, which the server cannot check | Low | High | Oid checks; replay; mirrors; export |

| Per-push drive writes cannot fall far below ~27 KiB: the head's If-Match overwrite alone is ~14 KiB ([owner decision 2](#od-2)) | Certain | Low | The binding DWPD and IOPS limits hold at ~27-43 KiB a push ([owner decision 140](#od-140)); D-TEST-11's §22.8 gate measures it |
| A shredded repo's statements and ciphertext stay up to 26 h in shared batches | Certain | Low | Keys go first (11.12); §2.8 states the bound |
| [Owner decision 148](#od-148)'s markers add ~12.5-14 KiB of drive writes a removed entry, and a collection window holds a fold re-creating a covered path for up to 30 s | Medium | Low | §22.8's fold row counts removals and markers a push before the 43 KiB gate; a window per ref at most nightly, and only re-creations over covered markers wait |
| A build's deadline or settle check fails, so a write lands after a later request on its key and a marker's DELETE removes a live entry | Low | Critical | §22.9's suite and FS-114 per build, upgrade and cluster, and StoreSettle.tla (§19.6, D-OPS-20); until a build passes, taskworker opens no collection window and markers stay |
| At [owner decision 172](#od-172)'s cadence the index adds ~2 KiB a push on 4 KiB blocks (~42-45 KiB at 2× year one, at D-TEST-11's 43 KiB) and ~4 KiB on 1 KiB blocks (~34-37 KiB) | Medium on 4 KiB blocks | Medium | 1 KiB blocks, chosen at M2 (D-TEST-11); D-TEST-13's computed gate, confirmed on production after the freeze ([owner decision 174](#od-174)); the write budget sheds the heaviest network |
| A writer corrupts index files others rely on | Low | Medium | Hosts with text verify; indexers re-derive and alarm ([owner decision 150](#od-150)); a rebuild from text |
| A diff's base or a deletion's mask leaves the index before the entries relying on it, so a fresh device misses or resurrects a document | Low | Medium | 11.14's dependency, merge, tombstone and roll-up rules; an unresolvable chain is `index_malformed` and reads not yet searchable; FS-107, FS-108 and IndexRollup.tla |

| Trigram precision falls as partitions grow, so phones show many possible matches | Certain | Low | Small buckets; overlap ranking; labels; confirmation on open ([owner decision 155](#od-155)) |
| The index is about twice the research's zstd sizes (~110-165 MB for five years at 100 messages a day) | Certain | Low | Phones fetch all only at "search more" or on Wi-Fi while charging; buckets ≤ ~5.4 MB |
| A hold keeps the index files that existed at its placement, staged copies written to seg/ | Low | Low | Later churn is purged as usual (11.13's hold rule); holds are scoped |
| Old or index-unaware clients leave commits unindexed | Medium | Low | Coverage, "not yet searchable", backfill within 10 min |
| A purge bug deletes content a retained version needs | Low | High | Kind 5 adopted only through CAS bases and its header's push; I-EVS-9 and I-EVS-10 model-checked; the purge's reread; §19.11's observe mode first |
| Users lose content they expected to keep | Medium | Medium | Versioning stays on below 64 MiB; history written while on stays; listings and `ur status` show the setting; a repo lock |
| A versionless file replaced mid-download makes a slow reader restart | Medium | Low | The 60 s allowance; all files change only at roll-ups and erasures |
| Pre-v1 devices in a migrated repo cannot read versionless files or the index | Medium | Low | FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED, never misread; §19.11's format2 gate |
| A git-mode tip needs a git-lfs object ur/lfs lost or a prune is removing (a force push to a pruned ancestor, a new ref or tag at old history, an import, a skipped pre-push hook) | Medium | Medium | The tip check touches what a prune could take and refuses what is gone, naming the objects and `git lfs push --object-id` (11.11); a prune keeps every tip of its start read; FS-73 with stock clients |
| Purges and sweeps add HDD DELETEs and HEADs | Low | Medium | ~1-4% of year two's drive operations; a rate per process; §22.8's hdd and trash rows |
| An evs crash leaves queued purges for up to ~26 h | Medium | Low | A 70 s drain on stop; the sweep; §19.8's sweep metric |
| A drop bug deletes content a live version needs | Low | Critical | The fence, two independent scans, the 25 h age rule, whole-object deletes only, I-EVS-15 model-checked, observe mode and its soak (D-TEST-18) |

| Inline content outlives the drop in packs | Certain until compaction | Low | Never served again; slot-keyed repos shred it at once; disclosed |
| Large repos' scans load the HDDs | Medium | Low | Rate caps, one job a cluster, the 50% pause, coalescing, dry-run marks reused |
| A stale mirror returns dropped content at a site-loss re-seed | Low | Low | The re-seeded job deletes it again; §19.10's close report names it |

| A merge bug drops true local matches | Low | Medium | It only collapses, inside the checked span, never the phone's confirmed hits; FS-83 against the oracle |
| Reader transfer binds the directory at 5,000 members | Medium | Medium | §16.11's polling policy, phones off the follow, heads reproduced from cards; a sharded cards ref if §22.8 binds |
| One cards ref's head limits the directory | Low | Medium | One ref sustains ~20-50 pushes/s against ~5.8 at 5,000 members' peak (2.3 at the Team limit of 2,000); FS-86's commit ceilings and §22.8's directory row; a sharded cards ref |
| A repo owner's revocation waits for a directory admin's device to erase its copies | Medium | Low | The private marker hides the name from honest readers at once; any directory admin's indexer or daemon runs it; the wait is shown and alarms past 24 h (§16.11); evs refuses every directory erasure below `admin` (11.12) |

| An erasure whose eraser's device is lost stays pending until another device that may erase it runs: masked and fenced, its derived fields openable to key holders | Low | Medium | Its CUTs' sets and ERASE notes keep it on evs; the member's other devices after 25 h, any eligible device once the eraser is revoked; status and the erasure event show it (11.12's reconcile row) |
| A ref's pending erasures fill its 16,208 B erasure set (about 600 documents), so a bulk erasure at the floor cuts in batches | Low | Low | Complete erasures leave at the next CUT; below the limit erasures complete in minutes; bodies go at the first ERASE whatever the set holds |

### 11.22 Phasing

- **v0a** (§23 M2): format 1 with 11.8's objects and protocols (parts, ref modes, the seal lease, batches, receipts, lazy folds with removal markers and their collection, placement); streams, deposits, slots and ERASE, and the owner-bound read-receipt budget, which an `EvsShare` reader needs before it reads (§16.8, D-MCP-18); subscriptions, Redis soft state, the verified head cache and reads of §7.9's `{acl_}e`; head mode; path epochs; the gate and HeadCheck's ref pins (§6.4); usage events, fair share and the write budget, with its classes, accounts and wallet (11.13); GC and hourly evacuation; mirrors and re-seeding; soft deletion; export; format 1's reservations for format 2 (11.6), refused as FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED (EvsPush flags 256 and 512, fields 33 and 34, EvsHead's index_epoch and the read states `drop_pending` and `dropped` among them; window bits 4 and 5 ignored), and its reserved names, the `.ur-index/` directory on file-mode refs and the `ur/index` and `ur/lfs` refs, which format-1 clients refuse to write (11.14); the `directory` kind, known from M2 (11.12); the slot rule (11.8's 5h and step 6), which format 2 requires, checked by format 1 from M2 too, since it costs one NVMe HEAD on a rare slot 412 and hardens erasure, though M10 suffices for drops; `ur evs rekey`, re-checkpointing every file of a repo under the current generation (§10.16). Format 1's specification freezes at M2's entry review, after peer review of 11.5-11.8 and RECORD.md, and its bytes at M2's exit (D-PHASE-7), after §22.8's drive-write gate (owner decisions [25](#od-25), [99](#od-99), [140](#od-140)).
- **v0b** (§23 M2, with v0a; no format change): the local git server, `git-remote-ur`, the identity hook, the proc-receive journal and imports, the desktop sync engine, overlays and conflict branches, which M2's twenty-agent test uses (§3.15).
- **v1:** compaction and retention; working-tree sync; Q-EVS-3's prefix rules; cross-network and derived shares; agent-subkey provenance; the `directory` kind at M6 on format 1's streams (11.12), with 11.9's streams read and moved listing; format 2 at §23's M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)): versionless files with staging, the purge and its sweep, rules and the repo lock, migration and the git-lfs store with its tip check (11.7, 11.11, 11.13), the search index (11.14) with its erasure cut and erasure sets, each repo's index built at its migration, the directory's versionless cards and its index, the drop-history action behind §19.11's `format2.drop` gate, observe first (D-TEST-18), and remote search, its app-host cases at the later of M10's and M8's exits and its team-indexer cases at the later of M10's and M6's.
- **Later:** full sync on mobile; a state commitment if measurements show head readers need pre-pin freshness; directory-resident children for append-only record directories (the reserved `layout`), if §22.8 shows stream entries' index objects binding; a tool moving placed repos between clusters with one commit point ([owner decision 145](#od-145)), built to land before the earliest cohort exhaustion §19.9's cohorts row projects; a per-cluster batcher, two evs processes batching each cluster's records near ~5 a batch, if §22.8 shows it saves a set; a segment placement that keeps the receipt check and moves upload load, not only new repos, before any added HDD set, ordered by §19.9's hdd trigger ahead of year two's HDD load; a reverse citation index in `pidx/`, if §22.8's `drop` row shows scans binding; for the index, a word complement or semantic layer in the same buckets, Elias-Fano key sets, and per-field postings if §22.8 shows field-scoped queries common.
- **Blocking:** §7's token exchange, `rev/`, authorization log and bootstrap, §8's projection, consent rule and access logs, and §10's objects block v0a; counsel's confirmation of [owner decision 133](#od-133)'s condition precedes holds (M5, §21); X13's clusters passing §22's suite and 11.13's benchmark block production storage.

## 12. DNS: the ur.network zone and per-network zones

### 12.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns public naming: the user root (X4), the network label (X5) and X17; the `dns` engine and dns edge; DNSSEC; zone content and reverse zones; the record API; DNS-01; custom domains; private names (with §17); takedown hooks (§21). §13 owns certificates and CAA, §14 and §15 mail record content, §19 the dns edge hosts, §20 quotas. Notation follows D-ARCH-1.

### 12.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |

### 12.3 What exists today

- ur.network: Route 53, expires 2027-07-02; signed by a KMS key shared with bringyour.com, no DS (RDAP 2026-11-03; mmm/lag.dev/ops/dnssec.md:25-27); MX at Google Workspace, `_dmarc` `p=none`, no SPF or CAA (dig 2026-11-03).
- The platform left ur.network on 2026-10-01: `api`, `connect` and `mcp` are NXDOMAIN, though warp and vault list them (apple/app/network/Shared/Config/NetworkConfig.swift:19-23; warp/services/services.go:396-438; vault/main/services.yml:3-35,641-739; config/main/tls.yml:2-6).
- Public UDP 53 on the lb interfaces is connect's WhoDis transport; no TCP 53 (vault/main/services.yml:345-347; server/connect/transport.go:2321).
- network_name: 5-50 of `[a-z0-9-]`, edge hyphens and `xn--` allowed, nothing reserved; one rename path holds the old name 24 h; deletion frees it (server/model/network_model.go:178-206; server/controller/account_controller.go:13,161-166; server/model/account_model.go:379).

### 12.4 Roots: the registrable domain (X4, X17)

A **root** is a user-content zone that `dns` signs and serves (`config/<env>/dns.yml`). v0's one root, `<root>` = ur.network, carries user content only (owner decisions [13](#od-13), [16](#od-16)): burners live in network zones ([owner decision 32](#od-32)), and recurd.dev only redirects to ur.io/recurd (§19; [owner decision 15](#od-15)). Platform names, the report, lb and HELO hosts included ([owner decision 124](#od-124)), live on bringyour.com; `<root>` keeps only `ns1`, `ns2` (glue), `_psl` (the PSL's proof), `canary` (12.6), `<token>.acme` (certs' challenge targets) and §14.6's `_spf`, keeping SPF checks in the signed zone.

Until `<root>` is on the Public Suffix List (PSL), its networks share one site (cookies, saved logins), one reputation (§21.6), one Let's Encrypt budget and one DMARC organization ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.5; mmm/lag.dev/ops/psl.md:51-56). Steps (D-DNS-1):
1. M0: renew to 2036 under registrar lock; the PSL wants over 2 years of term at listing.
2. Move platform names and company mail off ur.network, warp and tls.yml; the lb sends `*.<root>` to tlsedge (§13.4), and only the apex redirects to ur.io.
3. Serve the zone from the dns edge, switch NS (no DS exists) and delete the Route 53 zone.
4. Set `_dmarc.<root>` to `p=reject` once company mail has left.
5. Once eligible (~3,000 active users, `_psl`, an abuse contact), apply to the PSL and request recategorization (connect/EXTENDERUPDATE.md §10.1).

Until listed: no URnetwork cookies on the root, HSTS preload with `includeSubDomains`, exact-host autofill (§15, §18), and §13.7's rule for session cookies on same-site requests from other networks' pages.

### 12.5 The network label (X5)

**Label ([owner decision 14](#od-14)).** 10 characters `[a-z][a-z0-9]{9}` from crypto/rand (~51 bits), allocated on first need, immutable, never reassigned, and not derived from network_id, whose ULID exposes creation time ([R:server-identity](design/design-research/server-identity.md) §2.11). A draw that hits an existing row or fails `ScreenName`'s reserved or brand rules is redrawn ([owner decision 97](#od-97)).

**Alias** (opt-in, "public forever (CT)"): the network_name, one per network: a copy of the label's records except challenges, live once §13's certificates name it. Labels and aliases share `dns_label`'s primary key (root, label) across kinds and states, so alias claims and `RenameNetwork` (§7.12) refuse any name a row holds, live, retiring or tombstoned.

**Validation** (aliases and new names, §7.12; every new name through `ScreenName`, §21.6): `ValidateNetworkName`; no edge `-` (Boulder refuses it); no `--` at positions 3-4 (no `xn--` or IDNA homographs); not reserved; not brand-confusable after mapping 0→o, 1→l, 3→e, 5→s and rn→m per `-` token ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §5). Team scope labels (v1; owner decisions [40](#od-40), [58](#od-58)), from the signed projection (§8), also avoid reserved owners, hosts, client names (§7.7) and word-number labels. Reserved, versioned in the sidecar repo:

```text
www mail mx smtp imap pop dns ns ns1-ns9 edge acme canary rpt out mta-sts autoconfig autodiscover
  wpad isatap localhost
api app web connect mcp gossip grafana taskworker proxy alt monitor mmm lb auth login account admin
  status abuse postmaster security support billing evs gkm sockets tlsedge smtpedge mxedge certs
fuji cosmic fireside crisp gala snow jazz honey, plus every services.yml host label (a release check)
*-lb *-v4 *-v6 main-* beta-* canary-* community-* local-* by-*
ur urnetwork bringyour recurd burner, plus a curated list of the most-phished brands
```

**Census** (a read-only query in M0):

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name !~ '^[a-z0-9-]{5,50}$') AS pre_rule,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name ~ '(^-|-$)') AS edge_hyphen,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE substr(network_name, 3, 2) = '--') AS dash34,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name = ANY($1) OR network_name ~ $2) AS reserved
FROM network;
```

**Renames, deletion and restore (D-DNS-10).** Renaming network_name changes nothing. A changed or released alias serves 90 days as `retiring` (outlasting 5-day sender retries) under CAA `issue ";"`, its certificates revoked (§13), then is tombstoned forever; deleting a network withdraws its records at once and tombstones label and alias, whose certificates are revoked or expire within 45 days. After a Postgres restore and 12.6's restore step (§19.10), taskworker re-reads CT for `<root>` names logged since the restored dump's time minus 7 d and inserts each name `dns_label` lacks as `retiring` with no network; `label-reclaim` (12.8) re-binds it to its network, and the rest tombstone after the 90 days, so I-14 holds across the gap.

### 12.6 Hosting: the self-hosted dns edge

```text
write (api or dns route), one transaction: under a decision, §16.6's gate first (12.8): a stored result
  for the request's effect_key answers it with no write, else the spend check, then the approval_use claim;
  lock the dns_root row (503 while restoring), serial+1, records + dns_zone_journal diff (+ the use's
  result), commit; then raise {dns}serial:<root> to that serial (a script that never lowers it), which
  wakes the feed (PgBouncer's transaction pooling bars LISTEN/NOTIFY)
dns API blocks (dns.bringyour.com): GET /dns/journal?root=&after=<applied> (long-poll <= 25 s); /dns/snapshot
  (the rows at one serial); a poll the journal cannot continue (after < serial, no row after+1: a
  7-day gap, a restore) answers reload, with restore_serial; every answer also names each lb interface's
  reported custom-host version, with its probe name and the hosts it added, and the map-stale
  interfaces (§13.4)
  rows and snapshots stay readable across releases N and N+1: N ignores fields N+1 adds, and writes
  N cannot read wait until N+1 serves 100% (§19.11)
dnsedge on ns1, ns2 (host-pinned; UDP and TCP 53; no proxy in front, so RRL sees resolver addresses):
  apply each diff atomically, in serial order --> zone in memory + local snapshot; a reload swaps in
    /dns/snapshot's; a replaced snapshot older than restore_serial is kept only until POST
    /dns/reload-diff takes its diff, at most 24 h, and any other is deleted at once
  serve a zone build or key set only once its self-check passes, else keep the previous one
  answer from memory, sign online, rate-limit; SOA serial = root serial
  probe each lb interface every 10 s (owner decision 34; server/services_lb_inventory.go:11-17,35):
    tlsedge's alert on 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671 (§13.4; owner decision 121);
    on 443 also the route probe of the custom-host version the interface reported (§13.4), posted
      to POST /dns/route-probes;
    the 25 banner on §19.5's router interfaces
    drop one after 3 failures, or while the journal names it map-stale (§13.4), never all, and the one
    §19.5's W1 drains
      --> answered from the healthy set at answer time, with no journal write: the A, AAAA at *, @,
          each copy of *'s records and each mx host on router interfaces (12.7)
certs: GET /dns/ready?serial=s --> stale while restoring or for s <= restore_serial (certs writes again
  at a new serial, §13.8); else API blocks read each running NS's SOA over TCP --> ready when all >= s
restore (§19.10, after the dumps load and the abuse step, before api's replay; Postgres comes back at dump
  age with an empty journal, while ns1 and ns2 serve newer zones until they reload):
  §19.10 sets dns_root.restoring as the dumps load, before api or the dns blocks serve: every dns write
    gets 503, so the CT replay (12.5) and api's replay of revocations (§7.10), their DKIM and TLSA
    deletions (I-15) included, commit after this step; until the transaction below, 12.9's SuspendZone,
    SuspendHost and Restore set only their rows, taking no serial, so the suspensions and lifts
    §19.10's abuse step re-places (§21.10) are in its snapshot
  read each NS's SOA over TCP; an NS that does not answer is stopped, and serves again only from a
    reload, its local snapshot taken as the replaced one
  one transaction: serial := restore_serial := max(restored serial, the SOAs read, {dns}serial:<root>)
    + 2^24, above every serial the lost primary issued, since the key lacks only raises that failed or
    that a Redis failover lost (RFC 1982 allows a jump below 2^31); raise the key
  each edge reloads at restore_serial and posts its diff (POST /dns/reload-diff); once every running
    NS answers that SOA, restoring := false; the step lists, by network_id, owner and type, each RRset
    but challenges' and canaries' in a posted diff, and raises the custom-host map's version 2^24 above
    the restored one (dns_root.custom_host_map_version), every host's map_version with it, so W1 loads
    the map from the restored rows (§19.5) and each host stays pending until every interface is current for the new version
    (§13.4), listing the hosts that adds or drops, in the incident and in each network's admin events
    (§7.11), both kept 400 d, flagging networks with an open §21 case
monitor, at the site and on 1 outside host: rewrite canary.<root> TXT each minute through the journal;
  validate it through each NS against the KSK as a configured trust anchor (Unbound trust-anchor);
  2 public resolvers check propagation only until the DS, then validate as well;
  DNSKEY window > 7 d; equal SOA serials
  --> incident alert (server/monitor/alert_classes.go:3-8); from M5, both NS failing or a canary
      signature failing pages §19.8's rota at any hour, 30 min to acknowledge (owner decision 143)
```

```yaml
# config/<env>/dns.yml (sketch)
roots: [ur.network]
reverse: from smtpedge.yml's sending addresses   # M9; HE's classless delegation; unsigned
delegated: Team customers' _domainkey.<domain> zones   # v1 (§14.6); not roots
ns: [ns1, ns2]                  # two hosts at the site; IPv4 and IPv6 from different gateway blocks
ttl: {challenge: 60, edge: 60, mx: 300, mx_host: 300, tlsa: 300, mail_policy: 3600, caa: 3600,
      user: 300, user_range: [60, 3600], soa_minimum: 60, ns: 86400, ptr: 3600}   # edge: A, AAAA at *, @
rrl: {ipv4_prefix: 24, ipv6_prefix: 56, slip: 2, classes: [answer, denial, error]}
signatures_per_second: <cap per host>   # cached answers first
edns_udp_size: 1232
any: minimal                    # RFC 8482
client_subnet: ignore           # RFC 7871; never echoed or stored
tcp: {connections_per_source: <cap>, idle_timeout_s: 10}
```

**Placement (D-DNS-3; owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [123](#od-123)).** The `dns` engine (`sidecar/dnsservice`, miekg/dns) runs as server/cli/dns: API blocks serve §12.8's routes and the feed; the edge role, `dnsedge`, runs only on §19's dns edge hosts, whose own addresses leave the lb's UDP 53 to WhoDis (R-DNS-8), and deploys one host at a time (§19.11). Edges never query Postgres (I-12), so with the core down they keep serving and signing while writes and ACME wait. Both NS sit at the one site (12.15).

**Signing (D-DNS-5; owner decisions [69](#od-69), [109](#od-109))**, online from the first deploy:
- **Denial.** ECDSA P-256. Compact denial (RFC 9824; NXDOMAIN kept without DNSSEC) and wildcard answers signed as the queried name reveal neither which names exist nor which a wildcard covers.
- **Keys.** The KSK stays on an offline HSM, backed up in a second safe; a two-person quarterly ceremony pre-signs DNSKEY RRsets (current, next and standby ZSK) in 14-day windows, released one at a time. The current ZSK is a `secret_files` entry (warp/warpctl/run.go:172-204) mounted only on dns edges, rolled quarterly by pre-publication; the standby stays in vault.
- **DS.** Without one, validators treat the zone as insecure, so a fault harms no one and only the anchored monitors prove signing; the DS follows 30 clean canary days, before M7's TLSA, which §15.5's "validated" label checks ([owner decision 135](#od-135)).

**Runbook (§19.10).** NS down or flooded: resolvers retry the other; HE null-routes a flooded address. ZSK leak: mount the standby and hold a ceremony; forgery ends with the old windows (≤ 14 days). Both KSK HSMs lost: a new KSK's DS before the last window expires.
