### 16.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mcp_tool` or `http` hooks | no spawn | skipped at launch SessionStart; http needs a token in env (I-7) | rejected for v0 |
| Agent-supplied hash and risk | one generic tool | payload swaps, lowered risk; the approver sees no action | rejected: `canonical_action` |
| Server-side searchable encryption | bandwidth follows results | leaks search and access patterns, which leakage-abuse attacks exploit | rejected (D-MCP-20) |
| Fetch only a query's index blocks, or stop "search more" at enough hits | less download | the fetched set names the query's terms, or its size their selectivity | rejected: whole objects, fixed order |
| A fixed time to a cold "search more"'s first hit | one number to quote | a term only the oldest shard holds cannot arrive before its bytes do | rejected: 16.10's cold contract of progress, arrival and completion bounds |
| Verify candidates by fetching their bodies | exact hits everywhere | a query-dependent access pattern | rejected; only the CLI's explicit `--verify fetch` |
| Return untrusted hits' text by default | one call | every mail search taints its run and costs its harness evidence ([owner decision 142](#od-142)) | rejected (D-MCP-23) |
| Index every capture entry (tool calls, transcripts) | finest grain | indexes tool output, much of it outside text, at near the runs' size | Later, once §22.8 measures it |
| A member's indexer answers a phone's query over §6's e2e RPC | confirmed hits with no download | that device must be online; the query leaves the asking device | chosen for app hosts once an indexer is designated (owner decisions [175](#od-175), [177](#od-177), [178](#od-178); §11.14); MCP and `ur search` stay local |
| Announcements as record entries for good (the coordination log's claims) | one mechanism; native history; format 1 | a cold reader's current state costs a day's events, not one card a sidecar (~22 MB against ~1.5 MB at 500 members); renewals pile up | M6's carrier only (D-MCP-28) |
| One file per announcement | one item a file | per run a path's create, removal marker and collection, ~26.5 KiB more each ([owner decision 148](#od-148)) | rejected: one card a sidecar |
| An owned ref per sidecar | evs enforces the writer | a reader syncs one ref per sidecar (~7,500 head reads at 5,000 members) and one index per ref | rejected: one shared ref, readers enforcing paths |
| The `record` kind for the directory | no new kind | grantee readers that policy can change; no fixed path rules; any number per network | rejected: a new kind (D-EVS-61) |
| Keys derived from the config group | no second group or rotation | departs from [owner decision 60](#od-60); the directory's audience can never differ from the config's | not taken ([owner decision 182](#od-182)) |
| Data-repo seats for the directory | no change to [owner decision 144](#od-144) | members past ~1,000 member devices wait keyless | not taken ([owner decision 182](#od-182)) |
| The indexer alone indexes cards | readers fetch fewer heads | bends [owner decision 151](#od-151); heads are reproducible from cards anyway | rejected |
| Hints to every follower of the cards ref | instant views | ~10,000 followers × pushes/s; §11.10's 1,000-subscriber cap | rejected: polling, with leased notices (D-MCP-31) |
| Requests deposited to the approver's vault | private | vault deposits come only from the owner's own sidecars; one approver per request | rejected |
| Requests sealed to approvers inside the directory | others see no request; no per-target prefix | per-approver HPKE, approver sets fixed at filing, harder audit | Later |
| Erasure at the directory's `rw`, readers checking the signer afterwards (the v1 build) | a repo owner erases its copies with no admin device online | evs cannot see whose copies a key covers, so any writer, an agent included, destroys another's entries before readers refuse it, and an entry's key cannot be re-made | rejected: `admin` scope, a repo owner's erasure through the runner (D-MCP-33) |
| A slot-scoped erasure capability bound at each slot's creation | no admin device in a revocation | a run's writer cannot bind the right to another member's repo without a key only that repo's admins hold, and an index file holds many repos' documents | not taken |
| A mandatory directory mirror to restore destroyed keys | undoes a rogue erasure | the mirror's holder becomes the authority over every key, and [owner decision 177](#od-177)'s default has no mirror | rejected |
| A denial that writes only its decision entry (the v1 build) | one push fewer | a requester leasing only its notice never learns it, and its pending counts stand until expiry | rejected: one completion protocol (D-MCP-34) |
| One read request per moved stream | no route change | M6's announce entries cost ~64,000 requests a daemon-day at the Team limit | rejected: 64 streams a request (§11.9) |
| A proof of the signer's right carried in each repo file | verifiable without the log | a chain of RepoCreate and RepoAdmin statements, each with its own pin, and a later compromise revocation still needs the current log | not taken: retained history (D-MCP-35) |
| Prose at `member` trust (16.10's record rule) | richer agent coordination | auto-filed text broadcast to every agent with no person reading it | rejected (D-MCP-29); a per-team setting is Later |
| Person announcements | status messages | duplicate signed config facts in a member-written copy | rejected: views over the config |
| Services as their own kind | one item a service | multi-writer items for socket groups | folded into worker items |
| Live presence (heartbeats) | exact status | a write per beat and a server-visible presence feed | rejected: renewal times; a control-contract Ping on demand (§6.4) |
| A guest view for cross-network shares | discovery across networks | no cross-network evs read exists in v1 | Later |
| Recheck the hash, then rename the original over the path | simple | editors, shells and other harnesses take no lock, so a write between the check and the rename is lost | rejected: move aside, check the moved bytes, install only into a free name |
| An atomic exchange (renameat2's RENAME_EXCHANGE, renameatx_np's RENAME_SWAP) | the path never goes missing | none on Windows; undoing a mismatch can displace a later write | rejected: one protocol on every platform |
| Merge a conflicting path (git merge-file) | fewer manual steps | writes bytes that are no original version (RV2) | rejected: the conflict copy and the target |

### 16.13 Decisions proposed

**D-MCP-1 (proposed).** `sidecar/mcp` uses server's pinned go-sdk (v1.7.0), bumped in lockstep (§4.7), negotiating down from 2026-07-28; only `ur` links it, never sdk, gomobile or wasm. *Why:* permissive licenses, spec churn, sdk size gates.

**D-MCP-2 (proposed).** MCP runs in the §5 daemon, one `ServerSession` per relay connection (16.4), not in each `ur` process. *Why:* one client, keychain and key set (D-CORE-9).

**D-MCP-3 (proposed).** The 16.5 catalog, with O behind §5.4's gate, no admin tools, static text and subscribable `ur://` resources. *Why:* I-7, I-8, deterministic tool lists.

**D-MCP-4 (proposed).** Outside content returns only as tagged data; taint, lapsed hook coverage included, lasts the run; O actions need a run-bound decision from a 16.6 channel, after taint one on a tainted request (TS1), each use spent once per D-MCP-11, labeled by its evidence. *Why:* I-8, I-9, [owner decision 75](#od-75); the lethal trifecta (sidecar/design/market2.md:500-506).

**D-MCP-5 (proposed).** Ingest uses command hooks, transcript tails and hook-boundary scans through a sealed, pre-redacted spool. Hooks fail open but lapses taint the run; a Team "record required" policy may install fail-closed hooks (Claude Code `onFailure: block`, Cursor `failClosed`). *Why:* PLAN.md:109; an outage must not stop work, nor a removed hook reopen egress.

**D-MCP-6 (proposed).** Freeze 16.8's envelope at M3's entry review, after RECORD.md's ([owner decision 25](#od-25)), gated by §22's vectors and peer review, not external review ([owner decision 99](#od-99)), with 16.8's freeze rules (versions, stored-byte hashing, an open kind registry, log order, semantic commitments). *Why:* sealed chains, per-entry slots and salts, commitments and daemon-built requests cannot be retrofitted (REC:223).

**D-MCP-7 (proposed).** No URnetwork-hosted MCP serves sidecar tools; cloud agents run `ur` in their VM ([owner decision 49](#od-49)). *Why:* the owner directive forbids server-side plaintext.

**D-MCP-8 (proposed).** Restore is the W tool `run_restore` (16.7): writing only paths whose every change is the run's attributed edit (D-MCP-15), recorded, and behind a decision in a tainted run; apply moves each path aside, checks the moved bytes against its preview and installs the original only into a free name, so a concurrent writer's bytes go back to the path or stay beside it as a conflict copy, never overwritten (RV4). *Why:* R-CTX-16; §23.4's M3 exit; the apply lock binds only restores, and no platform renames on condition of the bytes it replaces (https://pkg.go.dev/os#Rename), so a hash check before a rename cannot exclude an editor's write.

**D-MCP-9 (proposed).** A harness prompt, or `ur`'s `/dev/tty` confirmation of a typed command, counts only under 16.6's `harness_ok`, signed by the daemon as channel `harness`: for outward actions and their own acl and bridge filings (16.6), never for key (but a member's first presence key), recovery, consent, admission or authority statements or other acl or bridge statements, and in a tainted run only where the matching `requests` rule names harness, never through `evidenceDefault` ([owner decision 142](#od-142)); a host holding a presence key prompts for it instead, and standing approval is a requested grant. *Why:* owner decisions [75](#od-75) and [142](#od-142); any same-uid process can forge a hook event, and an "always allow" click or bypass mode must not become standing reach (I-9).

**D-MCP-10 (proposed).** Every record repo keeps a mirror on an indexer that reads it once one is designated (owner decisions [150](#od-150), [177](#od-177)), `ur status` naming an unmirrored one, slot copies included; depositors spool until consumed, and re-seeds re-upload signed entries verbatim (16.8, §19.10). *Why:* a site loss loses server-held data (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94)); re-signing would break chains and pins.

**D-MCP-11 (proposed).** Each approval use is reserved durably before its effect, by an fsynced `Reserve` in the daemon's ledger or an `approval_use` row in the server-gated effect's transaction; components are idempotent per `effect_key`, each with a `Lookup` by which restarts and retries reconcile; a gate answers a use committed under its key before re-checking the decision, and a daemon reserves a server-gated use only until 60 s before `not_after`; an uncertain use stays consumed (16.6). *Why:* a signed count does not consume itself, so a crash, a lost response or two callers would spend one decision twice.

**D-MCP-12 (proposed).** Decisions bind their spender (`requester_sidecar_id`) and the projection pin they were made under. Every spender runs 16.6's spend check, and an approval activates one grant, under a `grant_id` derived from it, or at most `uses` bridge rules, under ids derived from their uses' `effect_key`s (§17.8). *Why:* gates cannot open the sealed request; replays must not mint grants or rules; a decision made on a forked projection must not spend.

**D-MCP-13 (proposed).** Results are version-aware (16.4, 16.6). *Why:* every promised MCP version must read the same tagged data.

**D-MCP-14 (proposed).** Only approval-capable devices (16.6) give `device` evidence or disable `harness_ok`. *Why:* a read-only or ephemeral device must not remove a working channel, and a second CLI must be able to approve.

**D-MCP-15 (proposed).** Restore points are local and exact (HEAD plus dirty-file copies); a change is the run's edit only when its edits' before and after hashes, each before checked against the bytes the edit applied to, chain across the scan interval, else shell or foreign; restore writes only attributed edits, shell paths only when named after a dry run as an O action. *Why:* scans cannot tell this run's edits from a person's or another run's, and an after-hash alone absorbs a person's earlier edit of the same path.

**D-MCP-16 (proposed).** Run taint is a monotone, fsynced bit in the run's file, written before untrusted data leaves the daemon; a missing or unreadable file means tainted. *Why:* a restart must not reopen egress (I-9).

**D-MCP-17 (proposed).** MCP's evs tools and `ur://evs` resources never touch `secret` repos or the team directory, never read or write the search index's files, never read the config repo and never write it or `mailcfg`, and `mail_alias_*` write their `mailcfg` record only after the decision; MCP signs no authority statement, only the acl and bridge statements 16.6 lists about this sidecar's own resources (its grants, rules and host address), and no approval statement but the daemon's harness decisions. `CanonicalAction` carries every field an O tool acts on, and approvers render only those. *Why:* the approver must see the daemon's action, not the agent's text; no agent changes policy, membership or consent, or reads a key (an ACME account key or a ShareKey, each in a `secret` repo; `K_sock` or a ShareSigner seed in the config; R-MCP-9); an index's outside text reaches agents only under 16.10's trust rules and the directory's prose only under 16.11's, and no agent writes an index or turns one off, or acts for a person in the directory.

**D-MCP-18 (proposed).** Read receipts are budgeted deposits made before decryption, a first read that cannot deposit fails closed, and ingest refuses, with an alarm, a receipt-only depositor's other entries. *Why:* a read-only reader cannot write the author's vault or inject into it, the author sees an attempt, and receipts must not need the author online.

**D-MCP-19 (proposed).** Presence evidence follows 16.6's profiles: WebAuthn with UP and UV per use, attested or asserted, and Secure Enclave keys labeled asserted; a presence countersignature (§7.9's presence row) runs the same check over its act's countersigned bytes, UV required and signCount not compared (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187)). *Why:* a P-256 signature alone proves no person was present; a countersignature stops a thief only if it needs the person, and a verifier of one statement holds no counter.

**D-MCP-20 (proposed).** Search is local and query-blind: one engine on the device serves `ur search`, `ur agents` and the three MCP tools on daemon hosts, an app host's remote search being §11.14's, writes nothing to evs but 16.10's read receipts, and fetches index objects only by sync position, `more` taking every missing all object whole, newest first (16.10; I-19). *Why:* the server then learns only object sizes, rewrite times, writers and sync positions; fetching by query, or stopping at enough hits, would leak a query's terms or selectivity (owner decisions [151](#od-151), [152](#od-152)).

**D-MCP-21 (proposed).** Search reaches only what `evs_read` reaches: 16.10's scopes over the repos §8's local evaluation lets this sidecar read, narrowed per agent; it names each exclusion but `secret` repos, and a reader of an owner-bound repo that is not a writer deposits receipts first. *Why:* owner decisions [23](#od-23), [126](#od-126); D-MCP-18.

**D-MCP-22 (proposed).** Hits carry §11.14's states (confirmed by field or text, possible, near) and rank by phase, latest before all, then by §11.14's tiers, the newest version winning by document key; only the CLI's `--verify fetch` fetches bodies to verify. *Why:* trigram precision falls as the searched set grows, and fetching candidates shows evs a query-dependent access pattern (owner decisions [152](#od-152), [155](#od-155)).

**D-MCP-23 (proposed).** Untrusted hits return as text-free stubs unless the caller asks for `untrusted: include`, which taints the run first; `ur search` withholds them on a non-terminal and, before printing them anywhere, taints each run its process ancestry binds. *Why:* I-9; a tainted run loses harness evidence ([owner decision 142](#od-142)), so finding a message must not cost the run its approvals.

**D-MCP-24 (proposed).** Record logs index each coordination entry and one derived run card per run, from that log's own entries only, and hits group by (network, sidecar, agent label), active groups first, then by recency. *Why:* [owner decision 166](#od-166)'s "find agents working on certain tasks"; indexing every capture entry would index tool output at near the runs' own size, and the team record's salted pointers must not leak through its index.

**D-MCP-25 (proposed).** Pages follow an opaque, session-bound cursor over the ref versions pinned at the search's start, in phase order, ending at an erasure or a lost read in scope; a call returns by `wait_ms` while phase 2 continues. *Why:* 16.4's 30 s bound; stable pages; no page outlives an erasure (D-EVS-26).

**D-MCP-26 (proposed).** Each team network has one directory, a repo of kind `directory`, which its first Owner device creates with the team. Every admitted sidecar reads it, under §7.9's leaves rule ([owner decision 182](#od-182)), and each writes only the paths 16.11's rules give it and its own stream. It is the team's coordination log: claims and handoffs are run announcements, and no network coordination log is created. *Why:* [owner decision 171](#od-171)'s one team repo, used by members and their agents; a second team log would separate the announce metadata from the coordination it serves.

**D-MCP-27 (proposed).** Announcements are runs, workers and repos. Each carries who (attested from the config), what and where, as 16.11's fields. People are views over the config, and services are worker items. A run announces at start with its title, project and branch, renews hourly while it moves, expires 90 min after its last renewal and hands off at its end, and nothing else of a session leaves the vault (I-20). Every general and record repo is announced at creation unless its owner marks it private, and an owner may revoke an announcement ([owner decision 181](#od-181)). *Why:* owner decisions [170](#od-170), [171](#od-171) and [181](#od-181); [owner decision 126](#od-126) keeps session contents in the vault.

**D-MCP-28 (proposed).** From format 2, each announcing sidecar keeps one versionless, signed card on the directory's shared file-mode ref, and each repo with an announcement or a private marker one file; renewals overwrite them. Before format 2, announcements are `announce` record entries with the same body. *Why:* a cold reader then fetches current state in proportion to the team's sidecars, not to a day's events; renewals leave no history (owner decisions [158](#od-158), [161](#od-161)); and M6 needs no format-2 feature.

**D-MCP-29 (proposed).** Prose in the directory's announcements, requests and decisions is untrusted; coordination entries keep 16.10's rule. Agents get stubs of attested and identifier fields, and prose only with `untrusted: include`, which taints the run first. Writes by devices parked for consent count for nothing. *Why:* I-9 and [owner decision 142](#od-142), since that prose is filed automatically ([owner decision 170](#od-170)) or to persuade and reaches every agent unread; [owner decision 126](#od-126) forbids an admin-minted device speaking as a member.

**D-MCP-30 (proposed).** A request is an entry in the requester's directory stream, with a notice under its target's prefix that the target's approvers' devices lease. Persons decide, on `/dev/tty` or in an app, by D-MCP-34's protocol: a repo admin by `RepoGrant`; an owner-bound repo's owner by `EvsShare`; a worker's owner or sponsor, as `autogroup:dst-owner`, by an `ApprovalDecision` the requester spends into a grant to reach the services the worker announces. An agent's or a tagged sidecar's request first needs its member's or sponsor's decision through §5.4's gate. *Why:* owner decisions [8](#od-8), [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75), [126](#od-126), [142](#od-142), [179](#od-179) and [180](#od-180); approvers learn of requests with no server-side list of who approves what.

**D-MCP-31 (proposed).** Directory readers poll rather than lease the cards ref, fetch changed cards by sync position and derive index heads from them, and read the streams each sync finds moved, 64 to a request (§11.9); only desktops keep the index's buckets, phones keep cards while the view is open, showing partial coverage past their metered cap, and a phone's "search more" asks a designated indexer, else fetches buckets and all (owner decisions [177](#od-177), [178](#od-178)); FS-86 holds them to 16.11's cost table. *Why:* at team scale, hint fan-out to every member's devices, reader transfer and per-stream reads bind the directory, not NVMe (16.11's costs).

**D-MCP-32 (proposed).** No agent drops history: a person does, at a device, after the server's dry run and a typed confirmation; MCP only previews. *Why:* an irreversible deletion of keep-forever content ([owner decision 173](#od-173)), and [owner decision 142](#od-142)'s taint rule.

**D-MCP-33 (proposed).** Key destruction in the team directory takes `admin` scope, as in every repo: evs takes its ERASE, CUT and CLOSURE pushes, their `?closure=1` uploads and `POST .../slots/delete` only from its admins, its creator and the config writers, each consented and not read_only, and refuses them below that before any commit or slot rewrite. A repo owner's revocation writes its private marker at once and files an `erasure_request`, which the directory's erasure runner, a directory admin's network-scope indexer or else any directory admin's daemon, checks as readers did and completes, the wait shown on the revoking device and in `ur status` and alarmed past 24 h. *Why:* evs cannot see whose copies a slot holds, so a reader's check after the fact restores no key, and an entry's key cannot be re-made by its writer; [owner decision 181](#od-181)'s revocation needs no erasure right for every writer, and [owner decision 177](#od-177)'s default of no mirror leaves nothing to restore from.

**D-MCP-34 (proposed).** Every directory decision, an approval or a denial, completes by one resumable protocol: the decider's device journals it, files an approval's statement, appends the decision entry, then rewrites the notice from the version it read, adding the entry's `DecisionRef`, decided once it holds a denial or the rule's count of approvals; the device resumes each step after a crash. The requester leases its own notice path and reaches the outcome by one notice read and a head read per entry the notice names. *Why:* a denial that rewrote no notice never reached a requester leasing only its notices, which is what phones do, and nothing bounded found a decision in another writer's stream with no indexer designated ([owner decision 177](#od-177)).

**D-MCP-35 (proposed).** A repo item, in an `r/` file or an M6 announce entry, counts only if its pin lies within 4,096 positions before its push's auth pin, and its signer's right is judged at that push pin, when it wrote, by retained history, the repo's access log in the config head with each statement's position and the rows' admission, consent and revocation positions, with no proof carried in the item, and a log entry ending that right more than 10 min before the push's time_ms voids it for a reader holding that entry; a repo admin's device re-signs an item whose signer leaves. *Why:* repo items carry no expiry, so the cards' reader-relative age check would drop a live announcement once the log moves 4,096 positions, while judging the right at an older pin would let a removed admin backdate one, and evs bounds a push pin only by its ref's head pin, which a writer's own stream or an idle cards ref can leave old.

### 16.14 Open questions

**Q-MCP-1.** [X20] Which record primitives does this design provide, and where is the record designed? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 25](#od-25)):** (b), 16.8's primitives and a frozen `record.proto`; RECORD.md, an M0 deliverable reviewed before format 1 freezes (§23.8), owns record semantics, each kind's search text (16.10 holds the search surface, header fields and run cards), exports, the verifiable log, disclosure, model receipts (D-CTX-5) and cost. *Residual:* none.

**Q-MCP-2.** Should bare `ur` speak MCP on a terminal? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 57](#od-57)):** (b), help on a terminal and MCP when stdin is not one; `ur mcp` always speaks MCP (16.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MCP-3.** For a single-device member without a presence key, what may approve O actions? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 75](#od-75)):** (c), the harness's own permission prompt ([owner decision 47](#od-47)), labeled `harness` (D-MCP-9) where §8.5's `evidence` allows it, in tainted runs only as Q-MCP-6 decides. *Residual:* none.

**Q-MCP-4.** Cross-cutting (X9 §4, X17 §12, §18). How do cloud agents use the sidecar? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 49](#od-49)):** (a), `ur` inside the VM with its keys, over the sandbox's HTTP CONNECT proxy (§4 C8, M4) to §18.9's published hosts, not remote MCP; it reads at once ([owner decision 114](#od-114); 16.9). **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 129](#od-129)):** the residual, a lone agent's shared writes without a witness: agents witness too, and writes stop only at `witness_bound_hours` (D-TRUST-10). *Residual:* §2.8's: no bound across a split the server makes, or in own groups.

**Q-MCP-5 (closed 2026-11-03).** By the design review, not peer review: (b), another device's identity key or a presence key signs approvals, with an SSHSIG for high risk (D-CORE-6); [owner decision 75](#od-75) adds harness evidence (D-MCP-9); applied in 16.6.

**Q-MCP-6.** May harness evidence approve an outward action in a tainted run (I-9), when any same-uid process can produce it? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 142](#od-142)):** (c), by default only device or presence evidence, and harness evidence where the matching `requests` rule's own `evidence` names it, never through `evidenceDefault`; untainted runs keep [owner decision 75](#od-75)'s fallback. 16.6's `harness_ok`, D-MCP-9 and I-9 state it, frozen with `record.proto` at M3's entry review. *Residual:* none.

**Q-MCP-7.** Should a run's title and project reach the network's coordination log without the agent claiming them, so that members and their agents find who works on what? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 170](#od-170)):** (c): in team networks runs announce by default, the harness config's `claims` defaulting to `auto` there and `off` in personal networks, members opting out per member and project; [owner decision 126](#od-126)'s boundary narrows to session contents (16.10, 16.11; I-20) (options (a), never, and (b), off by default, not taken). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MCP-8.** What does access to a worker mean in v1? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 179](#od-179)):** (a), reach: an approved request through the directory becomes a grant to dial the ports, sockets and published names the worker announces, under the access policy, with an approver, an expiry and receipts; delegating tasks to its agent and sharing its run sessions are later items, each a design of its own. *Residual:* none.

**Q-MCP-9.** Which repos does the directory announce, and may a run name a repo that some members cannot read? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 181](#od-181)):** every repo by default, with private repos and revocable announcements: general and record repos are announced at creation; an owner may mark a repo private at creation, so it is never announced on its own, and revoke an announcement at any time, which erases its copies; a run in an unannounced repo shows only its id and `private` (16.11). Owner-bound kinds and the team record are not announced by default, and config, mailcfg and the directory never, [owner decision 181](#od-181)'s reading. The owner confirmed that reading on 2026-11-05, group inboxes (announced with requests closed) included. *Residual:* none.

- **PLAN.md:20** ("cli that speaks stdio mcp by default"): bare `ur` on a terminal prints help (Q-MCP-2, [owner decision 57](#od-57)).

§5.4's `SidecarActionKind` names every O tool's kind, alias deletes and agent-config writes included, and its fresh decision is one on a tainted request (TS1); §5.8 and §17.9 sign 16.6's own-resource filings, a host's `BridgeAddress` included, from any mode; §17.8 derives each bridge rule's id from its use's `effect_key`, and §7.9 admits at most `uses` rules per decision, none withdrawn; §11.6 draws slot ids at random per push statement; §11.7's name-table rule makes a sequence name's row about 128 B, at most 140 B carried, and §11.12's ingest refuses, with an alarm, a receipt-only depositor's other entries; ### 16.17 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hook schemas change across harness versions | High | Medium | versioned adapters; §22 conformance tests; a missed event taints the run and voids harness evidence |
| The redactor misses a secret | Medium | Medium | owner-bound vault; shared writes refuse |
| An editor, shell or second harness writes a path while restore applies | Medium | High | apply checks the bytes it moves aside, never an earlier read, and installs only into a free name, so a concurrent write stays at the path or in a conflict copy (RV4); a write through a handle opened before apply that lands after its end reaches the deleted moved-aside file, as under git checkout |
| An approver signs unread, an agent drives the approver's device, or a harness prompt shows only the agent's arguments | Medium | High | devices render the daemon's action, the summary untrusted; each decision binds one action or a rendered template, each use spent once; per-call harness prompts; `evidence` may exclude `harness` |
| A same-uid process, such as a prompt-injected agent's shell, forges a PermissionRequest hook event (owner decisions [47](#od-47), [75](#od-75)) | Medium | High | presence prompt and default presence key (16.6); never for key, consent or authority statements; in a tainted run only where a `requests` rule names harness ([owner decision 142](#od-142)); records mark `source = hook` |
| Both of a member's devices run agents, and one approves the other's requests | Low | Medium | presence keys (16.6); approver screens render the daemon's action |
| A member's only presence key, a security key, is lost, so the device that registered it signs nothing §7.9's presence row covers, a new key's `KeyRegister` included, until another device of the member revokes it or its `not_after` passes | Low | Medium | `ur keys rm` from another of the member's devices, countersigned by that device's own presence key, which a device with none first registers (16.6's register and remove rows); a second key registered while the first works; a member with no other device admits one by its recovery code (§5.9), since the lost key also blocks that device's admissions ([owner decision 189](#od-189)); platform keys (Secure Enclave, Windows Hello, passkeys) are lost only with their device |
| An admin admits a device under the author to read the vault or approve as them | Medium | High | parked and alarmed until the author's `OwnerConfirm`, which MCP never signs ([owner decision 126](#od-126); D-CORE-13); unconsented devices give no evidence and register no keys |
| A site loss erases entries newer than every mirror and spool | Low | High | partial-mirror warnings (§11.13); D-MCP-10; §19.10 |
| No witness for a shared group's writer (weekend CI, a lone cloud agent, an absent team): writes stop at `witness_bound_hours`, capture spools, and a VM may end first (§2.8's bound, which a split defeats) | Medium | Medium | agents witness too; a 24 h alarm; 72 h by default, up to 168 h ([owner decision 129](#od-129)) |
| A search returns outside text and an injected instruction reaches the agent | Medium | High | untrusted text withheld by default; `include` taints first (D-MCP-16), so outward actions need a fresh decision, harness evidence only where a rule names it ([owner decision 142](#od-142)); `ur search` taints by process ancestry; evs tools never read index files |
| A writer's index omits or invents postings or display fields (a buggy client, a malicious member) | Low | Medium | desktops confirm against plaintext; possible hits are labeled, sourced to the index and checked on open; a designated indexer's rebuild check alarms (owner decisions [150](#od-150), [177](#od-177)); coverage shows `indexed_through` |
| Opening many possible hits, or `--verify fetch`, shows evs a query-dependent access pattern | Medium | Low | MCP never fetches to verify; mirrors verify locally; the flag says so; §2.8 discloses it |
| A stale or skipped index hides recent documents | Medium | Medium | per-repo coverage; the local layer indexes commits past `indexed_through` |
| Background all downloads spend transfer bytes and disk | Medium | Low | a daily byte cap per network, a cache cap with eviction, all only on `more` for ephemeral sidecars; `search_status` shows both |
| A cold "search more" for a term only the oldest shards hold waits out most of all's download | Certain | Low | 16.10's cold contract: progress, each shard's hits as it lands, complete only at the end; desktops keep all in the background; a designated indexer answers phones ([owner decision 178](#od-178)) |
| Scope `all` brings one network's content into another network's agent context | Low | Medium | network scope by default; every hit names its network |
| Free-form agent labels collide or mislead | Medium | Low | groups key on `sidecar_id`; labels show with device and member, `agent_asserted` |
| Injected prose in announcements and requests, filed automatically or to persuade, reaches every member's agents | Medium | High | directory stubs carry no prose; `include` taints first (D-MCP-16, D-MCP-29); identifier fields capped, charset-restricted and labeled |
| Request spam or persuasive reasons wear down approvers | Medium | Medium | an agent's request needs its member's endorsement, device or presence evidence in a tainted run; §20.4's per-requester and per-target limits; approver screens render only daemon-built fields, prose as untrusted |
| Reader transfer at 5,000 members (~2-2.6 TiB a day across a team's daemons), and per-stream reads in M6's form | Medium | Medium | polling, phones off the follow, heads reproduced from cards, moved streams read 64 to a request (D-MCP-31); FS-86 gates 16.11's cost table at the Team limit; a sharded cards ref if §22.8 binds |
| A device parked for consent, minted by one admin, announces or requests as its member | Low | High | its writes count for nothing, and alarm the member's devices ([owner decision 126](#od-126); D-MCP-29) |
| A repo owner's revocation waits for a directory admin's daemon to erase the copies that name the repo | Medium | Low | the private marker hides the name from honest readers at once; any directory admin's indexer or daemon runs the request; the wait is shown and alarms past 24 h (D-MCP-33) |
| A breach on the cards ref replaces or removes another writer's card, repo file or notice, and the purge deletes the replaced version | Low | Low | readers ignore it and alarm, naming the signer; each file's rightful writer reproduces it (16.11's repair row); stream entries take creates only, and erasure takes `admin` |

### 16.18 Phasing

- **v0 (M3), with I-8 and I-9 before M4's first O tools:** in-daemon MCP and `.ur`; R and W tools with `run_restore` and its restore points; version-aware results; Claude Code, Codex and Cursor hooks, ask rules and config hashes; transcript tails, scans, the redactor; persisted taint; the vault record, envelope frozen, with its mirror and its `EvsShare` readers' receipts (D-MCP-18), so no owner-bound share is read unreceipted; device, presence and harness approvals ([owner decision 142](#od-142)'s tainted-run rule), the spend check and use ledger; coverage.
- **M4-M9:** O tools with their components: §17, and C8 for cloud agents, in M4; §12 in M5, with its gate's `approval_use` and `POST /approval/cancel`; §13 in M5; §15's mail tools and same-network `mail_send` in M7; internet `mail_send` with §14 in M9; SSHSIGs; app approvals and wakes with §18's app hosts ([owner decision 88](#od-88)).
- **v1 (M6):** the team record and, in team networks, the team directory as the coordination log (16.11: its repo, keys, streams, `announce` entries, requests and decisions with their completion protocol, erasure requests with the erasure runner, `claims` and its instructions, `directory_list`, `directory_requests` and `directory_request`, `ur directory`), mirrored on admins' indexers once designated (Team; owner decisions [102](#od-102), [150](#od-150), [171](#od-171), [177](#od-177)), the directory's notices waking phones from M8; reach receipts; agent subkeys; filesystem events; model calls (Codex PostModelRequest, harness OpenTelemetry); retention policies; the `audit` reader ([owner decision 63](#od-63)), with its receipts; RECORD.md's verifiable log and client disclosure packets, RS2's (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:898), over 16.8's leaf hashes, order and commitments.
- **v1, §23's M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)), with format 2 ([owner decision 163](#od-163)):** the evs tools' versioning argument and fields (§11.7); `ur search`, `ur agents`, `search`, `search_agents` and `search_status`, the vault's run cards and §5.9's index cache; once M6's team record and directory exist, their projections and other members' agents; the directory's cards, repo files and index, with `search_agents` and `ur search` over it with history; `evs_drop_preview` and the drop states in `evs_history`, `evs_read` and `run_restore`; the engine's remote serving on designated indexers (§11.14); mailboxes search once §15's mailbox carries the index.
- **Later:** a team's own legal holds (§23's assurance stage); regex queries (codesearch's planner); semantic search on desktops and indexers; transcript text in the vault's index once §22.8 measures it; delegating tasks to a worker's agent and sharing its run sessions ([owner decision 179](#od-179)); requests sealed to their approvers; a guest view of the directory for cross-network shares.
- **Blocked by:** D-CORE-9, §5.4's gate and §5.8's `.ur`; §7.8's receipt scope; §7.9's config repo, authorization log and `read_only` admissions; §6.11's `SignedType`; §8.5's consent (M2; [owner decision 126](#od-126)); §11's streams, multi-part pushes, deposits, slots, ERASE pushes and mirrors; D-ACL-7; RECORD.md, with its search text per kind; §11's search index and versionless storage (owner decisions [159](#od-159), [163](#od-163)); for 16.11, M2's reservations of the `directory` kind, `autogroup:dst-owner`, `EvsShare.expires` and `ServiceSettings.directory`, and §7.9's leaves rule for its group.

## 17. IP addresses, subnet routing, and port forwarding

### 17.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns PLAN.md's bridge (PLAN.md:113-119): the overlay address plan (X18, owner decisions [28](#od-28), [132](#od-132)), subnet routing, provider port mapping, bridge rules, their engine and states, native IP principals (`WindowDelegation`), cross-network shares ([owner decision 86](#od-86), C18), the connect changes, `BridgeHost`, `ur tun` and `ur bridge`. §7.9 owns the config repo and authorization log; §8 policy, grants, shares and gates; §12 names; §13 `public-tls`; §18 the sdk seam, the forwarding role's setup in apps' VPN components ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) and app work; §20 billing.

### 17.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-BRIDGE-1 | A destination in a client's subnet goes to that client, not the default route | PLAN.md:115 |
| R-BRIDGE-2 | Providers rewrite destination ip:port by port mappings for same-network packets | PLAN.md:117 |
| R-BRIDGE-3 | Rules stored on the server, pushed in real time, decided locally | PLAN.md:119; owner decisions [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6) |
| R-BRIDGE-4 | The sdk device gains "ip addr, port forward" through Sidecar-implemented abstractions | PLAN.md:31 |
| R-BRIDGE-5 | A permanent private address per agent and service, plus routed subnets; Linux and WSL2 first | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:687, :894 |
| R-BRIDGE-6 | A forward is a grant (one agent, port and window, approved), encrypted between sidecars | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:680-681 |
| R-BRIDGE-7 | With a policy, agents reach only granted ranges and exit only through customer exits | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:689; [owner decision 120](#od-120) |

| R-BRIDGE-10 | With an ACL document, only rules open a provider's loopback, LAN, link-local or overlay addresses; its own daemon listeners never open, and unverified policy state opens nothing private | §2 I-10; owner decisions [50](#od-50), [105](#od-105), [120](#od-120) |
