**D-SDK-13 (proposed).** The forwarding role takes rules and names only from the `BridgeState` its own compile of the verified config produces and the anchored deltas after it, persists its posture (legacy, pending, enforcing), restoring enforcing state before the first packet, and signs each window client's `WindowDelegation` itself, with its forwarding key or a share's current `BridgeShareSigner` (18.6). *Why:* owner decisions [3](#od-3), [85](#od-85), [197](#od-197); forwarding must never wait on the app, a restart plus an unsigned `has_document = false` must not reopen a LAN, and §17.9's hosts admit only delegated window clients.

**D-SDK-14 (proposed).** Transport rejections are generation-bound and map to Unenrolled with a reason; only a verified `SidecarRevoke` maps to Revoked. *Why:* a lost or expired client is not a revocation (D-CORE-8), and a stale callback must not end a new pairing.

**D-SDK-15 (proposed).** `SidecarKeyStore` returns status codes and a `SidecarSecret` struct (18.5). *Why:* gobind carries no error type, and a crossing panic exits the app.

**D-SDK-16 (proposed).** Wakes follow 18.7: a slot-local script, a separate enqueue for token holders, client acks from connect's frame ack, a deferred check while live, and per-slot sentinels that reconcile a restarted master's tokens. Token projections follow each row's revision: every change, a removal's tombstone included, raises it in Postgres; a slot-local script applies a revision only above `tokrev` and within 60 s of the TIME its writer read before the transaction; a slot whose master changed is reconciled 90 s after the pass that found it; and each pass re-applies the rows changed since the last one. *Why:* Redis Cluster refuses cross-slot transactions, a stale live marker must not drop the only wake, and masters have no replicas and restart from their last RDB dump; a post-commit SET lands in no order that a Postgres commit or row lock sets, so an older POST's SET could replace a newer token or revive a removed one until the next launch (meta review F15).

**D-SDK-17 (proposed).** An ephemeral client's polls refresh its narrow `network_client_lease` row at most once per 5 min; it is reaped only with no open connection once that lease and its newest disconnect are both over 35 min old, 30-36 min after the later, and an unload beacon closes it early by a 128-bit capability (18.8). *Why:* no resident measures an HTTPS-only host's disconnect; `auth_time` refreshes hourly over `network_client`'s ~10 indexes, so a reap keyed on it revokes connected agents on any blip; `sendBeacon` sets no Authorization header, and the token stays in the Worker.

**D-SDK-18 (proposed).** Browser keys, tokens and the Worker live in a key origin that ur.io pages frame and message by exact origin, one Worker per network under a Web Lock. *Why:* one shared origin would let any ur.io XSS take the key, and two tabs' Workers over one IndexedDB would race refreshes, commits and keychain writes.

**D-SDK-19 (proposed).** The page Worker builds the root with `-tags sidecar_http`, linking no connect package: connect-facing and engine host (`host_*.go`) files are `!sidecar_http`, and the rest, token path included, use only §5.4's root types and `SidecarApi`. *Why:* importing connect links its IP stack, putting the 40 MB goal out of reach without C17.

**D-SDK-20 (proposed).** The forwarding role is `sidecar/device`, importing connect and `sidecar/protocol/bridge` only, with the root's forwarding files, the only root files the `ios_extension` leg links, whose file and descriptor lists `make check` holds (18.10). *Why:* [owner decision 197](#od-197) puts the config follower and compiler in the VPN component, and only an allow-list keeps every other root init and descriptor out of the jetsam-bound tunnel.

**D-SDK-21 (proposed).** Every host that searches a repo keeps its two latest buckets synced, phones' team directory aside (D-SDK-28). Desktops and indexers keep all in the background; phones fetch it at "search more" for repos no designated indexer answers and browser tabs at "search more", both also on Wi-Fi while charging, phones in OS windows, and tabs while open only where their browser reports both conditions; ephemeral agents fetch it only at "search more"; each device may override per repo, within 18.4's caps. A condition an app or browser has not reported counts as metered and not charging. *Why:* owner decisions [154](#od-154), [177](#od-177) and [178](#od-178); 154's per-device override covers browsers, since Safari and Firefox report neither condition and desktop browsers no network type, and ephemeral agents, whose in-memory caches would re-download all at every start; only OS windows let a backgrounded phone download tens to hundreds of MB.

**D-SDK-22 (proposed).** Apps search through `SidecarSearch` (18.5): one call streams replacing pages of hits labeled verified, confirmed, possible, near or unmatched, each naming the indexer that verified it if one did, with progress that names the bytes to fetch, any metered wait and the remote state. *Why:* gobind's limits; one implementation of masking and ranking on every host.

**D-SDK-23 (proposed).** Hosts report network and power conditions and the foreground, apps through `SetConditions` and `SetForeground` and browsers through the key-origin frame's network, battery and tab visibility, and apps grant background time through `RunBackgroundSync`; the Go core reads no platform API. *Why:* none is portable across gomobile, the C ABI and js, the OS decides when a backgrounded app may run, and without a foreground report each search opens its own contract, the timing [owner decision 188](#od-188)'s windows exist to hide.

**D-SDK-24 (proposed).** The page Worker links the search engine and keeps its search cache in its own IndexedDB store, written only by the Web Lock holder; pages receive hit views only, and the quick burner searches its buckets in memory and never fetches all. *Why:* [owner decision 76](#od-76)'s one browser runtime; eviction and Safari's 7-day rule make the cache disposable by design.

**D-SDK-25 (proposed).** Search meets 18.4's warm targets and §16.10's cold contract on phones, desktops and the page Worker, each search's masks inside its working set; §22 measures them on surrogate phones ([owner decision 100](#od-100)) and in Safari's wasm engine before M10's exit ([owner decision 169](#od-169)), and the remote targets on surrogates from the later of M10's and M8's exits. *Why:* the research left decryption rates on phones and in Safari's wasm unmeasured; a cold download's first hit depends on where the match lies, so only its progress, arrival and completion can be bounded.

**D-SDK-26 (proposed).** Where its network designates a search indexer that may answer, none being designated by default ([owner decision 177](#od-177)), app hosts ask it at "search more" by default. The mode is per device and network: `on` (own indexers, then other members' that §11.14 allows, each new answering member only after the app's notice), `own` or `off`, kept in §5.9's non-derived search state, never in the config repo. Keystrokes search only the phone, and a repo none answers falls back to [owner decision 155](#od-155)'s download. *Why:* owner decisions [175](#od-175) and [178](#od-178); the notice and the setting make a member's disclosure of team-repo queries known and reversible without changing that default.

**D-SDK-27 (proposed).** At foreground, an app host with remote search on sends Hello, with feature bit 1, to its first-choice own search indexer, which its hourly HeadCheck round counts among its own-device picks, unless its session there lives, and while in the foreground keeps that pair's §6.10 window with a Ping a minute, so no "search more" needs a new contract or Hello. It waits `Search.RemoteTimeout` (3 s unmetered, 5 s metered) before the next indexer, hedges only among own indexers, and skips a failed one for 2 min. *Why:* the contracts a search rides then open at foregrounds and window ends, not at the search unless it fails over or finds its session lost ([owner decision 191](#od-191)), so connect's stored rows and reports keep [owner decision 176](#od-176)'s promise ([owner decision 188](#od-188)); the first page saves 0.5-1.5 s; and no query reaches more devices than it must. The keepalive costs one small frame each way a minute while the app is in the foreground.

**D-SDK-28 (proposed).** Apps reach the team directory through `SidecarDirectory`, create private repos and announce or revoke repo announcements ([owner decision 181](#od-181)), and decide access requests through `SidecarApprovals`. Phones fetch announcements only while the view is open, ask a designated indexer at "search more", else fetch buckets and all, and lease notices for their member's targets and their own requests' notice paths, so every decision wakes its requester; past the metered cap a view shows partial coverage it can continue. *Why:* owner decisions [170](#od-170), [171](#od-171) and [181](#od-181); approvers and requesters in the apps need wakes, and a phone cannot follow a team's cards.

**D-SDK-29 (proposed).** Drop history in the apps is admin-only, behind the server's dry run and a typed name, and on an owner-bound repo only on its owner's consented devices. *Why:* owner decisions [126](#od-126) and [173](#od-173); an irreversible deletion takes a person's deliberate act.

**D-SDK-30 (proposed).** Apps list the member's devices and revoke another of them through `SidecarApprovals`' `GetDevices`, `PreviewRevokeDevice` and `RevokeDevice` (18.5), bound types under gomobile and JSON in the C ABI and js, which wrap §5.4's calls under §5.6's rules: the plan's copy before the person confirms, `SignWithPresence` wherever the plan sets `Presence`, in remote mode over the act's bytes the daemon's first call returns (§5.8), its evidence the countersignature every verifier checks (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187)), `authority_pending:<proposal_id>` while an AdminSet member's revocation, its target suspended, awaits other AdminSet devices' cosigns through `Decide`, and `REVOKE_NOT_CAPABLE` on hosts that are not approval-capable, the extension's alarms-only hosts among them, whose `ur native-host` relays none of these calls. *Why:* §5.6's app path had no bound call, `Decide` answering only pending items and `Core()` being Go-only; gobind's limits; and the binding must neither bypass §5.6's approval nor give a read_only or alarms-only host a signing path (§16.6).

**D-SDK-31 (proposed).** Apps check and follow internet sends through `SidecarMail`: before Send, `CheckSend` gives each recipient domain's mode, the message's encoded bytes, the DATA cap, the expected delay and a predicted outcome; after it, `GetSendResult` and the `mail_send` event give each domain's outcome, with 18.5's copy; `GetReceiverCoverage` speaks only of receiving. *Why:* [owner decision 125](#od-125) keeps the DATA cap, so a person needs the size, the cap and the one domain it stops, at composition or before MAIL, and an inbound API cannot explain an outbound limit (meta review K04).

**D-SDK-32 (proposed).** Forwarding is authorized by a forwarding Delegation the sidecar signs for keys its VPN component generated and never exports, and runs on forwarding clients the sidecar mints as its `forward_only` children, which the VPN component refreshes itself; the forwarding key signs only that sidecar's `WindowDelegation`s, and the Delegation ends with the sidecar, its `DelegationRevoke` or a newer one (18.6, §7.9). *Why:* [owner decision 197](#od-197)'s self-contained forwarding keeps the device one subject in policy, `ur devices` and admissions, and reuses the Delegation's signer path, reader wraps, rows, revocation and cascade.

### 18.13 Open questions

**Q-SDK-1.** [X14] What runs the extension's sidecar? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 26](#od-26)):** (a), a slimmed `sidecar.wasm` Worker, HTTPS-only first, and meanwhile (c), the native companion to a desktop `ur daemon`; never a hosted sidecar (18.8). *Residual:* 18.10's size spike, which decides C17 for the extension's streaming Worker only ([owner decision 22](#od-22)); pages use the `sidecar_http` leg (D-SDK-19).

**Q-SDK-2.** Where does the sidecar run beside a network process (PLAN.md:28, :31)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 87](#od-87)):** (a), in the iOS app and the desktop `ur daemon`; network processes stay keyless (D-SDK-1). **Amended by owner 2026-11-09 ([owner decision 197](#od-197)):** every app's VPN component (Apple's network extension on iOS and macOS, Android's VPN service, the Windows and Linux app services) runs the device's IP and port forwarding and nothing else of sidecar: its overlay address, port forwards into it, routes to other devices' subnets and its own advertised subnet, always on whenever the component runs, with no setting that turns it off, and self-contained, with its own forwarding key, taking rule changes directly so it never waits on the app (18.4, 18.6; D-SDK-32). [Owner decision 87](#od-87) holds for everything else, and on Android the sidecar role runs only while the app is open, as on iOS. *Residual:* none; forwarding's budget in the iOS extension, Q-SDK-7, is decided (owner decisions [215](#od-215), [216](#od-216)).

**Q-SDK-3.** Do phones get wake pushes? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 88](#od-88)):** (b), content-free APNs and FCM wakes from the first app hosts (M8; 18.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SDK-4.** How does the ur.io quick burner run (cli/UI.md:164)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 76](#od-76)):** (b), an ephemeral, labeled wasm sidecar in the page (18.8; Q-CTX-2). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SDK-5.** Cross-cutting (D-REPO-2). Where does the iOS device role's code live? Even with engines in `<svc>service` packages ([owner decision 104](#od-104)), a root-package device role links every root init and `protocol` descriptor into the iOS extension. **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (b) now. The device role is the leaf package `sidecar/device`, importing only connect and a generated `sidecar/protocol/bridge` (D-SDK-20); the root never imports it, and the iOS extension links neither the root nor `protocol`. Conditions: `protocol/bridge` imports only std and protobuf ([owner decision 52](#od-52)'s test); `make check` fails the ios_extension leg if its deps include the sidecar root or `sidecar/protocol`; `make size`'s 1 MiB gate stays and passes at M4; §2.10 gains the routing-integrity row; §17.10's `sidecar.Bridge` becomes `device.Bridge`. [Owner decision 197](#od-197) then put the config follower and compiler in every VPN component, so the extension links `sidecar/device` with the root's forwarding files and `protocol`'s config, acl, evs and gkm descriptors under 18.10's allow-list, the root still never importing `device/`, and the size gate follows [owner decision 215](#od-215). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SDK-6.** May a phone or browser ask one of its network's indexers to search all and return verified hits, instead of downloading all and showing possible matches? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 (owner decisions [175](#od-175), [177](#od-177), [178](#od-178)):** (c), amended: in v1 a phone's "search more" asks one of its network's designated indexers that reads the repo end to end over the sidecar subprotocol (Required mode) and gets verified hits, an owner-bound repo only on its owner's consented device, replies padded to 16 KiB steps (§11.14's remote search, with 18.4's notice and setting); a network has no indexer by default, so by default a phone downloads all and shows possible matches ([owner decision 155](#od-155)), as it does whenever none is online (options (a), never, and (b), later and opt-in, not taken). Browser tabs, whose Workers carry no connect client, keep the download (18.17's Later). *Residual:* none; connect's byte reports are [owner decision 176](#od-176) (§6's Q-PROTO-4).

**Q-SDK-7.** Cross-cutting (§4.7, §22.9). What budget does forwarding get in the iOS network extension, now that [owner decision 197](#od-197) has it follow the config repo and compile its own rules there? **Decided by owner 2026-11-10 (owner decisions [215](#od-215), [216](#od-216)):** (a), one implementation of the rule table, with measured numbers: the `ios_extension` leg adds at most 6 MiB (6,291,456 B) of executable, measured stripped as the shipped binding is, and the signed extension's ceiling rises from 50 MiB to 54 MiB (56,623,104 B) ([owner decision 215](#od-215)); a compile in the iOS and macOS network extensions is admitted only when 5 × rows + 2 × head + 1 MiB fits a 10 MiB cap and the room under a 30 MiB process ceiling, about 4,300 devices at the tunnel's connected baseline, and a larger network keeps its last verified state on that device, applies every revocation it can check and raises `bridge_alarm`, never going pending for a statement that waits on a compile ([owner decision 216](#od-216)). A second follower in `sidecar/device` (b) and the app compiling on iOS (c) were not taken; 18.10, §4.7 and §22.9 carry the numbers. *Residual:* none; a compile past the cap for larger teams on iOS is review-phase work.

### 18.14 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:13 ("all service code goes in the root").** The forwarding role's packet side is the leaf package `sidecar/device`, which apps' VPN components link with only the root's forwarding files, as §4.15 records (Q-SDK-5, closed by peer review; D-SDK-20; [owner decision 197](#od-197)).
- **PLAN.md:28 ("in the background ... as a web worker").** The extension's Worker follows ur.io's page Worker (M4) and its native companion (M8); Firefox's is session-scoped (Q-SDK-1).
- **PLAN.md:28 ("used directly by the apps").** Desktop apps use the `ur daemon`; iOS runs the sidecar in the app, not the tunnel, and every app's VPN component runs only forwarding (Q-SDK-2; owner decisions [87](#od-87), [197](#od-197)).
- **PLAN.md:31 ("initial goal", abstractions "that the Sidecar struct implements").** `device.Bridge`, not the whole `Sidecar`, implements `deviceBridge` (Q-SDK-2, Q-SDK-5), and sdk exposure arrives at M8, after M4's dark seams (Q-PHASE-1).

### 18.15 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the `sdk.Sidecar` API, gates, state reasons and approval kinds, a revocation proposal's cosign included; the member's device list and revocation (`GetDevices`, `PreviewRevokeDevice`, `RevokeDevice`) with its copy; `SidecarSearch`, the search policy, conditions and windows, remote search's requester side (modes, notice, `GetIndexers`, the foreground Hello, merged states) and the key origin's search operations; `SidecarDirectory`, `CreateRepo`'s `private` and access-request approvals; the drop calls and `History`'s states; the send check and results (`CheckSend`, `GetSendResult`, `mail_send`) with their copy; `deviceBridge`, forwarding's setup (its keys, the forwarding Delegation, the forwarding client and the hand-off), its following, compile and signing in the VPN component, posture, zone and local addresses, `BridgeHost` in `DeviceLocal`, bridge status; the forwarding leg's file and descriptor lists; the hosted mark; the browser sidecar, its key origin, the poll lease, the ephemeral reap predicate and the close capability, and the native host; the wake dispatch and payload; 18.4's per-host log retention (§5.9, §7.9); 18.9's host list; the `sidecar_http` leg; edge-login signatures (§13.7).
- **Consumes:** §4 (C4, C5, C8, C14, C16, C17, `make check`'s legs, `make size`); §7.9's forwarding Delegation, §7.4's `forward_only` mark, §7.8's config-read exchange and §10.5's forwarding key holder ([owner decision 197](#od-197)); §5 (gate, alarms, control mode, pairing, `SidecarHost`, every-leg types, `SidecarApi` and `sidecarTokenManager`, store states, §5.4's device revocation calls); §6 (the hint script's `tok` and `live`, `PollResponse`, `POST /sidecar/close`, `HeadCheckProof`'s 64 KiB); §7 (marks, P0 stages and DPoP, the ephemeral mint and its `close`, the exchange, admissions, `read_only`, the leaves rule, the log's fold and retention, recovery windows and `RecoveryVeto`, projection, the reaper); §8.5, §8.9; §9-§11; §12.9; §14-§17; §19; §20.8; §11.14's search engine and remote search, §5.9's index cache and non-derived search state; §16.11's directory; §11.7's and §11.13's drop.
- **Subprotocol messages:** `SearchRequest` (`SEARCH`, 0x1404) and `SearchReply` (`SEARCH_RESULT`, 0x1405) (§6.11, §11.14): app hosts send requests to designated indexers and take replies, as requesters only, never serving (M10).
- **API routes:** `POST /sidecar/push-token {platform: apns|fcm, token}` (Client; sets or, when empty, deletes the caller's wake token; M8).
- **Tables:** `sidecar_push_token(client_id, platform, token, rev, update_time, removed_time, slot)` (api; migration ≥926, §19's MG8; `rev`, 18.7's revision; `slot`, the hash slot of `{scp_<C>}`, indexed for 18.7's reconcile, and `update_time` for its sweep; a removal keeps the row as a tombstone without platform or token; no foreign key: each path that removes a client tombstones its row and sets `removed_time` in that transaction, and 18.7's sweep deletes the row 24 h later); `network_client_lease(client_id, seen_time, close_sha256)` (api; MG1, with the auth keys that mint the first ephemeral clients; read by the reaper; deleted with its client; 18.8); Redis `{scp_<C>}live` and `{scp_<C>}ack` (publishers), `{scp_<C>}tok` and `{scp_<C>}tokrev` (the token projection and its revision, which api, the push sender and taskworker change only through 18.7's apply script), `{tokgen_<n>}` (taskworker's 16,384 per-slot sentinels) and `{wakeq_<shard>}` (owning services, evs included, write; the push sender reads; 18.7); `{scp_<C>}hb` (api, the poll lease; 18.8).
- **Services and config:** `CheckOrigin` on connect's H1 upgrader (18.3); `https://ur.io` and the key origin `https://sidecar.ur.io` in `cors_origins` (warp/services/services.go:676) for api (auth included), evs and gkm, the lb's CORS headers extended additively (warp/warpctl/config.go:2136-2138): `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` gains PUT and DELETE, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` `DPoP`, `If-Match` and `If-None-Match`, and `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` `ETag` and `Retry-After`, the lb still sending no `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`; the key origin's loader, CSP and frame-ancestors, the page Worker, its label and `hosts/v1.json` (mmm), with a minimal ur.io/recurd page at `mmm/ur.io/astro/src/pages/recurd/` on mmm's `sidecar` branch: the served-code label, the key-origin frame, the sign-in hand-off, a record list, one record view and download links, unstyled beyond the site's layout, its visual design out of scope ([owner decision 223](#od-223)); extension `offscreen` and optional `nativeMessaging`; native-host manifests for URnetwork's extension ids only; APNs and FCM credentials (§19).
- **App work this design assumes (out of scope; external releases, §23):** running forwarding in every VPN component (Apple's network extension on iOS and macOS, Android's VPN service, the Windows and Linux app services) whenever it runs, with no setting that turns it off, its keys and state in the stores §5.9 names, and Android's VPN service in a process of its own ([owner decision 197](#od-197)); `GetBridgeRoutes`, a chosen RFC 1918 block included ([owner decision 132](#od-132)), lifted from §17.3's tun exclusions (Windows: WFP permits; Linux: the complement set), and `SetBridgeLocalAddresses` from the platform's routes and DNS settings; 18.4-18.7's seams (receiver, the composer's send check and results, autofill, push, approvals, alarms, presence key, §5.8's pairing); re-minting the device client after its forwarding role's first state (18.6); for search, 18.7's OS windows and conditions, the metered prompt with its byte count, labels for possible matches, 18.4's notice and setting, the indexer list and "verified by" labels; the directory view and access-request approvals; the drop dialog and pending drops' cancel (18.5); and, as prerequisites of §7.4's stage 2 (M3), 18.7's credential rules: the desktop app release and the extension release that stop persisting `by_jwt`.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §14 sends the extension's outbox mail as it does phones'; §6.8's hint script returns `tok` and `live` for 18.7's enqueue; §16.6 defines approval-capable hosts and the presence profiles; §5.6's `recovery_window` and §7.9's `RecoveryVeto` cover an admission by a binding the cascade restored as they do a recovery-signed authority statement, and §7.9's cascade list names each device that sealed to a binding it voids ([owner decision 149](#od-149)); §17.10's `BridgeHost` and `BridgeStatus` live in `sidecar/device`, which D-SDK-20's tunnel may import; §5.8's control mode carries a remote-mode app's forwarding setup (18.6) to its daemon, which signs the forwarding Delegation and mints the forwarding client for that app alone; §17.4 carves the local addresses `SetBridgeLocalAddresses` passes; §7.7's ephemeral mint inserts the lease row and §7.8's responses return its `close` once, §7.10's ephemeral job applies 18.8's predicate, §6.16's poll writes only the lease, never `network_client`, and §6.18 phases `POST /sidecar/close` with it (M1); §19.7 lists `network_client_lease` in MG1; §7.9's fold bounds the log tails 18.4 keeps, and FS-17's phone holder answers a `HeadCheckProofRequest` from them; §22.7's Redis-write assertion admits the `{wakeq_}` entries evs writes (18.7); §19.4's token row defers to 18.7's steps 0, 5 and 6, and its sender tombstones a token on a vendor 410 only while the row still holds the revision it read; FS-36 kills one master and restarts one from an older dump, and expects a count only for step 2's failed XADDs, and FS-120 delays applies past later commits; each path that removes a client (§7.10) tombstones its token row in that transaction; §19.10's api step raises every row's rev by 2^32 after a Postgres restore; §22.9's Browsers row opens two tabs on one network (18.8's instance rule); §5.8's control mode carries `Search` streams, status and policy calls to the daemon (18.7) and returns untrusted hits' text to a caller that asks for it; §6.4's control contracts carry SEARCH where reach does not (D-PROTO-21); §11.14 owns remote search's eligibility, failover and merge and cites 18.4's notice; §16.11 defines the directory, its notices and their `q/` leases; §5.4 carries the new event kinds and fields and the `Directory` and remote-search settings, and §5.9 keeps 18.4's overrides, modes and notice answers in its non-derived search state; §5.4's `Devices`, `PreviewDeviceRevoke` and `RevokeDevice` carry §5.6's rules and `REVOKE_` codes, and §5.8's control mode carries a remote-mode app's revocation calls and presence evidence to its daemon, the first call returning the act's countersigned bytes under Presence (D-SDK-30), and §7.9's presence row and §6.9 define the countersignature that `SignWithPresence`'s evidence becomes (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187)).

### 18.16 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sidecar.wasm` misses its goal or starts slowly | High | High | `sidecar_http` leg from M1; spike before M4; C17 only for the extension |
| An iOS tunnel jetsam regression reaches users unmeasured, now that forwarding compiles there ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) | High | High | `make size` from M4; surrogates ([owner decision 100](#od-100)); the forwarding leg's file list and budget (D-SDK-20; owner decisions [215](#od-215), [216](#od-216)); a compile past its cap keeps the last verified state and alarms |
| A compromised VPN component forwards as its sidecar and reads the config until its forwarding Delegation ends | Low | Medium | the forwarding key signs only that sidecar's delegations, and its client is `forward_only` (D-SDK-32); no mail, evs data, MLS, identity or recovery key there; `DelegationRevoke` or the sidecar's revocation (§2.10) |
| Android's VPN service shares the app's process, so a compromise there reaches the sidecar role while the app is open | Medium | High | app work runs the service in a process of its own (18.15); forwarding's keys under their own alias and files (§5.9) |
| Phone-only burner users miss mail, as wakes are throttled or dropped | High | High | [owner decision 12](#od-12)'s copy via `GetReceiverCoverage`; mail indexers ([owner decision 150](#od-150)); 18.7's deferred check (WK2) and per-slot reconcile; token projections in revision order, swept each pass (WK5) |
| Installed apps or the extension leave admin credentials agent-readable | Medium | Critical | D-SDK-11; §7.4's stages ([owner decision 45](#od-45)) |
| An XSS or extension in ur.io reads decrypted views while it runs | Medium | High | key origin, exact-origin messages, CSP (D-SDK-18); disclosed (§2.10) |
| A rarely opened page Worker resyncs each group it reads before showing records (KF5; stale Removes after 90 days), or finds itself revoked once a newer Worker's admitting device saw those Removes (§7.10's stale row) | Medium | Low | KF5's resync by external commit; re-enrollment through a consented device, or with self_admit off an admin's; sign-out revokes it |
| Phone users take possible matches for matches | Medium | Medium | labels; trigram-overlap ranking; confirmation on open (D-SDK-22); a designated indexer's verified hits where one is online ([owner decision 178](#od-178)) |
| No indexer is designated, so phones download all | High (the default, [owner decision 177](#od-177)) | Medium | [owner decision 155](#od-155)'s model; the app's indexer prompt names remote search; `ur indexer add --services search` |
| Members accept the notice without weighing it, and their team-repo words reach a team indexer's holder | Medium | Medium | own indexers first; the notice names the member, the device and the repos; per-device `own` and `off`; owner-bound repos never (D-SDK-26) |
| An indexer is offline when needed | Medium | Low | the foreground Hello; own failover; a fallback no worse than the default (D-SDK-27) |
| Remote search misses 18.4's targets on distant or congested links | Medium | Low | local buckets answer first; §22.8's netem runs; one step a reply |
| Search misses 18.4's targets on mid-range phones or in Safari's wasm | Medium | Medium | §22's gate on surrogates ([owner decision 100](#od-100)); buckets answer first (D-SDK-25) |
| A phone's all partition crowds its storage | Low | Medium | 18.4's 256 MiB and 10% caps; 30-day eviction |
| Safari's 7-day storage cap deletes an occasional user's page Worker, keychain and token included | Medium | Low | re-enrollment through a consented device; persistent storage where granted; stale leaves removed after 90 days (18.8) |

### 18.17 Phasing

- **v0, CLI hosts (M1-M4):** §5.17's daemon; 18.8's lease, reap predicate and close capability, with `POST /sidecar/close`, for §7's first ephemeral clients (MG1, M1); 18.7's credential rules, in the desktop app and extension releases, before §7.4's stage 2 (M3); M4's dark seam, posture, zone call and id refusal in `sidecar/device`, with the forwarding leg's file and descriptor rule; 18.9's host list with C8 (M4); `make size` from M4, at [owner decision 215](#od-215)'s budget.
- **v0, ur.io (M4, RS1):** the minimal ur.io/recurd page ([owner decision 223](#od-223)) and its `read_only` page Worker in its key origin (18.8), signing in by the ur.io session's hand-off ([owner decision 219](#od-219)), on the `sidecar_http` leg (import rule from M1, size measured from M2) within 18.10's gate or miss rule.
- **v1 (M6, RS2):** the team console on that Worker, with the directory's read-only views; the `sdk.Sidecar` shell, dark, with `SignEdgeLogin` for §13's `members-device`, app hosts joining it at M8; the directory's seams (`SidecarDirectory`, `CreateRepo`'s `private`, access-request approvals; §16.11's announce entries), in app hosts from M8; after M8, §17.9's egress spec on app devices.
- **v0, app hosts (M8, BS1):** Android and iOS local mode; desktop remote mode with §5.8's pairing; forwarding in every app's VPN component ([owner decision 197](#od-197)): its keys, setup, forwarding Delegation and forwarding clients, its own following, compile and signing, posture and private names on app paths, hosting after C16 in the device client's network, iOS links after §22.9; Android's sidecar role only while the app is open; `SidecarApprovals` and alarms ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), with the member's device list and revocation and, in team networks, revocation proposals' cosigns (D-SDK-30); wakes ([owner decision 88](#od-88)), directory notices' included, and the directory view's policy; the receiver and coverage APIs and the indexer prompt; from M9, the send check and results (§14.5); the quick tools; the native companion ([owner decision 26](#od-26)).
- **v1, M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)):** 18.4's search policy and targets, `SidecarSearch`, conditions and 18.7's windows on app hosts, and remote search's requester side (modes, notice, `GetIndexers`, the foreground Hello and §6.10's keepalive), at the later of M10's and M8's exits, in team networks at the later of those and M6's (§23); the page Worker's search operations, conditions and cache; the quick burner's in-memory buckets; remote mode's search stream; with format 2 (§11.7), `Write`'s versioning argument, the drop calls, `History`'s states and `EVS_DROPPED` (owner decisions [173](#od-173), [183](#od-183)) and the console's drop view, and the directory's cards and index with phones' directory "search more".
- **Later:** the extension's own Worker, Firefox session mode, browser streams (C4), C17 for the extension's streaming Worker if the spike needs it; browser Workers and ephemeral CLI hosts as remote-search requesters, browsers after C4.
- **Blocking:** §7.4's stage 1 blocks every host, stage 2 the first desktop sidecar beside the app or the extension ([owner decision 45](#od-45)); the page Worker ships within the `sidecar_http` leg's gate or, at M4's entry, its miss rule (18.10); C16, device hosting, once M8's entry has measured its latch ([owner decision 224](#od-224)).

## 19. Server services: deployment, data stores, operations

### 19.1 Purpose and scope

This section maps §9-§15, §18, §20 and §21's services to warp blocks, lb routes, addresses, stores and rollout classes. It owns X13 (the file clusters, decided: hardware, drive settings, telemetry, protection states, growth), the push sender, host clocks, the schema summary and dumps, dns edge hosts, paging, gates and runbooks; §10 owns gkm's sizes, §11 objects, placement and the write budget, §12-§14 DNS, the split and sending, §18.7 the wake trigger, §21 abuse review, §23 milestones.

### 19.3 What exists today

- A service is `server/cli/<svc>` plus a block in `vault/<env>/services.yml`'s top `versions[]` (warp/README.md:86-97); `beta 1 + g1 99` are lb upstream weights (warp/warpctl/config.go:1661).
- lb: 4 hosts, 10 interfaces, plus transparent ones on fireside and crisp (vault/main/services.yml:338-464), each keying one zone (450/min, burst 150, 50 connections) per `$binary_remote_addr` outside `exclude_subnets` (:66-80; warp/warpctl/config.go:1541-1599). http servers own TCP 80 and 443 with 16 MiB bodies (warp/warpctl/config.go:1301); nginx has `realip` and `ssl_preread` (warp/lb/Dockerfile:53-58). Stream ports send PROXY v1 (warp/warpctl/config.go:2506-2512) and yield router rules (warp/warpctl/vyos.go:238-300); host-pinned services own only UDP ports (warp/services/services.go:704-716).
- Postgres: one primary, no replica; the main dump reads a base-backup copy on edge-6, incremental against the base it keeps, every Sunday and Thursday at 06:00 UTC, its timer held since 2026-11-04 until the redesigned dump lands, one-off runs aside (xops/main/ansible/inventory.yml:152-182; on 2026-11-03 the newest dump anywhere was planetoid's of 10-03, :172-174), and keeps 9 generations (~4 months; :186-193); planetoid pulls daily and keeps 2 latest, 1 weekly and 1 monthly generations (host_files/planetoid/backup/README.md:3-6). edge-5 also pulls physical base backups of the primary, `main-pgbase-<date>` generations on its MinIO drives, by hand while `pg_basebackup_timer_enabled` is false (xops/main/ansible/playbook-pg-basebackup.yml:1-25). Redis: 48 masters, no replicas (xops/main/ansible/REDIS.md:3); rdb bundles kept ~8 months (inventory.yml:194-202).
- MinIO: edge-5, shared, at its request ceiling in the 2026-11-01 PUT surges (now capped at 1,024), without PR #21653 (inventory.yml:282-360; playbook-minio-clusters.yml:36-37).
- Host clocks: xops configures no clock sync on the hosts; warpctl sets NTP only on the routers (warp/warpctl/vyos.go:1236-1239).
- monitor notifies only through Slack (server/monitor/alert_slack.go:269); nothing pages.

New blocks serve `GET /status` on port 80, mount `{vault: no, config: yes, site: no}`, run as user 65532, call `server.ScrubCommandLogs()` first and gate readiness on the column above (server/router/warp_handlers.go:214). Non-issuer blocks mount only their audience's public JWKS (§7.8), not today's signing keys (server/oauth/token.go:258-268).

**Push sender ([owner decision 88](#od-88)).** A continuous taskworker loop delivers §18.7's triggers; nothing subscribes per client (R-OPS-8):

```text
input    each {wakeq_<shard>} stream, read through one consumer group, so an entry has one sender, and held by
         due time; an entry left unacknowledged is XAUTOCLAIMed after 30 s idle; entries older than 60 s, past
         §15.6's hold, are dropped and trimmed (clients resync, §6.8)
due      it MGETs {scp_<C>}ack, tok and tokrev: an ack at or past the entry's hint, or no token, drops the
         entry; otherwise it wakes, then XACKs (WK1-WK5, §18.7)
token    {scp_<C>}tok projects sidecar_push_token at the revision {scp_<C>}tokrev holds; api applies each
         change through §18.7's script, which refuses one older than tokrev or over 60 s past its TIME read;
         apps POST /sidecar/push-token at each launch; taskworker's 60 s pass reconciles each hash slot
         whose {tokgen_<n>} sentinel is absent or names another master's run_id, 90 s after it found it
         (§18.7's loss step), so one master lost or restarted from an old dump costs its slots that wait and
         ~2 s per million tokens, and re-applies the rows changed since 2 min before its last completed run
         began (§18.7's sweep); no Postgres read per hint
rate     per client, one wake per 10 s, plus one at the window's end if a hint arrived inside it; per APNs
         device 3 an hour (§18.7), per FCM device and topic 1 a minute; §6's hourly key for POST /sidecar/wake;
         counters under {wake_<C>}, each expiring within 1 h
errors   429 and 5xx: at most 3 retries with backoff; APNs 410 or FCM UNREGISTERED tombstones the row only
         while its revision equals the tokrev read with that token, then applies the tombstone (§18.7)
metrics  by platform, topic and result, never ids or tokens; sized for twice Y2's 6,000 hints/s
```

### 19.6 The file cluster (X13)

**Decided by the owner** (Q-OPS-1, Q-OPS-10; owner decisions [2](#od-2), [18](#od-18), [20](#od-20), [21](#od-21), [94](#od-94), [116](#od-116), [136](#od-136)-[140](#od-140), [145](#od-145)): MinIO from the final upstream source, archived since 2026-04-25 (https://github.com/minio/minio), with PR #21653's conditional-write fix (§11.3), is the system of record (Redis holds only soft state, 19.7); `ServiceHost.Blobs` (§4) lets SeaweedFS or Ceph RGW replace MinIO, and §22's suite gates every build. D-OPS-20's build of that source lives in `urnetwork/minio`, a public fork and sibling checkout with its own `sidecar` branch, which keeps MinIO's AGPL source in one public place; the owner creates the GitHub repo before any push ([owner decision 195](#od-195)). One site, no off-site copy: a segment cluster and one metadata cluster on 4 LAN hosts apart from edge-5, each with its own endpoint, credentials and unversioned bucket, since MinIO places a bucket's writes in pools by free space (cmd/erasure-server-pool.go:392-411, :637-656); the metadata tier grows only by whole clusters (19.9).

```text
cluster   drives                                     parity  objects
metadata  2 x Samsung PM9A3 1.92 TB M.2 per host:    EC:4    a placed repo's §11.8 repo/ head/ log/ pb/ hp/ idx/ slot/
          one 8-drive set, 15.4 TB raw, ~7.7 TB              pmap/ pidx/ spidx/ and its group's §10.6 gkm/ objects,
          usable (owner decisions 136-139)                   pb/'s batches also carrying staged versionless segments
                                                             from v1 (§11.7), and v1's drops/<repo>/_ (§11.13's drop
                                                             table and running job); the first cluster alone
                                                             also holds §11.8's place/, §7's proj/, projrows/ and
                                                             rev/, §10.6's per-sidecar gkm/ and §21.9's hold/
segment   16 x 16 TB HDD per host (1,024 TB raw):    EC:8    seg/, kind-5 (versionless) segments from v1 included, each
          four 16-drive sets, 4 drives per host,             purged a minute after its version's replacement (§11.13);
          ~512 TB usable                                     §11.13's pack/, holding records and log pages older than
                                                             24 h, at least 256 KiB a pack or 7 d old (owner decision
                                                             136), not a MinIO warm tier's small PUT per push; from
                                                             v1, drop jobs' dropscan/<repo>/<id>/<f>, each deleted 30
                                                             d after its job or dry run ends (§11.13)
```

- **Parity** ("2 replicas" as 50%, [owner decision 116](#od-116)): ~310 TB logical on HDD at 70% fill and 15% overhead. Writes need N/2+1 drives (cmd/erasure-metadata.go:557-558), surviving a host plus 3 HDDs or 1 NVMe drive, and an object reads while N/2 of its shards remain: any acknowledged one survives a drive; one whose write missed at most a host's share of drives (4 HDDs, 2 NVMe), as one written while a host was down, survives a host; only one whose every shard exists, written missing no drive or healed since, survives two:

```text
state      entered when                                     left when
protected  every drive online, no heal pending              -
degraded   a drive or host offline, or a heal pending       a full heal of the cluster's bucket (mc admin heal
           (MRF or scanner)                                 --recursive; cmd/admin-router.go:175-177) ends with
                                                            every drive online
at_risk    degraded and a further drive or host fails,      the failure is repaired and a full heal ends
```

**Durability (D-OPS-14; owner decisions [89](#od-89), [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94), [116](#od-116), [143](#od-143)).** A write returns only once N/2+1 drives of its set hold it, and nothing waits for a copy. A drive's failure therefore loses nothing acknowledged: RPO 0, inside [owner decision 89](#od-89)'s 5 min and 1 h targets, which cover drives and hosts only ([owner decision 94](#od-94)). A host's keeps RPO 0 for objects whose write missed at most a host's share of drives, and a second host's only for objects whose every shard exists: written while their set was protected and missing no drive, or healed since (the parity rule above). Site loss is total for what no device or dump holds (19.10).

```text
                                         dump: <= 24 h plus its <= 20 min run      evs and gkm sessions stop within
```

No operator copy holds slots or wraps, so a committed erasure is immediate at the cluster ([owner decision 90](#od-90)). Owner devices' sealed mirrors hold slots like any repo object, apply each erasure on its hint, and re-seed by 19.10. Repos no device mirrors, and deposits no depositor spools, die with the site (D-EVS-17, §16.8, §2.18). Sidecar tables leave the main dumps for D-OPS-18's daily dump (D-TRUST-7), and the Redis bundles leave out 19.7's families (D-OPS-16).

**Migrations (D-OPS-6).** Versions continue after main's last, 926 on 2026-11-04 (server/db_migrations.go:235); the catalog keys identities by slice position and aliases the slice in an `init` (server/db_migration_catalog.go:27-42), so a registered group never changes:

```text
pending   a group is registered in the migrations slice only by its own milestone's Gn-out commit (owner
          decision 118); until then it lives in server/db_migrations_sidecar_pending.go under build tag
          sidecar_pending, appended in the slice's initializer, since an init-time append would escape the
          catalog's alias
builds    local, T3 and canary set the tag; release legs never do; the pending file's initializer panics unless
          server.Env() is local or canary or the binary is a test (testing.Testing()), as evaluation credential
          overrides refuse anything but WARP_ENV=local (server/env.go:1148-1155)
promote   a Gn-out moves only its own group from the pending file into the slice, in order; canary databases
          rebuild after each merge
code      code reading a pending group's tables stays gated off (D-OPS-10) and unready without them (19.4)
```

- Groups add tables, nullable columns and new-table indexes; existing tables get `newOnlineSqlMigration` indexes (server/db_migrations.go:50-52). `acl_subject_client_id` turns NOT NULL through a validated `NOT VALID` check (precedent :5961-5969).
- Only `smtp_send` (daily, PK (send_day, send_id)), `tls_connection_record` and `mail_connection_record` (hourly) are partitioned, the last two's partitions UNLOGGED, so no physical copy holds them (19.6's copies row; [owner decision 210](#od-210)). Cleanups wait for every database job (connect/CODESTYLE.md:88). Pools per process (config/main/db.yml): dns and smtpedge 4, others 2; locks stay transaction-scoped.

**Redis (D-OPS-7).** Tags: `{scp_}`, `{wake_}` (§6, 19.4), `{wakeq_}`, `{tokgen_}` (§18.7), `{dpop_}` (§7), `{acl_}` (§8.9's `{acl_<networkId>}v`; §7.9's `{acl_<networkId>}e`, the verified projection cache, which only api writes ([owner decision 136](#od-136)), and `{acl_<networkId>}q`, the append limits' 25 h counter), `{sg_}`, `{sn_}`, `{sc_}`, `{svc_}` (§9), `{gka_}` (§10), `{evsq_}`, `{evsl_}`, `{evsh_}`, `{evsc_}`, v1's `{evsd_}`, `{nvb_}` (§11), `{evsn_}` (§20.7's nightly count; [owner decision 198](#od-198)), `{dns}` (§12), `{tes_}`, `{tcb_}` (§13), `{smq_}`, `{smg_}`, `{smd_}` (§14), `{mxr_}`, `{mxc_}` (§15), `{vhk}` (§13.9, §15.4: the daily visitor-hash keys, 25 h), `{sq_}` (§20). Every key is rebuildable: it projects Postgres or a cluster (the head and projection caches for 10 min, certs' budget from `network_tls_cert`, tokens per slot by taskworker's sentinel pass, drop hints by the nightly LIST of `drops/` within a day), returns by re-registration (leases, acks), restarts above its old values (the push sequence) or expires within 48 h (the write budget's allowance in 15 s, and its saved bucket, wallet and counter readings 48 h after the loop's last write, a lost one restarting the bucket and the wallet at zero, which is conservative); switches and halts reach Postgres first and reload within 60 s. The hint listener follows slot owners (`RunRedisShardSubscription`); caps (config/main/redis.yml): sockets 64, evs 32, others 16.

### 19.8 Observability and SLOs

- **Metrics** (`urnetwork_<svc>_*`, server/grafana.go:1-21) keep 90 days, logs 7 (config/main/grafana.yml:31-38). Labels are route template, result, code, cluster and tier; logs are scrubbed (server/scrub.go:3-21) and carry opaque ids only (I-13, W8).
- **Versionless (v1):** `urnetwork_evs_versionless_purged_bytes_total{by="commit"|"sweep"}`, `urnetwork_evs_versionless_staged_total{outcome="dropped"|"written"}`, `urnetwork_evs_versionless_purge_queue` and `urnetwork_evs_versionless_sweep_deletes_total{result="deleted"|"absent"}`, told apart by a HEAD before each sweep DELETE, since MinIO answers a DELETE 204 either way (cmd/object-handlers.go:2678-2691); the committing processes should delete nearly all, so the sweep's `deleted` share warns past 1% in a day (below).
- **Drop history (v1):** `urnetwork_evs_drop_jobs{state}`, `urnetwork_evs_drop_scan_bytes_total{pass="preview"|"mark"|"verify"}`, `urnetwork_evs_drop_deletes_total{result="deleted"|"absent"|"packed"|"held"|"young"}` and `urnetwork_evs_drop_freed_bytes_total`; a job ending refused {verify} or {mismatch} pages as a storage-integrity alert. **HDD share:** `urnetwork_evs_hdd_admission_refused_total{cluster}` (19.6's hdd row). None carries a network or repo label.
- **Write budget (§11.13):** per metadata cluster, with no network or repo label: `urnetwork_evs_budget_issued_bytes_total{cluster,class,kind}` (class p0, p1, p2_funded or p2_unfunded; kind, for P0 only, revocation, log, lifecycle, shred, erasure, remove or rotation); `urnetwork_evs_budget_p0_refill_ratio{cluster}`, P0's measured bytes over the last hour against that hour's refill, the P0 page's input (below); `urnetwork_evs_budget_bucket_bytes{cluster}`, B, never below zero, with `urnetwork_evs_budget_p0_forgiven_bytes_total{cluster,kind}`, P0's forgiven excess, its bytes past what B held, by P0's kinds, shown in drive-writes against the ~420 that five years at the refill leave under the drives' rating (19.6's wear row; [owner decision 190](#od-190)); `urnetwork_evs_budget_liability_bytes{cluster,class}` and `urnetwork_evs_budget_drain_seconds{cluster,class}` at the last hour's rate, the wallet and the funded and unfunded backlogs among them; the busiest drive's `urnetwork_filecluster_drive_dwpd{cluster,window}` over 24 h, 7 d and 30 d and `urnetwork_filecluster_drive_rating_days{cluster}`, the days until SMART's percentage used reaches 100 at the 30-day rate; `urnetwork_evs_path_epoch_moves_left{cluster}`, `urnetwork_evs_path_epoch_sources{cluster,n}`, `urnetwork_evs_path_epoch_deferred{cluster}` and `urnetwork_evs_path_epoch_sources_full_total{cluster}` (§11.6); and each cluster's `urnetwork_filecluster_exhaustion_days{cluster,resource}` (raw, inodes, wear, copy), with the first cluster's `urnetwork_filecluster_control_plane_bytes` (19.9's cohorts row).
