### 20.15 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking `team_credit` last slows escrow on the hot path | Medium | High | 20.9's gate; one index keeps each keyset page one scan |
| Redis loss over-admits leases, relayed reservations and rates, or reservations confuse the contract reconciler | Medium | Medium | lease size; grants that shrink near zero; own namespace; nightly reconcile; FS-45 |
| Soft evs limits overshoot by about a minute | Medium | Low | 5 s over-limit reads; 20.7's nightly count; batch-resident bytes from head windows until each hourly evacuation deletes their batch |
| Closure bytes land on both clusters: each `?closure=1` upload is one HDD PUT, up to two writes on each of its set's 16 drives (136 KiB shards, cmd/erasure-coding.go:121-131, past §11.3's 128 KiB inline bound), and CLOSURE pushes' inline records and staged index files ride their NVMe batch until evacuation moves or drops them; unpaced, an eraser could spend its day's 64 MiB in a minute, 5,000 uploads a second for a Team's 5,000 erasers, 12-20× the HDD sets' ~8,000-12,800 drive operations a second (§19.6), though that day's ~312.5 GiB averages ~3.5 a second, ~1%; on NVMe, CLOSURE pushes within the network's 60 a minute are P0, at most ~0.3 MiB a second a drive a network (under 2% of a set's 0.8 DWPD), which §11.13's budget does not bound across networks ([owner decision 186](#od-186)), and P1 past it, inside §11.13's budget | Low | Medium | 20.7's pacing: at most 4 uploads a second a network (~1-1.6% of the HDD sets) in equal turns, so no eraser starves another and each of 5,000 asking still gets 69 turns a day; at the floor, n full re-keys wait under ⌈n/3⌉ days and three turns, their entries openable meanwhile, and none waits below the limit ([owner decision 146](#od-146)) |
| A network's closure bytes scale with its erasers, not its live admissions: §7.9 exempts revocations, so a day's erasers reach its admissions plus that day's admission statements, and in v0 every closure byte stays stored past the limit: ~3.1 GiB a day for a Community network's 50 erasers (~128 GiB with churn to 2,050), ~312.5 GiB for a Team's 5,000 (with churn, pacing caps its uploads at ~358 GiB) | Low | Medium | each erasure re-keys only its entry's chains, so growth ends with the network's entries; §21.7 tightens the allowance to its 4 MiB floor (200 MiB a day for 50 erasers) and the network's admission statements; v1's compaction frees erased ciphertext, and format 2's index rewrites free their replaced versions a minute later, staged ones with their batch |
| The search index, on by default, uses storage: ~15-30% of the text it indexes (~5-15% of a mailbox's stored bytes, ~20-40% of a record repo's), plus replaced heads for up to 26 h | Certain | Low | `ur status` shows its share; repo admins turn it off; deleting its files is accepted at the limit (D-QUOTA-10) |
| A declared sidecar gets VPN egress | Low | High | CreateContract refusal; §22 test |
| Storage priced at §19.6's cost per usable TB recovers ~60% of cost: at 70% fill and 15% overhead, ~310 of the HDDs' 512 TB holds data ([owner decision 116](#od-116)), and each next metadata cluster ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) adds cost without HDD space | Medium | Low | yearly review from §19.6's current hardware ([owner decision 122](#od-122)); Team-only, ≤2 TiB a network |

### 20.16 Phasing

- **v0 (personal networks):** free and pro tiers, `sidecar:` blocks, overrides, counters, refusals and 20.8 (M1); the debit path, leases, usage batches, relayed reservations and the nightly stored count with maintenance at the limit, the per-eraser closure allowance and the network's closure pacing (M2; FS-44, FS-45, FS-47); C9 lease spending by tlsedge (M5), mxedge (M7) and smtpedge with the `smtp_*` quotas (M9, [owner decision 35](#od-35)); usage rollups (§23.4).
- **v1 (Team at M6, format 2 at M10):** D-QUOTA-9's comparator, index and 20.9's benchmark harness, built dark in M4 (§23.4), its index pending in MG6 until M6's Gn-out (§19.7; 20.9's gate), so M6's entry runs that benchmark and FS-46 on built code; then the `team` tier and its prices, seats, checkout, meters, credit line, downgrade jobs and share escrow; 5,000 `config_admissions` with no member-device cap ([owner decision 144](#od-144)); the team directory's request limits and accounting at M6 (D-QUOTA-11), its card cap with cards at M10 (D-PHASE-11); at M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)), with storage format 2, the search index counting as storage (§11.14), versionless content's counting and freeing (20.6, §11.13), the drop's rates, `limit` rule and freed-byte reports (D-QUOTA-12), freeing nothing until §19.11's `drop` gate turns on (D-PHASE-12), and remote search's relayed bytes with C19's rounding, which add no counter or tier key (20.6).
- **Later:** auto-recharge of Community and Pro data packs (Team is post-paid), invoicing above 25 seats, the assurance stage (§23.4).

## 21. Abuse, safety, and legal process

### 21.1 Purpose and scope

This section sets abuse policy: mail reputation, hosted-content and name abuse, network standing, intake and appeals, legal process and transparency. Mechanisms and default caps stay with their owners (§8-§20); §2.8 holds the metadata list and TTLs. No control acts on content (CONVENTIONS §0).

### 21.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-ABUSE-1 | Reports against a message halt the network's sending for a day | PLAN.md:91 |
| R-ABUSE-2 | Servers see only ciphertext and small header values, except D-SMTP-19's report and role-mail intake (§2.8 mx-4; D-TRUST-4) | owner directive 2026-11-03 |
| R-ABUSE-3 | Public names are explicit, authenticated by default and short-lived; no agent control panels | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:698 |
| R-ABUSE-4 | Gmail spam rate under 0.10%, never 0.30% | server/EMAIL1.md:109 |
| R-ABUSE-5 | Every retained field has a purpose and TTL; holds name accounts, carry a statutory kind and deadline, are counted, never block users' shredding and silently defer drops' deletions | D-TRUST-7; owner decisions [133](#od-133), [184](#od-184); 18 U.S.C. §2703(f), §2258A(h) |
| R-ABUSE-6 | No client IP is logged; no client token administers | I-13, I-6 |
| R-ABUSE-7 | A dated warrant canary is published with "end-to-end encrypted" | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:933; [owner decision 119](#od-119) |

### 21.3 What exists today

- Server has no abuse intake, case store, network suspension or takedown path (grep, 2026-11-03).
- `ValidateNetworkName` checks only length and `[a-z0-9-]`, so `paypal-support` passes (server/model/network_model.go:178-205).
- Creation allows 5 networks per 24 h per keyed /29 or /56 (server/model/network_create_rate_limit.go:11-12; server/ip.go:84-97); guest, wallet and seed-phrase sign-ins are anonymous (server/model/auth_model.go:34-43).

### 21.4 Principles and categories

Principles (D-ABUSE-1):
1. Act on names, metadata, rates and reports at the smallest unit (host, sending domain, label, network), never the root.
2. Count every routed name as public: modified sidecars skip sidecar-side controls (§13.7).
3. Machines act at once, only on 21.8's signals; each action holds until reviewed within 24 h, in business hours in v0 (owner decisions [95](#od-95), [134](#od-134)).
4. Each action is an appealable §8 hard deny with a case id, notified to Owners and Admins (21.8).

| Category | First action | Escalation |
|---|---|---|
| Spam | §14.8's ladder ([owner decision 37](#od-37)) | 3 halts in 30 d: suspend |
| Phishing, malware, command-and-control | host kill (§13.9) or `SuspendHost` (§12); by mail, a network halt with review (§14.8) | 2nd in 30 d: label kill, mail halt; 3rd: suspend |
| Copyright | notice forwarded; a 2nd valid one in 30 d: host kill | 3 upheld in 12 months: suspend (17 U.S.C. §512(i)) |
| Exposed agent or admin panel; compromise | a protective host kill; for compromise, a halt or kill until the device and its DKIM selector are revoked | no strike |
| CSAM; threat to life | suspend; report (21.9) | legal |

### 21.5 Mail abuse and shared reputation

From M9 ([owner decision 35](#od-35)), all networks and burners send from the shared lb addresses ([owner decision 124](#od-124); §14.6) under `<root>`, whose subdomains count together toward bulk status (server/EMAIL1.md:115). Above §14.8's per-domain and per-network halts, breakers guard what is shared (D-ABUSE-2):

| Trigger (trailing 24 h) | Action | Clears |
|---|---|---|
| `<root>` Postmaster spam rate ≥0.10% two days running, or feedback-loop complaints ≥0.10% of recipients | restricted networks pause; Community caps halve | 3 days below 0.08% |
| Either measure ≥0.20%, or a sending address on Spamhaus SBL/CSS or SNDS red | Community pauses (HALTED, queues held); the listed address leaves the sending set, not ingress, within the feed refresh, with no drain target (§14.6; [owner decision 124](#od-124)) | delisting, then 3 clean days |
| ≥0.30% | Community and Pro pause; trusted Team continues | owner |

Breakers act early: `<root>` cannot be replaced, and listings also block platform ingress (21.17).

### 21.6 Hosted content, names, certificates

| Control | Policy |
|---|---|
| Kill switch (§13.9) | host, then label (21.4), then revocation (`cessationOfOperation`, https://letsencrypt.org/docs/revoking/) and no renewal (§13.8); an abuse kill is lifted only through its case, never by a restore (21.10); a quota downgrade's suspension of standing names (§20.7) is no §21 action |
| Proactive check | published hosts and user record names, hourly, against Web Risk's locally matched Update API (https://docs.cloud.google.com/web-risk/docs/overview); Safe Browsing is non-commercial only (https://developers.google.com/safe-browsing) |
| CT watch ([owner decision 41](#od-41)) | the abuse worker sends 21.8 any name under `<root>` in CT that `ScreenName`'s current lists refuse; D-TLS-8 covers mis-issuance |

**Names (owner decisions [14](#od-14), [97](#od-97)).** Brands enter only through aliases, record owners, published hosts (`paypal-login.<net>.<root>`) and burner From domains. `ScreenName` applies §12.5's rules at creation: listed brands are denied unless the network verified the brand's domain (§7.6); brand-plus-keyword names (`login`, `secure`, `verify`, `account`, `support`, `wallet`, `update`) go to review, refused on probation; word-number names stay burners' (§12.7). §15.9's word list skips `ScreenName`'s lists. smtpedge screens declared From domains, burners' included (§14.5; owner decisions [32](#od-32), [79](#od-79)).

### 21.7 Network reputation and probation

`network_abuse_state` feeds §8's hard deny and the §12-§15 gates (D-ABUSE-4).

| State | Entry | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| probation | under 7 days old | same-network mail deposits only (D-SMTP-14); 1 endpoint, publishes ≤24 h; ≤5 user RRsets (`probation_dns_entries`), none A, AAAA or CNAME; no names held for review, aliases or outbound shares |
| standard | 7+ days old; 30 days without action | tier defaults (§20); internet mail 24 h after `POST /mail/enable` (§14.7) |
| trusted | Team with a verified domain, paid 30 days, clean 90 days | Team thresholds (§14.8); brand use |
| restricted | a network halt or a kill within 30 days | probation limits; internet mail resumes after the halt at Community caps |
| suspended | §8 suspension, until reviewed | no reach, publishing or sending; data kept, readable and exportable |

**Verification (owner decisions [41](#od-41), [96](#od-96)).** Public names (§12.8, §13.9) and internet mail (§14.7) always need `network_verified`: a payment method (an in-window paid `transfer_balance` row, server/db_migrations.go:1653-1655) or the owner user's verified phone or email, Apple and Google sign-ins counting (server/db_migrations.go:2131-2156); api caches it like Pro (server/model/pro_model.go:164).

**Limits.** Beyond the states above and 21.5's breakers, §21 tightens a network's limits only through `network_sidecar_limit` rows citing its case, none for forwarding or sockets (§20.5; [owner decision 66](#od-66)), and never `evs_closure_bytes_per_day` below its fixed 4 MiB floor: each eraser keeps its own allowance, so erasure stays possible at the storage limit, waiting at most as §11.13 and §15.7 state (§20.7; [owner decision 146](#od-146)). The abuse worker opens a case, with no machine action, for a network whose closure bytes taken at the storage limit grow its stored bytes past it (§20.7); review may tighten its erasers' allowances to the floor and its `config_statements_per_day`, which bounds the admissions, each a new eraser, that a day adds (§7.9's append limits, revocations exempt). Abuse of the team directory's access requests stays inside the network: §20.4's `directory_requests_*` and `directory_target_pending` limits and a directory admin's moderation (§16.11) handle it, since the server sees no request's content; §21 may tighten those limits the same way.

### 21.8 Intake, triage, appeals

**Intake** (D-ABUSE-5). `abuse@<root>`, `postmaster@<root>` (RFC 2142) and §14.8's reports to `<token>@rpt.bringyour.com` reach `rpt.bringyour.com`'s platform listener, SNI or not (D-SMTP-19, D-MAIL-10); a network's own `abuse@` reaches its admins (§15.8). Also: a form and a law-enforcement address on ur.io, feeds, and registrar, registry and Search Console notices.

**Header-only parsing** ([owner decision 78](#od-78)). Report and role mail get §14.8's parse and sealed copy or are dropped unread; an auto-reply points senders to the form, which takes URLs and header blocks.

**Pipeline.** Each report becomes an `abuse_case`, joined to a network by host or address (§12's label map; a burner address names its `<net>`), headers (§14.8) or edge `connection_id` (24 h); third-party data is dropped after the join, except a reported URL's path and query, which the case keeps until its first review ends, at most its review clock, so that reviewers open the page reported (§13.9; [owner decision 207](#od-207)); a reporter's address and free text are never kept, and of free text only an appeal's own reason is stored.

| Signal | Machine action | Review (v0: business hours, the action holding) |
|---|---|---|
| §14.8 high or medium join | §14.8's ladder | ≤24 h |
| Web Risk or feed hit; trusted-flagger report naming a URL | host kill | ≤24 h |
| Any registrar or registry notice about `<root>` or bringyour.com; a law-enforcement emergency notice, EU removal orders included | a host kill for a registrar's or registry's URL | pages both members of §19.8's rota at once, at any hour from M5 (owner decisions [134](#od-134), [143](#od-143)); handled within 1 h: removal orders and registrar or registry notices by the rota, production orders and other data requests routed to counsel's out-of-hours contact (`config/<env>/abuse.yml`) |
| A report of phishing, malware or command-and-control naming a `<root>` URL | none | ≤4 business hours, every tier |
| Other | none | ≤4 business hours on probation; 72 h paid, 7 d Community |

**Notice and appeal.** Owners and Admins get the category, target, case id and an appeal link unless a sealing order (18 U.S.C. §2705(b), §3123(d)) or a CSAM case bars it. Admins appeal (21.16, §14.8), and a second reviewer decides with reasons (DSA Art. 17); reviewers never see sealed reports.

### 21.9 Legal process under end-to-end encryption

**Posture ([owner decision 93](#od-93)).** Counsel reviews each order. Affected Owners and Admins hear of a request before production unless a sealing or nondisclosure order bars it (18 U.S.C. §2705(b)), and after it lapses. No prospective-collection capability is built, so pen register and trap-and-trace orders (§3123) reach only retained data. Through an EU addressee, production orders (Regulation 2023/1543, applied since 2026-08-18) need data within 10 days, 8 h in emergencies (https://www.reedsmith.com/articles/eu-e-evidence-new-service-provider-obligations-from-18-august-2026/), and their issuer informs the user (https://www.crossborderdataforum.org/analysis-eus-recently-adopted-e-evidence-regulation/), so counsel decides on URnetwork's own notice; terrorist-content removal orders need action within 1 h (Regulation 2021/784 Art. 3(3), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/784/oj). Out of hours, 21.8's pager meets the 1 h with the kill switch and the 8 h through counsel's out-of-hours contact.

**Production** reaches only §2.8's rows while retained, never content, keys, internal names or paths (§2.5), notably:
- accounts and identities (api-1, api-5), the projection's reach graph (api-7) and abuse cases (api-14);
- connect-1's contract pairs (client ids, bytes, times), for the horizon connect-1 states;
- evs's push history (sidecar ids, times, path tokens, padded sizes; evs-4, evs-12, evs-14), kept for the repo's life by default, DROP statements included: who, when, which token paths and how many versions (evs-12); its drops', drop jobs' and dry runs' state for 30 days after each ends (evs-28) and its 7-day request log (evs-7); gkm's membership as sidecar ids;
- edge records for 24 h (tls-3, with keyed visitor-address hashes; mx-2, with no sender address) and, from M9, send records for 30 days (smtp-3).

It never reaches relay frames or dials (connect-2), inbound sender addresses (mx-2), client addresses (I-13) or DNS queries (dns-2). A compelled URnetwork could, from then on, log client, visitor and resolver addresses (connect-3, tls-2, dns-2) and use §2.8's EX1-EX8, notably EX3 outside Team strict mode (owner decisions [98](#od-98), [135](#od-135)), but add no reader against customer signatures (§2.7).

**Preservation holds (owner decisions [133](#od-133), [184](#od-184)).** A hold keeps one network's in-scope records existing at placement until its kind's deadline (§2703(f): 90 days, renewable once; §2258A: 1 year), and collects nothing new. TTL sweeps skip those rows; `copied_rows` copies what drops or is overwritten on its own: rows of partitions that drop whole (tls-3, smtp-3, mx-2) and the Redis soft state existing at placement (evs-8's lease fields, gkm-10's acks; [owner decision 136](#od-136)); and api mirrors each hold as `hold/<network_id>/<case_id>/_` on the first metadata cluster (§11.8; [owner decision 145](#od-145)), so §11.13's GC and §10.6's reconciler skip in-scope objects on every cluster, and evacuation moves a held network's batched records, a shredding repo's included, into packs and parcels that nothing deletes while the hold stands (evs-19). A drop of a path's history (§11.7) whose targets a hold covers still commits: it reads, lists and bills as finished, as an unheld drop would, and its dropped versions are served to no one, while its deletions wait until every covering hold has ended (§11.13); no answer, listing or bill tells the network that a hold exists, so a sealed order stays sealed ([owner decision 184](#od-184)). A site loss voids what a hold kept on the file cluster, which has no off-site copy ([owner decision 94](#od-94)); §19.10's restore returns its rows and tells counsel.

```text
abuse_legal_hold(network_id, case_id, part, kind, scope, expire_time, copied_rows)
part     the primary key is (network_id, case_id, part): part 0 is the hold itself, and parts 1 and up each
         hold at most 16 MiB of compressed rows in copied_rows, so a busy network's tls-3 rows fit 21.16's
         seven tables
kind     preserve_2703f  90 d from placement, renewed once for 90 d by a renewed request (18 U.S.C. §2703(f)(2))
         report_2258a    1 year from the NCMEC report (18 U.S.C. §2258A(h)); not renewable here
overlap  holds over one scope keep it until the latest expire_time; expiry resumes TTL sweeps, GC, held shreds
         at §11.12's phase 5 and held drops' deletions (§11.13)
always   users' --now, the 7-day timer and per-entry erasure proceed under every kind, destroying keys; a hold
         keeps only the ciphertext they leave (owner decision 133; §11.12's phase 4); a drop, even with now, is
         not user-initiated shredding: a hold defers its deletions (owner decision 184)
counsel  before holds ship (M5), confirms each kind's applicability and owner decision 133's condition: that
         deleting wrapped keys to ciphertext URnetwork cannot read is permitted
```

**Copyright and child safety.** The edges are §512(a) conduits: host notices follow 21.4's ladder (§512(i)); evs notices go to the network. A §512(c)(2) agent is registered and renewed every 3 years (https://www.copyright.gov/dmca-directory/). On actual knowledge, CSAM goes to NCMEC, with no duty to scan (18 U.S.C. §2258A(a), (f)); a report places a `report_2258a` hold.

### 21.10 Retention and access

§2.8's list is the only TTL table (D-ABUSE-7): cases, actions and appeals stay 13 months after their case closes, legal requests, productions and `abuse_access_log` 3 years, holds until their kind's deadline (21.9), `network_abuse_state` only while current. An `abuse` role, separate from ops, looks up only by case id or join key, never in bulk; each read writes `abuse_access_log`; productions need legal and engineering sign-off.

**Restore.** A Postgres restore returns §21's tables, `network_tls_suspension`, zone and host suspensions and halts to the sidecar dump's age (§19.10); it lifts no recorded action:

```text
record   each action (kill, zone or host suspension, halt, §8 suspension, limit tightening) and each lift
         is sealed to a vault-held HPKE key in api and mailed, as it commits, to the abuse mailbox
         (config/<env>/abuse.yml), as {action_id, case_id, category, network_id, kind, target, until, time};
         kept as api-14's actions; each hold placed goes the same way to the legal-request mailbox, kept
         until its expire_time; both mailboxes sit at one provider outside URnetwork's Postgres and clusters,
         which the owner names, so it and SES see only each record's sender, time and size (owner
         decision 208)
restore  §19.10's abuse step, after the dumps load and before the token exchange reopens, the edges read
         the restored rows or §12.6's restore step builds the zone: the abuse role (§19.8's rota, at any
         hour) re-applies, in mail order and idempotently by action_id, every unexpired action and every
         lift mailed after the dump, each opened with the vault key, re-creating its case under its id
check    §12.6's step flags restored RRsets of networks with open cases; the abuse role clears each flag
gap      an action committed in the seconds before the primary's loss, its mail not yet sent, is lost
         with it; tlsedge still keeps a kill that Redis holds (§13.9), and feed and Web Risk hits recur
```

### 21.11 Transparency

A semiannual report counts requests by instrument and country, accounts affected, productions, holds, sealing orders, DMCA notices, abuse actions, appeals, NCMEC reports and root incidents. ur.io publishes the signed, dated quarterly canary (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:933) and the report template with "end-to-end encrypted" ([owner decision 119](#od-119); §23.8), and from M5, with `rpt.bringyour.com`, the RFC 3207 deviation that §15.4's 530 links ([owner decision 33](#od-33)).

### 21.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| A URnetwork warning page on user names; parsing report bodies | clearer to visitors; richer evidence | edge termination under a URnetwork key (PLAN.md:84), blinding the CT watch; user mail in URnetwork memory | ruled out (owner directive) |
| Content scanning in the sidecar | catches CSAM and phishing | breaks "private from us"; server-steered lists | rejected |

### 21.13 Decisions proposed

**D-ABUSE-1 (proposed).** Controls act only on names, metadata, rates and reports (21.4). *Why:* the directive; modified sidecars skip sidecar-side controls.

**D-ABUSE-2 (proposed).** 21.5's breakers guard `<root>` and the shared addresses, with thresholds in pro.yml `sidecar_abuse:`. *Why:* reputation is shared ([owner decision 124](#od-124)), and per-network rates stay below Gmail's feedback thresholds ([R:ext-email-zk](design/design-research/ext-email-zk.md) §2.8, §2.9).

**D-ABUSE-3 (proposed).** Takedown follows 21.6 and 21.8, within 1 h for public phishing or malware 21.8's signals confirm, and for paged removal orders and registrar or registry notices; `<root>` is verified in Search Console. *Why:* a registrar suspension, required for phishing since 2024-04-05, takes "all third-level domains" (https://www.icann.org/en/contracted-parties/advisories/documents/advisory-compliance-with-dns-abuse-obligations-in-the-registrar-accreditation-agreement-and-the-registry-agreement-05-02-2024-en), so every registrar or registry notice pages; passthrough leaves only connection refusal.

**D-ABUSE-4 (proposed).** Screening, standing and verification follow 21.6 and 21.7. *Why:* these are a brand's only ways in; Sybil networks are cheap.

**D-ABUSE-5 (proposed).** Intake and appeals follow 21.8, report mail never touching the SNI router. *Why:* reporters without SNI must deliver; the directive; AUTHZ1; DSA Art. 17.

**D-ABUSE-6 (proposed).** Legal process and holds follow 21.9 (owner decisions [93](#od-93), [133](#od-133)), each hold with its statutory kind and deadline. *Why:* a request reaches only what retention keeps; a hold revives no shredded key; one generic hold cannot carry §2258A's 1-year preservation.

**D-ABUSE-7 (proposed).** Retention, access, restore and transparency follow §2.8, 21.10 and 21.11. *Why:* D-TRUST-7; expired keys protect users even from a compelled URnetwork; a dump-age restore must lift no action.

**D-ABUSE-8 (proposed).** Holds defer drops silently: a covered drop commits and reads as finished, and its deletions wait for every covering hold to end (21.9). *Why:* owner decisions [93](#od-93), [133](#od-133) and [184](#od-184); a refusal would tell a repo admin that a sealed hold exists.

### 21.14 Open questions

**Q-ABUSE-1.** How far is §2.8's EX3 narrowed? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 98](#od-98)):** (c): per-message labels (I-11), DNS and CT watches, and §15.4's Team strict mode. *Residual:* none; [owner decision 135](#od-135) defines "validated" (§15.5).

**Q-ABUSE-2.** Do anonymous-only networks leave probation without paying? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 96](#od-96)):** yes, but public names and internet mail need `network_verified` (21.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-ABUSE-3.** May machines act alone, and who staffs review? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 95](#od-95)):** (a): machines act at once, people review within 24 h; business-hours staff in v0, 24/7 on-call by v1 (21.18). *Residual:* none.

**Q-ABUSE-4.** May screening and probation limit PLAN.md:25's "owns all entries"? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 97](#od-97)):** (a): screening at creation and probation record caps (21.6, 21.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-ABUSE-5.** What legal posture? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 93](#od-93)):** (a): 21.9's posture and 21.11's canary. *Residual:* none; holds await counsel (21.9).

**Q-ABUSE-6.** Cross-cutting (§19.8, §23.7). How do v0's review clocks run with business-hours staff? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 134](#od-134)):** (b): business-hours review, machine actions holding until then, plus a pager from M5 only for registrar, registry and law-enforcement emergency notices, EU removal orders included, every registrar or registry notice about `<root>` or bringyour.com counting as one (21.8); 24/7 in v1. The notices ride §19.8's out-of-hours rota, which pages infrastructure from M3 ([owner decision 143](#od-143)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-ABUSE-7.** Cross-cutting (§11.13). How does a preservation hold apply to a drop of a path's history? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 184](#od-184)):** (a), silent deferral: the drop commits as signed and reads, lists and bills as finished, its dropped versions served to no one and its bytes uncounted, while its deletions wait until every covering hold ends; nothing tells the network that a hold exists ([owner decision 93](#od-93)), which refusing the drop, (b), or refusing it only under notified holds, (c), would. *Residual:* none.

- **PLAN.md:25 ("owns all entries").** Screening and probation refuse some labels and records ([owner decision 97](#od-97); Q-ABUSE-4).

### 21.16 Interfaces

- **Provides:** 21.4-21.11's policies; `ScreenName`; `network_abuse_state` and `network_verified` (§8, §12-§15); 21.7's per-network limit tightening (§20.4, §20.5); `hold/` objects on the first metadata cluster (§11.8; [owner decision 145](#od-145)).
- **Consumes:** §12-§15's hooks (`SuspendZone`, `SuspendHost`, kill switch, revocation, label maps, joins, halts, send gate, mail key); §8 suspension; §7 roles, verified domains; §20.5's overrides and §20.7's stored and closure byte counts (21.7); §10.6's and §11.13's hold checks on every metadata cluster; §19.8's rota and pager ([owner decision 143](#od-143)); §19.10's hold recovery and abuse step; §12.6's restore flags.
- **Subprotocol messages:** none; state changes ride §6's `core`, `sock` and `mail` hints.
- **API routes** (api, §19.4): `POST /abuse/report` (Public, rate-limited); `GET /abuse/cases` (Network, read roles); `POST /abuse/appeal` (Owner or Admin; never a client token); `GET /abuse/status` (Client, own state; sidecar-classified, on §7.4's `strict_exp` allowlist); `POST /abuse/action` (staff, off the public API; it refuses a `network_sidecar_limit` row that sets `evs_closure_bytes_floor` or `evs_closure_uploads_per_s`, both fixed, or takes `evs_closure_bytes_per_day` below the floor: §20.5, §20.7).
- **Tables** (api; migrations ≥926 in §19.7's MG5): `abuse_case`, `abuse_action`, `abuse_appeal`, `network_abuse_state`, `abuse_legal_hold` (with `kind`, 21.9), `abuse_access_log`, `legal_request`.
- **Services and config:** the taskworker abuse worker (feeds, Web Risk, the CT watch, breakers, 21.7's closure-growth cases, TTL sweeps, hold copies); pro.yml `sidecar_abuse:` thresholds; `config/<env>/abuse.yml` for feeds, Web Risk, reviewer and pager routing, the abuse and legal-request mailboxes and counsel's out-of-hours contact; a Web Risk key and the mailboxes' HPKE key in vault.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §14 and §15 run `rpt.bringyour.com` from M5; §19.8's out-of-hours rota carries 21.8's notices from M5, paging both members at once, and review runs 24/7 from M6; §19.10 restores holds' rows, re-places later holds, tells counsel and runs 21.10's abuse step in 21.10's order, and §12.6's restore step flags restored RRsets of networks with open cases; §2.8's header and api-14 publish `copied_rows` (tls-3's, smtp-3's and mx-2's rows, evs-8's lease fields, gkm-10's acks), and mx-2's, evs-8's and gkm-10's ttls except a hold's copy; api-14 lists both mailboxes' sealed copies (21.10); §11.13 moves a held shredding repo's batched records, and §11.12 resumes its shred at phase 5 when the hold ends; §11.13's drop job rereads `hold/` before each batch of deletions and defers a covered drop's deletions until every covering hold ends, the drop reading, listing and billing as an unheld one ([owner decision 184](#od-184)); §16.11's daemons and readers apply the directory's request limits as `GET /sidecar/limits` gives them, §21's rows included (§20.4); §23.7 tracks counsel's confirmation of [owner decision 133](#od-133)'s condition and of each hold kind's applicability (`preserve_2703f`, `report_2258a`); §22 tests sweeps, access logs, holds beside shredding, a held --now shred's batched records packed, kept until the hold ends, then deleted (FS-6), hold kinds' deadlines (FS-48), clocks across a weekend (FS-49), held drops (FS-92) and, at M5, FS-39's report-intake cases and S7's SNI-less `abuse@<root>`.

|---|---|---|---|
| Safe Browsing flag (statichost.eu, 2025-09-25: https://www.statichost.eu/blog/google-safe-browsing/) or registrar hold on the root | Medium | Critical | 1 h kills, Web Risk, Search Console, the pager, a user-only root ([owner decision 13](#od-13)), the PSL later |
| Off-hours, a wrong kill holds until business hours, about 63 h over a weekend, and unpaged signals, a Search Console flag included, wait ([owner decision 134](#od-134)) | Medium | High | 21.8's signals only; appeals; 24/7 in v1 |
| Counsel rejects [owner decision 133](#od-133)'s condition or a hold kind | Low | High | asked before holds ship (M5) |
| A drop used to destroy evidence before a hold arrives | Low | Medium | the 7-day window keeps every byte for a hold to cover ([owner decision 183](#od-183)); `now` drops stay visible in push history (evs-12); held drops delete nothing ([owner decision 184](#od-184)) |
| False reports | Medium | Medium | reporter classes, host-level first, appeals |

| Without a policy, untagged sidecars and their agents reach providers' LAN and loopback (accepted, disclosed; owner decisions [50](#od-50), [120](#od-120)) | Medium | High | §2.18's disclosure; policies on any tier ([owner decision 73](#od-73)); suspension |

### 21.18 Phasing

- **v0 (M5), before any public name:** 21.6-21.10 with `rpt.bringyour.com` and 21.11's RFC 3207 deviation, less the later items below; the DMCA agent; Search Console and registrar contacts; business-hours review, with 21.8's notices on §19.8's rota (owner decisions [134](#od-134), [143](#od-143)); holds once counsel confirms (21.9). **v1 (M6):** 24/7 review; tightening the team directory's request limits (21.7).
- **M7:** reporters in the census (D-MAIL-9). **M8:** trusted flaggers. **M9** (owner decisions [35](#od-35), [124](#od-124)): §14.8's ladder, the send gate and 21.5's breakers. **M10** (v1's format 2, [owner decision 169](#od-169)): holds defer drops' deletions (§11.13).
- **With "end-to-end encrypted" (§23.8):** 21.11's trust documents; the first report six months after the first public name.
- **Blocking:** M5's names wait on intake, the report host, the kill switch and the pager; holds on counsel; M5's exit on FS-39's report-intake cases, FS-48, FS-49 and S7's SNI-less `abuse@<root>` (§22.7, §22.8); M9's sending on the breakers.

## 22. Testing and verification

### 22.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns verification: tiers, harness, hot-path gates, fuzzing, scenarios, privacy, admission and revocation suites, load, soak, the fault-schedule program, storage benchmarks, conformance, platform budgets and internal review gates. Sections keep their targets and mechanisms; this one names each target's test, invariant and gate. §19 owns environments, §23 milestones and the gate map.

### 22.6 Fuzzing

- **Envelope, chunks, every `sidecar/protocol` body:** the decoded message is `proto.Equal` to `proto.Unmarshal`'s, and its encoding equals `proto.MarshalOptions{Deterministic: true}`'s and decodes back equal; seeds hold reordered, repeated, unknown, packed and unpacked fields and non-minimal varints; signatures verify over the received bytes, never a re-marshal.
- **Typed `Signed` statements:** every registered type pair is refused as another type, a `GrantRevoke{grant_id}` presented as `OwnerConfirm{sidecar_id}` with equal field-1 bytes included.
- **`record.proto` headers:** a v1 reader verifies one with an unknown field and kind; re-encoding changes nothing a verifier checks; two writers' entries in one push order deterministically.
- **Stream, push and config-delta state machines:** nothing past `max_offset`; bounded memory; converge or resync.
- **tlsedge ClientHello, split across records:** SNI and ALPN equal `crypto/tls`'s.
- **PROXY v1 and v2:** pires/go-proxyproto agrees with mailgun/proxyproto.
- **SMTP at mxedge (pre-TLS), smtpedge (MX replies) and receivers:** §15.4 holds; nothing forwarded before STARTTLS's 220.
- **go-message, mox, ARF, RUA, TLS-RPT, DSN:** bounded expansion; no enclosed ARF body decoded.
- **Git pkt-line, pack, delta; head-mode codec:** equals go-git.
- **`EvsPush`, `EvsPushPart`, a DROP's `EvsDropHistory` and its lists, batch records, window entries, upload receipts, index entries, name tables, path maps, segments:** tampering fails before plaintext or adoption.
- **MLS messages, Welcome, GroupInfo, tree, `GkmCommitHeader`:** `mls_*` agrees with thomas-vilte/mls-go (0x0001) and tmc/mls (0x004F as 0x0010).
- **DNS feed, synthesis, validator; `dnssec_chain`:** no non-public or refused record; broken chains refused.
- **HuJSON compiler; `BridgeEgressPolicy`:** equal the reference.
- **Daemon hello, `.ur`, `ur hook` payloads, MCP arguments:** no secret echoed.
- **Index files** (slots, large entries, bucket and all shards, doc and tombstone tables, manifests, settings, the lock): decoding total and memory-bounded; tampering fails AEAD or the plaintext hash before use; re-encoding reproduces the bytes; non-minimal VByte, unsorted or repeated keys and docids, bitsets off their threshold, a key in both of a shard's tables and a tombstone in an all shard refused (FI-22); a current diff's chain that does not resolve leaves its document not yet searchable, never a miss, and a superseded diff's raises nothing.
- **Normalizer and trigram extractor:** idempotent; output within a fixed multiple of input; invalid UTF-8 mapped by one rule; trigram sets equal to a reference extractor's written apart.
- **Search arguments and cursors** (`ur search` and `ur agents` flags, MCP search arguments, §16.10's parser, planner and cursor decoder): bounded postings touched; forged or foreign cursors refused; no panic; no secret echoed.
- **`SearchRequest` and `SearchReply`** (pads, sizes, coverage, hits past their caps, unknown codes, repeated pages): decoding total and memory-bounded; the indexer answers a body off 4,016 B or with a non-zero pad as INVALID and a repeated page with its cursor's last reply; the phone refuses a reply off its steps × 16,384 B, drops hits and fields past their caps before the merge, and never reads an unknown status or served code as OK or served.
- **The remote-search merge**, against adversarial replies: it never adds a hit from a repo the request did not name or the requester does not read, never removes the phone's own confirmed hits, and collapses possible matches only inside the stated span (D-EVS-60).
- **`directory.proto`'s card, repo file, notice, request, decision and erasure request decoders:** decoding total and memory-bounded; a version past its caps (a card's 16 items in 16,208 B, a 4 KiB repo file, a 256 B notice) is ignored with an alarm, never shown; signatures verify over the received bytes (FI-25).

Seeds in `testdata/fuzz/` run in every `test.sh` ([owner decision 101](#od-101)); crashers become seeds and regression tests.

### 22.7 Scenarios, privacy, revocation

Scenarios mirror §3.7's flows (D-ARCH-3) on T2 fakes, then T3 (S1 only T3), with §7.4's route allowlist on; T6 repeats S5-S8 and S10.

- **S1** (F1, enroll): code-create 403; token never in MCP, env or logs; a genesis other than the invite's refused.
- **S2** (F2, write, notify): hint p99 ≤ 2 s; owned refs land; on a shared ref, disjoint pushes land on file-mode refs, and on a git-mode ref the second gets a stock non-fast-forward and its merge lands (§11.7, §11.11; [owner decision 141](#od-141); FS-5); every acknowledged commit is reachable; a non-writer's head refused.
- **S3** (F3, add a reader): a server-forged admission, KeyPackage or ReaderKey refused, and an authentic ReaderKey past its not_after or valid over 7 days; Adds and wraps only for readers, each late wrap judged at its own pin (FS-104); device form S3a (KF2) from M2, member form S3b at M6.
- **S4** (F9, remove): the revocation suite; device form S4a (KF4) from M2, member form S4b at M6.
- **S5** (F4, publish HTTPS): key only on device; each §13.7 audience, login-less visitors reaching only edge login; Community publishes verified, ≤ 7 days.
- **S6** (F5, send mail, M9): no record forwarded before its proof verifies; no unauthenticated MX; §15.10's forwarding rules; a message over the DATA cap is `too_large` for the non-CHUNKING recipient domain alone (FS-123).
- **S7** (F6, receive mail): 530 to plaintext; unroutable gets a temporary failure, the edge holding nothing; abuse@`<root>` without SNI reaches the platform listener; DNS changed between reception and ingest leaves the reception-time result, and tampered evidence fails; a message whose checks a bound cut is deposited and labeled from what was verified (FS-121).
- **S8** (F7, subnets, port maps): rules only from the config repo; LAN by rule once a document exists, else open to untagged sources ([owner decision 120](#od-120)) but never to the provider's own `127.0.0.1` daemon ports, while an unrelated loopback service passes; revoke resets.
- **S9** (F8, MCP work): vault only; redaction; gaps; evidence labels.
- **S10** (F10, burner lifecycle): a burned label gets 550 with no DNS change; a replying burner's first selector keeps its `<blabel>` MX and A, its last restores the wildcard-only state, and a receive-only burner creates no child.
- **S11** (F11, search and agents; FS-77 and FS-80, from M10): a claim filed on one device is in another's next search after its index entry lands: in a team network with the card push that carries it, in a vault after the writer's next companion push, at most a minute later on 1 KiB blocks, else five minutes ([owner decision 172](#od-172)); hits are grouped by agent, active first; an untrusted hit returns as a stub with the run untainted, and `untrusted: include` taints first; a parked device's search omits its member's vault and lists it as consent pending; an EvsShare reader's receipt precedes each index decrypt; an erasure ends open cursors and empties the caches of its postings; two searches with different queries over one state send evs identical request sequences.
- **S12** (F12, remote search; FS-83; from M10, app hosts with M8 and team indexers with M6): in a network that designates a search indexer (none is designated by default, [owner decision 177](#od-177)), a phone's "search more" asks its own indexer and shows verified hits merged with its own, a false possible match collapsed; with that indexer killed the next answers, and with none the repo falls back to the download; a team repo reaches the network's indexer only after the notice, and the member's vault never does; both devices' evs request logs are identical with and without the remote search; every search frame a relay carries has its kind's one size; the pair's close reports are each window's floor, whatever the searches (FS-125).
- **S13** (F13, announce, find and request; FS-84 to FS-88; from M6; [owner decision 171](#od-171)): B's agent finds member A's run within one sync, by `directory_list` at M6 and `search_agents` from M10, grouped by agent, its title withheld from B's agent and B's run untainted; a run in a repo marked private at creation shows `private` and the repo id; a run in an announced general repo shows its name and branch to every member; a revoked announcement leaves no readable copy of the name ([owner decision 181](#od-181)); B's agent requests read on the private repo by its id, a harness prompt endorsing it in an untainted run and device or presence evidence in a tainted one; the repo admin's devices are hinted, phones woken from M8; a person approves, B's devices read the repo, and B's daemon verifies the `RepoGrant` at its log position; B's agent then asks to reach a worker A owns or sponsors, A approving as `autogroup:dst-owner` (owner decisions [179](#od-179), [180](#od-180)), and B spends the approval once into a `GrantActivate` and dials only the worker's announced ports (FS-85's worker case); a denial shows its note; A's opt-out stops A's announcements ([owner decision 170](#od-170)), and A's removal masks them at once.

### 22.8 Load, soak, failure injection

- **sockets:** 100,000 listeners, ~6,700 registration calls/s (§9.8); Find p99 ≤ 50 ms server-side, in-flight share within ±25% of weight (proposed).
- **tlsedge:** 50,000 connections per process (§13.9), name scans, W2's per-address limits on the lb path; §13.5's p95.
- **evs:** the twenty-agent test: 20 agents push their owned refs and merge into `main` every 60 s for 1 h (4.3 pushes/s, §11.13), with no acknowledged commit lost, `git fsck` and export oids equal on a second device and §11.15's targets met; 1,000 subscribers per repo (§11.15).
- **push, config:** 10,000 networks save a config head in 1 min; 2× §19.6's Y2 hint rate, leases, push sequence and the head and projection caches included, at ≤ 50% Redis CPU per master; §8.9.
- **escrow:** §20.9's benchmark and FS-46 at M6's entry on M4's dark build (§23.4); the benchmark again at its exit.
- **smtpedge:** Team quota on many networks; halts ≤ 60 s, no overrun.
- **soak:** 72 h at 30%; heap, goroutines, Redis keys and orphan objects back to baseline.

**Fault schedules (D-TEST-10).** Each schedule runs on the tiers its row names, under the rules below; an oracle with read access to every store checks the named invariants after every step and at the end. Owning sections give each mechanism, and this catalog its schedule, check, tier and gate.

```go
// sidecartest/fault: one Schedule per FS row; Await and Release name testHookBarrier sites (22.4)
type Schedule struct {
	Id    string      // "FS-1"
	Seed  int64       // only the explorer's interleavings use it
	Steps []*Step
	Check []Invariant // FI-n, after every step and at the end
}
type Step struct {
	Actor    string         // "writerA", "evs1", "gc", "shred", "daemonM", "stripe"
	Action   func(ctx context.Context, net *Net) error
	Await    string         // run until Actor reaches this barrier, then hold it there
	Release  []string       // barriers to release, in this order
	Fault    *FaultPlan     // the result the next matching store, Redis or Postgres operation gets
	Advance  time.Duration  // fake clock, shared by every actor
	Kill     bool           // drop Actor's memory; Restart builds it again from durable state alone
	Restart  string         // instance to restart Actor on ("evs2")
	Counters *DriveCounters // fake metadata drive counters (FS-61)
}
type FaultPlan struct {
	Op        string // "put", "get", "list", "delete", "redis", "pg-commit", "http"
	KeyPrefix string
	Nth       int
	Result    FaultResult // ApplyThenDrop | FailBeforeApply | Precondition | Delay | QuorumLoss (T3) | DriveMiss (T3)
}
```

```text
FI-1   closure: a committed head's dependency closure (statements, records, entries, segments, slots, maps, wraps of
       its generation) is retrievable, from the one metadata cluster its place/ names or the packs evacuation made,
       and decrypts for a current reader, except what a durable, visible, authorized erasure, shred or executed drop
       removed (§11)
FI-2   outcomes: each operation ends committed, aborted or unknown; unknown never triggers destructive cleanup; a
       retry of a committed operation returns its original result, and a refusal a client received stays true:
       once any attempt of a push id is answered a refusal, no attempt of it commits, whenever it reaches evs,
       save one validated before its repo's shred began, which the shred destroys (I-EVS-3); a reclaimed
       preparation never commits later (§11, §16)
FI-3   commit-point authorization: every head transition carries, and the oracle re-verifies, the authorization pin,
       generation pin, path epoch and lifecycle state current at its head CAS, retries and seals included; nothing
       committing later than §10.6's window after a gate closes uses an excluded generation (§8, §10, §11)
FI-4   one ladder: each generation has one authenticated parent and commitment C_g, whichever path raised it; every
       reader converges on it; none regresses (§10)
FI-5   lifecycle: restore and shred have one winner; a restored repo holds its whole key closure; a shredded or erased
       object never returns, a stale re-seed included, unless no surviving device holds the ERASE (§11.12's
       residual), which §19.10's close report names, and a dropped object never returns, a stale re-seed included,
       except as FI-27 bounds it (§11, §19)
FI-6   visibility: nothing uncommitted evicts a file's newest committed version, which readers find in its entry or
       the head window, and no directory delta leaves the window before its name table holds it; every uncommitted
       object (a dead record with its slots, an unadopted segment, a staged wrap, an abandoned path map) becomes
       reclaimable after its deadline, found without the log; nothing committed or unknown is reclaimed (§11)
FI-7   effects: an approval use is reserved before its effect and stays consumed or explicitly uncertain after any
       crash; no second effect; run taint and requester bindings survive restarts (§16)
FI-8   attribution: a run restore changes only state attributable to its run, or reports ambiguity, and checks its
       preview on the bytes it moves aside, never on an earlier read, discarding no others (§16)
FI-9   git: an acknowledged push has the declared ref, tree, ancestry and per-ref outcome; stock clients see standard
       non-fast-forward errors; a git-mode tip commits only once ur/lfs holds every git-lfs object it requires, safe
       from every prune, and no prune removes an object a current tip requires (§11)
FI-10  witnesses: a witness names exactly the state it compared; stale peers cannot manufacture freshness; a fork
       under one epoch alarms or reads unwitnessed (§2, §6)
FI-11  path integrity: no application byte reaches a backend before its audience check, whatever the SNI or ALPN, nor
       a target after its flow's revocation (§17.6, D-BRIDGE-21); a proof accepts only what the MX's own state machine
       accepts (§13, §14, §17)
FI-12  recovery: after a Postgres or site loss, the newest copy a device or dump holds comes back exactly (oids, C_v,
       decryptability, identities, labels), save what §19.10's postgres step lists in the incident (a suffixed
       network name, a login left for a reset) or keeps at the main dump's age (rows the sidecar dump does not
       name), and nothing erased or dropped (but as FI-5 allows), shredded or revoked returns; an object whose every
       shard exists survives a second host (§19)
FI-13  accounting: (a) every metered byte debits at most once and, barring an unclean producer exit or a batch dropped
       past its 10-min retry horizon, exactly once; (b) a period's billed quantity equals its rows' newest values; (c)
       after each nightly pass, stored bytes equal the seg/, pack/ and hp/ objects' sizes plus the lengths heads and
       log pages give for records still in batches, less objects only a hold keeps, objects held for a drop included,
       and containers whose every record a newer container's pidx/ entry names (20.7); (d) 20.9's E-a to E-e (§20)
FI-14  write budget: (a) with the budget on, on each metadata set's busiest drive not under heal (§19.6's governor
       skips one), the writes of classes other than P0 over any 24 h stay within 24 h of refill plus the bucket's
       depth (0.8 DWPD) and one 5 s interval's issue times the pricing error, less the P0 writes the bucket held in
       those 24 h, which are P0's measured writes less its forgiven excess, the bytes past what the bucket held (owner
       decision 190), so the drive writes past that only by the forgiven excess; P0's bytes and forgiven excess are
       measured and reported by kind (§19.8), not bounded (owner decision 186); (b) conservation: each interval's P1
       and unfunded P2 debits stay within T, funded P2 spends only the wallet W, W never exceeds the priced funded
       backlog, and each push's deferred work is paid once, from W or as unfunded P2; (c) no P0 write waits or is
       refused; (d) a network is refused only while one with less queued priced bytes per weight is served (§11, §19)
FI-15  file-mode CAS (I-EVS-8): a file-mode push commits at u only if each file path it changes has, in the head
       history through u-1, newest version equal to its base_entry_version, 0 naming the path absent (never
       written, or removed), a removal being one of its versions, one past its last, which its marker keeps, and
       each creation's version max(its push's effective base version, the newest removal its marker or the window
       holds) + 1, an overlay's base counting its chain's base versions, so a path's versions never restart
       (owner decision 148) and no push based on a version from before a removal commits after it (5g while either
       holds the removal, 5f's base range once its marker is collected), however folds, reruns, copies and
       collection windows interleave, and 11.7's two-way directory checks hold; a head read or listing at head v
       serves each path's newest version through v, none newer (§11)
FI-16  purge: the content of a versionless version (a kind-5 segment, a staged record, a slot only that path's
       versions name) is deleted only after its replacing version is committed and a process saw that commit (its own
       200, a head reread or a Resolve), the 60 s in-flight allowance has passed on a checked clock, no hold keeps it
       when the delete issues (a hold covering the repo keeps what existed at its placement), and no version committed
       later names it; unknown and refused pushes purge nothing; every path's newest committed version keeps all its
       content; each candidate goes within the sweep's period once those conditions hold, and purged content never
       returns, a stale re-seed included (§11)
FI-17  versioning: a committed version names a kind-5 segment only as §11.7's citation rule allows, and a staged
       record only from its introducing version; versioning 1 never commits in config or mailcfg repos, on git-mode or
       creates-only refs or under a repo lock, and versioning 2 only under an index root (.ur-index/ on a file-mode
       ref, or ur/index) of a repo that may hold an index, a lock keeping it (owner decision 168); every version
       written with versioning on keeps its content for the repo's life (FI-1), whatever the path's later setting,
       unless an executed drop lists it (FI-27); format-1 code refuses each format-2 construct in use as needing
       format 2, or ignores or folds it where D-PHASE-9's reservation list says, never treating one as a fork,
       tampering or a missing segment (§11)
FI-18  index results: for every scope, device and sync state, the candidates for a normalized query include every
       covered document whose newest committed version in the scope contains it; a hit labeled verified or confirmed
       has a newest version whose text or display fields contain it, and a hit found through a corrected term says so;
       no hit rests only on a masked older version; an uncovered document is searched from the device's own text where
       it holds it, else reported not yet searchable, never silently absent; a seal, merge, slot reuse or roll-up
       changes no search's result set, nor does a fresh cache once the purge has taken every replaced index version,
       since every diff's chain and every tombstone a result needs stays in the committed index; a search's mask
       state stays within its working set whatever the partitions hold (§11, §16, §18)
FI-19  index erasure: once the erasure of a document completes, no committed version of an index file that a current
       reader's keys open holds its postings or display fields; every stored version that held them shares a key its
       ERASEs destroyed (one key per index path in slot-keyed repos), its ciphertext purged under FI-16 or kept
       unreadable under a hold; after the erasure's CUT on its ref no index file version but a CLOSURE's, which
       re-keys only a file that held it, is committed holding it, whatever index pushes were prepared before the CUT,
       delayed, resealed or retried, with no indexer and every hint lost; an erasure whose CUT committed finishes from
       evs's state on a device that may erase it; no device that applied the CUT or the hint returns the document from
       a search or a cache (§11, §15, §16)
FI-20  roll-up: each expired bucket of a ref is rolled into all by at most one committed roll-up, whose plaintext
       equals the deterministic merge of its inputs; the bucket's files leave the index only in the push that commits
       all holding their postings; a rerun after any crash converges to that result; until it commits, searches merge
       the expired bucket (§11)
FI-21  search scope and taint: every hit is from a repo the caller's subject may read by §8's local evaluation and
       §8.5's consent, an EvsShare or audit reader having deposited, and evs having acknowledged, a read receipt
       naming each index object before decrypting it; no hit, snippet or display field comes from a secret, config or
       mailcfg repo; an untrusted hit returns as a text-free stub unless its text is asked for, and a result carrying
       any field from untrusted content returns only after the run's taint is fsynced (I-9); no query, hit or cursor
       leaves the device except a remote search's, sealed end to end to an indexer FI-24 allows (§16, §2)
FI-22  determinism: every index object's plaintext is a function of its format version, normalization version and
       inputs alone, byte-equal on every build leg; decoders accept only canonical encodings, so re-encoding what one
       decoded reproduces its bytes; plaintext hashes are taken before encryption, and nothing is compressed (§11)
FI-23  fetch privacy: the index objects a search fetches, and their order, depend only on the device's sync state, its
       fetch rule and the results the user opens, never on the query; only a fetch's time shows that a search ran
       (§2.8, §11, §18)
FI-24  remote search: a query leaves an app host only for a designated search indexer §11.14's rule lets answer it,
       for repos both read, an owner-bound repo only on its owner's consented device, another member's device only
       after that member's notice; every hit names a repo the request named, which the requester reads, and a verified
       hit's newest version contains the query; each request body is 4,016 B and each reply steps x 16,384 B, whatever
       the query, scope, filters, results or failure after parsing; neither device sends evs, api or gkm a request
       because of a remote search; no query, hit, snippet or cursor persists on either device, and the served record
       names none; for a pair §6.11's bit 1 marks, each §6.10 window and direction has one report a contract, F on

FI-25  directory authorship: every card, notice and run or worker announce entry a reader shows or acts on was written
       and signed as §16.11's path and signing rules require, by a signer that is admitted, unrevoked, unreaped,
       unsuspended and, for a member device, consented in the reader's state, and every repo item by a signer that

FI-26  request soundness: every grant a directory decision produces (a RepoGrant, an EvsShare, or a GrantActivate
       spending its ApprovalDecision) is signed by an approver eligible for its target at its log position, names

       subject no wider than the request's, expires no later than asked when an expiry was asked, and exists only for

FI-27  drop history: a drop deletes a segment or slot only if (1) every version that names it, committed at any time
```

Beyond the schedules:

- **lb drain (warp/warpctl/run.go:1453); Redis failover; Postgres or PgBouncer restart; resident migration; 60 s ack timeout:** clients retry streamed PUTs, which nginx cannot (warp/warpctl/config.go:2307); sockets heal; halts reload; streams reset TRANSFER_FAILED; RPC retries.
- **Clocks ±10 min; migration N+1 before code; sidecar N vs server N±1:** tickets, skew and expiry hold; explicit VERSION or UNIMPLEMENTED.
- **Kills mid-keychain write:** the keychain opens at its old or new state (§5.9).

### 22.9 Conformance and platform budgets

- **git** (2.34, Ubuntu 22.04's, https://ubuntuupdates.org/package/core/jammy/main/base/git; 2.43, Ubuntu 24.04's and Claude Code cloud's; latest; Windows, Xcode; go-git, JGit, libgit2; OpenSSH): through the local tier, and `git-remote-ur` without a prior mount, oids equal a reference; stock non-fast-forward errors, sibling pushes from one base giving one; `git push --atomic` fails before any write; a two-ref push reports per-ref statuses; a daemon killed between the remote commit and update-ref reconciles from its journal; foreign new commits refused, signed imports accepted.
- **git-lfs** (3.x as Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 ship it, and the latest; `lfs.standalonetransferagent`; `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE`): FS-73's flows with stock clients, pointer files byte-exact and export's oids equal to git's, its tip check included over http, ssh and `git-remote-ur`, with no skip option set and with `--no-verify` and `GIT_LFS_SKIP_PUSH`.
- **Restore** (darwin on APFS; linux on ext4, xfs and an NFS mount; windows on NTFS; a FAT volume on each; symlinks on each, Windows with and without the symlink privilege): FS-115's apply through each volume's no-replace rename, its hard-link fallback, and `unsupported` where it has neither, with Windows's in-use refusal.
- **File clusters** (D-OPS-20's in-house MinIO build, every cluster, each build, upgrade and new cluster; D-OPS-4): stale conditions refused with a host or quorum lost (§11.3); §19.6's deadline and settle rules, by FS-114's late-drive cases: a request past its x-ur-deadline-ms refused where it takes its key's lock, no drive commit begun past it, and a PUT or DELETE whose drive commits are held after their checks past the 30 s drive timeout, its coordinator killed, taking effect before the next request on its key or never, the newer acknowledged state surviving release and a full heal, since a removal marker's collection deletes unconditionally ([owner decision 148](#od-148)), as from v1 do the versionless purge's and the marker collection's kind-5 and slot DELETEs and a drop job's DELETEs; the lag from a cancel to a write's last drive answer, measured and reported, which no margin relies on; no heal resurrects a deleted object or spreads a version fewer than a read quorum of drives hold; read-after-write and LIST consistency; checksums; ranged GET; Delete; lifecycle; one pool per cluster (FS-63).
- **MTAs** (Postfix (may, dane), Exim; Gmail, Outlook.com, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, iCloud, SES, Proton, Fastmail): in, D-MAIL-9's census with nothing lost; out, §14.4 levels, DKIM, strict DMARC, which B's selector fails for A's network and burners, FCrDNS, JMRP and CFL joins; aggregate reports as FS-39, a one-connection, ten-recipient send raising no alarm.
- **ZK preamble** (`smtpproof`, BDAT and DATA ([owner decision 125](#od-125)), on D-SMTP-16's hardware; census MXs): D-SMTP-16's adversarial corpus, FS-31's server-state cases included, fails before any effect; p95 times, coverage, interop.
- **ACME** (Pebble with 5% bad nonces in T2 and T3; LE staging; GTS, ZeroSSL): §13.8's challenges, ARI, CAA, an operator CAA at a custom host's exact target refused (FS-32); custom-domain desktops order and renew on Pebble; LE staging refuses URnetwork's account under a customer `accounturi`, which Pebble never checks (https://github.com/letsencrypt/pebble/blob/main/va/va.go, 2026-11-04); CT watch on a fixture (staging CT is unreliable: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/staging-environment/, 2026-04-10).
- **DNS** (zonemaster; Unbound, BIND, Knot Resolver; two public resolvers): R-DNS-7; compact denial and wildcards validate; before the DS, Unbound validates against the KSK as a trust anchor; a broken canary signature pages.
- **Browsers** (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, curl; Playwright on ur.io's page Worker and the native companion): 421 on coalescing; split PQ hellos; other origins' POST, subresource GET and WebSocket arrive sessionless, and login works without Fetch Metadata (§13.7); private audiences without a usable ALPN (FS-34) and custom hosts through the split (FS-35); another origin, a framed copy and localhost are refused the key origin, no key or token crosses postMessage, and a script injected on ur.io finds neither the Worker's key nor its token; IndexedDB survives a reload, and after Safari's 7-day storage cap evicts the key origin its page Worker re-enrolls through a consented device, the old leaf leaving by §10.9's stale-leaf rule; a storage-pressure eviction of a non-persistent bucket does the same, the re-enrollment's admitting device, an admin's in a Team with self_admit off, revoking each Worker it saw removed as stale from every group it is a leaf of that seated it, and the member's consented device, in that act or at its OwnerConfirm, offering to revoke the evicted one (§7.10's stale row; FS-97); the key-origin frame calls navigator.storage.persist(), and the page tells the person what an eviction costs (§18.8); in two ur.io tabs on one network only the Web Lock's holder loads state, refreshes, commits and writes the keychain, the other Worker relaying, and closing the holder's tab hands over the lock, relayed requests retrying; a vault record opens with C4 absent; no ICE candidate in the overlay block (§17.17), and a CGNAT fixture whose WAN address lies in the block keeps its carrier path and overlay reachability; no torn writes; no network `by_jwt` in the worker.
- **Memory, size** (darwin/arm64 iOS settings in T4; ios32 surrogate cells, one with a link; §18.4's other hosts): §18.4's budgets, and forwarding's within owner decisions [215](#od-215) and [216](#od-216)'s on an ios32 cell whose forwarding role compiles a 3,000-device team's config within its 10 MiB cap and refuses a 5,000-device one with bridge_alarm (owner decisions [197](#od-197), [216](#od-216)), a hooked NAT's per-flow UDP loop re-measured on constrained provider profiles at M8 (§17.6), in every LOWBAR phase on iOS, the link cell deciding links and holding an app-device host's NAT with bridge flows at §17.5's idles through C5's per-flow IdleTimeout, while its public egress flows keep the NAT's own; sizes unstripped (§18.10); `make check` fails an HTTP-only file importing connect; the mobile sender's 1,024-slot pin table, churned past 1,024 live pairs, routes the excess unpinned and refuses none (§17.5).
- **Index determinism** (darwin/arm64, linux/amd64 and arm64, windows/amd64, gomobile android/arm64 and the iOS settings, js/wasm in Node and, through Playwright, Chrome, Firefox and Safari): testdata/index/ reproduces byte-equal plaintext and hashes under GOMAXPROCS 1 and 16, repeated runs (Go randomizes map order) and changed TZ and locale; the linked `norm.Version`, `cases.UnicodeVersion` and `unicode.Version` equal the format's normalization version and x/text's linked module version equals `IndexFileHeader` field 14's, so a toolchain or x/text bump fails until a new one is assigned (D-TEST-15).
