### 22.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mock engines | fast | hide wire bugs | fakes at store interfaces |
| Random interleavings without named barriers | no hooks at protocol steps | a found race cannot be replayed; no commit point is held at its lost response | rejected: fixed schedules plus a seeded explorer (D-TEST-10) |
| Search results checked by the index's own decoder | simple | shares the index's bugs | rejected: an oracle written apart (D-TEST-14) |
| Purge or drop deletes on from format 2's first day | storage freed at once | a purge or drop bug destroys content no check restores | rejected: observe first (D-TEST-12, D-TEST-18) |

### 22.12 Decisions proposed

**D-TEST-1 (proposed).** T1-T4 gate merges, `sidecar/test.sh` running in RUN-ALL after connect; server tests of sidecar engines set `WARP_TEST_ENV_FAIL_FAST=1`; sidecar tests follow connect/CODESTYLE.md:200-217. *Why:* R-TEST-1, R-TEST-9.

**D-TEST-2 (proposed).** `sidecartest` rebuilds connect's helpers from exported API and ships fakes whose store suites server also runs on real stores. *Why:* the helpers are unimportable (Q-TEST-1); shared suites keep fakes honest.

**D-TEST-3 (proposed).** 22.5's gates and 22.9's budgets fail the build; raising one needs a reviewed change (sdk/build/APPLE_EXTENSION_MEMORY_BUDGET.md). *Why:* I-12; 4,690,096 B of iOS headroom.

**D-TEST-4 (proposed).** Every 22.6 target ships seeds and, given a second implementation, a differential oracle. *Why:* parsers face hostile peers, and protobuf encoding is not canonical (https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/encoding/#field-order).

**D-TEST-5 (proposed).** Every scenario runs 22.7's harness and guard; later, a synthetic main network repeats S2 and S5-S7 hourly. *Why:* R-TEST-3 is a system property.

**D-TEST-6 (proposed).** The revocation suite runs with evs's gate off. *Why:* server refusal is defense in depth (I-5).

**D-TEST-7 (proposed).** 22.8 runs per milestone and its soak before each release; conformance peers are pinned and rerun per pin change. *Why:* fan-out fails only under load; peers change silently.

**D-TEST-8 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 99](#od-99): no external review gates a freeze or the claim.

**D-TEST-9 (proposed).** Freezes pass 22.10's gates in D-PHASE-7's two steps. *Why:* one conditional write orders storage ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), and nothing is audited ([owner decision 99](#od-99)).

**D-TEST-10 (proposed).** Every state machine of §7-§21, and §5.6's device revocation, is tested by deterministic fault schedules (FS-1 to FS-125), each run on the tiers its row names (T2's fakes, T3's real stores) against FI-1 to FI-30, beside TLA+ models of the separate durable objects (`EvsCommit.tla`), of the index roll-up (`IndexRollup.tla`) and of the store's settle rule (`StoreSettle.tla`) and a Porcupine check of T3 histories with unknown outcomes. *Why:* single-object conditional writes order storage ([owner decision 2](#od-2)) and no transaction spans objects, so every commit point, retry and cleanup must be shown under lost responses, crashes and stale processes, and the roll-up is a multi-push protocol whose lock, CAS and erasure race no schedule alone exhausts; nothing is audited ([owner decision 99](#od-99)).

**D-TEST-11 (proposed).** §22.8's `nvme` run on the PM9A3 set gates M2's exit and format 1's freeze: at 2× year one's mix with the write budget on, refilled at 0.8 DWPD for the run, the budget refuses no push, at most 43 KiB is written per push per drive, its P2 work included and charged once from the wallet (FS-116, which runs first, on exact costs), P0's bytes by kind are measured against the refill, setting §19.8's P0 warn line at four times their hourly share, at most half the refill, with the P0 page silent at that mix (P0 past the refill is FS-117's, [owner decision 186](#od-186)), and writes stay within 50% of rated IOPS, on 1 KiB XFS blocks, or on 4 KiB only if format 2's projected mix (format 1's measured price table applied to §11.13's per-push index operations, the index on in every eligible repo) also fits there; its per-operation costs become §11.13's price table. *Why:* [owner decision 140](#od-140)'s binding limits, at most 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS, which the design meets at ~27-43 KiB a push, 43 KiB being 0.8 DWPD at 400 pushes/s; the run refills at that limit, not production's 0.768, which leaves room for the bucket's 1 h of depth (§11.13); the head's If-Match overwrite alone writes ~14 KiB ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), so the record's first ~10-15 KiB estimate was withdrawn (Q-EVS-9, decided); mkfs fixes the block size for format 2 too: at 2× year one format 1 writes ~40-43 KiB a push on 4 KiB blocks (~30-33 on 1 KiB), and the default-on index ([owner decision 156](#od-156)) adds ~4 on 1 KiB blocks at one companion push a minute per writer, and ~2 on 4 KiB blocks at one every 5 minutes ([owner decision 172](#od-172); §11.13).

**D-TEST-12 (proposed).** The versionless purge ships in observe mode (§19.11's `purge: observe`), logging candidates and deleting nothing while taskworker checks that no retained version names one; deletes turn on once FS-64 to FS-71 pass on their rows' tiers and a production soak after the final freeze (at least 14 days and 10,000 candidates) finds none that a retained version names, and until then the gate admits only internal networks and design partners (D-PHASE-10), so later networks get [owner decision 161](#od-161)'s purge from their first format-2 push. *Why:* a purge bug destroys content no other check restores, and only production shows real clients' citations.

**D-TEST-13 (proposed).** Format 2's bytes freeze only when its drive-write cost, projected from §22.8's M2 price table (D-TEST-11) and the M10 `index` row's T3 operation counts, with the index on in every eligible repo, purges and staging on and each companion push charged to the content pushes it indexes, meets D-TEST-11's gate; after the freeze, while §19.11's `format2` gate holds format 2 to internal networks and design partners, production's write budget must show measured over priced drive bytes within 10%, and a larger ratio holds the gate there until §19.9's next cluster or a later format change restores the fit; runs with the index off attribute each increment. *Why:* [owner decision 174](#od-174), which buys no staging drives and accepts that a miss found after the freeze costs more clusters sooner ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) or a format change; [owner decision 140](#od-140) binds format 2 too, and at [owner decision 172](#od-172)'s cadence §11.13's costs put a push, with the default-on index, at ~34-37 KiB at 2× year one on 1 KiB blocks but ~42-45 KiB on 4 KiB blocks, against the gate's 43.

**D-TEST-14 (proposed).** Every search schedule checks its results against `SearchOracle` (22.4), which shares no index code: a desktop's text-verified hits equal its set, every device's candidates include its covered set, and each uncovered document is found from local text or reported not yet searchable; the index schedules also search from a fresh cache after the purge has taken every replaced index version. *Why:* completeness needs extraction, masking, coverage and roll-ups all correct, and an oracle sharing their code shares their bugs; a warm cache or an uncollected version can hide a lost diff base or tombstone.

**D-TEST-15 (proposed).** testdata/index/ fixes vectors with plaintext hashes (normalization, trigram sets, deltas, head files, seals, merges, roll-ups, doc and tombstone tables, a merge keeping a head's base, a roll-up removing an older newer-bucket entry) that every test.sh reproduces byte for byte on every leg, js/wasm and gomobile included; decoders accept only canonical encodings; every leg builds with one Go toolchain, since x/text picks its Unicode 15.0.0 or 17.0.0 tables by toolchain (.gomodcache/golang.org/x/text@v0.43.0/unicode/norm/tables15.0.0.go:3, `//go:build !go1.27`; connect/go.mod:3 and sdk/go.mod:3, `go 1.27.3`), and the vectors check the linked `norm.Version`, `cases.UnicodeVersion` and `unicode.Version` and x/text's module version (`IndexFileHeader` field 14), and include examples of the 19,960 two-rune strings that v0.40.0's and v0.41.0's NFC compose wrongly under go1.27.3: the four Hebrew pairs (U+05D2 U+0307, U+05DA U+0307, U+FB32 U+0307, U+FB3A U+0307) and a supplementary letter, U+10044 U+0307, which v0.40.0 composes to U+1E0A (§4.7); v0.40.0, which connect/go.mod:33 requires, keys recomposition on runes clipped to 16 bits (.gomodcache/golang.org/x/text@v0.40.0/unicode/norm/forminfo.go:217; tables17.0.0.go:8070-8071 map 0x05D20307 to U+105C9 and 0x05DA0307 to U+105E4), while v0.43.0, which server/go.mod:59 requires, keys full runes (forminfo.go:217), and both report Unicode 17.0.0. *Why:* convergent roll-ups, local reproduction and the indexer's checks rest on determinism (FI-22), which map order, a toolchain or x/text's tables and code break silently.

**D-TEST-16 (proposed).** Remote search is checked against `SearchOracle` as local search is, and its privacy by a relay capture: one frame-size sequence per kind whatever the query, results or post-parse failure, and equal evs request logs on both devices with and without it (FS-83, FI-24). Its stored accounting is checked by FS-125's sweep: a window's reports are the same for zero to five exchanges over every background within its allowance, both directions, across its contracts. *Why:* fixed sizes and evs's blindness are [owner decision 175](#od-175)'s whole privacy claim, and one optimization would break either silently: an early short reply, or a sync before answering. [Owner decision 176](#od-176)'s claim fails just as silently when a fixture's background sits far from a multiple of 128 KiB (meta review F18).

**D-TEST-17 (proposed).** FS-86 gates the directory against §16.11's cost table: its M6 case on announce entries at M6's Gn-out, and its card case at the later of M6's and M10's, each at 500 members in physical time on T3 and, as fake-clock days with one physical peak hour at 3x bursts beside §22.8's 1x year-one mix, at the Team limit (2,000 members, 5,000 admissions) and at a 5,000-member stress case; a golden schedule (`DirectoryCostOracle`) computes each reader's expected requests, path reads and ciphertext bytes from the events and sync times alone, the measured ones staying within 1.25 times them per reader-day and per team-day, and disabling coalescing, head reproduction or unchanged-card suppression fails that check; the cards ref's commits meet the table's p99, rerun and 429 ceilings, and injected store delays fail them; the year-one mix keeps its p99; a cold phone past 8 MiB on a metered link shows partial coverage it can continue; priced NVMe bytes per push per drive meet §11.13's price table, and the directory's pushes join format 2's computed write gate, which production confirms after the freeze (D-TEST-13; [owner decision 174](#od-174)). A miss at the Team limit blocks its gate, and the owner hears then. *Why:* reader transfer, per-stream reads and one ref's head are the directory's binding terms, and a number recorded with no ceiling cannot fail.

**D-TEST-18 (proposed).** Drop deletes ship in observe mode (§19.11's `drop: observe`): jobs run every phase and record their delete sets, deleting nothing, while the drop oracle (taskworker's verify, written apart from mark) checks each set against every retained version. Deletes turn on only once FS-89 to FS-96 pass on their tiers, TLC checks I-EVS-15 and FI-27, and a production soak on internal networks and design partners of at least 30 days and 200 jobs, half of them on repos with renames and cross-ref copies, finds no delete-set member that a retained version names. *Why:* a drop deletes keep-forever content ([owner decision 173](#od-173)), the costliest bug class, and observe mode shows its sets on real histories first.

### 22.13 Open questions

**Q-TEST-1.** Cross-cutting (X9, §4): copy connect's test helpers or export them? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a), `sidecartest` builds on connect's exported API; every T2 scenario using the fake contract issuer or ControlId sink also runs in T3 on server's exchange (server/connect/resident.go:902), and a divergence fails; a connect pin change reruns both tiers; a recurring drift, or a helper needing unexported state, raises an X9 row for `connect/connecttest` to the owner. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-2.** The local stack lacks an object store, and its one Redis node accepts cross-slot commands production's cluster rejects. **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a) plus (b), in 22.4's topologies: locally a 3-master Redis Cluster on 8.10.2 and one 8-drive MinIO at EC:4 from the production source; in T3 and at the release gate the same cluster and MinIO as 4 × 2 at EC:4 and 4 × 4 at EC:8; a runtime and static CROSSSLOT lint; canary is no substitute. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-3.** Who reviews externally? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 99](#od-99)):** nobody for now; 22.10's gates stand in. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-4.** How is the iOS tunnel's footprint verified without an iPhone (connect/MEMSTEADY.md:18)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 100](#od-100)):** (b), surrogate cells only (22.9), accepting 22.16's jetsam risk. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-5 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 24](#od-24); §11 holds the residual.

**Q-TEST-6.** Does §6.11's `oneof` ban cover every sidecar proto or only envelope, stream and push messages? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (b). No `oneof` appears in envelope, stream or push messages, or in any message they carry transitively; 22.5's descriptor lint walks from those roots over the released descriptors and fails on a oneof outside its explicit allowlist, empty in v0; other protos may use one. The reason is allocation: protobuf-go allocates a wrapper for each set oneof field, and hot-path decodes stay allocation-free (§10.4's `UrMlsCredential` has none). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-7.** Where does continuous fuzzing run? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 101](#od-101)):** (c), nowhere; seeds run as Go tests (22.6). *Residual:* none.

### 22.14 Departures from PLAN.md

None. PLAN.md says nothing about testing.

- **Provides:** `sidecartest` (harness, fakes, store suites, `PrivacyCapture`, `SearchOracle`, `DirectoryCostOracle`, which computes FS-86's expected reads and bytes from a schedule's events and sync times alone) and `sidecartest/fault` (schedules, faults, barriers); `sidecar/test.sh`; fuzz corpora; the `metadata_list.yml` guard; 22.7's suites; FI-1 to FI-30 and FS-1 to FS-125; the drop oracle (D-TEST-18); the storage benchmark, whose `nvme` costs become §11.13's price table (D-TEST-11); model checks (`EvsCommit.tla`, `IndexRollup.tla`, `StoreSettle.tla`); testdata/index/; the ZK corpus; the 0x0010 interop artifact.
- **Consumes:** §2.8's list; `make check` (§4); `testHookSecret` sites (§5, §9's `K_sock`, `K_tok` and `K_seal`, §10, §11, §13-§15, §17's ShareKey and ShareSigner seeds) and `testHookBarrier` sites at every linearization point (§7-§21, and §5.6's revocation posts); §5-§21's targets; §19's environments, W2, drive counters and M2's staging cluster (§19.11); §23's milestones and gate map; from M6, §16.11's directory; from M10, the barriers of the purge, the sweep, evacuation's staged decision, seals, merges, the roll-up lock, the migration and the drop job (§11), §11.14's remote search, §16's search tools, §18's injected network and charging state, RECORD.md's search fields and, after format 2's freeze, production's write-budget counters ([owner decision 174](#od-174)).
- **Subprotocol messages, API routes, tables:** none; release builds carry no test route.
- **Services and config:** server/local's 3-master Redis Cluster and 8-drive MinIO, T3's MinIO clusters (22.4); RUN-ALL, TEST-PERF and test-main cells.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §19 runs T6 with test roots and LE staging, runs M2's staging cluster on the production hosts' PM9A3 set with §19.6's settings and counters, rebuilt empty and SMART-rechecked before M3 (§19.11), runs 22.9's file-cluster suite on every new cluster before `place_new` names it, and gives §19.11's format2 gate a purge mode and a `drop` mode (observe, on) that admit only internal networks and design partners while observing (D-TEST-12, D-TEST-18); §23.8 gates freezes in D-PHASE-7's two steps, the escrow order at M6's entry on FS-46 and 20.9's benchmark, and burners on D-MAIL-9; §23.4's M2 exit names FS-57 to FS-63, FS-113, FS-114's head and marker cases, FS-116 to FS-118 and FS-72's and FS-95's format-1 cases, and §23.6's gate map lists each FS at every gate its row names, later parts included (FS-19, FS-23, FS-30, FS-38, FS-39, FS-41, FS-42, FS-47, FS-66, FS-69, FS-76 to FS-78, FS-80, FS-83 to FS-88, FS-92, FS-97 to FS-101, FS-106, FS-109 to FS-112, FS-114, FS-124 and FS-125; FS-82's mail and coverage cases at M7 and M8), FS-63 and FS-119 again at each next metadata cluster, FS-119 first at M3-out, M10's schedules, and S7's SNI-less abuse@`<root>` case at M5; every index file an erasure rewrites fits §11.12's closure upload bound; each owning section names a barrier at each linearization point (22.8's rules).

### 22.16 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unaudited novel crypto passes every test, 0x0010 having no vectors ([owner decision 99](#od-99)) | Medium | Critical | 22.10's interop artifact; §10.4's mapping and KATs; its disclosure ([owner decision 119](#od-119)) |
| A scanner gap lets a leak pass | Medium | High | decompression, self-test, schema guard |
| A race no schedule names passes every test | Medium | High | barriers at every linearization point; the seeded explorer; TLC and Porcupine (D-TEST-10) |
| Measured drive writes miss D-TEST-11's gate (format 1) or D-TEST-13's (format 2, the index on everywhere) | Medium | High | 1 KiB blocks and §19.6's settings, chosen at M2 on format 2's projection too; [owner decision 172](#od-172)'s companion cadence; M2's exit and each freeze wait for their gate, format 2's on D-TEST-13's projection, confirmed on production after the freeze ([owner decision 174](#od-174)) |
| The governor's accounts charge P2 twice, let a class other than P0 issue while P0 holds the bucket empty, or keep the other classes stopped after a P0 storm ends, so pushes are refused early or the drives wear past the budget by more than P0's forgiven excess | Low | High | one conservation equation and FI-14 (a) and (b), checked after every step; FS-116's exact-cost schedule and its mutant before D-TEST-11's hardware run; FS-117's day of P0 alone past the refill, the day after it, and its mutants |
| HE refuses port 25, blocking outbound conformance | Unknown | High | asked in M0 (§23.7) |
| Test hooks reach a release, exposing keys or stalling steps | Low | Critical | build tag; `make check` |
| A jetsam regression reaches users | Medium | Medium | surrogates; `make size` |
| A purge bug deletes a newest version's content | Low | Critical | observe mode and its soak (D-TEST-12); FI-16 model-checked; FS-64 to FS-71 |
| The oracle shares a normalization bug with the index | Medium | Medium | written apart, sharing only the published tables; fixed vectors; 22.6's reference extractor |
| A phone's "search more" leaks the query through what it fetches | Low | High | FI-23's trace equality; no body fetched before an open; a remote search's sizes and evs logs are FI-24's |
| A malicious server injecting mail reads trigram presence from padded sizes (DBREACH) | Medium | High | no compression; Padmé and §11.14's keyed pad; 22.7's fixture fails the build on a recovered code |
| A drop bug deletes live content | Low | Critical | D-TEST-18's observe soak; FI-27 and I-EVS-15 model-checked; FS-89 to FS-96 |

## 23. Phasing, milestones, and rollout

### 23.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns X15: milestones M0-M10 on two tracks, staffing, exit criteria, the gate map, freezes, lead times, publication and merges. What each milestone builds belongs to §4-§18 and §21; environments, hardware and releases to §19; tests and gates to §22.

### 23.3 What exists today

- No repo has a `sidecar` branch; sidecar is PUBLIC since [owner decision 118](#od-118)'s flip, its two `main` commits holding only documents (§4.3).
- Releases check out `main` in every repo (build/all/run.sh:666-671, :825-876). server's lock pins each sibling's commit (server/local/source-graph/lock.yml:7-39), checked against each HEAD (server/local/source-graph/source_graph_test.go:135-141); sn builds server's packages and repeats its replaces, which Go does not inherit (sn/go.mod:212-215).
- A migration's version is its slice index plus one (server/db_migrations.go:163-165), so an applied migration cannot move.

### 23.4 Milestones

Each milestone is a vertical slice (PLAN.md:36) with entry and exit reviews and a dark deploy. RS1-RS3 are recURd's stages (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:892-904; RECORD.md, §16.8), each released once its last item lands; BS1 is the burner launch. **v0** is what personal networks get, M0-M5 and M7-M9, with app hosts at M8; **v1** is M6, M10 and M7-M9's Team items, M10 bringing versionless objects and search to every network ([owner decision 163](#od-163)); **Later** follows M9 and M10. `sidecar` branches start at M0 in every touched repo ([owner decision 196](#od-196)): sidecar, connect, server, sdk, build and sn, which must repeat server's sidecar replace (23.3); xops for D-OPS-18's dumps; warp for §19.11's W5, W2 and W8; mmm; config (pro.yml's `sidecar:` blocks, `preview_networks`); vault; and the minio fork for D-OPS-20's build ([owner decision 195](#od-195)). M0-M10 build straight through on those branches, in dependency order; 23.8 says what happens at a gate the build cannot meet ([owner decision 194](#od-194)).

### 23.5 X15: two tracks and staffing

Team A (recURd) builds M0-M4 and M6; team B (mail and burner, [owner decision 9](#od-9)) builds M5 and M7-M9, with four engineers by M2's exit: one from M0 on `smtpproof`'s BDAT and DATA proofs ([owner decision 125](#od-125)) and mail's lead times, then one each for edges and DNS, mail ingress and receivers, and app seams. M5 is on track B because M7 needs its dns edge, DNSSEC soak, C9 and abuse intake, and RS2 its TLS edge. If team B is not staffed by M2's exit, team A builds M5 before M6, M7-M9 follow M6, and the owner hears then.

M10 is track A's ([owner decision 169](#od-169)): about three more engineers, hired from M3's entry, build §11's format 2, the index and the search tools from M4's exit beside M6, about 9-12 engineer-months by inference; its hold, team, mail and phone cases wait for M5, M6, M7 and M8 (D-PHASE-8). If the engineers are not there by M4's exit, M10 follows M6, and the owner hears then.

M2's critical path is §10.4's subset ([owner decision 43](#od-43)'s 2-4 engineer-months) and §22.10's 0x0010 interop; §7.9, §11 and gkm build in parallel against a fake of the subset, and D-TEST-11's run needs the production hosts and their PM9A3 set before M2's exit (23.7). If either slips, M2's exit and every later milestone's exit slip with it, since both tracks share M0-M2; the build goes on, with formats unfrozen ([owner decision 194](#od-194); 23.8).

### 23.6 Decisions that block each milestone

Peer review closed every question owner decisions [1](#od-1)-[135](#od-135) left to it on 2026-11-04; owner decisions [141](#od-141)-[145](#od-145) decided the five it raised (Q-EVS-8, Q-MCP-6, Q-OPS-9, Q-KEYS-15, Q-OPS-10), [owner decision 140](#od-140)'s corrected record closed Q-EVS-9, owner decisions [146](#od-146)-[166](#od-166) settled the second round and the 2026-11-05 additions, and owner decisions [167](#od-167)-[184](#od-184) answered every v1 question (Q-EVS-19 to Q-EVS-23, Q-MCP-7 to Q-MCP-9, Q-SDK-6, Q-PROTO-4, Q-ACL-11, Q-KEYS-16, Q-ABUSE-7, Q-PHASE-9 and Q-PHASE-10; 23.12, Appendix B), [owner decision 185](#od-185) the SDK fixes' question, owner decisions [186](#od-186)-[191](#od-191) the final meta review's (Q-EVS-24, which [owner decision 190](#od-190) refines, Q-PROTO-4's answer, which owner decisions [188](#od-188) and [191](#od-191) amend, and the presence countersignature's reach), owner decisions [192](#od-192)-[196](#od-196) those of the implementation handoff, and [owner decision 197](#od-197) the apps' network extensions, whose design raised two owner questions: Q-SDK-7, which owner decisions [215](#od-215) and [216](#od-216) decide for M4's entry, and Q-BRIDGE-8, open now, at M8's (18.13, 17.14). The map puts each item at the review that needs it: a Gn-in needs its design closure, a Gn-out its schedules passing on their rows' tiers, each step at the Gn-out of the milestone that ships its mechanism. The owner keeps one launch call on measured data: accepting the SNI loss M7's census finds, before BS1 (D-MAIL-9; [owner decision 34](#od-34)).

### 23.7 External lead times

Each item gives (due; start).

- **Domains** (their dates; M0): ur.network expires 2027-07-02, renewed to 2036 (§12.4); bringyour.com 2027-11-15 (RDAP, 2026-11-03).
- **File cluster** (the hosts with their PM9A3 set before M2's exit, staging M2 for D-TEST-11 until M3 rebuilds them empty (23.4); the rest by M3; M0): §19.6's 4 hosts at one site, each with 2 × Samsung PM9A3 1.92 TB M.2 22110 (the 8-drive metadata set), 16 × 16 TB HDDs, 2 × 25 GbE and free NVMe bays; 2-4 PM9A3 spares and the cold spare chassis with its drives (owner decisions [20](#od-20), [21](#od-21), [94](#od-94), [116](#od-116), [136](#od-136)-[139](#od-139)). The next metadata cluster, a tracked year-one item, is ordered when §19.9's triggers fire or monitor's 30-day trend projects one within its lead time, at about 1.25× year one's load (about 1.2× with v1's index on 4 KiB blocks). The second takes the hosts' free bays and later ones new hosts at the site, whose lead time the projection includes. §19.9 sizes year two's count from §22.8's per-push, per-object and per-batch measurements (D-OPS-17). The segment placement and added HDD capacity are ordered by §19.9's hdd trigger, ahead of year two's HDD load, and the move tool by its cohorts row, before the earliest projected cohort exhaustion.
- **`urnetwork/minio`** (before any push; M0): the owner creates the GitHub repo of D-OPS-20's fork ([owner decision 195](#od-195)).
- **LE domain override** (M5; M0): "a few weeks", untimed (mmm/lag.dev/ops/letsencrypt.md:291-294).
- **dns edge** (M5; M0): two new hosts at the site, with their own addresses (owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [123](#od-123)).
- **Platform names, company MX** (M5; M2): off ur.network before the NS switch (§12.4).
- **On-call, abuse readiness** (M3, M5, then M6; M2): a two-person out-of-hours infrastructure rota on one pager service, 30 min to acknowledge before escalation ([owner decision 143](#od-143)); DMCA agent, registrar and Search Console contacts, business-hours abuse review, and registrar, registry and law-enforcement notices on that pager from M5 (owner decisions [95](#od-95), [134](#od-134)); 24/7 review from M6 (§19.8).
- **Counsel** (M5; M3): confirms [owner decision 133](#od-133)'s condition and each hold kind's applicability (`preserve_2703f`, `report_2258a`) before holds ship (§21.9).
- **DNSSEC** (M7; M5): 30 clean days before the DS (§12.6).
- **HE TCP 25 egress, reverse delegation, feedback loops** (M9's entry; M0): unknown, so ask first; PTRs name bringyour.com hosts ([owner decision 124](#od-124); §14.9).
- **App releases** (M3, then M8; M1): 18.7's credential rules, in the desktop app and extension releases that stop persisting `by_jwt` (the extension's in `chrome.storage.local`), before §7.4's stage 2 ([owner decision 45](#od-45); D-SDK-11, D-TRUST-3), then the burner and bridge seams (§18.15).

### 23.8 Review gates

- **G0.** Peer review of DESIGN.md; the density rule: no content duplicated across sections (each item in its owning section, cited elsewhere), normative formats and state machines in fenced blocks, prose dense; D-ARCH-4's assembly check passes; 23.6's M0-M2 items settled; RECORD.md reviewed here or by M2's entry. The density rule replaced the OUTLINE word ceilings (+10%) on 2026-11-04: the normative formats and state machines peer review required put every section over its ceiling (the assembly's word table), and a ceiling cuts normative content where this rule cuts repetition. The owner signed G0 on 2026-11-06 ([owner decision 193](#od-193)). A reviewer's re-check of the 21 items DESIGN-REVIEW-RESPONSE.md places at G0, the density review and RECORD.md's draft run beside M0's bootstrap, and their findings return as Q- items (D-PHASE-2), so a finding can change something already built.
- **Freezes.** With no external review ([owner decision 99](#od-99)), each format freezes twice: its specification at Gn-in, its bytes at Gn-out on 22.10's evidence, whose FS rows are 23.6's schedules for that gate (D-PHASE-7). At M2: §7.9's records, its presence row and §6.9's countersignature fields among them (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187), [189](#od-189), [192](#od-192)); format 1, whose bytes, D-PHASE-9's reservations included, also wait for D-TEST-11's nvme gate, its erasure and deposit bytes freezing on §22.5's §11 tests, FS-23 and FS-47 while FS-13, FS-23's mailbox case and FS-47's mail case keep their M7 gates; credential 0xF552, suite 0x0010 and D-KEYS-10's delivery wire (ReaderKey, KeyDelivery and gkm's wrap and recovery paths), whose bytes freeze with §22.10's 0x0010 interop artifact, a gap in any step it requires holding the freeze unless a second peer covers that step. At M3: `record.proto`, [owner decision 142](#od-142)'s tainted-run rule and CanonicalAction's reserved field 37 included. At M6: the escrow order (D-QUOTA-9), frozen at M6's entry once FS-46 and 20.9's benchmark pass on M4's dark build, the benchmark rerunning at its exit; `directory.proto`'s announcement, request, decision and notice messages, specified at M6's Gn-in, bytes at its Gn-out. At M9: `smtpproof/SPEC.md`. At M10: format 2, with the DROP payload and `directory.proto`'s cards, its bytes also waiting for D-TEST-13's computed gate ([owner decision 174](#od-174)), repos migrating only after it (23.9); `search.proto`'s messages, types 0x1404 and 0x1405 and Hello's feature bits 0 and 1, additive to M2's wire.
- **Gn-in.** 23.6's design closure for the gate; specifications freeze; changes since G0 and §22's exit-test plan reviewed.
- **Gn-out.** Exit criteria shown, with 23.6's schedules passing; formats freeze; §22's privacy assertions pass; §2.8's list updated (I-18); `commit-msg --scan main..sidecar` clean (connect/CODESTYLE.md:83); the owner approves the deploy and merges (23.9).
- **Gates the build cannot meet.** M0-M10 build straight through in dependency order on the `sidecar` branches, with no stop at a Gn-out ([owner decision 194](#od-194)). Each gate's local checks run and are reported, and anything needing hardware, production or people stays listed open: M2's format-1 freeze on D-TEST-11's PM9A3 run, M0's and M1's stages in production, each Gn-out's approval to merge. This changes how the milestones are executed, not what freezes when: the Freezes order above still decides what may reach a production store (D-PHASE-7). Formats stay unfrozen meanwhile, so a later hardware miss can force rework in later milestones.
- **Releases.** D-TRUST-3 holds; RS1's copy discloses I-10's no-policy allow-all ([owner decision 120](#od-120)); "end-to-end encrypted" waits only for D-TRUST-4's document, §21.11's canary and §2.18's unaudited-cryptography disclosure (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:932-934; owner decisions [77](#od-77), [119](#od-119)); BS1 waits for 23.6's census call and M8's mail-indexer readiness, never for a user's indexer ([owner decision 12](#od-12)).

### 23.9 Branches, merges, and the source-graph lock

1. **Publication.** sidecar is public from [owner decision 118](#od-118)'s flip (2026-11-04), as it is ([owner decision 117](#od-117)); every `sidecar` branch uses its repo's normal remote (§4.8).
2. **Merges.** At each Gn-out, every touched repo merges `sidecar` into `main` in §4.8's order (D-REPO-5), re-pinning the lock (23.3); deploys, pilots and releases build from `main`, gated in `config/<env>/sidecar.yml` (D-OPS-10).
3. **Migrations.** §19.7's groups stay pending under `sidecar_pending` (D-OPS-6) until their own Gn-out registers them, and never change after (23.3), so one track's merge never applies the other's group (FS-54) and M3's pilot runs on production ([owner decision 118](#od-118)).
4. **Format 2.** After M10's Gn-out, §19.11's `format2` gate opens to internal networks and design partners; admitted networks' repos migrate as §11.6 states; the purge runs in observe mode until D-TEST-12's production soak shows no candidate a retained version names, then deletes; drops run in observe mode until D-TEST-18's soak, then delete (D-PHASE-12); D-TEST-13's production confirmation runs while the gate admits only those networks, a miss holding it there ([owner decision 174](#od-174)); and only then does the gate open by percent (D-PHASE-10).

### 23.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Merges held until RS1 on private mirrors ([owner decision 107](#od-107)) | no unreleased server code public | pilot and edges wait or run on canary | rejected ([owner decision 118](#od-118)) |
| One freeze per format | one review | at Gn-in, no implementation evidence; at Gn-out, no fixed specification for M2's parallel work | rejected (D-PHASE-7) |
| Format 2 inside M6 | v1 as defined today; one fewer milestone | RS2 waits for an unrelated feature; M6 grows by ~9-12 engineer-months | not taken ([owner decision 169](#od-169)) |
| Versionless fields in format 1 at M2, their collection later with the index | the cheapest format change | the owner chose v1 with a new format ([owner decision 163](#od-163)) | ruled out |
| D-TEST-13's gate computed from M2's price table and T3's counts, confirmed on production after the freeze | no hardware bought early | a miss found after the freeze costs clusters sooner or a format change | chosen ([owner decision 174](#od-174)) |
| The next cluster's 8 × PM9A3 as M10's staging set | measured before the freeze | drives bought ahead of the trigger, its model fixed early | not taken ([owner decision 174](#od-174)) |

### 23.11 Decisions proposed

**D-PHASE-1 (proposed).** Build 23.4's milestones in dependency order, straight through on the `sidecar` branches ([owner decision 194](#od-194); 23.8), staffed as 23.5 proposes, releasing each recURd stage once its last item lands. *Why:* R-PHASE-4, whose stages ship whole (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:907), and R-PHASE-10; the sections' Phasing share these dependencies; and several gates need hardware, production or people the build does not have, where stopping at each Gn-out and building M0-M2 then re-planning were not taken.

**D-PHASE-2 (proposed).** No code is written before G0, which the owner signed on 2026-11-06, its re-checks, density review and RECORD.md draft running beside M0's bootstrap ([owner decision 193](#od-193); 23.8); an unsettled blocker defers what it blocks; until the owner decides an open question, text written at its recommendation is marked "(proposed; Q-...)" (D-ARCH-4); and an implementation finding that changes a D- item returns to review as a Q- item, as do those re-checks' and that review's findings. *Why:* R-PHASE-1; owner rule 8.

**D-PHASE-3 (proposed).** §7.4's stage 1 and D-TEAM-14 reach production log-only at M0's Gn-out, so the 14 log-only days overlap M1; the desktop app and extension releases with §18.7's credential rules, then stage 2, reach production before M3's pilot; until stage 2 is live, sidecar enrollment is limited to `config/<env>/sidecar.yml`'s `preview_networks`. *Why:* D-TRUST-3, kept off the critical path.

**D-PHASE-4 (proposed).** 23.7's M0 items, and §10.4's MLS subset with its X-Wing KAT, start in M0. *Why:* each is slow or unpredictable to finish, and the subset is M2's critical path (23.5).

**D-PHASE-5 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 118](#od-118): every touched repo merges `sidecar` into `main` at each Gn-out (23.9).

**D-PHASE-6 (proposed).** The design-partner pilot starts at M3's exit; its measures (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:913-920) feed M6's entry review, which may re-plan the recURd track. *Why:* "Rework the developer hook before building the team layer" (:915).

**D-PHASE-7 (proposed).** Each frozen format freezes twice: its specification at its milestone's Gn-in and its final bytes at its Gn-out, on 22.10's evidence (23.8); no production store holds a format before its final freeze. The escrow order (D-QUOTA-9) is the one Gn-in that needs implementation evidence: M4 builds it dark, and M6's Gn-in freezes it on that build (23.8). *Why:* an entry review cannot show implementation evidence unless an earlier milestone built the code, and [owner decision 92](#od-92)'s hot-path benchmark must pass before M6's billing builds on the order; data on local, T3, canary and the staging cluster is rebuilt, so a change between the two freezes costs no migration.

**D-PHASE-8 (proposed).** Format 2 is milestone M10 (23.4), built on track A from M4's exit beside M6 with its own entry and exit reviews; no recURd stage waits for it, and its hold, team, mail and phone cases run at the later of M10's exit and, respectively, M5's, M6's, M7's or M8's. *Why:* [owner decision 169](#od-169) places it, and [owner decision 163](#od-163) puts all of it in v1; RS2's items (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:897-899) do not include search, so holding RS2 for format 2's freeze would delay a release for another feature.

**D-PHASE-9 (proposed).** A format that freezes reserves the numbers a decided later format or milestone needs. Its code refuses data that uses a later format's numbers as needing that format, never as tampering; knows a reserved kind, applying its fixed kind default (the `directory` kind's readers and writers, §8.5, D-ACL-24); ignores a field that only guides writers; and from the freeze honors a reserved access limit and evaluates a reserved policy atom, as the implicit document's directory rule names `autogroup:dst-owner` from M2, Team documents from M6 (§8.4, §8.5). Format 1 reserves at M2 format 2's numbers, the drop's and the erasure cut's among them (EvsPush flags 256 and 512 and fields 33 and 34, EvsHead's index_epoch, window bit 5, the read states `drop_pending` and `dropped`), and M6's directory's: the `directory` kind, acl.proto's `autogroup:dst-owner` atom and `EvsShare.expires`, and config.proto's `ServiceSettings.directory` (§7.9, §8.4, §8.8, §10.5, §11); the search index's own encoding (`evsindex.proto`, sealed inside the versioning-2 files format 1 reserves), its tombstone tables and diff rules included, needs no number at M2 and freezes with format 2 at M10 (§11.14); `record.proto` reserves CanonicalAction's field 37 at M3 (§16.8); no number is reserved for keep-last-n ([owner decision 165](#od-165)). *Why:* [owner decision 163](#od-163), and the directory (owner decisions [171](#od-171), [180](#od-180)) writes into formats that freeze at M2; an upgrade must not raise fork or missing-segment alarms on older devices, a config field or atom that older devices refused would stop the network, and a reader that ignored a share's expiry would widen access.

**D-PHASE-10 (proposed).** Format 2 reaches production only after its final freeze, through §19.11's `format2` gate in 23.9's order, and deletes replaced versionless content only after D-TEST-12's soak and dropped history only after D-TEST-18's (D-PHASE-12). *Why:* D-PHASE-7's data rule; a purge or migration bug must surface on internal data first.

**D-PHASE-11 (proposed).** The directory ships at M6 on format 1: announce, request, decision, erasure request and coordination entries in its streams, read 64 to a request (§11.9), and versioned notices; its erasure takes `admin` in M2's code, as every repo's (§11.12). It moves to cards, repo files and its index with M10, its format-2 cases running at the later of M6's and M10's exits. M2 reserves its kind, atom and fields (D-PHASE-9). *Why:* [owner decision 169](#od-169) keeps RS2 off format 2, and [owner decision 170](#od-170)'s announcements need only streams.

**D-PHASE-12 (proposed).** Drop deletes reach production only after D-TEST-18's soak, through §19.11's `format2.drop` gate in 23.9's order. *Why:* as D-PHASE-10, for the costlier delete path ([owner decision 173](#od-173)).

Options (a), early staging drives, and (c), synthetic repos on production, were not taken. *Residual:* none.

| A Gn-out merge breaks the running release | Medium | High | R-PHASE-8; pending migrations (D-OPS-6; FS-54, FS-55); gates off by default (D-OPS-10) |
| From M6 until M8's wakes, an unwitnessed shared group stops writing at `witness_bound_hours` | Medium | Medium | agents witness; a 24 h alarm; the bound goes up to 168 h ([owner decision 129](#od-129)) |
| Reader transfer, not NVMe, binds a 5,000-member Team's directory, and per-stream reads its M6 form | Medium | Medium | §16.11's policy (phones off the follow, 15-minute desktop syncs, reproduced heads, moved streams read 64 to a request); FS-86 gates §16.11's cost table at the Team limit from M6's exit, a miss going to the owner; a sharded cards ref if §22.8 binds |
| Senders without SNI defer; phone-only users, on iOS or Android, miss codes | High | High | the M7 census gates BS1; M8's mail indexer paths and prompt; the `foreground-only` copy before a first burner (owner decisions [12](#od-12), [197](#od-197)) |
| Format 2 misses D-TEST-13 at 2× year one with the index on everywhere ([owner decision 156](#od-156)), holding M10's freeze | Medium | High | 1 KiB blocks chosen at M2 on its projection (D-TEST-11); [owner decision 172](#od-172)'s companion cadence; the write budget sheds; the next cluster sooner (§19.9) |
| A purge, drop or migration bug destroys live content on production | Low | Critical | D-PHASE-10's and D-PHASE-12's staged rollouts, D-TEST-12's and D-TEST-18's soaks; FS-64 to FS-72 and FS-89 to FS-96 at M10-out |
| M10's engineers are not hired by M4's exit, and search lands after RS2 | Medium | Medium | 23.5's fallback, M10 after M6, which returns to the owner; no stage waits for it |
| No indexer is designated, so phones download all at "search more" ([owner decision 177](#od-177)) | High | Low | [owner decision 155](#od-155)'s model; the app's indexer prompt names remote search; `ur indexer add --services search` |
| Format 2's computed write cost misses on production after the freeze | Medium | High | [owner decision 174](#od-174)'s accepted risk: §19.9's next cluster sooner ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) or a later format change; the gate holds at internal networks and design partners meanwhile (D-TEST-13) |
| A rollback to format-1 binaries after format-2 data exists strands staged content | Low | High | FS-72's rollback case; format-2 batches left to a format-2 evacuator |
| A G0 re-check or the density review, running beside M0's bootstrap, finds something that changes what is already built ([owner decision 193](#od-193)) | Medium | Medium | Findings return as Q- items (D-PHASE-2); the first format freeze is M2's (23.8), so a finding before it touches no frozen format |
| Later milestones build on formats that stay unfrozen, so a hardware miss, at D-TEST-11's run or later, forces rework in them ([owner decision 194](#od-194)) | Medium | High | 23.8's freeze order still decides what reaches a production store (D-PHASE-7), and data on local, T3, canary and the staging cluster is rebuilt |

### 23.16 Phasing

23.6 is re-read at every Gn-in; work after M9 and M10, RS3 included, is 23.4's "Later"; M10's later cases are re-read at M5's, M6's, M7's and M8's Gn-in.
